Thirdly, we derive a thermodynamically consistent three-dimensional diffuse-interface model for solute-containing droplets that is formulated as a three-phase Cahn-Hilliard/Allen-Cahn system. By numerically solving the coupled system of equations, we explore representative scenarios that show that this model reproduces and generalizes features of the sharp-interface model. These interconnected studies on the dynamics of aerosol droplet evaporation are relevant in order to quantitatively assess the airborne infection risk under varying environmental conditions.

articles.title: Hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet 2³S(L = 0)-state in the two-muonic helium {}³He μ₂ atom
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.33059v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet 2³S(L = 0)-state in the two-muonic helium {}³He μ₂ atom is determined to high accuracy. Such a structure arises as a result of hyperfine (or spin-spin) interaction between the triplet two-muonic shell and non-zero spin of the central helicon nucleus. Our result for the hyperfine structure splitting is Δ approx 2.5811701551505 · 10⁸ MHz, where the standard uncertainty has been evaluated as ± 100 Hz.

articles.title: A Momentum-weighted Interface Stabilization Approach for Fluid-Structure Interaction with Strong Added-Mass Effects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.42034v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partitioned fluid-structure interaction (FSI) schemes enable the reuse of standalone fluid and structural solvers but may exhibit poor convergence under strong added-mass effects, particularly when structural inertia is small relative to fluid inertia. This work examines the added-mass instability of Dirichlet-Neumann partitioned coupling through a fixed-point analysis of the discrete FSI system. Comparison with the monolithic formulation identifies the interface momentum contributions lagged during partitioned iterations and establishes spectral conditions governing convergence. Motivated by this analysis, a momentum-weighted interface stabilization (MWIS) method is developed by augmenting the fluid pressure operator with an approximation of the coupled interface momentum response. The augmentation is fixed-point consistent, leaving the converged discrete solution unchanged when the coupled equations are solved to convergence. A sparse approximation constructed from fluid and structural interface operators and element metrics limits additional storage and inter-solver data exchange. Numerical experiments involving a linear FSI model and established nonlinear benchmarks demonstrate improved convergence and coupling robustness under strong added-mass effects compared with the baseline Dirichlet-Neumann scheme. The results establish an operator-based framework for stabilizing partitioned FSI iterations while retaining the modularity of standalone solvers.

articles.title: Trajectory-based cycle-level pedestrian crash prediction at intersections: A novel non-linear link function for block maxima led Bayesian GEV framework addressing heterogeneous traffic conditions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.12963v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This study develops a cycle-level framework for estimating pedestrian crash risk at signalized intersections under heterogeneous, non-lane-based traffic. Existing approaches often assume linear relationships between covariates and parameters, oversimplifying the complex, non-monotonic interactions among motorized vehicles (MVs), non-motorized vehicles (NMVs), and pedestrians. To address this limitation, the framework introduces a non-linear link function within a Bayesian generalized extreme value (GEV) structure to capture how traffic effects vary. It applies extreme value theory through the block maxima approach using post-encroachment time as a surrogate safety measure, with each signal cycle serving as an analysis block. It also proposes a behaviour-normalized modified crash risk (MRC) metric to account for pedestrians' habitual risk-taking behaviour in Dhaka's mixed traffic. Seven hierarchical Bayesian models were estimated using Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulation and compared using the deviance information criterion. Models with a non-linear link function only in the GEV location parameter fit the data better than their linear counterparts. Results suggest pedestrian speed is negatively associated with crash risk, while flow and speed of MVs, pedestrian flow, and NMV conflicting speed show positive associations, though all remain uncertain. The selected model's MRC estimate was close to the observed crashes at a 93% confidence level tuned to this dataset. These results suggest that the non-linear structure adds flexibility for capturing the non-stationary and non-linear nature of traffic extremes. This framework is a step towards proactive identification of pedestrian crash risk and after wider validation, it could support adaptive signal control and safety interventions in mixed-traffic environments.

articles.title: Scoliosis5K: Multimodal Gait Analysis via Clip-Conditioned RGB-Silhouette Fusion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Color walking video records body boundary motion alongside clothing folds, surface appearance, and recording-environment cues. To examine what an explicit binary silhouette contributes to participant-level classification of scoliosis-related gait when a classifier already observes the paired color sequence, we construct Scoliosis5K, a multi-site collection of 4,998 corridor-walking sequences across 3,010 participant identifiers in which RGB person crops, binary silhouettes, and two-dimensional poses share each recording identifier and frame index. Our architecture uses each patch's pixel deviation from its clip mean to weight two low-rank query and value updates inside a pretrained RGB encoder, fusing the resulting video representation with a silhouette transformer sequence and regional kernel ridge scores extracted from one native-resolution RGB frame per window. Across 988 participants in five participant-disjoint cross-validation folds and three training seeds, the complete system reaches 83.77% accuracy and 79.91% macro-averaged F1, compared with 83.27% accuracy and 79.56% macro-F1 when the video RGB encoder remains frozen under identical inputs. Zeroing the silhouette vector at fixed weights shifts overall accuracy by only 0.10 percentage points while raising positive-category recall from 68.52% to 77.78% and lowering recall for both remaining categories. Macro-averaged AUROC is 0.950 across the cohort and 0.879 among participant pairs matched on acquisition site and recording-count group.

articles.title: A Continuous Relaxation of Quantization-Aware Training
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.27056v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantization is a critical piece of the deployment pipeline in the era of large generative models. Low-bit quantization, particularly 2-bits or sub-2-bits, is a notoriously difficult problem, particularly when using a channelwise quantization scheme which has been shown as a leading candidate for hardware-efficiency. The key challenges with low-bit quantization range from limited quantization levels to saddle points or flat regions in the loss surface. In this paper, we look at the problem of flat quantization loss surfaces through a lens of dynamically changing bitwidth. Unlike existing techniques which either change the bit-precision abruptly or keep it fixed, we propose to gradually alter the bitwidth as the model trains. To this end, we propose RelaxQAT, a continuous relaxation of the QAT process. We also provide simple theoretical and empirical insights behind why RelaxQAT helps the QAT performance. Our extensive experiments demonstrate up to 6.3% average accuracy gains on vision and up to 7.7% better average accuracy on natural language tasks, compared to the leading QAT methods.

articles.title: A Frugal AI Framework for India: Responsible and Right-sized AI
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.27189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: India's AI debate often swings between two insufficient options: replicating the compute-intensive, capital-heavy foundation-model programmes of the United States or China, or remaining a downstream adopter of foreign AI with localised interfaces and safeguards. Neither serves a country that must deliver AI to a very large, diverse population across uneven infrastructure and within constrained budgets. This white paper from the Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI), IIT Madras, proposes a third path: Responsible Frugal AI, which applies principle-based frugal engineering alongside Responsible AI. Responsible Frugal AI is right-sized AI: it fixes the functional requirement first, asks whether AI is needed at all, and then chooses the smallest sufficient model, meeting the requirement with minimal resources while keeping a verified margin, robustness and responsible governance. The framework applies frugality across four dimensions (data, compute, model and operations) through seven levers spanning the AI lifecycle, each with practices and measures. It calls for public AI rails, vernacular-first design, measured resource use, human oversight for high-stakes decisions, and a cap on total resource consumption so that efficiency gains are not cancelled out by rising usage. We argue that India is resource-imbalanced rather than resource-poor, and that frugal principles offer the most viable route to population-scale deployment, fit naturally with India's digital public infrastructure, and make sovereignty operational by preserving India's capacity to specify, deploy, govern, inspect and adapt its AI systems. A seven-point adoption checklist and eleven policy statements translate the framework into practice, positioning AI in India as a responsible, frugal public-value system that maximises social value per rupee and per joule.

articles.title: Block Search Conditioned on Features for Sequential Quantum Data Encoding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.27587v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sequential quantum data encoding is addressed through the joint selection of input features and encoding blocks within a fixed quantum register. At each step, a new feature, a block of operations, its placement, and its rotation weights are selected together from training data, extending the incremental construction of Q-FLAIR. With direct-loss selection (RAW), nine to twelve features were retained in four qubits across five new Bars and Stripes datasets. Under the same final calibration, mean changes relative to the calibrated Q-FLAIR reference were +5.53 percentage points in balanced accuracy, -15.83% in binary cross-entropy (BCE), and +7.79% in area under the ROC curve (AUC). The prespecified success criterion was met in four of five datasets and for the mean paired differences. These results were obtained by comparing complete procedures under a common cap of 32 operations.

articles.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation resolves atomic-scale motion and predicts the structural, mechanical, and dynamic properties of materials, making it cen- tral to materials design and discovery. Yet an MD study requires an expert-driven workflow: designing the simulation, writing reliable input scripts, executing them, and analyzing the results with separate tools. Here we present ChatAtom, a multi-agent large language model system that translates a natural-language request into a complete MD workflow without the user writing input scripts or analysis code. Each agent has a defined responsibility within the workflow. An orchestrator plans the study; the LAMMPS and OVITO agents each use a generator-reviewer pair to prepare and review simulation and visualization scripts before execution; a high-performance computing agent dispatches jobs to remote resources; and an analysis agent interprets the completed run. The work- flow is accessible through a browser interface that streams thermodynamic data and rendered frames during local execution, allowing users to follow the simu- lation as it progresses. The architecture also supports new capabilities through loadable skills without modifying the agents, enabling autonomous hypothesis generation and testing. We evaluate ChatAtom through script-generation bench- marks, an end-to-end study of crack propagation, and a closed-loop campaign. By bringing script generation, execution, visualization, and analysis into one reviewed and observable pipeline, ChatAtom lowers the barrier to conducting MD studies and broadens access to advanced simulation workflows.

articles.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.27741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have endowed multimodal agents with increasingly strong visual perception and long-horizon reasoning capabilities, making VLM-based autonomous game playing feasible. Existing game benchmarks primarily evaluate whether an agent can select appropriate actions from the current visual state across different scenarios and games. However, most of them adopt a step-by-step interaction paradigm where the current visual observation is sent to the agent before each action. In practical deployment, this paradigm introduces two fundamental limitations: the game loop must wait for model inference, making real-time interaction impractical, and repeated VLM calls incur substantial cost. Therefore, we propose PlayScriptBench, a script-based game benchmark that evaluates whether VLMs can synthesize an executable game-playing program from game states. This setting jointly evaluates visual grounding, understanding of game dynamics, long-horizon strategic reasoning, and executable program synthesis, providing a more comprehensive assessment of game-playing agents. To support more tractable evaluation for current general-purpose VLMs, we further introduce a four-stage pipeline --- Explore, Perception, API Construction, and Strategy Composition --- that decomposes controller synthesis into game exploration, state perception, interface construction, and strategic control, enabling agents to progressively construct an executable program. Experiments on 16 games spanning 4 genres show that even strong VLMs struggle on our benchmark, revealing a substantial gap between passive visual game understanding and executable closed-loop game control. These results establish script-based controller synthesis as a complementary direction for benchmarking VLM-based game-playing agents.

articles.title: QuASAR: Toward an LLM-Assisted Framework for Screening, Prototyping, and Assessing Quantum-Advantage Opportunities in Scientific Computing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.27778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying scientific computations that could benefit from quantum algorithms requires both domain knowledge and fluency in quantum algorithm design, expertise that rarely resides in one person. We report results from QuASAR, an experimental, two-agent, LLM-driven pipeline intended to bridge this gap. One agent screens scientific literature for computational kernels with a plausible quantum-algorithmic analogue and proposes candidates, each backed by citations. A second agent independently verifies those citations. For candidates that survive verification, it reconstructs the source's computational structure, formulates a quantum mapping, builds and executes a prototype, and benchmarks it against classical baselines. We applied this pipeline to ten candidate computations drawn from the astrophysics literature. Nine candidates were carried through to a small-scale, benchmarked prototype. We report three in detail, chosen as the clearest examples with the least redundancy across the set. They span combinatorial optimization, stochastic simulation, and Bayesian inference. The pipeline attempted to supply quantum-design expertise a domain scientist might lack, reconstructing source algorithms where one existed and building original, disclosed mappings where none did. None of the three case studies achieved quantum advantage at the tested scales, and their astrophysical framing has not yet undergone expert validation. What the experiment does show is that the pipeline can turn a published idea into a runnable prototype, which a scientist can then inspect, test against classical methods, and decide whether to pursue. QuASAR is an exploratory framework, offered to the community for evaluation, critique, and further development, with an approach that could broaden the use of quantum computing in scientific research and extend to computational improvements more generally.

articles.title: What Helps Language-Model Agents Review Violent Video? A Controlled Comparison with a Human Evidence Reference
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Systems that flag violent video for a human operator can now be built from language models without training, by combining perception models and letting a language model decide. We ask how the observations of the perception models should reach the decision, and which evidence matters. On the XD-Violence test set (799 clips) we fix one set of perception agents (video description, object detection, sound tagging, speech recognition and speech tagging) and one reasoning model, and compare three interfaces: messages between agents, a typed evidence graph explored with tools, and flat text read in one pass; and a single audio-visual model given the raw clip. Two annotators provide a human reference that records the decision, the incident segments and whether they relied on sight, sound or speech. Flat text matches the single model (F1 0.967 against 0.968), while the graph agent and message passing are less accurate; a variant of the graph agent developed on a separate set did not close the gap, and both graph summaries and multi-turn tool use lowered accuracy. These results hold with reworded prompts and with a larger reasoning model, except that the larger model weakens message passing enough for the graph agent to beat it. Sound events improve F1 by +0.012 [+0.004, +0.021], in line with the annotators, who used sound or speech on most violent clips. Citations of stored observations are faithful, changing about half of the decisions when removed, but no more so with the graph than with flat text, and the agent pipeline costs about 3 times the GPU time of the single model. We also report two artefacts of vision-language describers that mislead pipelines built on them.

articles.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
articles.abstract: Author(s): Takuya Nomoto, Kohei Shinohara, Hikaru Watanabe, and Ryotaro Arita A structure-generation framework based on oriented spin space groups enforces uniform site moments and leverages spin-orbit coupling hierarchies to enable accurate, high-throughput prediction of magnetic ground states. [Phys. Rev. X 16, 041052] Published Mon Nov 23, 2026

articles.title: Symmetry-Guided Prediction of Magnetic-Ordered Ground States
articles.abstract: Author(s): Yuhui Li, Sike Zeng, Yutong Yu, Renzheng Xiong, Yu-Jun Zhao, Xiaobing Chen, and Qihang Liu A symmetry-guided framework based on oriented spin space groups systematically generates reliable candidates of magnetic configurations via the online platform SPINGEN, enabling high-throughput theoretical prediction of magnetic ground states. [Phys. Rev. X 16, 041053] Published Mon Nov 23, 2026

articles.title: Early steps in pathogen-induced TTR-amyloid formation
articles.abstract: Motivated by correlations between SARS-CoV-2 infections and transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis, we use molecular dynamics simulations to study whether three protein fragments from the SARS-CoV-2 virus can initiate dissociation of the TTR homotetramer as the first step in the pathway to TTR amyloidosis. We find that the peptides reduce the frequency of transient hydrogen bonds at the monomer–monomer interfaces, potentially decreasing the stability of the TTR tetramer.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Machine-learning molecular dynamics reveals dynamic interfacial structure and active-site accessibility in Fe–N–C single-atom catalysts
articles.abstract: Fe–N–C single-atom catalysts are promising Pt-free catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction. However, molecular-level understanding of their aqueous interfaces remains limited because ab initio molecular dynamics is restricted to small systems and picosecond timescales, whereas existing classical force fields lack the accuracy and transferability required to describe Fe–water coordination and interfacial solvent structure. In this study, we developed an ensemble of equivariant neural-network potentials for the Fe–N–C/water system using spin-polarized density functional theory reference data. Using these potentials, we performed molecular dynamics simulations of up to 5 ns for an interface containing 320 water molecules. Our simulations reveal persistent axial coordination of water at the Fe sites and a locally stabilized hydrogen-bond network. Enhanced sampling shows that coordinated water can exchange between opposite sides of the Fe–N 4 plane through a low-energy pathway with a barrier of ∼0.07 eV, whereas blocking backside solvent access in a bilayer model strongly suppresses this exchange and prolongs site hydration. Constrained ab initio simulations further show that O 2 can approach the Fe site from the side opposite to the coordinated water, while no physically reasonable direct-displacement pathway is identified from the water-coordinated side within the present sampling protocol. Additionally, electronic-response calculations averaged over multiple configurations reveal a contact region with low polarizability, which limits the electronic capacitance of the contact layer under ion-free conditions resembling the potential of zero charge. These results clarify how dynamic hydration governs interfacial structure and active-site accessibility at Fe–N–C/water interfaces.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Controlling excited state intersystem crossing in pyrazolate-bridged Pt(II) dimers by excitation photon energies
articles.abstract: Controlling intersystem crossing (ISC) pathways in transition metal complexes is one of the most challenging topics in photochemistry, as different triplet channels can yield markedly distinct photophysical and photochemical outcomes. Strong Pt–Pt stretching vibrational modes in a di-Pt(II) complex in the metal–metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MMLCT) excited-states have been identified as a key reaction coordinate to modulate the spin–vibronic interactions, enabling ultrafast branched ISC dynamics within short tens of femtoseconds. However, direct experimental evidence for the dominating ISC pathways remains elusive. Here, we employ broadband transient absorption spectroscopy with 10 fs temporal resolution to gain insights into the excited state dynamic pathways by tracking coherent vibrational wave packet motions in a single pyrazolate-bridged Pt(II) complex. By tuning excitation energy within the vibrational manifold of the MMLCT state, we reveal two distinct ISC pathways and the excitation energy dependent branching. High energy excitation launches a 130 cm −1 wave packet coherence on the triplet MMLCT potential energy surface, whereas lower energy excitation induces an additional 140 cm −1 singlet coherence and a delayed 100 cm −1 mode on a ligand centered triplet state. This work provides new insights into spin–vibronic selective photochemistry and a way to control reaction pathways via excitation photon energies.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Optical fingerprinting of di-tyrosine and 3-nitrotyrosine biomarkers as rapid spectroscopic detection of oxidative and nitrosative stress induced by low-temperature plasma
articles.abstract: Di-tyrosine and 3-nitrotyrosine are well-established biomarkers of oxidative and nitrosative stress, often associated with cellular damage. In this study, we investigated the formation of these tyrosine-derived modified products in L-tyrosine solutions treated with low-temperature plasma. The results revealed that plasma treatment leads to the formation of both products, not only in the amino acid solutions but also in the dipeptide glycine–tyrosine solutions. Initially, detection and structural characterization were performed using mass spectrometry, then complemented by absorbance and fluorescence spectroscopies. Optical spectroscopic analysis showed specific features attributed to the formation of di-tyrosine and 3-nitrotyrosine in the plasma exposed samples. These findings confirm di-tyrosine and 3-nitrotyrosine as potential molecular indicators of plasma-induced stress and crucially, offer a fast accessible alternative to the mass-spectrometry workflows, which are technically more complex and require lengthy processing time and analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Spectroscopic characterization of PH 4 ● radical and PH 4 + cation: A matrix isolation and CCSD(T) study
articles.abstract: The simplest species with tetracoordinated phosphorus, PH 4 ● radical and PH 4 + cation, can be relevant to the processes occurring in the radiation-induced and photochemical transformations of the various media containing phosphine molecules, particularly, in astrochemistry and atmospheric chemistry. To our knowledge, the vibrational spectrum of PH 4 ● radical is still unavailable, either experimentally or theoretically, while the infrared (IR) spectrum of PH 4 + cation is known only in strongly interacting media. In this work, we generated the PH 4 ● radical by reactions of thermally mobilized hydrogen atoms in a krypton matrix. Based on comparison with the electron paramagnetic resonance data and quantum chemical calculations at the CCSD(T) level of theory with anharmonic corrections, we have assigned for the first time six vibrational fundamentals in the IR spectra of this radical (assignment of the two strongest modes was confirmed by deuteration). The isolated PH 4 + cation was produced in different noble-gas matrices (Ne, Ar, and Kr) under prolonged x-ray radiolysis of the PH 3 –Ng systems and identified by IR spectroscopy based on comparison with the CCSD(T) calculations. Both fundamentals of PH 4 + were observed in the IR spectra. To confirm the assignment, a two-step experiment was performed in krypton: first, the PH 4 ● radical was generated by vacuum ultraviolet photolysis followed by annealing the photolyzed sample at 35–40 K, and then the PH 4 + cation was produced by ionization of PH 4 ● using x rays. The mechanism of formation of PH 4 + upon x-ray irradiation of isolated phosphine molecules in noble gas matrices without preliminary generation of PH 4 ● and possible role of proton mobility are discussed.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Quantum flow algorithm: Quantum simulations of chemical systems using reduced quantum resources and constant depth quantum circuits
articles.abstract: We assess the performance of the Quantum Flow (QFlow) algorithm employing cost-effective solvers based on the unitary coupled-cluster Ansatz with single and double excitations (QFlow-SD). The resulting energies are benchmarked against those obtained with an analogous QFlow formulation defined in the same active spaces but augmented by higher-rank excitations, including triples and quadruples (QFlow-SDTQ) within a matrix-based implementation, to isolate the effect of excitation rank. Across all molecular systems considered, QFlow-SD closely reproduces the QFlow-SDTQ energies thereby requiring substantially fewer variational parameters while preserving the reduced-qubit footprint of the QFlow algorithm. For this implementation, we perform a series of calculations, including a composite two-step downfolding workflow for H 2 O. To enable simulations beyond the matrix implementation, we introduce and demonstrate a second-quantized many-body formulation of QFlow. Using this formulation, we perform QFlow calculations of larger problems, including H 8 in 6-31G, H 2 O in 6-31G, and a 4 × 4 two-dimensional Fermi–Hubbard model, reducing the parent qubit requirements (26–32 qubits) to eight-qubit active-space subproblems. We compare our results against benchmark DMRG energies and show rapid convergence over QFlow cycles and recovery of a large fraction of correlation energy.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Ion–adsorbate–solvent organization and acceptor-dependent hydrogen transfer at a K + -containing aqueous interface
articles.abstract: Electrolyte ions reorganize electrified aqueous interfaces, yet how such interfacial reorganization governs hydrogen transfer toward chemically distinct acceptors remains poorly understood. Here, Fe 2 N 4 @G is employed as a structurally defined model platform to investigate nitrate reduction at H 3 O + - and K + -containing explicit-water interfaces. The K + -containing environment substantially reorganizes the reaction interface, producing systematic N–O elongation and weakened intramolecular N–O bonding in adsorbed nitrate, together with a persistent and dynamically fluctuating K + –nitrate association. This local ion–adsorbate organization is accompanied by pronounced reorientation of interfacial water and spatial redistribution of hydrogen bonds. Crucially, slow-growth sampling reveals that hydrogen-transfer accessibility within the same K + -containing interface is strongly acceptor dependent. Transfer from interfacial water toward the Fe site to form surface H exhibits a maximum sampled-pathway free-energy requirement of ∼0.84 eV, whereas direct protonation of NH 2 requires only ∼0.06 eV along the sampled pathway. Hydrogen-transfer accessibility therefore emerges as a local, acceptor-specific property of the aqueous interface. These results establish a microscopic ion–adsorbate–solvent picture in which nitrate bonding, cation association, solvent organization, and acceptor identity collectively define the accessibility of interfacial hydrogen-transfer pathways. This acceptor-dependent response provides a physical mechanism for understanding electrolyte regulation of nitrate electroreduction beyond conventional descriptions based solely on intermediate energetics.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Ultrafast excited state dynamics in 5-fluorouracil radical cation
articles.abstract: 5-Fluorouracil (5FU) is a halogenated uracil analog widely used as a radiosensitizer in radiotherapy. Understanding its ionization and subsequent dynamics is essential for elucidating its role in radiation-induced damage mechanisms. In this work, we present a theoretical investigation of the nonadiabatic excited-state dynamics of ionized 5FU and discuss it in connection with a previous extreme-ultraviolet pump–probe experiment performed using high harmonic generation sources. The simulations are carried out using trajectory surface hopping dynamics combined with multireference complete active space self-consistent field electronic structure calculations to describe ultrafast electronic relaxation pathways. Motivated by the experimental conditions and hypotheses, we initiate the dynamics on the second excited state, D 2 , as well as higher-lying excited states up to D 5 . The computed radiationless decay lifetime from D 2 is very fast, in good agreement with the experimentally observed time constants. In contrast, the D 3 state exhibits comparatively slower relaxation, with a decay constant longer than 200 fs, exceeding those of both D 2 and D 5 . We further observe pronounced oscillatory population transfer between the D 1 and D 0 states, which provides a signature of the vibrational modes involved in the nonadiabatic transitions between these two states. Finally, we compare our results with previously reported theoretical uracil cation dynamics and find that 5FU shows a faster decay of the D 1 state compared to uracil. We also observe three ring-opening pathways during the dynamics, with C4–N3 bond cleavage being a more favorable pathway than C2–N1 and C2–N3.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Does spatiotemporal heterogeneity impact conductivity? Reflections from steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopic studies
articles.abstract: Understanding the microscopic origin of ion transport in terms of solution structure and dynamics is fundamental to the development of advanced battery electrolyte systems. Here, we investigated the interconnection between ion conductivity and spatiotemporal heterogeneity in a model electrolyte system comprising of triethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G3) and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) by examining the correlations between the measured conductivities at different LiTFSI concentrations and the spectroscopic data of the corresponding solutions obtained via steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopic experiments. Temperature-dependent measurements were carried out for exploring the dynamic coupling between two solution transport quantities—solution viscosity and conductivity. The addition of LiTFSI to G3 induced pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity, evidenced by excitation wavelength-dependent dispersion of fluorescence emission (Δνem) measurements and fractional viscosity dependence of the measured relaxation rates. Experimental ion conductivities exhibit an inverse power-law dependence on the dissolved solute’s rotational and solvation timescales, σ∝τ−m, revealing a non-homogeneous coupling between local friction and ion transport. The solution spatial heterogeneity, described by Δνem, has been found to correlate inversely with conductivity, indicating that heterogeneous environments hinder ion motion in this electrolyte system. Dynamic heterogeneity, however, did not show such a correlation. To place these observations in a broader context, heterogeneity parameters extracted from literature conductivity–viscosity data for ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents were examined and a correlation between conductivity and spatiotemporal heterogeneity observed. These results suggest micro-heterogeneity as a critical factor for guiding ion transport and should be taken into consideration while designing high-performance electrolyte systems.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Disentangling covalent and noncovalent contributions to excimer stabilization
articles.abstract: This work elucidates the physical origins of excimer stabilization in aromatic and rare-gas systems by jointly analyzing intermolecular noncovalent interactions and electron delocalization. Deformation Density-based Energy Decomposition Analysis (DD-EDA) is extended to excited states within single-reference frameworks, specifically equation-of-motion coupled cluster and time dependent density functional theory, enabling the partitioning of interaction energies into electrostatic, exchange, spin-repulsion, induction, and dispersion contributions. For rare-gas excimers (Ne, Ar, and Kr), a systematic assessment of basis set effects was also performed. In these excimers, excitonic coupling is accompanied by a pronounced enhancement of polarization energy, only partially attributable to dispersion. In polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (benzene, naphthalene, anthracene, and pyrene), dispersion increases significantly upon excitation and represents the dominant attractive contribution; however, it alone does not account for the observed binding strength. Instead, DD-EDA reveals a disproportionate increase in intermolecular exchange relative to spin-repulsion, a feature absent in rare-gas systems. Domain-averaged Fermi hole and delocalization index analyses further uncover the emergence of covalent character. Rare-gas excimers exhibit substantial electron sharing consistent with their strong excitonic coupling, whereas aromatic excimers show pronounced interfacial delocalization, in contrast to the weak or negative delocalization indices in ground-state dimers. Overall, the combined energetic and electronic analyses provide a framework for relating the changes in noncovalent energetic contributions to the intermolecular electron delocalization observed in excited-state complexes, without implying a unique causal decomposition of their stabilization.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Ultrafast free-carrier dynamics and interfacial electron extraction in perovskite/fullerene heterostructures probed by mid-infrared spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Triple-cation perovskites have attracted considerable attention as absorber materials for high-efficiency solar cells. In the present study, ultrafast carrier dynamics in FA 0 . 84 Cs 0 . 12 Rb 0 . 04 PbI 3 thin films and heterostructures containing PCBM and Bis-C12 electron transport layers were investigated by femtosecond visible-pump/mid-infrared (MIR)-probe spectroscopy. The MIR probe at ∼3 μ m directly monitors free-carrier absorption and provides information on carrier-density dynamics. Under low-fluence excitation, the bare perovskite film exhibited carrier-density-dependent decay dynamics. Because the films were relatively thick (∼600 nm), the transient kinetics were analyzed using a diffusion-scaling kinetic model that accounts for dispersive carrier dynamics. A conventional model with γ = 1 did not fully reproduce the fluence-dependent decay behavior, whereas allowing γ to vary improved the description of the experimental kinetics. Global analysis of the bare-perovskite decays yielded a common dispersive exponent of γ = 0.575, consistent with dispersive carrier dynamics. Upon ETL deposition, an additional effective carrier-depletion process associated with interfacial charge extraction was observed. PCBM exhibited a larger effective carrier-depletion parameter than Bis-C12, indicating a larger effective first-order carrier-depletion contribution under the present transport-limited conditions. These results demonstrate that apparent interfacial charge-extraction kinetics in thick polycrystalline perovskite films are strongly influenced by bulk carrier transport. Ultrafast MIR spectroscopy combined with diffusion-scaling kinetic analysis provides a useful framework for evaluating transport-limited carrier dynamics and interfacial charge-extraction processes in perovskite heterostructures.

articles.title: Benchmarking the photophysics of a rigid square-planar Ni(II) complex using GASSCF, MC-PDFT, and TDDFT
articles.abstract: Due to their luminescence and photoredox properties, 4d and 5d metal complexes gained high interest over the recent decades. Among these, many square-planar Pt II -based complexes feature long lived metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) states with lifetimes up to the microsecond timescale. In contrast, their square-planar 3d 8 Ni II analogs have comparatively short-lived sub-nanosecond excited state lifetimes, which are related to a tetrahedral distortion of the square-planar coordination environment and, consequently, to a rapid population of low-lying metal centered (MC) states. This limitation was addressed previously by introducing a molecular design, which combines a rigid tridentate (td) N-heteroleptic carbene ligand with a sterically demanding monodentate (md) ligand and forming a [Ni(td)(md)] + complex. In the present study, our quantum chemical analysis allowed us to elucidate structure–property relationships in [Ni(td)(md)] + by means of a detailed evaluation of the excited state properties related to the energetics of the MLCT and MC states and the composition of the underlying electronic configurations. Therefore, state-of-the-art multiconfigurational methods were utilized to account for both static (RASSCF and GASSCF) and dynamic electron correlation, i.e., RASSCF in combination with multi-configurational pair-density functional theory as well as scalar-relativistic time-dependent density functional theory. Furthermore, the excited state relaxation pathways and the structural properties of the lock-like coordination environment in the excited state manifold were unraveled. Therefore, the present contribution will be the foundation for future joint synthetic, spectroscopic, theoretical studies targeting long-lived excited states in square-planar 3d 8 complexes.
