articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting part distortion before fabrication remains challenging in laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), while thermomechanical simulation is computationally expensive for repeated design evaluations. This study presents a two-branch graph attention network (GAT) to predict three-dimensional surface displacement directly from STL-derived graphs. The first branch learns geometric relationships among connected vertices of a densified STL surface mesh, while the second incorporates 12 part-level descriptors of mass distribution, build-plate contact, overhang, size, and shape. Displacement labels from ANSYS Additive Print simulations are mapped onto STL vertices using Gaussian-kernel weighted averaging. Evaluated on 117 parts using five-fold cross-validation split by part, the model achieves an R² of 0.946 and a mean absolute error of 0.0178 mm for displacement magnitude. Relative to a node-wise multilayer perceptron, GAT improves R² from 0.913 to 0.946; for build-direction displacement, R² increases from 0.903 to 0.939. GAT also outperforms GraphSAGE (R² = 0.936) and a graph convolutional network (R² = 0.934) across all five folds. Ablation experiments show that removing mass-distribution descriptors reduces magnitude R² to 0.900, while removing build-plate contact and overhang descriptors reduces it to 0.920. These results demonstrate the value of combining local mesh connectivity with global geometric descriptors to predict LPBF distortion, enabling faster design iteration and earlier identification of distortion-prone geometries.
articles.abstract_zh: 在激光粉末床熔合 (LPBF) 中，在制造前预测零件变形仍然具有挑战性，而热机械模拟对于重复设计评估的计算成本很高。本研究提出了一个二分支图注意网络 (GAT)，可以直接从 STL 派生图预测三维表面位移。第一个分支学习致密 STL 表面网格的连接顶点之间的几何关系，而第二个分支则包含质量分布、构建板接触、悬垂、尺寸和形状的 12 个零件级描述符。使用高斯核加权平均将 ANSYS Additive Print 模拟中的位移标签映射到 STL 顶点。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 在激光粉末床熔合 (LPBF) 中，在制造前预测零件变形仍然具有挑战性，而热机械模拟对于重复设计评估的计算成本很高。本研究提出了一个二分支图注意网络 (GAT)，可以直接从 STL 派生图预测三维表面位移。第一个分支学习致密 STL 表面网格的连接顶点之间的几何关系，而第二个分支则包含质量分布、构建板接触、悬垂、尺寸和形状的 12 个零件级描述符。使用高斯核加权平均将 ANSYS Additive Print 模拟中的位移标签映射到 STL 顶点。该模型使用按部件划分的五重交叉验证对 117 个部件进行评估，其 R² 为 0.946，位移大小的平均绝对误差为 0.0178 毫米。相对于节点式多层感知器，GAT 将 R² 从 0.913 提高到 0.946；对于构建方向位移，R² 从 0.903 增加到 0.939。 GAT 在所有五个折叠上的性能也优于 GraphSAGE (R² = 0.936) 和图卷积网络 (R² = 0.934)。烧蚀实验表明，移除质量分布描述符可将 R2 幅度降低至 0.900，而移除构建板接触和悬垂描述符会将其降低至 0.920。这些结果证明了将局部网格连通性与全局几何描述符相结合来预测 LPBF 失真的价值，从而实现更快的设计迭代和更早识别容易失真的几何形状。

articles.title: Stability Bands for Feature Attribution: The Core, the Nucleolus and the Bargaining Set of Explained-Variance Games
articles.title_zh: 特征归因的稳定带：核心、核仁和解释方差博弈的讨价还价集
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Shapley-value attributions are the default way of explaining machine-learning predictions in economics, but they report a single number per feature and say nothing about whether a coalition of features that jointly accounts for more than it receives could contest that allocation. We study feature attribution through the core, the nucleolus and the bargaining set of an explained-variance game, in which the worth of a set of features is the variance of the model's predictions that those features generate. For every feature we report a stability band (its range of shares over the core, or over the least core when the core is empty), with the nucleolus as distinguished point and a certificate that the allocation admits no justified objection. Three results organise the approach. First, for linear models the game is exactly 2-additive, with pairwise Harsanyi dividends 2βᵢβⱼσᵢⱼ, so multicollinearity is what creates coalitional structure. Second, in every 2-additive game the prenucleolus coincides with the Shapley value, the (least) core is point-symmetric around it, and the core is non-empty if and only if every cut of the interaction graph has non-negative weight. The Shapley value thus always lies in the prebargaining set, and stability adds information only through band widths and interactions of order three or more. Third, for convex games the bands have a closed form and any allocation can be certified with one minimum cut. In a hedonic price model, the usual mean-SHAP explanation admits a justified objection by the coalition Ratings, ROM, Battery. In a gradient-boosting forecaster of retail orders the exact game has an empty core and strong higher-order interactions; the nucleolus departs from the Shapley value by up to 0.19 variance shares, and sparse third-order surrogates recover it where pairwise ones cannot.
articles.abstract_zh: 沙普利值归因是解释经济学中机器学习预测的默认方式，但它们报告每个特征的单个数字，并且没有提及共同解释的特征联盟是否可以对这种分配提出异议。我们通过解释方差博弈的核心、核仁和讨价还价集来研究特征归因，其中一组特征的价值是这些特征生成的模型预测的方差。对于每个特征，我们报告一个稳定带（其在核心上的份额范围，或者当核心为空时在最小核心上的份额范围），以核仁作为区分点，并证明分配不存在任何合理的反对。三个结果组织了该方法。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 沙普利值归因是解释经济学中机器学习预测的默认方式，但它们报告每个特征的单个数字，并且没有提及共同解释的特征联盟是否可以对这种分配提出异议。我们通过解释方差博弈的核心、核仁和讨价还价集来研究特征归因，其中一组特征的价值是这些特征生成的模型预测的方差。对于每个特征，我们报告一个稳定带（其在核心上的份额范围，或者当核心为空时在最小核心上的份额范围），以核仁作为区分点，并证明分配不存在任何合理的反对。三个结果组织了该方法。首先，对于线性模型，博弈完全是 2 加法，成对的 Harsanyi 红利为 2βᵢβⱼσᵢⱼ，因此多重共线性是创建联盟结构的原因。其次，在每个 2-加性游戏中，前核仁与 Shapley 值一致，（最小）核心围绕其点对称，并且当且仅当交互图的每个切割都具有非负权重时，核心才非空。因此，沙普利值始终位于预协商集中，并且稳定性仅通过带宽和三阶或三阶以上的相互作用来添加信息。第三，对于凸博弈，带具有封闭形式，并且任何分配都可以通过一次最小削减来认证。在特征价格模型中，通常的平均 SHAP 解释承认评级、ROM、电池联盟的合理反对。在零售订单的梯度提升预测器中，精确博弈具有空核心和强大的高阶交互作用；核仁与 Shapley 值的偏差高达 0.19 个方差份额，而稀疏三阶替代项可以在成对替代项无法恢复的情况下恢复它。

articles.title: When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?
articles.title_zh: 积分约束何时以及为何可以提高基于物理的神经网络的准确性？
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adding constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the loss has been reported to improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in several applications, but mathematical understanding of these benefits remains limited. For several partial differential equations (PDEs), we derive stability estimates for losses with and without integral constraints. The comparison reveals that in certain parameter regimes, the standard loss has very weak control over specific error components, and that the integral constraints restore uniform control of these components. This explains when and why the constraints improve accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments support this interpretation. In parameter regimes where the standard loss is predicted to have weak control over those components, the two losses indeed show clear differences in accuracy. Conversely, in regimes where the standard loss retains sufficient control, both losses yield similar accuracy.
articles.abstract_zh: 据报道，通过将控制方程积分到损失中来添加约束可以提高物理信息神经网络（PINN）在多种应用中的准确性，但对这些好处的数学理解仍然有限。对于几个偏微分方程（PDE），我们推导出有和没有积分约束的损失的稳定性估计。比较表明，在某些参数范围内，标准损失对特定误差分量的控制非常弱，而积分约束恢复了对这些分量的统一控制。这解释了约束何时以及为何提高准确性。最后，数值实验支持了这一解释。在预计标准损失对这些组件的控制较弱的参数体系中，这两种损失确实在准确性方面表现出明显的差异。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 据报道，通过将控制方程积分到损失中来添加约束可以提高物理信息神经网络（PINN）在多种应用中的准确性，但对这些好处的数学理解仍然有限。对于几个偏微分方程（PDE），我们推导出有和没有积分约束的损失的稳定性估计。比较表明，在某些参数范围内，标准损失对特定误差分量的控制非常弱，而积分约束恢复了对这些分量的统一控制。这解释了约束何时以及为何提高准确性。最后，数值实验支持了这一解释。在预计标准损失对这些组件的控制较弱的参数体系中，这两种损失确实在准确性方面表现出明显的差异。相反，在标准损失保留足够控制的情况下，两种损失都会产生相似的准确性。

articles.title: Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models
articles.title_zh: 差分隐私分数估计及其在基于分数的生成模型中的应用
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating the score function of a distribution plays a central role in statistics and machine learning, with applications in distribution estimation, sampling, and score-based generative modeling. However, learning scores from sensitive data raises privacy concerns. These concerns are particularly pronounced in score-based generative modeling, where trained models may memorize individual training examples and expose sensitive information through membership inference and data extraction attacks. Although non-private score estimation has been extensively studied, the statistical limits of its private counterpart remain less understood. In this work, we study score estimation under (α,β)-differential privacy for d-dimensional sub-Gaussian distributions with locally γ-Hölder-continuous scores. We develop a sampling-based private score estimator using quadratic B-splines and the exponential mechanism, and we implement our proposal through projected Langevin Monte Carlo with runtime polynomial in the sample size n. The proposed estimator satisfies (α,β)-differential privacy, and achieves expected density-weighted squared error mboxpolylog(n) max(n⁻²γ/⁽d⁺²γ⁺²⁾,,(nα)⁻²γ/⁽d⁺γ⁺¹⁾). We also establish a nearly matching private minimax lower bound, thereby characterizing the privacy-accuracy trade-off for score estimation. As an application, we construct a differentially private diffusion model whose privacy guarantee is independent of the number of denoising steps. We show that, with an appropriate discretization scheme, the resulting diffusion model attains nearly minimax optimal expected total variation error among all private distribution estimators. We validate our theoretical findings through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
articles.abstract_zh: 估计分布的得分函数在统计和机器学习中发挥着核心作用，可应用于分布估计、采样和基于得分的生成模型。然而，从敏感数据中学习分数会引发隐私问题。这些问题在基于分数的生成模型中尤其明显，其中经过训练的模型可能会记住单个训练示例，并通过成员推理和数据提取攻击暴露敏感信息。尽管非私人分数估计已被广泛研究，但其私人分数估计的统计限制仍然知之甚少。在这项工作中，我们研究了具有局部 γ-Hölder 连续分数的 d 维亚高斯分布的 (α,β) 差分隐私下的分数估计。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 估计分布的得分函数在统计和机器学习中发挥着核心作用，可应用于分布估计、采样和基于得分的生成模型。然而，从敏感数据中学习分数会引发隐私问题。这些问题在基于分数的生成模型中尤其明显，其中经过训练的模型可能会记住单个训练示例，并通过成员推理和数据提取攻击暴露敏感信息。尽管非私人分数估计已被广泛研究，但其私人分数估计的统计限制仍然知之甚少。在这项工作中，我们研究了具有局部 γ-Hölder 连续分数的 d 维亚高斯分布的 (α,β) 差分隐私下的分数估计。我们使用二次 B 样条和指数机制开发了一个基于采样的私有分数估计器，并通过样本大小为 n 的运行时多项式的投影 Langevin Monte Carlo 来实现我们的建议。所提出的估计器满足 (α,β)-差分隐私，并实现预期的密度加权平方误差 mboxpolylog(n) max(n⁻²γ/⁽d⁺²γ⁺²⁾,,(nα)⁻²γ/⁽d⁺γ⁺1⁾)。我们还建立了一个几乎匹配的私人极小极大下界，从而表征了分数估计的隐私准确性权衡。作为一个应用，我们构建了一个差分隐私扩散模型，其隐私保证与去噪步骤的数量无关。我们表明，通过适当的离散化方案，所得到的扩散模型在所有私有分布估计器中实现了几乎最小最大最优期望总变异误差。我们通过对合成数据集和真实数据集的实验验证了我们的理论发现。

articles.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
articles.title_zh: 用于可推广熔池几何预测的物理信息特征表示和预训练表格基础模型
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26235v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser processing conditions with material thermophysical properties, improve melt pool prediction over raw process parameters. We systematically benchmark seven models: four classical ML methods (Gaussian process, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) and three pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabDPT, and TabICLv2). Experiments span 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets, covering regression of melt pool width and depth and classification of melting modes. Dimensionless features yield comparable or superior predictive performance in most settings, with the largest gains in cross-material depth prediction (R² = 0.96). Tabular foundation models generally achieve stronger classification performance than classical baselines, particularly for multi-material datasets. These findings indicate that combining physically meaningful dimensionless representations with pretrained tabular models can improve data-efficient melt pool modeling and support more transferable process-window identification in LPBF.
articles.abstract_zh: 为先进制造开发可推广、数据高效的机器学习 (ML) 模型仍然具有挑战性，因为实验数据集有限，而且工艺性能关系因材料和操作条件而异。在激光粉末床熔化 (LPBF) 中，熔池宽度、深度和熔化模式（传导、过渡或小孔）控制着工艺稳定性和缺陷形成。传统的机器学习模型通常使用维度工艺参数，这些参数仅隐式地表示激光与材料的相互作用，并且可能会限制跨材料传输。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 为先进制造开发可推广、数据高效的机器学习 (ML) 模型仍然具有挑战性，因为实验数据集有限，而且工艺性能关系因材料和操作条件而异。在激光粉末床熔化 (LPBF) 中，熔池宽度、深度和熔化模式（传导、过渡或小孔）控制着工艺稳定性和缺陷形成。传统的机器学习模型通常使用维度工艺参数，这些参数仅隐式地表示激光与材料的相互作用，并且可能会限制跨材料传输。本研究评估了两种基于物理的无量纲特征（归一化焓和佩克莱特数），将激光加工条件与材料热物理特性相结合，是否可以改善对原始工艺参数的熔池预测。我们系统地对七个模型进行了基准测试：四种经典的机器学习方法（高斯过程、支持向量机、随机森林和 XGBoost）和三种预训练的表格基础模型（TabPFN、TabDPT 和 TabICLv2）。实验涵盖 316L 不锈钢、IN625、IN718 和组合材料数据集，涵盖熔池宽度和深度的回归以及熔化模式的分类。在大多数设置中，无量纲特征可产生可比或卓越的预测性能，在跨材料深度预测中收益最大 (R² = 0.96)。表格基础模型通常比经典基线具有更强的分类性能，特别是对于多材料数据集。这些发现表明，将物理上有意义的无量纲表示与预训练的表格模型相结合可以提高数据效率的熔池建模，并支持 LPBF 中更可转移的工艺窗口识别。

articles.title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The transition from fossil fuels presents significant challenges in energy management. To ensure a sustainable energy future, it is crucial to reduce energy consumption when possible and to synchronize electricity consumption and storage with the production from sources with low greenhouse gas emissions. This thesis explores a variety of energy management methods used to manage batteries, heat pumps, and other energy-related systems. The thesis presents three simulation cases alongside one real-world experiment to compare energy management done through simple rules, optimization, and machine learning methods. Furthermore, this thesis introduces TreeC, a novel machine learning-based method that learns understandable yet efficient energy management strategies, applicable to many cases. The three key contributions of this thesis can be summarized as follows: 1) The developed TreeC method demonstrates competitive performance compared to a variety of energy management approaches, such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning, across a diverse set of energy management problems. The understandability of TreeC's energy management strategies greatly improves the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning-based energy management. 2) The real-world experiment highlights the need to validate energy management methods on actual hardware and not solely on simulations. Both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse than in simulations, due to, respectively, insufficiently representative training data and the real-time input data not being reliable enough. 3) Energy management algorithms reduce costs in electrified Belgian dwellings, particularly in poorly insulated dwellings, electric vehicle chargers, and photovoltaic installations. However, on average, these cost savings do not yet outweigh the current costs and effort required to implement such algorithms.

articles.title: Exact Bayesian layers via characteristic functions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayesian neural networks provide principled uncertainty estimates, but training them with Monte Carlo sampling can be expensive. Sampling-free variational inference algorithms make training Bayesian neural networks feasible, but existing approaches assume a Gaussian output distribution, which can be inaccurate in applied problems. Here, we introduce CF-Prop, an uncertainty propagation method that uses characteristic functions to compute the exact output distribution of a Bayesian ReLU layer, without any sampling, even in non-Gaussian settings. Because CF-Prop propagates characteristic functions, the evidence lower bound---the objective of variational training---can be computed in closed form for a broad class of likelihoods, including the Gaussian, Poisson, and Gamma. This allows to implement an efficient resulting variational inference algorithm, CF-VI. On CIFAR-100, CF-VI achieves the lowest calibration error of any tested method, improving on the next best method by about 35%. On a heavy-tailed insurance claim dataset, CF-VI accurately captures tail uncertainty that is severely underestimated by both other sampling-free methods and Monte Carlo methods.

articles.title: Should Belgians Install an Advanced Energy Management System in Their Electrified Dwelling ?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As dwellings electrify and more complex electricity pricing spreads in Belgium, the question arises: What are the potential benefits of installing an advanced energy management systems in an electrified Belgian dwelling ? To answer this question, we simulate 500 representative Belgian dwellings in which fossil systems are replaced by controllable electric technologies: space heating via air-to-air heat pumps, domestic hot water via electric boilers, and private transport via electric vehicles with home chargers. Photovoltaic systems are assigned according to current adoption rates. We evaluate two advanced energy management systems (EMS): model predictive control (MPC) and TreeC, a machine learning method using decision trees to model the EMS strategy. These are compared to a rule-based controller (RBC) that mimics default operation and an MPC with perfect forecasts (MPC P) as an upper bound. Performance for these EMSs is assessed for 2023 under a real contract with hourly prices and a monthly peak tariff. Average annual savings versus RBC are 82.5 EUR, 116.6 EUR, and 177.4 EUR for TreeC, MPC, and MPC P, respectively. All EMSs deliver similar thermal comfort (26-31 Kh). MPC saves more, while TreeC achieves higher EV charge completion (93.3% vs 88.8% for MPC, with a max charge of 95%) and a smoother aggregate load across the 500 dwellings. Savings remain modest relative to EMS purchase (280-680 EUR) and subscription (0-360 EUR/year) costs which is not favourable towards widespread adoption. The data and code to reproduce this study are available at https://github.com/EVERGi/should_belgians_install_advanced_ems_paper.

articles.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a classical decoder fast enough to process syndrome measurements at the rate at which they are generated, and to return its decisions with low latency. This is most demanding for superconducting processors, whose fast syndrome cycles force a trade-off between decoding speed and accuracy. Decoders fast enough to keep up sacrifice accuracy, which must be compensated for with larger codes and thus additional physical qubits. Here we introduce Rapids, a streaming neural decoder that is both fast and accurate. We achieve this by co-designing the decoder with a field-programmable gate array (FPGA): the network is built from operations that map cheaply onto the device and trained in its integer arithmetic. For the distance-19 surface code, Rapids decodes each round of syndromes in under a microsecond on a single FPGA, fast enough for superconducting processors, and returns its decisions with the low latency that fault-tolerant algorithms require. Its logical error rate is 240 times lower than that of existing real-time hardware decoders. The same design extends to the color code and the [[144,12,12]] bivariate-bicycle code, on which our decoder is 16 times more accurate than the real-time Relay decoder. We further show that the decoder scales: spread over several FPGAs or hardened into custom silicon, it becomes faster, more accurate, or able to decode larger codes. Classical hardware thus becomes a further resource, alongside qubits, that can be scaled to improve fault-tolerant quantum computers.

articles.title: Learning Multinomial Logits in O(n log n) time
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.04423v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A Multinomial Logit (MNL) model is composed of a finite universe of items [n]=1,dots,n, each assigned a positive weight. A query specifies an admissible subset---called a slate---and the model chooses one item from that slate with probability proportional to its weight. This query model is also known as the Plackett--Luce model or conditional sampling oracle in the literature. Although MNLs have been studied extensively, a basic computational question remains open: given query access to slates, how efficiently can we learn weights so that, for every slate, the induced choice distribution is within total variation distance ε of the ground truth? This question is central to MNL learning and has direct implications for modern recommender system interfaces. We provide both adaptive and non-adaptive algorithms for this task. Our first adaptive algorithm makes O(fracnlog nε²) queries and learns every choice distribution in total variation distance ε. We also provide a second adaptive algorithm that with O(fracn log nε³) queries provides a stronger guarantee: each choice distribution is approximated to a multiplicative 1±ε error (except for subsets of mass smaller than ε). We complement these algorithms with lower bounds of Ω(fracnlog nε²) for total variation distance and Ω(fracn log nε³) for the multiplicative error guarantee, showing the optimality of our adaptive algorithms. Our non-adaptive algorithm makes Oleft(fracn²ε³log n logfracnεright) queries to obtain guarantees under the multiplicative error notion. We complement this result with an Ω(fracn² log nε²) lower bound for any non-adaptive algorithm, showing that our algorithm is almost tight in n (within a log n factor).

articles.title: Prior-Amortized In-Context Bayesian Inference for Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.24422v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hierarchical data is ubiquitous in the empirical sciences and most commonly analyzed with generalized linear mixed-effects models (GLMMs). Bayesian inference for GLMMs yields calibrated uncertainty estimates but requires Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). The gold-standard No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) is slow and must restart from scratch for every new dataset, model and prior specification. We introduce MetaBeta, a pretrained amortized model for in-context Bayesian inference over GLMMs. The full prior and model specification are supplied as context at test time, and the model returns an asymptotically exact posterior at the speed of a forward pass. Two set transformers and two conditional neural spline flows mirror the GLMM's hierarchical structure and are trained jointly on millions of realistic simulated datasets with continuous, binary and count outcomes. The flow posterior is refined by Independence Metropolis-Hastings against the unnormalized posterior. This yields tuning-free asymptotically correct inference. Alternatively, MetaBeta can warm-start NUTS. This gives nearly identical inference 3.5-13x faster than cold-started NUTS and removes over 98% of NUTS' divergent transitions. On controlled benchmarks with ground-truth parameters, MetaBeta matches NUTS in parameter recovery, posterior calibration and out-of-sample prediction. On real datasets with unknown parameters, priors and model structure, its posteriors closely agree with those of NUTS. Furthermore, it remains faithful where amortized models typically struggle: under misspecified likelihoods, misspecified priors, out-of-distribution predictors, collinear designs and data-poor regimes. On real data, a full prior sensitivity analysis including model comparison takes a few seconds with MetaBeta against 14-18 core-hours for NUTS, tracing its posteriors throughout. Our model is open-source and open-weights.

articles.title: MS-Point: Multi-Modal Hierarchical Spectral Learning for Point Cloud Understanding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Point-image alignment learns useful object representations, but different local feature patterns can produce the same pooled descriptor and receive the same alignment signal. We introduce MS-Point, a cross-modal pretraining framework that directly supervises intermediate point features and their neighborhood responses. At selected encoder stages, we compute neighborhood averages and residuals before pooling and align their branch descriptors with image features. Branch-level objectives align each representation with its visual target, while cross-level consistency and adaptive fusion coordinate information across branches. A common interface of intermediate features and spatial neighborhoods supports both graph encoders and point Transformers. Evaluations across object classification, few-shot adaptation, dense prediction, and low-label scene learning demonstrate the transfer value of this design. Same-backbone comparisons and capacity-matched and computation-matched controls connect these improvements to the structure of supervision. Together, our findings support directly supervising intermediate features and neighborhood variation to learn transferable, geometry-aware representations across modalities.

articles.title: MemMend: A Selective Revision Framework for Memory Question Answering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Revising every answer from a long-term memory can consume substantial inference budget and damage facts that were already correct. We introduce MemMend, a modular selective revision framework that routes potentially incomplete answers to an editor, represents corrections as bounded exact-text replacements, and accepts only edits with resolvable source coordinates and valid edit operations. The editor preserves the current answer when no legal repair is proposed; accepted edits require no additional semantic-verification call. On 1,986 LoCoMo development questions, MemMend achieves 67.17 conversation-macro F1 and 88.35 mean Judge score, improving over a verified revision chain by 0.82 and 1.24 points while using 62.37% fewer revision calls. Routing uses 54.15% fewer revision calls than ungated local review, with similar F1 but a 0.67-point lower Judge score. Applied directly to native PropMem, Mem0, and SimpleMem answers, the editing interface raises F1 by 3.79, 6.44, and 0.42 points. It outperforms same-gate rewriting and saves 49.85-83.72% of editing calls relative to ungated editing, which retains higher F1 in this adaptation. A source-by-editing factorial supports local editing for F1 but leaves an independent quality benefit from source obligations unresolved. Transfer to 451 LongMemEval-V2 Small questions also favors revision efficiency, while an external PerLTQA dialogue subset reveals a completeness gap. These results support selective editing as a reusable quality-cost operating point.

articles.title: Duopra: From Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Agency
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full-duplex interaction models exhibit strong conversational agency, enabling natural, low-latency turn-taking, backchannels, and interruptions. However, completing tasks further requires task agency: timely tool invocation and argument revision following user corrections. Frontend-backend agents separate initiation from execution: the frontend decides whether and what to request, while the backend determines how. Execution can be offloaded, but unsent requests cannot be executed, and incomplete ones can misdirect the backend. On Full-Duplex-Bench v3 (FDB v3), most failures of Realtime-Venus-Audio + Harness in our streaming pipeline occur before a domain tool executes. We introduce Duopra, a full-duplex interaction model that learns task execution alongside conversational control. Duopra treats the backend as a tool, accepting a self-contained natural-language request. Direct calls and backend delegation share an action interface and requirements for faithful initiation and correct execution. Its three-stage training combines protocol SFT, full-duplex RL rewarding timely and complete execution, and projector-only repair of talker conditioning after thinker updates. With the same backend, Pass@1 rises from 4.7% to 44.7%; Duopra achieves 47.7% calling tools directly (26.0% after SFT) and 49.3% with a DeepSeek backend. It improves three FDB v1.0 takeover rates over the base model. These results show that task agency can coexist with key conversational agency.

articles.title: Explainable AI for Solar PV Power Forecasting: From Model Selection to Trustworthy, Reproducible Deployment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning (ML) is now a standard tool for forecasting the output of solar photovoltaic (PV) plants, yet published accuracy figures are often hard to compare and harder to trust. Many studies validate with random splits, report no reference forecast, and present feature attributions without saying what they can and cannot show. This paper reviews the main families of ML methods for PV power forecasting and resource assessment, from tree ensembles to deep and foundation models, and sets out a reproducible workflow that combines automated model search with explainable AI. The workflow is then tested on an openly available dataset: a 16.32 kWp plant in Porto, Portugal, forecast one day ahead from a 4 km numerical weather prediction grid. Over a full test year, the best models reach a normalised root mean square error (nRMSE) of 11.6% of installed capacity, about half the error of smart persistence. The choice of input features changed accuracy far more than the choice among strong algorithms, and shuffled cross-validation was mildly optimistic. After conformal calibration, the nominal 80% prediction intervals covered 81.7% of observations, against 64.5% before. SHAP rankings stayed stable when the model was retrained on different periods but shifted when correlated inputs were removed, so attributions should be read as properties of a model rather than of the plant. The paper closes with practical lessons and open problems, including deployment on edge hardware and the effect of a changing climate.

articles.title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulation-driven design of real engineering components has to meet three conditions at once. It runs on few solves, since a nonlinear finite-element simulation of a 3D part takes hours; its design space has many values, the hundreds to thousands of values of the part's CAD model; and a better design often needs a redesign, coordinated changes of the part's proportions rather than local polishing of its surface. Automated optimisers meet at most two of these conditions. Classical optimisers, Bayesian or derivative-free, need a person to cut the design down to a few parameters, and on all the values they need far more solves; industrial shape optimisers move every surface node of the mesh in one solve per cycle, but only in small steps that polish rather than redesign. We ask whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can meet all three by joining what it knows with what the simulation shows. GPT-6 Astra edits a magnesium stent through a CAD geometry parametrisation of about 1,650 values, with a budget of 15 simulations; every proposal is built in CAD, meshed and simulated with large-deformation plasticity and contact, and the LLM reads the full results of every solve. Within that budget it lowered the objective, a high percentile of the strains in the stent's bends, by 32%; on the same budget, the industrial shape optimiser Tosca improved the original design by a tenth and then stopped improving. An earlier GPT-6 Astra design, 25% lower in the same objective, was checked in an independent, higher-fidelity model of the full deployment with crimping and damage: it was 14% less strained than the original after the full chain, and its most damaged spot began to fail later and carried 63% less damage at full expansion. LLMs can thus join their learned knowledge with simulation data to adjust more than a thousand design values and reach valid designs with real improvements.

articles.title: Client Exits - A Way to Increase LLM Transparency on the Client Side
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Textual recommendations generated by large language models (LLMs) can be difficult to inspect. This paper introduces emphClient Exits, a lightweight mechanism for enriching LLM responses while separating semantic intent from client-specific presentation. The model inserts predefined, machine-interpretable markers into its output, and the receiving client decides whether and how to realize the corresponding enrichments. This allows supplementary information to be presented as graphics, text, speech, or other modalities without prescribing a concrete interface. We implement a prototype combining a finetuned Qwen model with a modified LibreChat client. Using the Question--Option--Criteria (QOC) approach including three XML-based client exits. We evaluate two QOC-oriented model variants trained on essentially the same examples, with client-exit annotations added for one variant. Across 100 test questions, the client-exit model includes all three markers in every response. An LLM judge, informed about the mechanism without being instructed to favor it, prefers this model's answers in 66% of the comparisons. These results demonstrate successful marker generation on the evaluated test set and support the feasibility of client-controlled enrichment.

articles.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves effective navigation with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain. Rather than teaching the brain to predict geometric goals, we equip it with a semantic tool-calling interface for conveying movement decisions to an action expert in natural language. We first adapt the action expert to carry out these movement requests, then jointly improve the brain's movement decisions and the action expert's continuous execution through closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL). Trained on the same navigation episodes, ZeroVLN substantially outperforms representative SFT-based hierarchical VLN methods on standard VLN-CE (continuous environments) benchmarks, while inducing only minor changes to the brain's weights and largely preserving its general capabilities. To our knowledge, ZeroVLN is the first slow-fast VLN framework with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain, and the first to jointly optimize its slow and fast policies through closed-loop agentic RL in VLN-CE.

articles.title: ReLay: Bidirectional Layout-Code Translation and Library Evolution for Reusable and Process-Portable Analog Design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Analog layout generators provide a programmable interface for design reuse and process migration, but their coverage is limited by handcrafted libraries. The designer knowledge embedded in complete layouts remains implicit in their geometry, making it difficult to capture in reusable generator libraries. We present ReLay, a bidirectional layout-code framework that recovers generator programs from existing layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs. Constructions that recur across recovered programs are promoted to library functions, so the library evolves as layouts accumulate. We also introduce the first layout-code benchmark: 1,050 hand-drawn layouts from 27 circuit families across three open-source PDKs, ranging from primitive cells to full chips. Learned functions account for 53-66% of layout-building calls in held-out layouts, demonstrating reuse beyond the learning corpus. Frontier LLM agents use ReLay to produce new layouts at 64-77% lower API cost per completed task than direct geometry generation, with comparable completion rates and electrical quality.

articles.title: An LLM-Driven Traffic-Control xApp for Dynamic 5G RAN Intents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Programmable Radio Access Networks (RANs) enable runtime deployment of traffic-control functions, but selecting the appropriate configuration remains challenging as network conditions and service requirements change over time. Conventional solutions often rely on static rules or learning-based controllers with predefined state and action spaces, limiting their ability to accommodate changing intents. This paper introduces an LLM-driven xApp for traffic control in programmable RANs. The proposed architecture combines operator-defined service intents, runtime E2 interface telemetry, and the currently deployed configuration to generate traffic-management policies without blocking packet forwarding or the processing of incoming E2 measurements during LLM inference. Experiments on an OpenAirInterface 5G environment show that the proposed controller dynamically adapts the traffic-control pipeline to runtime intent changes, achieving an average intent satisfaction ratio of 0.91, compared with 0.52 for a static TC-RAN configuration. When channel conditions degrade, the controller maintains an intent satisfaction ratio of approx. 0.88, compared with approx. 0.4 for the static baseline.

articles.title: Cetyltrimethylammonium bromide-metal complex assisted Gold@sulfamerazine nanoconjugates: Synthesis and characterization
articles.abstract: Cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) is one of the most potentially cationic surface-active agents, widely used in DNA extraction, as a strong capping agent in the synthesis of nanomaterials, and in cosmetics. In this work, the formation of cetyltrimethylammonium-AuCl 4 complex (CTA-AuCl 4 , yellow-orange color) was visually observed and characterized by UV-visible spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The solution color from yellow to bark brown with increasing CTAB concentration resulted from the interactions of HAuCl 4 with aggregates of the CTAB with fine anti-interference. The gold@ sulfamerazine nanoconjugates were prepared by the chemical reduction of CTA-AuCl 4 in the presence of sodium borohydride. The surface morphology, crystalline nature, position of surface plasmon resonance band (SPR), size distribution, elemental composition, and elemental mapping were established by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), UV-visible spectroscopy, TEM, and electron dispersive microscopy (EDX), respectively. The 1 H and 13 C NMR spectroscopy was used to determine the presence of sulfamerazine (SMZ) and CTA + onto the surface of the as-prepared AuNPs. XRD patterns reveal the formation of face-centered cubic metallic gold with space group = 225: í µí°¹í µí±�3í µí±� : lattice constant (α = β = γ = 90.00 0 , a = b = c = 0.4076 nm, and V = 67.745 Ȧ 3), crystallite size = 2.283 nm, strain = 0.00 %, and content = 100 %. Surfactant metal complex, CTA-AuCl 4 can itself act as a source of metal ions and nanoparticle protectors for the fabrication of advanced nanomaterials with desired morphology for industrial and medicinal applications.

articles.title: Multivariate Optimization of the Synthesis of ZnCl 2 -Activated Biochar Functionalized with Bimetallic Au-Ag Nanoparticles for Catalytic Application in the Reduction of p-Nitrophenol
articles.abstract: The valorization of agro-industrial residues to produce carbonaceous materials offers a sustainable route for developing heterogeneous catalysts. In this study, passion fruit peel was used as a precursor for ZnCl2-activated biochar, whose synthesis was optimized using a Central Composite Rotatable Design (CCRD), considering carbonization temperature, residence time, and impregnation ratio. The optimized conditions were 525 °C, 60 min, and a biomass-to-ZnCl2 impregnation ratio of 2.0 (w/w). The resulting optimized biochar (BC-OT) exhibited a high specific surface area of 1411.64 m2 g-1. Pyrolysis promoted carbon enrichment, reduced the H/C and O/C ratios to 0.338 and 0.381. BC-OT showed a point of zero charge (pHPZC) of 6.53 and a lactonic group content of 1.50 mmol g-1. The biochar was subsequently functionalized with Au and Ag nanoparticles (NPs) and applied as a heterogeneous catalyst for the NaBH4-mediated reduction of p-nitrophenol. For Au0.5-Ag0.5 NPs/BC-OT, EDS confirmed the presence of Au and Ag, while HRTEM revealed nanoparticles with an average diameter of 7.4 ± 3.4 nm. Lattice fringes and SAED patterns showed interplanar spacings consistent with face-centered cubic Au and/or Ag domains and wurtzite ZnO. Among the evaluated materials, 50:50 Ag:Au exhibited the highest apparent rate constant (kapp) of (15.18 ± 2.27) × 10⁻³ s⁻¹, outperforming the monometallic catalysts and the non-functionalized support. The catalyst remained active over four reuse cycles. These results demonstrate the potential of passion fruit peel as a renewable precursor for porous carbonaceous supports containing Au-Ag nanoparticles for the catalytic reduction of nitroaromatic compounds.

articles.title: Flame retardant poly(ionic liquid) coating for polyethylene terephthalate fabrics: Improving anti-dripping performance with silica-containing flame retardant
articles.abstract: Poly(ionic liquid) (PIL)-based flame-retardant coatings were grafted onto polyethylene terephthalate (PET) fabrics by UV-initiated polymerization, using either physically dispersed nano-SiO₂ or copolymerizable polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS)as the silicon component. PET@PIL with a grafting add-on of 22.7 wt% lowered the peak heat-release rate (PHRR) by 25.5% and increased the cone-calorimeter residue by 126% relative to pristine PET, consistent with PIL-assisted dehydration and charring. Adding 25 wt% nano-SiO₂ to the combined PIL/silica solids reduced PHRR and total heat release (THR) by 38.7% and 12.7%, respectively, and eliminated melt dripping, yielding a UL-94 V-0 rating. At an IL/POSS molar ratio of 1:0.75, PHRR decreased by 32.8%, the limiting oxygen index reached 23%, and the fabric achieved V-0 without dripping. Char morphology and Raman results indicated that nano-SiO₂ reinforced an inorganic barrier, whereas covalently incorporated POSS promoted a more integrated silicon-containing network. TG-IR of the nano-SiO₂ system supported combined condensed- and gas-phase activity. These results clarify how silicon-source chemistry and bonding mode affect flame retardancy and anti-dripping behavior.

articles.title: Optimized Design of Liquid Hydrogen Turbo-Pump for Heavy-Lift Class Rocket
articles.abstract: Liquid hydrogen (LH₂) turbopumps operate under extreme thermofluidic and mechanical loading conditions, including cryogenic temperatures, high rotational speeds, and cavitation-prone flow regimes, placing stringent demands on both aerodynamic performance and structural integrity. This study presents an integrated computational workflow for designing and evaluating a cryogenic centrifugal impeller, combining parametric blade geometry generation, steady-state computational fluid dynamics (CFD), one-way fluid–structure interaction (FSI), and modal analysis. An in-house Python routine was used to generate optimized blade geometry, which was subsequently modelled in ANSYS BladeGen, meshed in ANSYS TurboGrid, and analysed under LH₂ operating conditions (44.9 kg/s mass flow rate, 91 bar outlet pressure) using ANSYS CFX. Resulting pressure and thermal loads were mapped onto a structural finite element model in ANSYS Mechanical to assess stress, deformation, and dynamic stability across seven candidate materials: Inconel 718, four high-entropy/medium-entropy alloys (HEAs/MEAs), and two Al6061-based metal matrix composites (B₄C- and SiC-reinforced). The CFD analysis confirmed target performance, achieving an outlet pressure of 91.2 bar and a hydraulic efficiency of 0.939. FSI results showed all candidate materials remained within acceptable elastic limits, with the Al6061 + SiC composite exhibiting the lowest stress (118 MPa) and the CoCrFeMnNi HEA showing superior stiffness-to-weight characteristics. Modal analysis confirmed that natural frequencies for all materials avoided the pump's operating speed range, ensuring resonance-free operation. These findings demonstrate that HEAs and particle-reinforced MMCs are viable, lightweight alternatives to conventional nickel-based superalloys for next-generation cryogenic turbomachinery, offering pathways toward more efficient and cost-effective LH₂ propulsion hardware.

articles.title: Thermodynamic Analysis of a Two-Stage Selective Carbothermic Reduction Process for Deep-Sea Polymetallic Nodules: Part I. Selective Recovery of Critical Battery Metals
articles.abstract: Deep-sea polymetallic nodules are a promising resource for critical metals, but their fine-grained mineralogy and complex Mn–Fe oxide matrix make conventional processing challenging. This study presents a thermodynamic analysis of the first stage of a proposed two-stage selective carbothermic process to recover Cu, Ni and Co as a Cu–Ni–Co–Fe alloy while suppressing manganese reduction. Equilibrium calculations were performed using the Equilibrium Composition module of HSC Chemistry® 7.1 for a representative nodule composition. The effects of temperature, carbon addition, total pressure, atmosphere and nodule composition on metal recoveries and alloy composition were evaluated. The results demonstrate a well-defined thermodynamic operating window in which Cu, Ni and Co can be selectively recovered with limited iron reduction while manganese remains predominantly in the oxide phase. The predicted reduction sequence and recovery trends were consistent with published experimental observations. The study establishes the thermodynamic basis for Stage I and provides a manganese-rich residue for subsequent high-temperature production of a ferromanganese–silicide alloy in Part II.

articles.title: Green Microwave Combustion Synthesis of Magnesium Ferrite Nanoparticles Using Tinospora cordifolia for Electrical Relaxation Studies
articles.abstract: Nanocrystalline MgFe2O4 was synthesized through a rapid microwave-assisted green combustion route using Tinospora cordifolia (Giloy) stem extract as a naturally derived fuel and complexing medium. The combustion process produced crystalline MgFe2O4directly without requiring post-synthesis calcination, demonstrating the effectiveness of plant-derived phytochemicals in promoting spinel ferrite formation. X-ray diffraction confirmed a single-phase cubic spinel structure (space group Fd3̅m), while crystallite sizes determined using the Debye-Scherrer, Williamson-Hall (W-H), and Size-Strain Plot (SSP) methods were 15.10, 18.36, and 18.26 nm, respectively, indicating good crystallinity with only minor lattice strain. FTIR spectra exhibited the characteristic metal-oxygen vibrations of the spinel lattice, whereas SEM revealed a porous agglomerated morphology produced during rapid combustion. EDS analysis verified Mg, Fe, and O as the principal constituent elements without detectable metallic impurities. Frequency- and temperature-dependent electrical measurements (1 Hz–100 kHz, room temperature to 400°C) showed pronounced dielectric dispersion together with thermally enhanced dielectric permittivity, loss, and AC conductivity. Electric modulus analysis revealed a broad distribution of relaxation times, confirming non-Debye relaxation behaviour. Arrhenius analysis of the selected high-temperature M″ relaxation branch yielded an activation energy of 0.758 eV, indicating thermally activated electron hopping between Fe2+ and Fe3+ ions. The results demonstrate that the Giloy-assisted microwave combustion approach provides an efficient and environmentally sustainable route for producing nano crystalline MgFe2O4 with favourable dielectric characteristics suitable for frequency-dependent ferrite applications.

articles.title: Leaf harvesting and seasonal flooding are associated with distinct soil bacterial communities in carnauba palm groves
articles.abstract: Carnauba palm groves occupy seasonally dry floodplains where extractive management and hydrological variation may jointly shape surface-soil microbiota. We compared bacterial communities across four field conditions defined by leaf harvesting (managed/unmanaged) and water regime (seasonally flooded/non-flooded) in Caucaia, Ceará, northeastern Brazil. Surface soil (0–10 cm) was sampled beneath six palms per area, and the 16S rRNA V4 region was sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform. Community composition differed significantly among conditions (PERMANOVA R² = 0.431, p = 0.001), with the managed, seasonally flooded area the most compositionally distinct. This area also showed the lowest estimated richness and markedly higher Na, exchangeable sodium percentage, S, Ca, Mg, clay content, and cation exchange capacity than the others. Shannon and Simpson diversity were lower under managed and flooded conditions. Bacillota and Bacillales were proportionally enriched in managed soils, while Acidobacteriota predominated in unmanaged soils. LEfSe and niche-occupancy analyses identified condition-associated taxa and a higher proportion of generalists in unmanaged areas. Exploratory co-occurrence networks varied in size and topology, though interpretation is constrained by small within-condition sample sizes. Since each management–water combination was represented by a single area, findings reflect site-condition contrasts rather than independent causal effects of harvesting or flooding. Land use, hydrology, and edaphic properties must therefore be considered jointly when assessing bacterial communities in semiarid floodplain soils.

articles.title: Effects of Roasting Conditions on Furan Formation and Volatile Aroma Profile of Dibek Coffee
articles.abstract: Roasting conditions critically influence both aroma development and the formation of potentially harmful process contaminants in coffee. This study investigated the effects of roasting temperature (127–212°C) and time (4.19–46.21 min) on furan formation and volatile aroma composition in traditional Turkish Dibek coffee using response surface methodology and GC–MS-based analyses. Furan concentrations increased approximately 2.9-fold, from 18.24 ± 0.61 µg/kg at 127°C to 52.12 ± 0.22 µg/kg at 212°C, with roasting temperature exerting a substantially greater influence than roasting time. The quadratic response surface model explained 95.2% of the variation in furan formation (R2 = 0.952). Among the 47 identified volatile compounds, pyrazines, phenolic compounds, and furan derivatives generally increased with roasting severity, whereas several aldehydes and ketones were more abundant under mild roasting conditions. Pearson correlation analysis revealed positive associations between furan and Maillard-derived aroma-related compounds, while principal component analysis explained 70.08% of the total variance and differentiated roasting treatments according to their volatile profiles. These findings demonstrate that roasting conditions promoting aroma-related compound formation may simultaneously increase furan accumulation, highlighting the importance of considering both aroma composition and process contaminant formation when developing roasting strategies for Dibek coffee.

articles.title: Singular Value Thresholding Algorithm Based on Variational Quantum Pre-compression
articles.abstract: Singular value thresholding (SVT) is a core subroutine in low-rank matrix recovery and quantum machine learning, but suffers from high computational complexity. The quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) algorithm improves performance, yet its resource usage still depends polynomially on the full rank (r) or dimension (sqrtpq), leading to prohibitive costs for large-scale matrices. Based on the mathematical theory of low-rank matrix approximation, we propose a variational quantum algorithm framework, termed Variational Quantum Low-Rank SVT (VQLR-SVT). This framework utilizes a low-complexity variational quantum circuit to extract the low-dimensional submanifold spanned by the effective rank (r_ϵ) of the matrix, and directly learns the threshold function from the phase estimation register, thereby compressing high-dimensional control information into a single flag qubit and implicitly realizing a low-dimensional approximation. Theoretical analysis shows that, under the mild assumption of variational training convergence, the resource complexity of QSVT operations can be reduced from (poly(r)) to (poly(r_ϵ)), where (r_ϵ ll r). We rigorously prove the accuracy guarantee and complexity upper bound of the pre-compression algorithm using matrix perturbation theory. Subsequently, through five numerical simulation experiments, we validate the efficiency advantage in terms of resource consumption versus effective rank, the theoretical upper bound of output fidelity, circuit expressibility testing, convergence of variational quantum circuit training trajectories, and cross-validation with classical algorithms along with resource comparison. Experimental results demonstrate that in typical scenarios with rapidly decaying singular values, VQLR-SVT can reduce quantum gate calls by more than (50%) while maintaining fidelity above 0.97, and the quantum resources exhibit scale-independence with respect to matrix dimensions.

articles.title: Giant spin-to-charge conversion by tailoring magnetically proximitized topological Dirac semimetal
articles.abstract: Author(s): Masayuki Ishida, Soichiro Fukuoka, Takahiro Chiba, Yohei Kota, Masaaki Tanaka, and Le Duc Anh Tailoring magnetic proximity enables highly efficient spin-to-charge conversion in Fe/ α -Sn heterostructures.The estimated inverse Edelstein length reaches −3.1±1.0 nm—among the largest reported at room-temperature—when α -Sn thickness is 25 nm. This performance is attributed to the interplay of magnetic proximity and spin diffusion. Topological surface states at the Fe interface are suppressed, whereas those at the opposite interface are preserved by thickness tuning. These findings establish magnetic proximity engineering as a promising strategy for realizing efficient spintronic devices. [Phys. Rev. B 114, L260404] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026

articles.title: Spiraling spins bring coordinated quantum motion to diamond sensors
articles.abstract: Trapped within diamond's crystal lattice are tiny defects called nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, where a nitrogen atom sits beside an empty gap where a carbon atom should be. Because of their quantum spins, electrons trapped at these defects behave like tiny magnets, turning diamond into a highly sensitive detector for magnetic fields.

articles.title: Single-Channel Lunar Penetrating Radar for Rover Localization via Revisit-Aware Amplitude-Phase Learning
articles.abstract: GNSS-denied lunar rover localization relies heavily on surface vision, which degrades under extreme solar angles, featureless regolith, and permanent shadows. Exploiting stable, visually invariant subsurface features via single-channel Lunar Penetrating Radar (LPR) offers a promising auxiliary means, yet repurposing in-situ geophysical probing remains unexplored, because revisit benchmarks are scarce and single-channel echoes are strongly attenuated. Here we establish the first revisit-aware localization benchmark from Chang’E-4 Yutu-2 500 MHz LPR observations, keeping non-revisited training/validation traverses strictly disjoint from the physically revisited scenes used for evaluation. By disentangling single-channel sweeps into energy envelopes and continuous unit-circle phase manifolds with structure-preserving aggregation, our early-fusion representation captures high-contrast scatterers and faint stratigraphic horizons. Across lunar and terrestrial radar datasets, our approach reaches 78.05% top-1 recall on lunar revisits, outperforming raw-echo (70.73%) and the strongest learned baseline (73.17%). Existing single-channel LPR payloads can thus support localization without extra hardware in visually degraded scenarios.

articles.title: Room Temperature Corrosion of Iron Foam for Sulfur Anion Modulation of Hydroxysulfide Electrocatalysts for Oxygen Evolution
articles.abstract: Ni–Fe-based compounds are promising electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in water electrolysis because of their low cost and tunable intrinsic activity. Here, we use a room-temperature immersion corrosion strategy in which iron foam (FF) serves as both the conductive substrate and the iron source. The slow release of sulfur from thioacetamide enables the insitu growth of sulfur-doped nickel–iron hydroxide (S-NiFe(OH)x) on FF. The optimized S-NiFe(OH)x-0.01/FF electrode requires an overpotential of 236 mV to deliver a current density of 50 mA cm⁻² in 1 M KOH and exhibits a Tafel slope of 86 mV dec⁻¹. It also shows an overpotential increase of less than 10 mV during 12 h of operation at 50 mA cm⁻². Sulfur incorporation modifies the electronic environment of the NiFe sites and is proposed to balance OH⁻ adsorption and O₂ desorption. This approach combines simple fabrication, inexpensive raw materials, and mild synthesis conditions to prepare efficient transition-metal-based OER electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Exploring Discrete Algorithms in Quantum Computing
articles.abstract: Quantum computing introduces a new computational paradigm by extending the classical binary representation of information through quantum bits, which can exist in superposed states and exhibit entanglement. This work presents a systematic study of fundamental concepts, computational mechanisms, and discrete algorithms in quantum computing. The introduction discusses binary bits and qubits, classical logical gates, and their quantum counterparts, highlighting the reversible nature of quantum computation. The materials and methods examine XOR-based classical cryptography, quantum cryptography, quantum teleportation, and mathematical representations of quantum states using probability amplitudes, superposition, and entanglement. The results and discussion focus on the quantum computing model and the implementation of reversible logic through important quantum gates, particularly the Toffoli and Fredkin gates. The role of superposition and entanglement in manipulating quantum information and performing computations is also analyzed. Based on these foundations, the proposed framework emphasizes discrete quantum algorithms for solving problems involving Boolean functions, binary strings, search spaces, integers, graphs, and combinatorial structures. Representative quantum algorithms, including Deutsch, Deutsch–Jozsa, Bernstein–Vazirani, Simon, Grover, and Shor, demonstrate the application of quantum principles to discrete computational problems. The study further explores the relationship between quantum computing, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Quantum Machine Learning (QML), where quantum representations and algorithms can support optimization, classification, search, and data-processing tasks. The work concludes by identifying future research directions involving quantum AI, hybrid quantum–classical architectures, error-resilient quantum systems, scalable hardware, and practical discrete quantum algorithms.

articles.title: Quantum Percolation Pathways in Disordered Semiconductor Nanorod Networks
articles.abstract: Charge transport in disordered semiconductor nanostructure networks is governed by both structural morphology and quantum-mechanical coupling between neighboring building blocks. Here, we present an image analysis guided computational framework for identifying tunneling-assisted quantum-percolation pathways in disordered InAs nanorod ensembles. Experimentally reported nanorod dimensions are used to reconstruct statistically realistic networks incorporating variations in size, position, orientation, and local density. Automated image analysis extracts the geometrical descriptors of individual nanorods, which are subsequently combined with finite element electronic structure calculations and Bardeen transfer Hamiltonian analysis to evaluate inter-nanorod tunneling rates. The resulting weighted connectivity graphs are analyzed to identify boundary-spanning quantum percolation pathways. Representative ensembles containing 28, 35, and 38 nanorods reveal a transition from isolated tunneling clusters to boundary-spanning transport pathways as the nanorod density increases. A complementary geometrical percolation analysis demonstrates that the predicted threshold is highly sensitive to the selected connectivity criterion: increasing the geometrical cutoff from 2 to 6 nm shifts the characteristic critical nanorod number from 48.5 to 26.5, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 45%. These results highlight the limitations of purely distance-based connectivity models and demonstrate that long-range transport pathways are governed by the collective distribution of quantum-mechanical coupling strengths rather than by geometrical proximity alone. The proposed framework provides a versatile approach for linking structural morphology with quantum transport behavior and can be extended to a broad range of disordered nanoscale materials.

articles.title: Long-lived evolved magmas and dynamic plumbing system hidden beneath monotonous basalts: the Erta Ale volcano case (Afar, Ethiopia)
articles.abstract: Erta Ale Volcano (EAV), Afar, hosts one of Earth's few persistent lava lakes and accommodates rifting largely through slow endogenous growth rather than voluminous eruption. It hosts a transcrustal plumbing system capable of locally producing rhyolitic interstitial melts. However, whether such shallow, highly differentiated domains represent a persistent feature of the EAV system remained unknown. Here we present whole-rock geochemistry and high-resolution electron microprobe mapping of 23 basaltic lava flows sampled along a ~40-m stratigraphic section of the EAV caldera wall, predating the volcano's recent, near-complete caldera infilling. Whole-rock major and trace elements contents show monotonous compositional range with limited, non-systematic variation through the sequence, indicating that bulk magmatic conditions remained comparatively stable over the time recorded by this section, and that these older lavas were, on average, slightly more primitive than present-day EAV lava flows. In contrast, the chemical maps show mineral textures and compositions that reveal a highly dynamic picture invisible at the whole-rock scale: destabilized high-An plagioclase cores overgrown by oscillatory rims, oscillatory Cr2O3 zoning in clinopyroxene, and locally deformed crystal frameworks together record repeated cycles of recharge, differentiation, and reactive mush processes. In one sample, texturally distinct mushy enclaves document shallow protracted differentiation of Erta Ale magmas. It contains interstitial evolved glass pockets with quartz, skeletal apatite and Fe-Ti oxides that closely mirrors the evolved rhyolitic domains previously described in explosively ejected cognate blocks at EAV. These results demonstrate that the shallow, rhyolite-producing mush beneath EAV is not an isolated snapshot but a recurring feature of the plumbing system, active well before the present caldera formation, with direct implications for the potential mobilization of evolved, explosive magmas at EAV, a question raised anew by the 2025 Hayli Gubbi eruption nearby.

articles.title: An In Vivo Model of Ischemic Spinal Cord Injury in Awake Rats Identifies Early Mixed Macrophage Polarization and Impaired Inflammatory Resolution
articles.abstract: Study Design: Animal study. Female Sprague-Dawley rats. Objectives: To establish an awake, anesthesia-free rat model of ischemic spinal cord injury (SCI) and characterize the molecular and cellular mechanisms associated with lesion progression during the first 24 h after paralysis. Setting: Brazil and USA. Methods: Ischemic SCI was induced in awake rats by repeated transauricular maximal electroshock seizures (MES). Neurological function, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), histopathology, cellular responses, and transcriptomic profiles were evaluated during the acute and early subacute phases after injury. Results: Repeated MES produced reproducible thoracic (T8–T12) watershed infarcts predominantly involving the anterior spinal cord, with bilateral “owl’s-eye” lesions on MRI, paralysis below T9–T10, and progressive tissue vacuolization between days 3 and 5. Integrated cellular, molecular, and transcriptomic analyses revealed early monocyte recruitment, dysregulated inflammatory signaling, mixed macrophage-associated phenotypes, impaired inflammatory resolution, and limited astrocytic response. Transcriptomic profiling identified activation of the DHA–lipoxygenase pathway associated with endogenous inflammatory resolution, whereas genes involved in astrocytic DHA biosynthesis were downregulated by 24 h, suggesting a temporal mismatch between pro-resolving signaling and substrate availability for specialized pro-resolving lipid mediator biosynthesis. Conclusions: An awake, anesthesia-free model of SCI reproduces key pathological and clinically relevant features of human ischemic SCI and reveals early dysregulation of the inflammatory–lipid resolution axis. These findings identify impaired coordination between inflammatory signaling and endogenous lipid-mediated resolution as a potential mechanism contributing to secondary lesion progression and provide a platform for evaluating time-sensitive neuroprotective interventions. Sponsorship: FAPERJ; Brazilian Ministry of Health; and NY State SCI Research.

articles.title: Energy-Level-Matched Electrocatalysis on Au–Nb 2 O 5 /Histidine-Aspartic Acid-Functionalized B,P-Codoped Graphene Quantum Dots for Selective Bisphenol A Detection in infant care products
articles.abstract: Noble-metal sensing materials are limited by poor selectivity and restricted detection limits in complex-matrix trace analysis, because their zero bandgap enables nonselective electron transfer and precludes energy filtering. To overcome this, an Au–Nb2O5 composite decorated with histidine/aspartic acid-functionalized B,P-co-doped graphene quantum dots (HDBP-GQDs) was designed. HDBP-GQD served as chelating agents and interfacial modifiers, sequentially coordinating Nb(V) and Au(III); two-step annealing at 400 and 900°C then yielded Au–Nb2O5/HDBP-GQD composite. Lattice-confined Au atoms formed atomic-scale electron-coupling centers, reducing charge-transfer resistance by > 26.7-fold and increasing electroactive surface area by > 9.7-fold. Catalytic activity increased by > 1.9-fold relative to pristine Nb2O5. HDBP-GQD also enabled multi-heteroatom interfacial band engineering, tuning the band gap and interfacial energy levels to match oxidation potential of bisphenol A. This alignment established a selective electron-transfer pathway, in which energy-level gating favored bisphenol A electrooxidation and suppressed coexisting interferents, enhancing catalytic specificity. Among twenty small organic molecules, only bisphenol A elicited a sensitive electrochemical response, confirming excellent selectivity. The sensor exhibited a linear range for bisphenol A of 0.01–150 µM and a detection limit of 0.0031 µM, with reliable performance in infant care products. Beyond bisphenol A sensing, this electronic-state engineering strategy provides a general route to convert zero-bandgap materials into energy-selective electrocatalysts, with broad implications for trace analysis in complex matrices and beyond.

articles.title: Suppression of propellant sloshing in a spacecraft tank: a two-sided upwind implicit–explicit difference scheme for a Saint-Venant model with nonlocal feedback and its exponential stability in the sense of Lyapunov
articles.abstract: Sloshing of liquid propellant, which accounts for a large share of the mass of launch-vehicle stages and spacecraft, exerts a time-varying force on the vehicle and degrades attitude-control and manoeuvre accuracy. In this paper the longitudinal sloshing of propellant settled at the tank bottom by engine thrust is modelled by the Saint-Venant (shallow-water) equations written in coordinates attached to the tank. One end of the tank is a rigid wall, the other a damped elastic diaphragm; for the diaphragm, conservation of volume introduces a nonlocal term (the integral of the free-surface elevation) into the boundary condition. The acceleration of the vehicle is chosen proportional to the total momentum of the liquid relative to the tank, (:aleft(tright)=kPleft(tright)), (:P=int:₀¹vhspace0.17emdx); this enters the equations as a second nonlocal term, a spatially uniform source. The linearized problem is written in Riemann invariants, and a new two-sided upwind implicit–explicit scheme is constructed for it: the two characteristic families are computed by implicit sweeps in opposite directions, the two boundaries are coupled at the new time level by a closed-form formula, and the nonlocal source and the nonlocal boundary term are treated explicitly. For a classical discrete Lyapunov function with exponential weights adapted to the direction of wave propagation, the inequality (:Vⁿ⁺¹le:qₐₛₜ:Vⁿ), (:qₐₛₜ:<1), is proved under conditions depending explicitly on the grid parameters; these conditions do not require the Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy (CFL) condition. In the passive case ((:k=0)) the estimate coincides with the exact spectral decay rate. A stability theorem is also proved for a second scheme, the predictor–corrector B-variant, which evaluates the nonlocal terms at the half time level; it halves the nonlocal lag error and, under strong feedback with large time steps, remains stable in the region where the A-variant is unstable. As consequences, estimates are obtained for the cumulative dissipation of momentum and for the total velocity change (:varDelta:v) of the vehicle. It is shown that with rigid walls there is no exponential decay for any (:k), and that the system is unstable for (:k<0). Spectral analysis shows that the feedback raises the damping ratio of the fundamental sloshing mode from (:1.7%) to (:27%), and numerical experiments show an (:18)–(:50)-fold reduction of the sloshing force. For deep (full) tanks the model is extended by an equivalent depth consistent with finite-depth dispersion: it reproduces the frequency and the sloshing mass of the fundamental mode exactly as given by potential theory, while the dimensionless equations, the scheme and the theorem remain unchanged. The results are applied to the 623 L P/N 80451-1 hydrazine tank used on the WorldView-4 (GeoEye-2) spacecraft.

articles.title: Automated Smart-Contract Settlement and the Sustainable Utilization of Distributed Solar Energy: An Agent-Based Assessment on Benchmark Low-Voltage Networks
articles.abstract: Smart contracts are often credited with large efficiency gains in local electricity markets, but such claims rarely separate automated settlement from price signals and demand flexibility. We developed an agent-based model of 99 customers on a benchmark low-voltage feeder (SimBench), driven by 15-min load and photovoltaic (PV) profiles and coupled to an AC power flow. Four scenarios with identical random inputs combine centralized or conceptual smart-contract settlement with or without price-responsive shiftable load, over 732 paired daily replications (2016). Settlement alone left all physical outcomes unchanged. The 20.3% lower community energy cost it produced equals the retail–feed-in price spread on locally matched energy minus fees, a transfer from the retailer, and prosumers were slightly worse off. With the local price guiding shiftable load, local PV utilization rose by 1.46 percentage points and upstream imports fell by 1.7% relative to centralized settlement with the same flexibility, while losses changed by under 1%. The effects kept their sign in a nine-factor sensitivity analysis and on five further feeders, and the physical gains grew with the flexible-load share. Within the assumptions of this model, the resource-use benefits of smart-contract settlement depend on demand flexibility rather than on settlement automation itself.

articles.title: HelixVault: A Full-Stack Web Application for DNA-Based Digital Data Encoding with AES-256 Encryption, Reed-Solomon Error Correction, and Biological Steganography
articles.abstract: Digital data is expanding much faster than our ability to store it. Magnetic tapes and hard drives wear out every few years, and running massive air-conditioned server farms consumes enormous electrical power. DNA offers a compelling way out: it packs petabytes into microscopic volumes and stays readable for centuries without electricity. However, moving DNA storage from wet-lab experiments into usable software remains difficult. Most existing tools are isolated scripts with no web interface, zero encryption, and no mechanism to protect files against physical degradation. In this work, we present HelixVault, an open-source web platform that handles the full digital-to-DNA lifecycle. We wrote a custom Base-3 codec that solves the homopolymer problem: chemical synthesizers struggle when identical nucleotides repeat, so our mapping strictly prevents identical consecutive bases by construction. Before encoding, files are encrypted with AES-256-CBC using PBKDF2 key derivation. We then apply Reed-Solomon RS(255, 205) error correction, which can rebuild up to 25 damaged bytes in each codeword. For security and camouflage, HelixVault can also hide payloads inside real E. coli genomic sequences pulled from NCBI. The platform includes an interactive plasmid cloning tool for pUC19/pBR322 vectors, an automated biosecurity screen, and a local Groq AI assistant. Built with FastAPI and React, our implementation recovered 100% of tested files under simulated mutations.

articles.title: Zn²⁺ Content-Dependent Structural, Magnetic, and Electrochemical Properties of MgSrZn x Fe 2 O 4 Nanoferrites for Electromagnetic and Energy-Storage Applications
articles.abstract: The ferrite materials MgSrZnₓFe2O4 (x = 0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15 and 0.20) were synthesized and systematically studied to clarify the impact of Zn substitution on the structural, morphological, magnetic and electrochemical properties. The surface morphology of prepared samples was analysed by using FESEM and it was found that the particles were found to be primarily irregular and agglomerated in nature. The MgSrZn0.15Fe2O4 composition had additional elongated rod-like properties. The EDS analysis revealed the presence of Mg, Zn, Sr, Fe and O, which are in agreement with the elemental composition of synthesized ferrite system. The magnetic studies showed a strong association of the magnetic response with the Zn level. Among the studied compositions, the composition MgSrZn0.15Fe2O4 showed a high saturation magnetization of 157.53 emu g− 1 and a coercivity of 67.60 Oe, indicating a favorable combination of high magnetization and relatively low coercive field. The electrochemical properties were further investigated by using 1M Na2SO4 solution. The MgSrZn0.15Fe2O4 electrode shows a specific capacitance of 271 F g− 1 at 5 mV s− 1 by cyclic voltammetry and 372 F g− 1 at 1.5 A g− 1 by galvanostatic charge-discharge measurements. The Trasatti study suggested that the process was mostly inner/diffusion-controlled and the kinetic investigation based on scan-rate showed an increasing surface-controlled effect at high scan-rates. The tunable magnetic properties together with the large electrochemical charge storage capacity show the potential of MgSrZnxFe2O4 ferrites for magnetic and electrochemical applications.

articles.title: A Novel Kokumi Peptide RSQPVGV from Yeast Extract via CaSR-Mediated Taste Enhancement
articles.abstract: Kokumi peptides enhance food palatability, often via the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR). We identified candidate peptides from yeast extract using LC–MS/MS and high-throughput molecular docking to CaSR. Molecular dynamics confirmed the novel peptide RSQPVGV formed a stable CaSR complex, and surface plasmon resonance confirmed direct binding (KD = 1.91×10− 5 M). Human sensory evaluation showed RSQPVGV (1 g/L) significantly enhanced kokumi, salty, and umami intensities of a monosodium glutamate–NaCl solution (MNS). Electronic tongue analysis confirmed increased richness. Mouse behavioral assays revealed RSQPVGV enhanced MNS responses and increased umami-evoked neural activation in the gustatory cortex. Human EEG recordings showed RSQPVGV alone had minimal cortical responses but significantly increased MSG-evoked P300 amplitudes and β-band power, indicating enhanced umami processing. These findings identify RSQPVGV as a novel yeast-derived kokumi peptide, providing multiscale evidence for its taste-enhancing activity, CaSR-binding, and taste-related neural modulation.

articles.title: Study of chemical fiber treatments on moisture absortion and tensile properties of Rhectophyllum Camerunense fibers
articles.abstract: Natural lignocellulosic fibers are increasingly investigated as sustainable reinforcements for polymer composites, but their hydrophilic nature limits performance under humid conditions. This study evaluates the effect of surface chemical treatments alkaline (NaOH), benzoylation, and acetylation on the physical and tensile properties of Recthophilum camerunense (RC) fibers. Experimental results show that untreated fibers exhibited the highest water absorption 204.5% and tensile strength 430 MPa (Mega Pascal), with an elastic modulus of 1770.83 N/m². Chemical modification significantly reduced hydrophilicity: 161.3% for alkali-treated, 152.4% for benzoylated, and 148.6% for acetylated fibers. However, tensile strength and stiffness decreased after treatment, reaching 140 MPa NaOH, 280 MPa benzoylation, and 200 MPa acetylation. The reduction in mechanical strength is attributed to partial degradation of hemicellulose and amorphous cellulose during chemical processing. Overall, benzoylation and acetylation treatments provided the best compromise between reduced water absorption and acceptable mechanical strength, indicating their potential for enhancing the performance of natural fiber reinforced composites.

articles.title: Iontronic triboelectric tele-perception enabled by ion-relaxation engineering and a lightweight 1D-CNN decoder
articles.abstract: Robots must recognize what is approaching before they touch it. Triboelectric tele-perception meets this need, but its responses stay pinned to the material permittivity (dielectric constant) of the target: the voltage waveform collapses to a scaled copy of the electrostatic coupling, and material identity must then be recovered from a handful of amplitudes. We show that ionic relaxation in an iontronic dielectric breaks this constraint. Dispersing room temperature ionic liquid of BMIMTFSI (10 wt%) in thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) gives an iontronic triboelectric sensor (ITS) whose mobile ions relax on the time scale of an approach event, so that ionic polarization and electrostatic induction act as two independent contributions to the same voltage transient.
