Our experiments quantified the rates of reductive and oxidative side-reactions in NMC532 vs. graphite cells containing 12 different electrolyte formulations. We found that gains in interphasial stability were highly correlated, with successful additives decreasing both types of side-reactions by similar magnitude. This dual action could be indicative of the role of crosstalk on cell degradation, as soluble species formed on one electrode can decompose at the other end of the cell. Although electrochemical tests are insufficient for understanding mechanisms of improvement, they can reveal interesting effects that complement other characterization tools.

articles.title: High-Power Short-Wavelength Frequency Comb from Coherent Radiation of Uncompressed Electron Beams
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-power frequency combs at short wavelengths would open new opportunities for precision measurements and high-resolution spectroscopy. Here, we propose a frequency comb based on coherent undulator radiation from uncompressed electron bunches. An optical frequency comb serves as the seed, establishing a common phase reference for microbunching in successive electron bunches and transferring its phase coherence to short-wavelength harmonic radiation. By exploiting interference between distinct laser-induced microbunching pathways, we reduce the sensitivity of the harmonic bunching phase to electron-beam energy fluctuations, a major challenge for maintaining interpulse coherence. Start-to-end simulations demonstrate frequency comb generation in the vacuum-ultraviolet (148 nm) and soft X-ray regimes, yielding average radiation powers of approximately 1 W and 100 mW, respectively, with approximately 6 μW and 100 nW concentrated in individual comb teeth. These results establish a promising route toward high-power, phase-coherent short-wavelength frequency combs for precision spectroscopy, including searches for the nuclear transition in trapped ²²⁹Th ions.

articles.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu₂O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu₂O Rydberg excitons with a SiNₓ nanophotonic waveguide. Under non-resonant excitation, excitonic emission from the Cu₂O microcrystal is coupled to the guided mode, routed along the waveguide, and collected from an output grating. The spectrum shows the phonon-assisted 1s orthoexciton emission together with the low-lying 2p and 3p lines of the yellow Rydberg series. Spatially selective excitation excludes substrate background and direct scatter, and the enhanced linear polarization of the grating-collected signal identifies the TE-like guided mode as the collection channel. These results establish the complete material--device--measurement stack for a novel platform of nonlinear quantum nanophotonics based on Rydberg excitons.

articles.title: Finite-Key Analysis for Multiple-Antenna Quantum Key Distribution with Continuous Variables
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26066v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques, known for their use in wireless communications, can also find applications in quantum communications systems. This is, for instance, relevant to satellite-based quantum communications when atmospheric turbulence and the time-varying nature of the channel can make their implementation difficult. Here, we study the application of MIMO techniques to continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD) in the realistic setting where a finite number of signals are exchanged. We show how data collected during the brief overpass time of low-earth-orbit satellites over ground stations can be processed to estimate MIMO channel parameters, extract a secret key, and quantify the key generation rate. For 2× 2 MIMO settings with Gaussian encoding and heterodyne detection, our finite-key analysis indicates that MIMO CV-QKD could outperform both multiplexed (with a nominal 3~dB improvement) and single-mode (with a nominal 6~dB nominal improvement) scenarios. Furthermore, we conjecture that the ultimate enhancement of a multiple-antenna CV-QKD system can be characterized by the product of the number of its inputs and outputs.

articles.title: Efficient calculation of the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled biphotons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The spatial biphoton state generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enables applications in high-dimensional quantum information processing and is often described in Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes. However, calculating the full LG spectrum for arbitrary radial and orbital angular momentum (OAM) indices requires computationally demanding multidimensional integrations. We present a generating-function approach that analytically performs the four-dimensional transverse spatial integral without approximating the phase-matching function. The source geometry can be completely described by a few dimensionless parameters, which reduce to two parameters for wave-vector-degenerate photons with equal waists. Our derived expressions for the full LG spectrum allow for computationally efficient and numerically stable evaluation at high mode orders, addressing a crucial obstacle in previous works. To illustrate our approach, we compare OAM spectra obtained by projection onto the lowest radial order and by radially insensitive detection, and investigate how high-dimensional maximal entanglement can be approached by tuning source parameters. Our results provide a new analytical tool for efficiently characterizing and engineering high-dimensional spatial entanglement in SPDC.

articles.title: Quantum Zeno Effect with a Superposed Measurement Schedule in Relational Time
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26371v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the Page-Wootters construction in which time is a quantum clock reading and the global system state is stationary, we propose a quantum circuit that explores the observable consequences of treating measurement timing as a quantum degree of freedom. We place two Zeno measurement schedules of a driven qubit in a coherent superposition using a schedule qubit. We show that, for a fixed drive strength, the interference visibility between the two schedules depends only on the time offset between them, not on the number of intermediate measurements taken. Then we show that, for one schedule-readout outcome, the Zeno trend reverses, predicting a result that complements the standard Zeno probability. We propose a circuit implementation with physical memory qubits and show that measuring the memory register's joint X-basis parity distinguishes a coherent schedule from a classical or dephased one. We give the gate count and an error budget for a superconducting-qubit implementation. The Page-Wootters picture motivates this protocol and provides an equivalent stationary representation, although the predictions follow from the standard circuit description without requiring a relational-time interpretation. This is consistent with the Page-Wootters framework recovering standard quantum dynamics through correlations between a clock and the rest of the system.

articles.title: Dressed Subsystems in Classical Gravity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2501.10450v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper considers the problem of consistently defining subsystems in gravitational theories. It is argued that a subsystem is a spacetime subregion in which the observables form a closed Poisson algebra. In a generally covariant theory, the location of the subregion must be determined in relation to other degrees of freedom. It is proposed that these degrees of freedom should live within the region, so that an observer can determine its edge by only measuring fields inside of it. This turns out to be equivalent to the property that observables in the subregion generate field-dependent gauge transformations on the causal complement. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that this is exactly what is necessary for the observables to form a Poisson algebra and thus to constitute a consistent subsystem. Observables in spacelike separated "dressed subsystems" are shown to commute. Several examples are given in the context of General Relativity. Along the way, new perspectives on the covariant phase space formalism are introduced that clarify well-known issues, such as the factorization of subregions in gauge theories and the unambiguous definition of Noether charges associated with one-sided boosts. Finally, prospects for extending these results to a perturbative quantum setting are discussed.

articles.title: Spacetime-Foam Correlations as the Origin of Cosmological-Constant Dark Energy: Their Effects on Cosmological Evolution and Astrophysical Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.15881v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wheeler spacetime foam at the Planck scale is characterized by quantum-gravitational fluctuations that create, oscillate, and annihilate microscopic spacetime structures. We model these structures as a Planck-scale lattice using Euclidean quantum gravity on a simplicial complex. Their long-wavelength collective excitations are described by interacting scalar fields, which we call ``foamons,'' in analogy with phonons in a crystal lattice. Through Coleman--Hawking interactions, foamons couple to quantum or classical field operators at scales much larger than the Planck length. These operators provide physical infrared scales that determine the characteristic correlation lengths of the foamon fields. We use a Wilsonian renormalisation-group framework to study their scaling-invariant behaviour near infrared and ultraviolet fixed points. Integrating out the foamon degrees of freedom generates effective actions for physical field operators, with the foamon correlation lengths setting the corresponding macroscopic scales and effective couplings. We apply this framework to cosmology and astrophysics, where the Ricci-scalar sector gives rise to an effective cosmological term Λ_Rsimξ_R⁻² with equation of state p_Λapprox -ρ_Λ. For a cosmological correlation length ξ_Rsim H⁻¹, this yields ρΛ_Rsim Mᵣₘ ₚₗ²H², providing a possible mechanism for the small observed dark-energy scale. The effective cosmological term Λ_R varies in spacetime and interacts with matter through its dependence on the Ricci scalar. We investigate its effects on cosmic evolution, galactic rotation curves, and the deflection of light grazing the solar surface.

articles.title: Full-field-of-view aberration correction for large arrays of focused beams
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.15967v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose and implement an aberration correction method for the creation of extended arrays of spots well beyond the isoplanatic region of any optical system. The method relies on an extensive calibration of aberrations in terms of Zernike polynomials over the full accessible field of an optical system. We introduce a modified Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm for generating holographic phase masks creating fully corrected arbitrary arrays of spots. By applying the method to an aspherical lens, and using a liquid-crystal spatial light modulator (SLM), we increase the aberration-free field of view from 50 to 500 μm, only limited by the largest diffraction angles accessible to the SLM. This opens new perspectives for the generation of large arrays of optical tweezers, especially for neutral atom based quantum processors and simulators.

articles.title: Chiral Temporal Structures in Molecular Rotational Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.37896v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce chiral rotational wavepackets: coherent superpositions of a few low-lying rotational states of a molecule for which the expectation value of a molecular axis traces a three-dimensional chiral trajectory in the laboratory frame. The handedness is a dynamical property of the quantum state rather than of the equilibrium structure, and we show that it can be imprinted on linear rotors as well as on spherical and symmetric tops. We derive the action of space inversion, time reversal, and their product on such wavepackets in the Wigner D^JMK basis, and define the rotational enantiomers of a given wavepacket. To quantify their handedness we introduce two derivative-based pseudoscalar measures: a geometrical measure built from the curvature and torsion of the trajectory, which is even under time reversal, and a dynamical measure, which is odd under time reversal. The latter is shown to be proportional to the geodesic curvature of the trajectory projected onto the unit sphere, which links it, via the Gauss--Bonnet theorem, to the solid angle enclosed by the projected trajectory and to the parallel-transport holonomy of a molecule-fixed vector. Finally we show that a nonzero geometrical measure is a sufficient condition for the wavepacket to exhibit true chirality through its orientation trajectory in the sense of Barron.

articles.title: Quantum Nondecimated Wavelet Transform: Theory, Circuits, and Applications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.21478v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The quantum nondecimated wavelet transform uses a shift register to apply circular shifts to an amplitude encoded signal before a single orthogonal wavelet transform. We show that tracing out the shift register gives level probabilities equal to the normalized nondecimated wavelet energies, invariant under circular shifts. Its diagonal gives moving averages of squared coefficients. We derive a multinomial model for the level counts and show how to read the autocovariance at lag one for all but the coarsest detail level. For these global statistics, direct Fourier basis measurement of the input is at least as precise and uses a simpler circuit. For denoising, we insert a block encoded shrinkage operator between the transform and its inverse. Postselection on the shift register implements the cycle spinning average exactly as a linear combination of unitaries. Weights shared within each level give a translation equivariant filter with zero phase. Local weights also preserve translation equivariance when indexed by the nondecimated translate. The circuit provides access to individual decimated branches and combines them coherently. We illustrate the method with James Stein shrinkage, local empirical Wiener filtering, and a scaling analysis of turbulent wind velocity. Gate simulations verify the construction, and we report state preparation, weight estimation, and output costs separately.

articles.title: On the Coupled Cluster Doubles Truncation Variety of Four Electrons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.16580v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend recent algebro-geometric results for coupled cluster theory of quantum many-body systems to the truncation varieties arising from the doubles approximation (CCD), focusing on the first genuinely nonlinear doubles regime of four electrons. Since this doubles truncation variety does not coincide with previously studied varieties, we initiate a systematic investigation of its basic algebro-geometric invariants. We show that for 4 electrons in n ≥ 13 orbitals, the CCD truncation variety is not a complete intersection, and we present numerical and symbolic evidence that for the remaining cases it is a complete intersection defined by binomn-44 quadrics. Using representation-theoretic arguments, we uncover a Pfaffian structure governing the quadratic relations that define the truncation variety for any n, and show that an exact tensor product factorization holds in the distinguished limit of disconnected doubles. We connect these structural results to the computation of the beryllium insertion into molecular hydrogen (BecdotsH₂ → H--Be--H), a small but computationally challenging bond formation process where multiconfigurational effects become pronounced.

articles.title: Spatio-temporal air flow properties in a 3D personalised model of the human lung
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.17265v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a multi-scale lung model to investigate spatio-temporal distributions of ventilation variables. Lung envelope and large airway geometries are derived from CT scans; smaller airways are generated using a physiologically consistent algorithm. Tissue mechanics is modeled using nonlinear elasticity under small deformations, coupled with local air pressure from fluid dynamics within the bronchial tree. Airflow accounts for inertia and static airway compliance. Simulations employ finite elements. Using this model, we explore spatio-temporal airflows and shear stresses distributions.

articles.title: The Price of an Explanation: What Demanding Verifiable Artifacts Costs, and What It Buys Back
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25896v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative models produce many candidate solutions but provide no intrinsic signal by which to rank them. One mitigation is to demand a emphverifiable artifact: a program that can be executed against the available evidence. A common concern is that requiring executable verification incurs costs in both solution quality and computational budget. We measure these two costs on the 120-task ARC-AGI-2 evaluation set. Demanding a verifiable artifact from an LLM reduced the score from 93 to 68 of 120 tasks (77% to 57%). Of those 25 tasks, 21 were reached by no program-producing configuration we ran, at any budget, by sampling or by search; yet for 27 of the 28 tasks that only the answer-only arm solved, some program arm held a program that reproduced every demonstration and still failed the test. The bottleneck is obtaining an explanation that emphgeneralizes, not finding one. A short evolutionary search over two already-sampled programs, at no additional model cost, beats best-of-2 sampled code by 9.2 ± 1.4 tasks, and over a single sampled program beats 1-shot sampling by 9.9 ± 1.3. Moreover, because a program can be checked against the training examples, any program-producing protocol can terminate early once a task is explained: under the same stopping rule, best-of-n sampling declines up to 38% of its budget and the evolved arm up to 49%, whereas an answer-only baseline cannot terminate early. Applying the same methodology to decoder synthesis for quantum error correction yields interpretable decoders evaluated against a certified panel of published decoders on held-out exam shots.

articles.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly integrated into self-driving laboratories (SDLs) to plan experiments and interpret results. However, analytical reasoning alone does not make a laboratory autonomous: autonomy in an SDL is achievable only when the agent can be trusted to act on physical hardware unsupervised and knows when to defer to a human. Here, we present an architecture that integrates an agent at the Analyze-Design interface of the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle, enabling agent-driven measurement selection and data interpretation while ensuring that state-changing operations are authorized, validated, and auditable. We demonstrate this architecture on a liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) instrument in an oxidant-screening campaign for synthesizing an organic dye. Within human-defined campaign limits, the agent submitted measurement jobs, interpreted mass spectrometry (MS) and diode-array detection (DAD) data, flagged failed experiments, and produced an oxidant ranking. This ranking matched that obtained from scripted peak integration, and organic chemists confirmed the agent's spectral interpretations and failure assignments. In a simulated environment that replays the archived LC-MS data, where the agent chose which wells to inject under varying injection limits, it measured the highest-yielding condition at about its seventh injection, against 14.5 on average for a random order, and identified it in every campaign with a limit of eight or more injections. An agent can therefore close the analysis-to-design gap while its actions stay bounded and verifiable, which is a step toward greater autonomy for SDLs.

articles.title: GaussTrans: A Gaussian Interface Framework for Multi-Layer Refractive Transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate surface modeling of multi-transparent interfaces to achieve accurate light transmission. The interplay of errors in geometric structure, light paths, and observation results during the reconstruction of transparent media with a high number of layers makes this a challenging problem. Some existing techniques address the reconstruction of transparent scenes by reducing the number of layers or simplifying light paths; however, this limits their direct applicability to high-order transparent scenes. We propose GaussTrans, a compact framework for light transport in high-order transparent scenes, consisting of three components: Gaussian-Field Hybrid Surfaces, Transport-Coupled Refinement, and Primitive-Guided Implicit Intersection. Gaussian-Field Hybrid Surfaces use a hybrid approach combining Gauss surfaces and fields to reconstruct different interfaces. Transport-Coupled Refinement reduces coupling errors by evaluating the entire light path. Primitive-Guided Implicit Intersection combines primitive support regions to reduce errors in the intersection of interfaces and rays. In experiments on datasets such as RefRef, GaussTrans achieves significantly higher accuracy with relatively low spatial storage requirements.

articles.title: Context as a Resource
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Managing concurrent tasks across separate agent sessions quickly exhausts human attention, motivating always-on personal agents behind a single continuous interface. Yet when every context shares identical frozen backbone weights, funneling interleaved dialogues and external events into one linear session induces cross-topic constraint bleed and head-of-line stalling. Conversely, router-ticket hierarchies incur lossy prose handoffs, heavy routing overhead, and blind merges - collapsing true-conflict repository merges to a 33.3% three-run mean despite high isolated branch passes. Rather than scheduling anthropomorphic roles, we introduce ClonAct, a routerless architecture that virtualizes context blocks directly through a pluggable single-pass non-generative Context MMU, in-place Context Cells, a footprint-aware Synaptic Bus with an isolated trial merge gate, and a wave-flushed Shared Trunk. Across three programmatic multi-stream benchmarks and three model families, our portable trial merge gate lifts true-conflict merges to 63.3%, while ClonAct's routerless virtualization attains this ceiling with 45.9% fewer prompt tokens and prevents compact-model router collapse. Under continuous surge streams, ClonAct matches top completion (95.0%) with the lowest median wait and zero timed-out status checks.

articles.title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Set pieces produce about a third of non-penalty expected goals (xG), yet they are usually evaluated by what happened next. We present Monte Carlo Pass Search (MCPS) for set pieces, which treats a corner or a lofted free kick as a distribution over plausible executions and plausible futures instead of a single realised event. From the pre-kick state, MCPS proposes counterfactual deliveries and counterfactual set-ups (where the attackers stand at the kick), plays each out many times in a world model (3D ball physics, a generative model of all 22 players, the keeper's come-or-stay decision and a Player-to-Touch model) and scores every future with a value model. On 249 deliveries from 30 Serie A 2025/26 matches, with every model applied only to matches it never saw, the best available delivery is worth 0.0085 xG more than the one kicked (+28 %), mainly because it reaches an attacker before the keeper. Searching where the attackers stand as well adds +0.0027 xG with the observed ball and +0.0033 on top of the best ball; designing their runs too adds +0.0007 more. We show how to keep such a search honest, and estimate how much more data each component needs before a club could rely on it.

articles.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When multimodal decision models determine actions, moderation outcomes, or quality judgments, their reliability depends on preserving semantic decisions across presentation changes, ignoring irrelevant additions, and distinguishing information consistent with task evidence from information that conflicts with it. Existing evaluations study decision-interface biases and multimodal model behavior in separate settings, leaving no common protocol to compare multimodal decision models with their backbones on practical tasks. We introduce MM-SystemOneBias, which evaluates 13 models on 5,323 original instances from nine public datasets and 11 task scenarios using six paired interventions: option order, option label, external judgment, image--text description, irrelevant information, and rating scale. Across seven matched decision-model--backbone pairs, decision models are more stable under option-label, irrelevant-information, and rating-scale changes in all seven pairs; six pairs also show lower option-order flip rates. They incur smaller accuracy losses under incorrect external judgments in all seven pairs and conflicting descriptions in six. In six pairs, they gain less accuracy from correct external judgments and show less favorable accuracy changes under consistent descriptions. Among pairs with unchanged semantic decisions, mean absolute changes in answer probabilities range from 4.56 to 11.55 percentage points, revealing input effects that accuracy alone misses.

articles.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. In simulation, MAWAM reaches 90.3% mean success on eight tasks with teams of up to four arms. Ablations show that cross-agent attention and team-stage future-video supervision both improve coordinated control: without attention, a four-arm relay falls from 95.0% to 39.0%, and without this supervision, Place Food falls from 78.0% to 47.0%.

articles.title: From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As LLM agents increasingly generate RTL alongside the tests and reviews that validate it, self-generated evidence is a weak foundation for trustworthy hardware. We present our seven-stage verification-gated workflow, evolved during a post-quantum design port, in which a gate counts only if shown able to fail on negative controls and fault mutants, and reviewer agents audit work before commit. We then audit this evidence with tool-selected netlist mutants, flaw replays, and formal checks. The flow ported an ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65 accelerator to a 300 MHz Zynq UltraScale+ key-custody card: all six operations are byte-exact on the board, and it passes all 85 interface-applicable NIST ACVP cases (of 285) and 484 ML-DSA known answers. However, passing module tests overstate the verification strength. Across three RTL modules, existing simulation gates kill only 76% of 399 tool-selected netlist mutants; specification-derived tests guided by the survivors raise the fresh-draw decapsulation kill rate from 48% to 74%. In pre-registered single-model replays on flaws invisible to known-answer tests, undirected whole-design review catches two verifier flaws in only 3/6 and 1/6 sessions, whereas module-scoped review catches every known flaw in all 54 sessions. Even scoped review detects planted key-custody flaws in only 3/20 sessions, whereas formal checks (one added for the replay) flag every one. In this study, trustworthy agentic hardware needed author-independent mutants for test gates, module-level scoping for LLM review, and formal checks for custody invariants.

articles.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mobile agents on personal smartphones can affect private data, payments, settings, and the foreground screen. We present MATE (Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution), an execution-layer system that controls the boundary between agent action proposals and device effects without modifying the underlying model. MATE represents each UI primitive as a structured action record that combines the instruction, target app, screen context, primitive, and action fields. Runtime Guardrail (RG) maps this record to an allow, block, or user-approval decision; Predefined Task Routing (PTR) serves recurring requests through verified routes with post-execution screen checks; and a floating interface keeps execution in a compact overlay. On MobileSafetyBench, MATE raises high-risk blocking from 29.7% to 97.0% under GPT-4o. On AndroidWorld, it reduces LLM calls by up to 6x and raises recurring-use task success to 95.7%.

articles.title: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.25760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents increasingly carry out long-horizon development tasks, autonomously planning and executing multi-step actions that span files, tools, and sessions. Because developers rarely follow each action, and agents resuming the work depend on records of what was done, the agent's work report often becomes the primary account of what was changed and established. When the report contains false or unsupported claims, it gives recipients false assurance: incomplete work may be accepted without verification, incorrect assumptions about the current state can propagate to later steps and agents, and evaluators that credit stated success may reward the report rather than the work. Yet little is known about what unfaithful reporting looks like in real development work, or how developers and agents handle it once it surfaces. Starting from real developer--agent conversations in SWE-chat, we conduct a systematic mixed-methods analysis of self-admitted unfaithful reports. We identify eleven subtypes in four categories: misreported observations, misattributed evidence, overstated task success, and faulty technical explanations, with overstated task success the most common. Handling these problems involves on average 4.3 further user turns and 12.71 minutes of recorded response and execution time, and users express dissatisfaction more often. Among 435 work reports that we separately sample and annotate, NaturalPositiveShare{}% contain at least one unfaithful claim. We also develop FaithDetector, a detector for unfaithful reporting informed by the observed patterns. On naturally sampled reports, FaithDetector attains NaturalDetectorMacro{}% macro-F1, about 13 percentage points above the baseline. Together, our findings and FaithDetector provide empirical evidence and an automated method for checking reporting faithfulness, informing agent evaluation and training feedback.

articles.title: Automated Runtime Verification of EV-Charging Software Using Physics-Informed Oracles and Search-Based Threshold Synthesis
articles.abstract: This paper presents an automated runtime verification approach for electric vehicle charging software that checks Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP) telemetry against an independent physical oracle at the edge. Integrity faults or attacks can preserve statistical plausibility while violating the physical charging process, which limits software-side anomaly monitors that observe only reported data. The proposed approach treats the charging station as a cyber-physical software system and combines two executable runtime oracles: a protocol and statistical oracle over OCPP MeterValues and a physics-informed oracle derived from local hardware power measurements and constant-current/constant-voltage charging dynamics. Their scores are normalized and fused by a transparent decision rule. Two decision thresholds are synthesized automatically with particle swarm optimization under a shared false-alarm budget, turning calibration into a small search-based software engineering problem. A seeded simulation benchmark evaluates five telemetry mutation operators: scaling, bias, replay, stealthy value manipulation, and protocol-timing corruption. At a 5% target false-positive rate, the cross-layer monitor detects 93.1% of attacks with a 4.6% false-positive rate and an area under the ROC curve of 0.953, compared with 72.8% and 0.845 for the physics-only monitor and 44.1% and 0.691 for the cyber-only monitor. Average detection latency is 2.36 min and processing cost is 50.8 textmu{}s per session. The results show that physics-informed runtime oracles can strengthen automated software assurance for cyber-physical telemetry while remaining interpretable and lightweight. External validation on measured charging-station data remains future work.

articles.title: Development of Periodically Poled Lithium Niobate Waveguides for 780 nm Femtosecond Lasers
articles.abstract: 780 nm femtosecond lasers are important for laser processing, multiphoton imaging, terahertz generation, and quantum-entangled light sources. This study presents the fabrication of periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) waveguide chips and packaged devices for these applications. By optimizing chip design, periodic electrode fabrication, domain inversion, waveguide etching, end-face polishing, and antireflection coating, high-quality PPLN ridge waveguides of different lengths were fabricated. A stable, plug-and-play device with fiber-coupled input and free-space second-harmonic output was developed. Under pump conditions of 40.0 mW average power, 50 fs pulse duration, and 80 MHz repetition rate, the device generated 17.2 mW at 780 nm, achieving a conversion efficiency of 43.0%, significantly exceeding that of conventional bulk PPLN. When the fundamental-wave average input power increased to 80.0 mW, the pulse duration broadened to 100 fs. The measured second-harmonic power was 30.1 mW, corresponding to a conversion efficiency of 37.6%. The results indicate that increasing fundamental-wave average power leads to pulse broadening and consequently reduces conversion efficiency. Under both input conditions, the output power stability was better than 0.2% RMS over 2 hours. These waveguides combine efficient nonlinear frequency conversion with high power-handling capacity, making them suitable for high-power, high-efficiency 780 nm femtosecond second-harmonic generation. This work advances the investigation of nonlinear properties in thin-film lithium niobate and the engineering application of femtosecond frequency-doubling waveguides.

articles.title: Study on the Removal Performance and Mechanism of U(VI) from Rare Earth Wastewater Using Phytic Acid-Crosslinked Chitosan@Attapulgite Composites
articles.abstract: Deep removal of U(VI) from uranium-bearing rare-earth wastewater is difficult for conventional adsorbents: uranium occurs only at trace concentrations, while coexisting ions such as Ca²⁺ and K⁺ interfere strongly with adsorption. A phytic acid-crosslinked chitosan/attapulgite composite (ATP-CS-PA) was prepared by blending, using phytic acid (PA) as the crosslinking agent. The best performance was obtained at an ATP:CS:PA mass ratio of 3:10:10. At an initial U(VI) concentration of 10.00 mg/L, an adsorbent dosage of 0.10 g/L, pH 5.0 and 298 K, adsorption reached equilibrium within 120 min with a capacity of 98.34 mg/g. The maximum capacity obtained from the Langmuir model was 526.16 mg/g. Adsorption was attributed mainly to inner-sphere coordination with phosphate groups. As a hard Lewis acid, UO₂²⁺ preferentially coordinates with phosphate groups to form P–O–U bonds, with amino and surface hydroxyl groups also contributing. The composite retained high selectivity in the presence of coexisting ions, including Ca²⁺ and Fe³⁺ at 10–100 mg/L, and achieved a uranium removal rate of 83.48% after five adsorption–desorption cycles. Treatment of rare-earth wastewater containing 0.30 mg/L U(VI) reduced its concentration to 0.02 mg/L, meeting the limit specified in GB 26451–2011.

articles.title: Mechanical characterization and constitutive modelling of 8011-O aluminium alloy sheets for fin forming
articles.abstract: Accurate representation of anisotropy, strain rate sensitivity and fracture is needed to simulate the forming of thin aluminium fins. This study characterizes 8011-O aluminium alloy sheets with a thickness of 0.3 mm and develops material descriptions for fin forming. Room-temperature uniaxial tensile tests were conducted along seven in-plane orientations, and tests in the rolling direction covered strain rates from 10⁻⁴ to 10³ s⁻¹. Shear and notched tensile tests were used to characterize fracture under different stress states. The measurements showed pronounced directional variation in yield stress and plastic strain ratio, together with an increase in flow stress with strain rate. A modified Hill48 formulation was fitted to the directional yield stresses and plastic strain ratios, and a Johnson-Cook constitutive model with a polynomial strain rate coefficient was introduced. A Johnson-Cook fracture model was calibrated using the fracture tests. These material descriptions were then used in finite element simulations of fin piercing and flanging. The simulations identified localized thinning near the punch radius. Comparison with forming experiments gave a maximum relative error of 9.68% in the thinning ratio. Both the simulations and experiments showed fracture at a punch speed of 500 mm s⁻¹. The results provide a basis for assessing thickness variation and fracture during 8011-O aluminium fin forming.

articles.title: Precise Object Selection in Dense Virtual Environments Using Single Hand Gesture with 2D Interfaces
articles.abstract: While Raycasting remains the standard for freehand target selection in virtual reality (VR), it fundamentally relies on a single ray casting from the hand, which merely detects the first intersected object. Consequently, Raycasting exhibits significant performance degradation in dense environments and fails to effectively select occluded objects. To overcome these inherent limitations, we introduce Single-Hand Gesture Widget Selection (SHGWS). SHGWS leverages a combination of volumetric area selection, hand gestures and a 2D widget to facilitate target disambiguation. We validated the efficacy of SHGWS through a comparative user study with 27 participants, evaluating it against standard Raycasting and a Double-Hand Widget Selection (DHWS) baseline. Our findings indicate that SHGWS yields superior selection performance compared to both alternatives. This work contributes the design and empirical evaluation of a novel interaction technique that empowers robust, single-handed object selection in bare-hand VR environments.

articles.title: Spatial and decadal variability of drought in Burkina Faso and associated teleconnections: a multi-scale analysis using the SPI and SPEI (1981–2025)
articles.abstract: In Burkina Faso, drought is generally described at a national level, as if it were evolving uniformly. This study has three objectives for the period from 1981 to 2025: to delineate homogeneous drought regions; to characterise the decadal variability of drought within each of these regions, as well as the proportion attributable to evaporation demand; and to identify the associated teleconnections and their stability over time. Six indices (3-, 6- and 12-month SPI and SPEI), calculated for the 47 provinces using CHIRPS precipitation data and AgERA5 reference evapotranspiration, enable these three objectives to be achieved. A principal component analysis with Varimax rotation, followed by clustering using Ward’s method, distinguishes four regions: the north-eastern Sahel, the central-west, the central-east and the south-western Sudan, the boundaries of which do not correspond to the administrative divisions of 2025. The 1981–1990 decade was, on average, the driest everywhere. In the north and centre, drought subsequently decreased sharply, with the six indices increasing by between 1.09 and 1.82 standard deviations between 1981–1990 and 2011–2020. In the south-west, the increases (+ 0.46 to + 0.93) are not significant for any index, as evaporation demand offsets between 18 per cent (3 months) and 44 per cent (12 months) of the increase due to rainfall; in the far south-west, rainfall itself has not recovered. The Mediterranean Sea surface temperature is the only oceanic index significantly linked to drought during the rainy season in all four regions (r = + 0.46 to + 0.53 for SPI-3 and SPEI-3). The Gulf of Guinea plays a role only in the south-west, independently of ENSO, although this link is tenuous. The link with ENSO, which was clear until the mid-2000s, has since weakened.

articles.title: Ba-Modified Bi4Ti3O12 Nanoparticles for Enhanced Electrochemical Energy Storage and Photocatalytic Methylene Blue (MB) Degradation
articles.abstract: To study the effect of Ba-substitution on the morphological, optical, structural and electrochemical and photo catalytic properties of Bi4Ti3O12 nanoparticles (NPs), the Ba-modified Bi4Ti3O12 NPs were successfully synthesized. XPS, XRD and EDX confirmed the formation of bismuth titanate crystal structure and phase purity. Non-linear GCD profiles indicated that a pseudo capacitive charge-storage mechanism and electrochemical analysis demonstrated a significant dependence on a specific Ba concentration. The optimized BBTO-2 composition exhibited a maximum specific capacitance(Cs) of 691 Fg− 1 at 1 Ag− 1 due to improved interfacial ion-transport kinetics and reduced charge-transfer resistance, as demonstrated by electrochemical EIS and Bode analysis. Moreover, the optimized sample showed better catalytic activity toward the photo catalytic degradation of methylene blue (MB) under solar light irradiation with 87% degradation efficiency within 80 min. Results demonstrate that the controlled Ba modification can be utilized to synthesize the multifunctional Bi4Ti3O12 NPs, applications in energy storage and environmental application.

articles.title: Quantifying the Relative Contributions of Marine Air Penetration and Agricultural Irrigation to Planetary Boundary-Layer Development in California’s Central Valley
articles.abstract: Summertime planetary boundary-layer height (PBLH) across California’s Central Valley (CV) is modulated by both agricultural irrigation and marine air penetration (MAP), with distinct regional patterns. Previous studies have examined these effects separately, using numerical models for irrigation and observational or reanalysis data for MAP. This study uses numerical modeling to quantify the relative contributions of irrigation versus MAP on PBLH changes across the CV during 21–27 July 2022 and to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Four experiments are conducted with the combinations of with (WIR) and without (WoIR) agricultural irrigation, and with and without MAP. The MAP effect is removed by filling mountain gaps to a minimum of 700 m. Compared with WoIR, the cooler surface temperature (i.e., lower sensible heat flux) due to stronger evapotranspiration in WIR weakens dry convection, resulting in a decrease of PBLH in the northern (southern) CV by 0.5–1.5 km (0.5–1 km) where the irrigation rate is high. In contrast, the MAP effect stabilizes the lower atmosphere by advecting cold air to the lower atmosphere and reduces PBLH across the CV by roughly 0.5–1 km. The stabilization layer by MAP in the northern CV is shallower than that in the southern CV. Overall, between the two effects, irrigation contributes more than 50% of the total PBLH reduction in the northern and southern CV, whereas MAP contributes to ~ 100% of the total PBLH reduction in the central CV, decaying away from the MAP sources.

articles.title: The Triple Duty Law for Mortality Accounted Infrastructure
articles.abstract: Modern civil engineering commits one measurable error at planetary scale: it builds single-duty objects. A bridge that only carries traffic, a dam wall that only resists water, a government building that only shelters files, each consumes land, cement, steel, money and carbon to perform exactly one function, then decays in silence until it fails in public. This article proposes a replacement doctrine and then subjects it to the mathematics it demands of others. The doctrine has two halves. First, the Triple-Duty Law: every new publicly funded structure above a threshold value must simultaneously (1) bear load, (2) store value (gravitational or electrochemical energy, harvested water, or usable heat) and (3) confess, meaning it must continuously sense and publicly report its own structural condition. Second, Mortality Accounting: every such structure is sanctioned with a dated, public Structural Passport stating its design death date, and a ring-fenced Mortality Escrow, proposed at 4% of capital cost, spendable only on that named asset. The quantitative core is derived, not asserted. A Weibull reliability model (shape β = 2.5, scale η = 75 years, both labelled assumptions) shows that a nominal 75-year asset carries only 30.5 years of 90%-reliability life, and that monitored maintenance (η = 95) cuts the 50-year failure probability from 30.4% to 18.2%. A 60-year life-cycle net-present-value model of a representative Rs 10 crore asset finds the triple-duty design cheaper by Rs 0.89 crore (7.2%) at a 7% real discount rate, with a break-even construction premium of 20.9% and a break-even discount rate near 11.6%, and it fails, openly, if the second duty's value is not counted. Storage duties are sized from first principles: 10,000 cubic metres of water at 30 metres of head stores 818 kilowatt-hours gross (613 usable); 1,000 square metres of roof in Andhra Pradesh yields about 750 cubic metres of harvested rain a year; 500 square metres of photovoltaic surface yields 146 megawatt-hours a year. A Bayesian calculation prices the third duty: a sensor alarm raises the probability of actionable deterioration from a 2% prior to 26.9%, and sensor silence lowers it to 0.21%. The article closes with a 36-month district pilot whose sample sizes are derived from a stated power calculation, and five pre-registered predictions. If the predictions fail, the doctrine fails. That is the point.

articles.title: Frequency-Dependent Electrical Behavior of Al/CuO/n-Si Schottky Barrier Diodes: Interface-State Analysis and Series-Resistance Effects
articles.abstract: In this work, an Al/CuO/n-Si/Ag heterostructure was fabricated using physical vapor deposition and radio-frequency sputtering. Its voltage- and frequency-dependent electrical properties were systematically investigated from capacitance–voltage (C-V) and conductance–voltage (G/ω-V) measurements performed over a wide range of frequencies and applied voltages. The electronic parameters were also analyzed at different frequencies to investigate how they change with frequency. The interface trap density (Nit) values were obtained using the low-high frequency capacitance (CLF-CHF) model, the Hill–Coleman method, and the parallel conduction method. The results showed a strong dependence of capacitance and conductance on both applied voltage and frequency, particularly at low and intermediate frequencies. The observed dispersion is mainly related to the response of the interface states and dielectric relaxation, while the effect of the series resistance becomes more evident at higher frequencies and in the accumulation region. The barrier height (ΦB), depletion width (WD), and electric field (Em) obtained from the measurements showed a clear dependence on frequency. Since the effect of series resistance becomes more significant at high frequencies, the 1 MHz data were corrected for the series resistance before further analysis. The analysis shows that Nit has a stronger effect on the device response in the depletion and inversion regions at low frequencies. At high frequencies, the effect of series resistance plays a dominant role, particularly in the accumulation region. The values of Nit obtained from the three methods were not the same, showing that the calculated interface-state density can vary depending on the model and measurement conditions. Therefore, both interface states and series resistance need to be considered when analyzing the electrical characteristics of CuO/n-Si-based Schottky diode structures.

articles.title: Enhanced modeling of expandable polystyrene synthesis: effects of n-pentane on polymerization process dynamics
articles.abstract: Expandable polystyrene (EPS) polymerization and impregnation processes were performed in Aspen Polymers software with modifications implemented through innovative user-model routines in order to represent the effect of the blowing agent (n-pentane) on the process dynamics. The modified model showed errors below 10% compared to experimental data from the literature, validating the process. Then, four EPS synthesis scenarios were proposed to improve batch cycles. The application of heating ramp and intermediate dosage of initiator – after 70% of conversion – was efficient for a high conversion production of EPS with more homogeneous properties, which guarantees a commercial-grade product without residual monomer. The continuous dosage of the blowing agent since the beginning of the polymerization was effective in minimizing the gel and glassy effects, besides eliminating the n-pentane addition step and reducing the batch cycle. Therefore, the commercial simulation model modified with the novel user-model routines implemented proved to be effective in improving the dynamics of the EPS synthesis process.

articles.title: Storage Memory in Non-Newtonian Annular Particle Transport and Its Conservative Reduction
articles.abstract: Temporary storage and subsequent release of drill cuttings alter surface recovery, making release timescales central to both hole-cleaning assessment and model selection. This study develops a mass-conserving model with one mobile state and two storage states. Window integration connects outlet flux to volumes derived from interval weighing. Analytical results establish a biexponential memory kernel, a condition for exact storage aggregation, and the residence-time variance lost through reduction. Equal storage release rates permit aggregation without changing the outlet response. With unequal release rates, a reduction that preserves the outlet rate coefficient, total capture rate, and mean residence time loses a nonnegative variance term proportional to the squared difference between release timescales. In annular experiments, a square-root onset relation gives a mean absolute percentage error of 3.18% for held-out particle sizes. Across 20 numerical trials with known input and initial conditions and approximately 5% relative observation noise, the median error in predicting recovery under an independent feed history is 1.03% for three states and 12.28% for two states. For 11 field recovery windows, assuming zero input and the same retrospectively selected release-enhancement windows, the three-state reconstruction has a root-mean-square error of 0.03054 m³, 10.36% below the two-state result. The analysis quantifies the loss of response broadening caused by storage aggregation and links model complexity to release timescales and observation resolution.

articles.title: Sea Surface Temperature Changes and Their Impacts on Agricultural Activities and Food Production in Coastal Communities of Rivers State, Nigeria
articles.abstract: Coastal agriculture in the Niger Delta is highly sensitive to ocean-driven climatic change, yet the specific contribution of sea surface temperature (SST) variability to agricultural decline and food insecurity in Nigeria's coastal communities remains under-researched at the sub-national level. This study evaluates the impacts of SST changes on agricultural activities and food production in coastal Rivers State, Nigeria, over a thirty-year period (1995–2025). A mixed-methods design integrated satellite-derived SST records with Land Surface Temperature (LST) and Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) change products, alongside household surveys, key informant interviews, and focus group discussions across the coastal local government areas of Bonny, Andoni, Opobo/Nkoro, Degema, and Okrika. Results show SST rose by approximately 1.5–3°C between 1995 and 2020–2025, with warming spreading from localised industrial hotspots into a regionally integrated pattern. This warming corresponds spatially with rising LST and declining NDVI across central and eastern local government areas – Obio/Akpor, Eleme, Tai, Oyigbo, and Khana – indicating reduced vegetation vigour and heightened crop stress, while limited pockets of NDVI improvement in western and central inland areas suggest localised adaptive resilience linked to freshwater access. Household data corroborate these geospatial patterns: a majority of surveyed farming households reported irregular rainfall, increased flooding, saltwater intrusion into farmland, and declining crop yields, which they directly associated with changing sea and land temperatures. The study concludes that SST-driven climatic variability is a measurable and spatially differentiated driver of agricultural decline and food insecurity risk in coastal Rivers State, and recommends climate-smart agriculture, improved irrigation and drainage, and salinity management as priority interventions.

articles.title: Effect of surface treatment on bonding strengths of hard and soft reline materials to 3D-printed denture base resin
articles.abstract: To evaluate the effects of surface treatment and thermal cycling on the tensile bond strength of hard and soft reline materials to a 3D-printed denture base resin (3DP) compared with a conventional heat-polymerized resin (HC). Specimens of 3DP and HC resins received no treatment, alumina sandblasting, dichloromethane priming, or 4-META/MMA-TBB resin (4-META) application. One hard reline material (HR), two acrylic-based soft reline materials (AC1 and AC2), and one silicone-based soft reline material (SI) were evaluated. Tensile bond strength was measured after 24 h of water storage (TC0) or 5,000 thermal cycles (TC5000) (n = 20). A significant four-factor interaction demonstrated that bond strength depended on the denture base resin, reline material, surface treatment, and thermal-cycling condition (P < 0.05). The hard reline material showed significantly higher bond strength than all soft materials (P < 0.05). For the 3DP resin, 4-META yielded the highest bond strength for AC1 under both aging conditions (P < 0.05) and improved bonding of HR and AC2 relative to untreated specimens (P < 0.05). In contrast, the silicone-based reline material exhibited limited responsiveness to surface treatment, and thermal cycling generally reduced bond strength. Bond durability between denture base and reline materials was influenced by the interaction among resin type, reline material, surface treatment, and thermal aging. Among the evaluated surface treatments, 4-META improved bonding for acrylic-based reline materials on the tested 3DP. The surface treatment protocols should be tailored to the specific denture base–reline material combination and anticipated aging condition.

articles.title: Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Additively Manufactured Bimetallic TC4-8Cu Alloy/316 Stainless Steel
articles.abstract: Titanium/steel bimetallic structures combine the high specific strength and excellent corrosion resistance of titanium alloys with the high ductility and low cost of stainless steels, offering broad application prospects in aerospace, nuclear energy, and marine engineering. However, direct joining is restricted by significant differences in their thermophysical properties and metallurgical compatibility, which readily lead to brittle Fe-Ti intermetallic phases and interfacial cracking. In this work, a TC4 alloy powder containing 8 wt.% Cu (TC4-8Cu) was used to fabricate a TC4-8Cu/316L bimetallic structure via electron beam powder bed fusion (EB-PBF). A metallurgically bonded, crack-free interface was obtained, consisting of the TC4-8Cu matrix, a Cu-rich zone, an intermetallic compound (IMC) layer, and the 316L matrix. Cu preferentially reacted with Ti to form Ti2Cu near the interface, which consumed the available Ti, restricted Fe-Ti interdiffusion, and effectively suppressed the formation of continuous brittle Fe-Ti layers. Tensile tests revealed a distinct two-stage fracture process. At room temperature, the 316L side fractured first at a peak stress of 482 MPa, followed by load transfer to the titanium side, resulting in an ultimate tensile strength of 636 MPa. At 350°C, the fracture sequence reversed: the TC4-8Cu side failed first at 618 MPa, and the remaining 316L section sustained a load-transfer stress of 190 MPa. These results demonstrate that powder-composition design with Cu can regulate interfacial reactions and preserve structural integrity in EB-PBF-fabricated titanium/steel bimetallic structures.

articles.title: Copper–tetracycline complexation steers pollutant resistance and removal by a Chlorella–Agrobacterium consortium
articles.abstract: The widespread co-occurrence of copper (Cu) and tetracycline (TC) in livestock wastewater poses challenges for bioremediation, yet the responses of algal–bacterial consortia (ABC) to such combined pollution remain unclear. As such, a Chlorella vulgaris–Agrobacterium sp. consortium was cultured in a simulated livestock wastewater and its physiological defenses and pollutant removal performance were investigated under single and combined Cu (0.5, 1.0 mg L− 1) and TC (5.0, 10.0 mg L− 1) stress. Single Cu or TC promoted growth at low doses, whereas combined treatments caused inhibition followed by later-stage recovery. Under combined stress, the ABC upregulated superoxide dismutase and catalase activities and enhanced secretion of polysaccharide-dominated extracellular polymeric substances (EPS). Speciation analysis showed that > 99.99% of Cu complexed with TC as CuTC and CuHTC⁺, which promoted Cu accumulation (removal up to 45%) via complexation-facilitated absorption, while shifting TC degradation toward abiotic hydrolysis. Cu removal was absorption-dominated (> 80%), and TC removal remained high (> 85%) despite reduced biodegradation. The reduction of chemical oxygen demand (COD), total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP) in the ABC culture was maintained or enhanced under both Cu treatments (0.5, 1.0 mg L− 1). FTIR spectroscopy confirmed that protein amide, carbonyl, and polysaccharide glycosidic groups served as primary binding platforms for Cu–TC complexes. Our findings reveal a bidirectional interplay wherein Cu–TC complexation alters the bioavailability of pollutants, thereby providing a framework to optimize ABC-based remediation of livestock wastewater co-contaminated with heavy metals and antibiotics.

articles.title: Soil organic matter quality and phosphorus forms in shaded and unshaded coffee-growing systems
articles.abstract: Coffee agroforestry systems exert effects on soil organic matter (SOM) quality through differences in litter inputs, root turnover and nutrient cycling. This study evaluated how contrasting coffee management systems (traditional polyculture (TP), shade specialized plantation (SSP), and unshaded (US)) affect SOM and how the related distribution of organic and inorganic forms of phosphorus (P) influence the quality of SOM in three coffee cultivation systems. Soil organic carbon (SOC), total nitrogen (N) (elemental analyzer), SOM thermal stability (DSC-TG), and forms of P (spectroscopy 31P NMR) were determined in upper mineral soil layer (0–10 cm in depth). Shaded systems (TP and SSP) showed higher SOC and total N concentrations compared to US system. Extractable P concentrations differed substantially among systems, with TP showing the highest, SSP intermediate values, and US the lowest. Thermal analysis showed that soil labile compounds were dominant (57–70%) in all systems, being highest in the shaded systems, which indicates enhanced nutrient turnover and more active soil biological activity. The 31P NMR spectra revealed changes in the distribution of the different P forms due to management type. TP showed the highest total and organic P concentrations but soil P was dominated by inorganic forms, indicating a fast nutrient recycling, whereas SSP showed the highest relative proportion of organic P (higher Po:Pi ratio), suggesting stronger microbial P immobilization. The research findings highlight the important role of shaded coffee agroecosystems to improve SOM content and quality of soil P, and therefore to enhance long-term sustainability in coffee systems.

articles.title: First Geodetic Documentation of Progressive Crustal Deformation Reversal Over 15 Years Following the 2011 Mw 9.1 Tohoku-Oki Earthquake
articles.abstract: Following a giant subduction earthquake, continental surface motion is expected to reverse from seaward to landward as postseismic transients decay and the megathrust relocks. This reversal has so far been reconstructed only piecemeal from snapshots of different margins in different earthquake-cycle phases, never observed continuously in space and time at a single margin, hindering efforts to model the long-term deformation of the subduction system. Using more than 15 years of dense GNSS observations, and deliberately retaining the secular trend, we map this reversal for the first time following the 2011 Mw 9.1 Tohoku-Oki earthquake. The reversal initiates within one year in southern Hokkaido and southeastern Chubu-Kanto and propagates toward central Tohoku as two fronts advancing at 19.2 and 13.3 km/yr from the south and north, forming an arcuate boundary deflected toward the trench above the rupture. Both fronts decelerate with time, and stations that reverse later take proportionally longer to complete the switch to landward motion. The transition is also mildly asymmetric, with the seaward velocity decaying to zero somewhat more abruptly than landward motion subsequently builds up. Systematic north-south offsets in propagation rate and reversal duration reveal distinct temporal characteristics of surface-deformation recovery in the northern and southern segments. These observations provide new margin-scale constraints on the evolving balance between postseismic transients and renewed megathrust loading, and quantitative benchmarks for future coupled models of megathrust recovery.

articles.title: Strain engineering-induced photothermal enhancement: Co/MnO@C heterostructure for high-performance phase change materials
articles.abstract: Carbon-based photothermal phase change materials (PCMs) is one of the most effective photothermal storage materials which offer a promising route to convert intermittent solar energy into storable thermal energy, however face intrinsic limitations from uncontrollable carbon skeleton defects and poorly tunable non-radiative relaxation pathways. In this study, we propose a novel strain engineering induced photothermal enhancement strategy, in which a metal-organic framework (MOF)-on-MOF-derived heterostructure is constructed to design a Co/MnO@C porous framework for encapsulating PCMs. The lattice mismatch between Co and MnO introduces localized strain, inducing the formation of interfacial defect states. Interfacial defect states serve as non-radiative recombination centers, efficiently converting solar energy into lattice thermal energy. After PCMs encapsulation, the composite achieved a photothermal conversion efficiency of 96.3% with 100 mW/cm2 solar irradiation. Photo-thermal-electric tests returned sustained outputs of 91.3 mV and 26.9 mA from the composite. It also achieves an improvement in formaldehyde removal in photocatalytic degradation and shows excellent anti-icing and de-icing capabilities. This work expands the application of strain engineering from charge control to phonon-driven energy conversion, offering a new idea for designing efficient and multi-functional photothermal storage materials.

articles.title: Rubidium-Referenced Frequency-Doubled Pockels Laser with High-Speed Electro-Optic Tuning
articles.abstract: Narrow-linewidth lasers with rapid frequency control are essential for atomic physics and quantum technologies, yet combining these capabilities in chip-integrated sources at visible wavelengths remains challenging. Here we demonstrate a hybrid integrated InP/thin-film lithium niobate Pockels laser that emits at 780 nm through intracavity second-harmonic generation and supports gigahertz-bandwidth frequency tuning. A periodically poled lithium niobate waveguide is embedded in a laser cavity terminated by an extended distributed Bragg reflector, which provides electro-optically tunable feedback only at the 1560 nm fundamental wavelength. This design yields a singly resonant cavity that enhances frequency conversion while allowing the second-harmonic output to follow rapid tuning without resonance alignment. The laser achieves intrinsic linewidths of 2.7 kHz at 1560 nm and 9.0 kHz at 780 nm, with electro-optic tuning bandwidths beyond 1 GHz at both wavelengths. A mode-hop-free tuning range of 6.48 GHz at 780 nm enables direct spectroscopy of the rubidium D2 transition. Locking the second-harmonic output to this transition reduces the standard deviation of its frequency fluctuations from 135 MHz to 8 MHz and transfers the atomic frequency reference to the fundamental. These results establish integrated frequency-doubled Pockels lasers as compact, rapidly tunable sources for atomic and quantum photonic systems.

articles.title: Correlations between Structural Disorder, Electronic States, and Charge Transport in AlCo, AlZn, FeCo, and FeZn Layered Double Hydroxide
articles.abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are promising 2D materials, but their electrical transport mechanisms remain strongly dependent on composition. Here, four equimolar (1:1) LDHs (AlCo, AlZn, FeCo, and FeZn) were synthesized by PVA-assisted co-precipitation and investigated using XRD, TEM/SAED, XPS, electrical conductivity, and thermoelectric power measurements. The Al-based samples showed more ordered crystalline structures, whereas the Fe-based samples exhibited greater structural disorder. Temperature-dependent transport analysis revealed non-adiabatic small-polaron hopping (SPH) at higher temperatures and Greaves’ variable-range hopping (VRH) behavior in the intermediate-temperature regime. The SPH assignment was supported by the Holstein–Emin bandwidth criterion, the calculated-to-experimental temperature comparison, and Meyer–Neldel compensation behavior. The apparent activation energy ranged from 0.397 eV for AlZn to 0.981 eV for FeZn. At 400 K, AlZn exhibited the highest reported conductivity and calculated hopping mobility (1.19 × 10− 4 cm2 V-1 s-1), whereas FeZn showed the lowest mobility (9.70 × 10− 8 cm2 V-1 s-1). These findings highlight the role of carrier mobility, alongside composition and local structure, in governing electrical transport in equimolar LDHs.

articles.title: Two-body fragmentation dynamics of pyrimidine dications induced by C 5+ ion impact
articles.abstract: The two-body fragmentation dynamics of doubly ionized pyrimidine (C4H4N22+) is investigated by highly charged ion impact using a reaction microscope. By combining multiparticle coincidence measurements with potential energy calculations along the reaction coordinate, we identify three distinct two-body fragmentation channels. Among them, the C4H4N22+ → CH 2 N + + C 3 H 2 N + channel dominates the fragmentation with a relative branching ratio of ∼92.02%. This pronounced selectivity can be primarily attributed to the preferential initial cleavage of the lowest-barrier C2–N3 bond, indicating the site-selective dissociation at the nitrogen heteroatom. Analysis of the potential energy surfaces further reveals that intramolecular hydrogen migration occurs in all identified channels and effectively lowers the energy barriers for the dissociation of C4H4N22+. These findings provide insights into ion-induced radiation damage in biological matter, as well as the formation and evolution of nitrogen-containing molecules in astrochemical environments.
