We propose that M is drawn from the mesoscale turbulence in which storms form, and measure the rotational content of this turbulence in ERA5 winds over the western Pacific. Including the storms, the rotational part of the one-dimensional spectrum along latitude circles follows the Coriolis branch Cf²k⁻³ of rotating stratified turbulence, with C=0.047, about a third of the theoretical value, from 12^circ to 24^circN. Between storms, this value is lower and grows, approximately, as f; we interpret the storms as its magnified, predominantly cyclonic tail. Toward the equator the energy of the turbulence persists but its rotational content collapses: equatorward of sim6^circN, more than one third of the energy is divergent. Typhoon Vamei, which formed at 1.5^circN in December 2001, was preceded by rotational variance above the 99th percentile of December climatology.

articles.title: GenerativeQC: A Generative, GPU-Accelerated Quantum Chemistry Program
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GenerativeQC is an open-source, GPU-accelerated quantum chemistry program that computes energies and analytic nuclear forces from Hartree-Fock (HF) and density functional theory (DFT) to closed-shell density-fitted CCSD(T) and an MP2-assisted CCSD(T)/complete-basis-set (CBS) composite. Its scientific compiler translates symbolic equations into C++ and CUDA code and uses automatic differentiation to generate the derivative and response programs that analytic forces require. A native runtime executes these programs together with hand-written iterative solvers and integral routines. Across HF and DFT benchmarks for eight methods on water clusters of up to 96 atoms, GenerativeQC is faster than GPU4PySCF in all 128 comparisons on an RTX 5090 GPU and in all but two comparisons on an H100 GPU. For correlated wave functions, compiler-generated derivative contractions and transpose Jacobian operators enable complete density-fitted CCSD(T) and CCSD(T)/CBS analytic forces on GPUs, completing a CCSD(T)/CBS energy-and-force calculation for heptane (23 atoms) in 4.5 min on a single H100 GPU (17 min on RTX 5090).

articles.title: Instability of layered two-phase flow in a vertical plane channel
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The equilibrium two-phase flows in a vertical plane channel are explored by adopting an approximate Boussinesq-like model. The class of stationary parallel flows examined in this paper features three-layer configurations in which the central core is less dense than the peripheral layers. Such flows are considered purely buoyant, induced by the density difference between the phases. The simplified scheme leads to a formulation where the parameters driving the transition to linear instability of the equilibrium flow are the Archimedes number and the dimensionless positions of the interfaces between the phases. The analysis takes into consideration symmetric and asymmetric flows, including, as special cases, also two-layer configurations with one phase close to the left-hand boundary wall and the other close to the right-hand wall. In particular, the completely antisymmetric flow, where the equilibrium velocity profile is an odd function of the transverse coordinate, shows up as the least stable configuration among those examined in this study.

articles.title: A boundary integral formulation for microscale Marangoni surfing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a model for collections of surfactant-producing particles moving along the surface of a viscous fluid under their self-generated Marangoni flows. Such systems are challenging due to their nonlocal nature: particle motion is coupled to Marangoni stresses distributed across the entire fluid surface and to the resulting flows in the bulk. In the low Reynolds and Péclet number limit, we reduce these nonlocal effects to a system of integral equations supported solely on the particles and their boundaries. This formulation is not only computationally tractable, but also provides a framework for systematically coarse-graining many-particle systems. Numerical simulations, performed with a custom spectral method, show collective dynamics are highly sensitive to shape. In particular, among elliptical particles, we find prolate particles tend to attract while oblate particles tend to repel, and these geometric details control the stability of polarized populations. We rationalize these behaviors through a far-field expansion of the boundary integral equations and its corresponding reduced-order model.

articles.title: xTBloom: GPU Batching for High-Throughput GFN-xTB Calculations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conformational searches and multiwindow free-energy sampling require large numbers of GFN-xTB energy and force evaluations across molecular conformations and sampling windows. Processing each system separately on a GPU makes it difficult to amortize memory management, host-device data transfer, and kernel-launch overhead. Here, we present xTBloom, a GPU batching library for GFN-xTB energy and force evaluations. xTBloom sorts evaluation queues by atomic orbital (AO) count before forming batches, accommodates size differences through a native ragged layout, maintains independent self-consistent charge (SCC) and failure states for each system, and selects execution paths according to data residency. We focus the quantitative evaluation on GFN2-xTB through cross-program comparisons on QM9 and OMol25, CPU-CUDA comparisons, finite-difference force checks, and controlled failure tests. On a near-size OMol25 workload, GPU execution achieved a 2.9-fold speedup over xTBloom's single-core CPU backend. A companion LAMMPS plugin integrates cross-window batching with periodic quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) simulation. In a short synchronized test with 48 windows on one GPU, the complete coupled workflow achieved an aggregate speedup of approximately 14 over sequential execution of the same windows. These results demonstrate the throughput benefits of batched GFN-xTB evaluation for repeated electronic-structure calculations and multiwindow sampling.

articles.title: Consistent interfacial flow numerics - Part I: The gravity force term
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The OpenFOAM solver interFoam for incompressible two-phase flows combines the single-phase PISO/PIMPLE algorithm for the pressure-velocity coupling with an interface advection step. It relies on the standard finite volume discretisation of the momentum equation, which assumes smooth fields, but across a water-air interface the density jumps by a factor of about 1000. The geometric Volume-of-Fluid method isoAdvector, used in interIsoFoam, made the advection step consistent with a sharp interface, but spurious velocities near it remain due to the momentum discretisation. This series revisits it term by term. Here we treat the gravity term, which acts only at the interface and depends on the local interface height. Both solvers crudely assign this height using the face centre positions. We show that this is a key source of the spurious air velocities. Taking the height from the reconstructed interface instead gives an exact discrete balance between pressure and gravity for a horizontal interface on any mesh. We implement this geometric gravity model in a new solver, interIsoGoam. In a tilted box of still water, where the original solvers give air speeds of metres per second, it keeps the velocity of order 10⁻⁹ m/s. This holds for density ratios up to 10⁷ and, with a hydrostatic initial pressure, on skewed and locally refined meshes. In a progressive wave, interIsoGoam has the lowest maximum velocity of the three solvers. At maximum Courant numbers of 0.1 and below it therefore needs up to 43 % fewer steps and up to 38 % less wall-clock time. At 0.5 the wave grows by up to 12 % over 15 periods, so we recommend 0.1 or less. One error remains, namely an overprediction of the horizontal water velocity below the wave crest. All three solvers exhibit this error, which grows steadily with time. In Part II we trace this error to the implicit discretisation of the momentum convection term.

articles.title: Time-Varying Medium from an Ensemble of Laser-Dressed Quantum Emitters
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a minimal quantum-mechanical model of a frequency dispersive, time-modulated medium that explicitly incorporates the pumping mechanism. It consists of a homogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters dressed by a pump laser. We analyze their dispersive, time-varying response to a perturbative probe field by deriving the macroscopic polarizability of the ensemble, and then solving Maxwell's equations via the Floquet formalism. This yields a rich band structure that departs from conventional analyses in which the modulation source is neglected, arising from the interplay between the dispersive polaritonic and time-varying responses. These results shed light on the role of the modulation source in time-varying media and pave the way toward realizing dispersive time-varying media from driven quantum-mechanical systems.

articles.title: Consistent interfacial flow numerics - Part II: The momentum convection term
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The two-phase Volume-of-Fluid solvers of OpenFOAM overpredict the horizontal water velocity near the crest of a water wave, and the error grows as the wave propagates. Part I of this series removed the spurious air velocities caused by the gravity term but left this error unchanged. Here we show that it is caused by the momentum convection term. Its mass flux is computed in the interface advection step from the velocity at the start of the time step, whereas the convected velocity is taken at the end of the step, because convection is discretised implicitly. In a progressive wave, where the horizontal and vertical velocities are 90 degrees out of phase, this time lag produces an upward flux of horizontal momentum, proportional to the time step, which accumulates in a spurious current near the surface. The same mismatch makes the response to a force depend on the density at the wrong time level. Explicit convection removes the lag and makes the response consistent with the gravity force, but requires the convected face velocity at the interface to be taken from the upwind cell. Only then is the new velocity of a cell a weighted average of old velocities, whatever the density ratio. We demonstrate both requirements with prescribed flows and with the full solver. For a progressive wave, explicit convection with upwind face velocities at the interface reduces the overprediction of the crest velocity from 26-31 % to within 1 % and removes the near-surface current. The resulting solver, fluxinator, is meant for maximum Courant numbers of 0.1 and below, where it keeps the wave height within 1.5 % over 15 periods on meshes with six or more cells per wave height. Because the spurious velocities that limit the time step are removed, it needs 34-42 % less wall-clock time than interFoam for the tested wave.

articles.title: Kinetic study of Reaction-Control-Jet Interference in Rarefied Hypersonic Crossflow
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A 1975 wind-tunnel study at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) of a helium jet blowing from a flat plate into a Mach 11 to 12 air crossflow at three freestream densities is revisited using two- and three-dimensional Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) computations at Knudsen numbers 0.021 to 0.125. The planar slot used in two-dimensional model computations reproduces the shock topology, the sign and two-lobed structure of the interference pressure and its trend with rarefaction, and its plate-alone boundary layer is consistent with the three-dimensional one and with a similarity solution with slip and temperature jump. However, two-dimensional simulations overpredict the peak interference pressure about twelvefold at every condition and carry it farther upstream. A resolution sweep at the most rarefied condition converges the planar interference to within 1% of its extrapolated limit. Three-dimensional DSMC reproduces the measured interference pressure at all three densities, within 25% at the lobe peak and 3 mm in its position, although two- and three-dimensional simulations overpredict the plate-alone wall pressure by 50 to 75%. Continuum breakdown around the jet persists even at the lowest Knudsen number examined. Fully three-dimensional kinetic simulations are underway to extend the present validation to a comparison of jet strength and forces over wider Knudsen number ranges, and to an examination of lateral relief as a reason for the discrepancy.

articles.title: Strong Epsilon-Near-Zero Confinement and Interface-Controlled Dynamics in Inverse-Designed Transparent Conducting Oxide Cavities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving optical modulation that is both strong and ultrafast remains a central challenge in time-varying photonics. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that combining inverse-designed cavities that utilize transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) operating at the epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) point with boundaries that support carrier transport can meet this requirement. This is achieved by leveraging ENZ-enhanced optical absorption and electron heating with interface-engineered carrier relaxation. A multilayer inverse-design framework, combined with a structural disorder-aware correction loop, is developed to preserve robust resonant absorption in ultrathin TCO films under realistic material disorder. Relative to conventional TCO cavity geometries, the inverse-designed structures exhibit stronger light confinement, greater electron temperature modulation, and markedly faster recovery. Beyond cavity design, interfacial barrier engineering and adjacent-layer doping emerge as effective degrees of freedom for co-designing spectral and temporal dynamics. Furthermore, our theoretical framework shows that the inverse-designed cavity supports richer oscillatory transmittance dynamics on the few-optical-cycle timescale compared to its single-film counterpart, with interfacial control enabling further temporal compression. The combined control of optical confinement and interfacial dynamics establishes inverse-designed TCO cavities as a viable platform for time-varying photonic media capable of supporting strong and ultrafast optical responses.

articles.title: Relative periodic orbits of a free spinning loop
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23582v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A closed elastic string with no external forces can hold any shape while its material moves steadily along the curve (a steady axial motion), because its tension and the force needed to turn the material around a bend are both proportional to the curvature. I compute the periodic motions that grow from the simplest of these motions, the spinning ring, by Newton's method on a chain of masses. They include rotating waves that turn at twice the rotation rate of the material, standing "flappers" with two to five lobes, and period-doubled and period-tripled orbits. The chain only approximates the string. The orbits and their strong instabilities change little with more masses and are properties of the continuous string. Most weak instabilities change with the number of masses and are artifacts of approximating the string by a finite chain. The saddle flapper of a loop stretched 30% beyond its natural length is neutrally stable at small heights and unstable at large ones. An unstable saddle flapper trades energy back and forth with an in-plane oval, and at large amplitude the energy spreads to the shortest waves of the chain. For Keller's linear string, whose tension is proportional to the stretched length, every motion is periodic, and every knot carries an exactly periodic flapper. For a Hookean string the curvature of a knot couples a ripple to stretching waves that travel at a different speed, and in the simulations a ripple on a sliding knot does not return to its starting shape. Whether a Hookean knot carries any periodic flapper is open.

articles.title: MAIC-2 v2.3: A Fortran program for simulating the surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation of the planet Mars
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23643v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Mars Atmosphere-Ice Coupler MAIC-2 is a computationally efficient, zonally-averaged model designed to simulate Martian surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation over timescales of 10⁵ to 10⁷ years. While sophisticated General Circulation Models (GCMs) provide high-resolution simulations of the Martian atmosphere, their high computational cost makes them largely unsuitable for studies covering millions of years of orbital evolution. MAIC-2 addresses this gap by utilizing physically-based, zonally-averaged parameterizations, including a Local Insolation Temperature (LIT) scheme and a mass balance engine driven by free-convection and instantaneous mixing physics. Version 2.3 introduces a fully modularized Fortran architecture that improves maintainability and ensures that the software remains entirely self-contained, requiring no external numerical libraries or specialized data formats for execution. Demonstrated through a 20-million-year transient simulation, the model successfully reproduces the primary characteristics of the Martian polar layered deposits. MAIC-2 provides the planetary science community with a versatile, open-source tool for investigating the long-term climatic impacts of orbital variations on the Martian surface.

articles.title: Kernel Design in Particle Mesh Ewald Methods: Splitting, Interpolation, and Upsampling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23737v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For more than thirty years, particle mesh Ewald (PME) methods have dominated the computation of electrostatic interactions in molecular dynamics. A PME method uses a splitting kernel to divide the interaction into a local part, summed within a cutoff, and a smooth part, computed on a grid with a spreading and interpolation (SI) kernel. The established methods use Ewald's Gaussian split with B-spline SI kernels, and the recent Ewald summation with prolates accelerates them severalfold by using a prolate spheroidal wave function (PSWF) for both kernels. Neither choice meets two needs of molecular dynamics: a smooth energy, which long simulations need in order to conserve it, and a low-order SI kernel that stays accurate on coarse grids and gains accuracy as the grid is refined. We present a framework for designing both kernels to meet these needs. For inverse powers from the Coulomb to the dispersion interaction, our splits make the local part smooth at the cutoff to any order while keeping the Fourier concentration of the smooth part close to optimal. We show that with analytic differentiation, the force error of a continuous SI kernel of fixed shape vanishes under grid refinement only if every particle, wherever it lies, gives the grid its exact charge and dipole moment. Our SI kernel for the Coulomb interaction ensures this by construction and is twice continuously differentiable. Compared with the B-spline of the same order, it needs fewer grid points by a factor of up to nearly five; on coarse grids, it mostly needs a lower order than the PSWF kernel. In simulations of liquid water over 100 million time steps, the new kernels reduce the energy drift of both the established and the PSWF kernels by about three orders of magnitude, with a smaller force error than either. Existing PME codes can adopt them by replacing only the two kernels and the Fourier multiplier.

articles.title: OmniFish: A Bioinspired, Modular, Reconfigurable Soft Robotic Fish Enabling Multi-Modal Swimming
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24511v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we introduce OmniFish, a bioinspired modular soft robotic fish designed to emulate the full spectrum of body and/or caudal fin (BCF) locomotion modes within a single robotic platform. The design combines morphology averaging across representative fish species with a tendon-driven compliant segmented spine whose effective stiffness can be reconfigured through progressive mechanical jamming. By selectively constraining body segments, OmniFish shifts deformation from whole-body undulation to posterior body bending and localized tail oscillation, enabling bioinspired Anguilliform, Subcarangiform, Carangiform, Thunniform, and Ostraciiform swimming using a single tendon-driven actuator. The design was guided by morphometric analysis and evaluated through caudal-fin thrust characterization, numerical body-drag simulations, kinematic analysis, and swimming performance experiments. Kinematic analysis confirmed the intended robot transition from distributed body undulation to localized tail oscillation. Swimming experiments demonstrated distinct mode-dependent performance, with the Ostraciiform configuration achieving the highest straight-line velocity of 8.14 cm/s and the lowest cost of transport of 2.42 at 1.5 tail beats/s. These proof-of-concept results show that a mechanically simple stiffness-reconfigurable architecture can generate distinct BCF swimming modes and provide a versatile strategy for developing multimodal soft robotic fish.

articles.title: Electric combined-field-only P1 Galerkin BEM for PEC scattering with scalar Helmholtz operators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a Galerkin boundary element method for the indirect electric field-only combined-field integral equation (ECFOIE) for perfectly electrically conducting obstacles with smooth surfaces. The method is free of low-frequency breakdown and of spurious resonances. It applies scalar Helmholtz operators componentwise, so that fast scalar solvers can be reused, with less memory than a Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) discretization. The iteration count of the Calderón-regularized ECFOIE (R-ECFOIE) is constant under mesh refinement and, with a complex-wavenumber Calderón regularizer, grows only mildly with frequency. The discretization uses continuous, nodal piecewise-linear basis functions on flat triangular meshes, with essentially as many unknowns as an RWG discretization, and tangential and normal projections and the mean curvature of the obstacle's surface carry the vector structure. On flat meshes the curvature is concentrated on the edges, and we average the edge measure obtained from the first variation of area over vertex patches, which gives sparse curvature matrices. At low frequency, four Lagrange-multiplier constraints on the induced charge and on the longitudinal dipole moments of the far field keep the R-ECFOIE accurate in the quasi-static regime, tested on scatterers eight orders of magnitude smaller than the wavelength. Under mesh refinement, the errors decrease at about second order. A Helmholtz resonator, a rounded Fichera cube, and a smoothed Stanford bunny are compared with electric field integral equation (EFIE) solutions, and the first two also with electrostatic references at extreme low frequency.

articles.title: Shedding Light on Quantum Non-Classicality: Witnessing Wigner Negativity with Free Electrons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24834v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Certifying quantum non-classicality like Wigner negativity typically demands full optical state tomography. This work introduces a noise-resilient framework for witnessing optical Wigner negativity using phase-resolved quantum photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (QPINEM). By mapping electron coherences directly to symmetrically ordered optical characteristic functions within a coupling-limited phase-space region, the protocol bypasses full optical reconstruction. A post-measurement witness matrix is constructed via Bochner's theorem from recorded electron spectra, where negative eigenvalues certify non-classicality. To ensure reliability under realistic experimental conditions, a noise-aware selection procedure decouples discovery from statistical validation. Benchmarked across various optical preparations-including vacuum-Fock superpositions, odd cat states, and GKP states-the protocol provides a statistically bounded pathway for probing quantum features with free electrons.

articles.title: Matter without mass: do we really need the concept of mass?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2106.01346v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Einstein's most famous equation -- E=mc² -- generated a short-circuit between the concepts of mass and energy, which also affects other concepts like matter, radiation, and vacuum. Physics currently has a mixture of classical, relativistic, and quantum concepts of mass, which generates a great deal of confusion and many problems. Clear definitions need to be established if one wants to avoid ghost hunting. In particular, by abandoning the idea of mass as a primitive concept and focusing on time and energy, some interesting implications are emerging. It is noted that the cutoff frequency of the quantum vacuum energy, which would reproduce the observed value of the cosmological constant, is within one order of magnitude of the present-day peak frequency of the Cosmic Microwave Background. The previous versions of this essay speculated on a physical link between the two frequencies, and on a rotating universe described by a Kerr-de Sitter metric. In this revised version, I show that the coincidence holds only at the present epoch -- it is another way to state the well-known cosmic coincidence problem -- and that the speculations built on it must be dropped.

articles.title: Bandgap fluctuations and robustness in two-dimensional hyperuniform dielectric materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2302.02815v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We numerically study the statistical fluctuations of photonic band gaps in ensembles of stealthy hyperuniform disordered patterns. We find that at low stealthiness, where correlations are weak, band gaps of different system realizations appear over a wide frequency range, are narrow, and generally do not overlap. Interestingly, above a critical value of stealthiness χ gtrsim 0.35, the bandgaps become large and overlap significantly from realization to realization, while a second gap appears. These observations extend our understanding of photonic bandgaps in disordered systems and provide information on the robustness of gaps in practical applications.

articles.title: Numerical study of nitrogen oxides chemistry during plasma assisted combustion in a sequential combustor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2306.15539v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Plasma Assisted Combustion (PAC) is a promising technology to enhance the combustion of lean mixtures prone to instabilities and flame blow-off. Although many PAC experiments demonstrated combustion enhancement, several studies report an increase in NOx emissions. The aim of this study is to determine the kinetic pathways leading to NOx formation in the second stage of a sequential combustor assisted by Nanosecond Repetitively Pulsed Discharges (NRPDs). For this purpose, Large Eddy Simulation (LES) associated with an accurate description of the combustion/NOx chemistry and a phenomenological model of the plasma kinetics is used. Detailed kinetics 0-Dimensional reactors complement the study. First, the LES setup is validated by comparison with experiments. Then, the NOx chemistry is analyzed. For the conditions of operation studied, it is shown that the production of atomic nitrogen in the plasma by direct electron impact on nitrogen molecules increases the formation of NO. Then, the NO molecules are transported through the turbulent flame without being strongly affected. This study illustrates the need to limit the diatomic nitrogen dissociation process in order to mitigate harmful emissions. More generally, the very good agreement with experimental measurements demonstrates the capability of LES combined with accurate models to predict the NRPD effects on both turbulent combustion and NOx emissions.

articles.title: A note on semidiurnal motions in the deep Mediterranean
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.03771v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Mediterranean Sea is known for its limited tidal motions. For example, surface barotropic tidal elevations have an amplitude of about 0.1 m in the Northwestern Mediterranean. Nevertheless, small significant peaks occur at semidiurnal frequencies in spectra of temperature variance measured near the 2450-m deep seafloor at a multiple-line mooring. These semidiurnal signals appear to be surface tides commonly measured by pressure sensors, but are only observable in temperature under near-homogeneous conditions when buoyancy frequency N < f, the inertial frequency. After transfer of pressure to temperature units via the local adiabatic lapse rate, the observed internal-wave temperature signals may thus be corrected for 1.5x10⁻⁵ degrC amplitude semidiurnal, predominantly lunar barotropic tides. The remaining baroclinic tides are embedded in the broad and featureless inertio-gravity wave (IGW) band, with small but significant energy enhancement near its boundaries including the precise semidiurnal frequency, also under tenfold-larger energetic stratified-water conditions. The similar IGW bands under both stratification conditions suggest slanted convection during stratified-water conditions, as the stratification is near-homogenous in the direction slanted to the vertical. The use of multiple instruments improves spectral statistics at frequencies exceeding IGW, and including the IGW band under some near-homogeneous conditions but not under stratified-water conditions during which more coherent motions prevail.

articles.title: Closer look at some sum uncertainty relations and related relations: Their weak points
articles.abstract: arXiv:2504.09122v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze the weak and critical points of some state--dependent uncertainty relations that follow from the inequalities for the norms of vectors in the Hilbert space of states of a quantum system. Uncertainty relations for sums of standard deviations, for sums of variances, and other relations between standard deviations or variances are studied. The obtained results are compared with the conclusions obtained in similar cases using the standard Heisenberg--Robertson uncertainty relation. We also show that, in critical cases, the right--hand sides of sum and stronger sum uncertainty relations provide similar information regarding lower bounds on the left--hand sides of these relations as the Heisenberg--Robertson uncertainty relations do. New reverse uncertainty relations for a sum of variances are derived.

articles.title: Transversal surface-code game with reconfigurable qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.18979v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Qubit platforms supporting flexible connectivity have opened the door to theoretical advances in fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC), offering a compelling alternative to lattice surgery by leveraging transversal gates. Among such systems, neutral atoms have demonstrated notable progress enabled by large-scale parallel atom transport. However, a crucial gap remains between the theory of FTQC and its practical realization with these systems. Most critically, a key theoretical requirement, that syndrome extraction must be performed frequently enough to keep error accumulation below a threshold constant, is not satisfied in a scalable manner in the existing approach due to increased transport times. In this work, we develop a theoretical framework that closes such a gap, bridging theoretical advances in fault-tolerant protocols with the latest experimental capabilities. Building on the "game of surface code" framework originally developed for superconducting qubits, we introduce an alternative game-based paradigm for transversal-gate FTQC, formulating the protocol as a transversal surface-code game governed by rules for mode transitions of code cells. The rulesets are designed to enable syndrome extraction at any intermediate step during logical gate implementation, ensuring compatibility with the threshold theorem, while fully exploiting the capabilities of the hardware to scale and accelerate FTQC. As an application, our framework offers a systematic methodology and high-level abstraction for resource estimation and optimization; an exemplary estimation for a neutral-atom system demonstrates performance competitive with a baseline lattice-surgery-based approach on superconducting qubits, even with physical operations orders of magnitude slower. These results bridge the theory and experiment of FTQC with reconfigurable qubits toward scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computers.

articles.title: Instantaneous velocity during quantum tunnelling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.16385v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum tunneling, the phenomenon by which particles traverse regions forbidden by classical mechanics, underpins a range of processes including nuclear fusion, photosynthesis, and superconducting qubits. Its fundamental dynamics, however, remain heavily debated. A prominent open controversy concerns the apparent energy--speed paradox reported by Sharoglazova et al., where particles with lower incident energy exhibit a higher tunneling "speed". Here we resolve this paradox using a dynamical framework of tunneling. We show that, at the rising edge of the incident wavepacket, the particle velocity inside the barrier continuously decreases from an initially large value; it stays constant across the wavepacket plateau and reverses sign at the falling edge. In tandem with this velocity evolution, the in-barrier probability density gradually accumulates, holds steady over the plateau, and subsequently decays. We further derive closed-form expressions relating velocity and dwell time to barrier width and height, and investigate how coupling between internal and external states modulates the tunneling of massive particles. This dynamical picture reconciles the counterintuitive lower-energy--"higher-speed" paradox and provides a theoretical basis for time-resolved tunneling measurements.

articles.title: EEG2MCU: Sensing-to-Execution Co-Design for Wearable EEG Inference
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wearable EEG inference is constrained not only by model size, but also by the channel-dependent sensing front end that must process high-dimensional inputs before compact downstream computation. We present EEG2MCU, a sensing-to-execution co-design framework that treats electrode count as a hardware design variable through task-aware montage selection. EEG2MCU retains a compact time-frequency representation and generates only the INT8 regions required by each first-layer tile, avoiding full input materialization. Halo reuse and access-aware placement across Flash, SRAM, and tightly coupled memory further reduce redundant generation and data movement. On a Cortex-M7 MCU, EEG2MCU reduces peak SRAM by 11.38x relative to the baseline, including a 1.71x reduction from the 62-to-19 electrode montage, while reducing latency by 2.57x and energy by 2.48x. It retains 94-96% of full-montage accuracy, demonstrating practical high-dimensional EEG inference under tight embedded-resource constraints.

articles.title: How Uncertain Is My Action? Self-Correcting Visual Planning with Frozen World Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A frozen latent world model combined with sampling-based model predictive control is a visual planner. At deployment, the executed action can depart from the commanded one, and the frozen model has no way to notice. We show that the model can be run in reverse: for any hypothesized actuation shift, it predicts what it should have observed under that shift, and comparing this prediction with what was actually observed quantifies the shift and lets the planner correct itself. Unlike the residual energy, which mixes the shift with the model's own error, the score keeps only the part of the residual that a shift can produce. This shift score detects the shift with a locally optimal test, estimates it with Cramer-Rao error bars, names the dominant generator, and compensates the planner once an alarm fires. On PushT, TwoRoom and OGBench-Cube with a frozen latent world model, measured detection follows the prediction to within 0.05 AUROC. Self-correction raises success from 0.650 to 0.862 on PushT and from 0.378 to 0.432 on the harder Cube task, levels with an oracle that is told the true shift at the same block, better than five common test-time adaptation methods. On a real robotic arm, the score identifies a base-joint offset that no joint encoder registers and reduces the reach error from 36 mm to 3-5 mm, and under shifts drawn at random and sealed before the session, estimates recover 92-94% of the error reduction achieved with the true shift. The broader implication is that a frozen world model can act as a filter by predicting the future, testing action-interface uncertainty and validity, and finally correcting failures.

articles.title: A Fast, Programmable GPU-to-CPU Invocation Layer for GPU-Initiated Communication
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern GPU workloads increasingly rely on device-initiated communication to let GPU kernels communicate directly without synchronizing with the host at kernel boundaries. Existing libraries commonly favor placing transport control on GPU threads, an approach known as GPUDirect Async (GDA), and treat reverse offload to host proxy threads as a slower fallback. We argue that reverse offload can outperform GDA and should be a first-class communication path. We further propose exposing reverse offload as a programming interface that lets users define workload-specific communication operations. We present KIWI, a programmable reverse-offload framework that achieves sub-microsecond one-way device-to-host latency and hundreds of millions of operations per second. We address practical challenges of scaling reverse offload, including contention on shared queues, polling overhead, and load imbalance across proxies. KIWI-P2P, a SHMEM-like library built on KIWI, outperforms state-of-the-art GDA implementations in both latency and bandwidth. More importantly, KIWI-EP redesigns low-latency mixture-of-experts dispatch and combine kernels around workload-defined operations, lowering expert-parallel communication latency by up to 2.3x over the best existing backend on AMD GPUs and time per output token in vLLM by up to 29%. The source code of KIWI is available at https://github.com/AMDResearch/kiwi.

articles.title: LAGR: Language-Aware Grasp Re-Ranking for Task Oriented Grasping
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Grasping is a fundamental capability for robotic manipulation, with the appropriate grasp depending on the downstream task. For example, a hammer should be held by its handle for hammering but by its head when it is handed over. Selecting such a grasp requires consideration of two criteria: physical feasibility on the object and suitability for the task. Developing such an approach requires dense grasp labels with both feasibility and task scores on real observations, but existing task-oriented grasping datasets are small, synthetic, or costly to annotate. To address this gap, we construct a dataset of 2.68 million scored 5-DoF grasp annotations over 100,911 image-task pairs from 17 object categories. Additionally, we introduce LAGR, a task-oriented grasp detection method that explicitly addresses both these challenges. Given vision-language inputs, LAGR first generates task-independent grasp proposals along with a physical feasibility score, and then scores the generated grasps with a language-conditioned re-ranker that reasons over all proposals jointly. Experiments show that LAGR outperforms the next best method by 9.3 percentage points. We further validate LAGR on real objects by executing task-oriented grasps with a Franka Research 3 robot.

articles.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed to beyond what the task reads or writes; and feature coverage, the application features beyond what the task uses. Existing works set each dimension on engineering grounds, but they do not measure its effect on training. How complete must an environment be to train a capable agent, and along which dimensions? In MobileGym, we adjust each dimension separately, train Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, and evaluate every policy in the original full environment. A verifier that rewards only one reference path lowers success by 10.53 points, and removing unneeded records also lowers success. Pruning unneeded features instead raises success from 51.61% to 56.13%, entirely on tasks whose environments it left unchanged. The gain reverses when each episode is weighted equally and vanishes when only episodes on the pruned tasks are balanced. Without pruning, length weighting there reinforces long detour successes that erode skills on other tasks. Following these findings, we build MobileGym-Lite, which keeps reward and data coverage complete and prunes unneeded features. It outperforms Full in the full environment (55.48% versus 51.61% success) with lower construction cost.

articles.title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24039v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic AI platforms-systems in which LLM agents plan, invoke tools, retain memory and coordinate to change the state of enterprise systems-are being procured faster than they can be measured. Public agent benchmarks score models in fixed harnesses; enterprises buy integrated platforms whose orchestration, memory, governance and tooling layers dominate outcomes, and they buy them largely on the strength of vendor demonstrations. We report an industrial evaluation programme ("bakeoff") run by the innovation laboratory of a global bank in which ten platforms-spanning open-source frameworks, proprietary products and hyperscaler ecosystems-were assessed by a cross-functional panel on nine capability dimensions across three financial-services workloads: counterparty credit risk, retrieval-augmented generation and process automation. Scores separate the field into three tiers that are stable under alternative weightings, and surface workload-specific strengths that aggregates hide. A secondary analysis, however, finds Cronbach's alpha = 0.98 across nominally distinct dimensions and rank correlations >= 0.93 with the total for eight of nine: a halo effect indicating that demonstration-based scoring measures presentation as much as capability. From these lessons we propose a gate-then-score evaluation protocol with four layers (capability, execution reliability, governance gates, business value), trace-level reliability metrics estimated over repeated runs, an autonomy-readiness scale and a reproducibility protocol. We state precisely what the present evidence supports, and what a controlled harness must add to turn enterprise platform evaluation from structured judgement into measurement.

articles.title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing volume of topically similar papers makes it difficult to identify new work that can offer useful research insights or methodological guidance. We present KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight discovery tool that combines multiple sources of evidence into personalized reading priorities. Users specify topics, priorities, exclusions and dates; the system brings together topical relevance, recency, author research histories, collaboration paths and direction-specific institutional context. By exposing each score component and its supporting sources, KnowMe helps readers select promising papers for their current questions and discover relevant work beyond familiar authors. Automatic acquisition, version merging and graph-cache reuse keep this workflow convenient without large language model (LLM) inference during ordinary use. Experiments on 174,640 acquired records show more than threefold faster repeated context preparation, while cached abstracts improve normalized discounted cumulative gain at rank 10 (NDCG@10) from 0.412 to 0.598 on expert-judged retrieval tasks. Complementary analyses examine how the same accumulated records support semantic retrieval, research-history modeling and literature-grounded planning. A browser interface and a structured command-line interface (CLI) make these capabilities available to both researchers and research agents, positioning KnowMe as a practical upstream tool for literature-informed recursive self-improvement (RSI) workflows.

articles.title: Space-X: Self-Evolving Spatial Agents Weaving Clues into Evidence Chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial reasoning connects visual observations, geometric estimates, and linguistic decisions into a coherent derivation. Yet tool-augmented agents often acquire evidence without clear targets, combine outputs under inconsistent object or reference-frame semantics, and misjudge evidence sufficiency. Thus, more tools or calls do not reliably improve reasoning. We introduce Space-X, a spatial-reasoning framework that self-evolves toward complete, continuous evidence-chain construction. An Execution Agent acquires, associates, and judges evidence per problem using role-specific memory. A Control Agent diagnoses evidence-chain breaks from execution traces and jointly revises tools, interfaces, skills, memory organization, and decision rules. This loop co-evolves capability and evidence use: evidence needs guide capability development; usable results guide actions. Across multiple benchmarks, Space-X yields gains with four base models. Relative to baselines, GPT-6-sol improves answer accuracy on ViewSpatial and MMSI by 50.39% and 23.07%, respectively; Gemini-3.8-Flash gains 47.50% and 25.22% on these benchmarks. This provides a unified route from fragmented spatial clues to traceable, derivable answers.

articles.title: Risk-Triggered Search: Behavior-Preserving Safe Control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pre-trained visual world models generate multi-step action plans from current and goal observations, yet terminal-proximity objectives fail to prevent forbidden-zone traversal or rigid-body collision sliding. Purely visual interfaces may lack analytical dynamics, structured states, or explicit collision geometry, requiring internal prediction of action-conditioned process risk. We propose Risk-Triggered Search (RTS) for frozen Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models. Rather than relying on static state features that cannot distinguish candidate plans sharing an observation, RTS unrolls action-conditioned future latent prefixes in the frozen world model and trains a lightweight risk head with process-violation supervision. To intervene selectively while preserving safe nominal behavior, RTS uses the same predicted prefix-risk criterion as both the search trigger gate and hard feasibility gate: safe nominal plans execute directly, whereas alarms trigger local Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) search to minimize nominal deviation within the feasible set. To prevent isotropic Euclidean minimal modification from shrinking obstacle-directed actions into zero-amplitude stalling, we introduce an amplitude-preserving metric dAP that retains tangential progression while maintaining a unique zero at the nominal plan. Under unified gating and this unique-zero condition, bypassing safe-state search yields closed-loop trajectories strictly identical to every-step same-kernel search. Evaluated under a process-safety benchmark and Safe Arrival Rate (SAR) metric across five tasks, RTS improves SAR over Direct by 12.67--41.67 percentage points on navigation and articulated control and +2.08/+4.17 pp on Cube/PushT boundary cohorts, maintaining 100% action identity with every-step search while cutting controller time by 17.71%--70.41% across 1,968 paired trajectories.

articles.title: The Obsolescence of High-Level Code: Agentic Generation from Semantic Artifacts
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper argues that high-level source code need not remain the primary persistent artifact of software development when AI agents can generate, validate, and regenerate executable implementations from semantic intent. We place this claim in historical context by revisiting application generators, CASE tools, model-driven development, and platforms such as GeneXus, where developers already maintained higher-level representations from which code and other artifacts were derived. We propose a unifying view in which generation is the fundamental operation: given a semantic specification S = (R, C, I, T, O), maintained as the semantic authority, an agent produces a generated executable artifact A. Functional requirements, contracts, and interfaces are assessed as semantic obligations, while tests and operational objectives are assessed by an explicit external oracle V(A, S). We operationalize this framework through an experiment in independent generation: multiple LLVM artifacts are generated directly from one frozen semantic authority and evaluated by the same external oracle. The experiment reports regeneration coherence on an evaluated domain, not a proof of absolute correctness. It provides initial evidence that independently generated executable artifacts can produce the same observable outcomes under a common semantic authority and external oracle. We conclude by discussing reproducibility, specification-centered evolution, and the implications of treating implementation representation as a deployment choice rather than the primary maintained artifact.

articles.title: StatePortal: Agentic Checkpoint Synthesis for Testing Deep States in Interactive Software
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models have reduced the effort to generate code for interactive software with graphical user interfaces (GUIs). For such software, a key testing bottleneck is reaching a deep state, one that requires a long interaction history. The cost of reaching it recurs across commits, and the GUI automation that could amortize it assumes a DOM or accessibility tree that self-rendered engines do not expose. We introduce StatePortal, an agent that synthesizes a checkpoint, an artifact that restores that state and can be versioned and replayed, from a natural-language functional test case and read-only access to the target's source code. The checkpoint is restored through a per-application hook that an onboarding agent binds or synthesizes once without hand-written hook code. Because a checkpoint can satisfy state checks while rendering incorrectly, checkpoints are scored by hybrid programmatic-state and visual evaluation: acceptance requires both a programmatic-state oracle and a visual oracle to pass. We calibrate the visual oracle against a blinded cross-VLM reference. We release DeepStateBench, 61 deep-state tasks across 10 interactive applications that span five language families and six rendering stacks, with source sizes from 874 to 7.2M lines. Across three registered models, a GUI agent seeded with synthesized checkpoints completes 10.4% of trials, compared with 0% without seeding under the same pixel action space, while StatePortal, which also delivers the target action through the hook, completes 27.5%. Over 1,361 replays of 112 checkpoints, 98.90% reproduce the original verdict with zero model calls, and the hybrid oracle detects 96.25% (77/80) of controlled visual faults invisible to programmatic-state checks alone. We open-source our code at https://github.com/pzy2000/State_Portal and website at https://stateportal.mineyosemite.chatgpt.site

articles.title: Ephyra: A Property-Based Testing Framework for the LLM Era
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents now write a growing share of software tests; however, property-based testing (PBT) libraries are designed with historical considerations. We present Ephyra, a PBT library in Rust built on three concepts: customizability, observability and generator synthesis. Ephyra lets users compose their own testing loops from generation, mutation and shrinking, and synthesize these components to satisfy functional predicates. Applying Ephyra to 14 open source systems, we have found 349 bugs and reported 300 of them, in database management systems (SQLite, Turso, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, DataFusion), the verified policy engine (Cedar), the SQL equivalence prover (QED), the URL parser used in Node.js (ada-url), reimplementations of existing open source systems in Rust (coreutils, brush, gitoxide), and compilers (binaryen, OCaml, and OxCaml).

articles.title: NullTok: empirical-null token selection for training-free long video understanding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long video understanding remains a daunting challenge for existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs), mainly due to the large number of visual tokens accumulated in long videos. Currently, frame selection and token selection are two main paradigms for addressing this issue, both aiming to select relevant visual information to form a compact input for MLLMs. A natural approach combines these two paradigms by selecting frames before pruning tokens, but noisy frame-level relevance estimates can cause irreversible evidence loss. In this paper, we study this problem from the perspective of assessing the spatiotemporal distribution of query-specific evidence and propose a novel and training-free approach termed NULLTOK. For every patch across all frames, we construct an empirical-null distribution from 64 group-matched irrelevant control queries, capturing the scores expected in the absence of target-specific evidence. Target affinities are calibrated against these same-position references into right-tail Monte Carlo p-values, which are discrete super-uniform under a conditional exchangeability assumption. Calibrated screening and a high-recall semantic guard produce candidate tokens for deterministic visual deduplication and joint spatiotemporal budget allocation. To validate NullTok, we apply it to two representative MLLMs and conduct extensive experiments on a set of video benchmarks. The experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness under a bounded visual token budget. For example, it achieves 65.81% and 68.85% on Video-MME using frozen LLaVA-Video-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B backbones, respectively, at a cap of 64 full-frame equivalents (FFE), without subtitles or audio. These results outperform all evaluated baselines on Video-MME under the same budget for both backbones. Code is available at https://github.com/potato-kitty/NullTok.

articles.title: Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In latent diffusion models, expanding the latent dimension of variational autoencoders (VAEs) is essential to push the upper bound of reconstruction quality. However, without explicit structural constraints, such unregularized expansion easily yields a rugged and ill-conditioned latent manifold, causing generated latents to drift off the manifold during generation (i.e., off-manifold problem). Recent works smooth this manifold by using external foundation models (e.g., DINOv2) as a topological regularizer. However, we argue that tying the latent space to frozen external priors inherently restricts generalization: bound by their pre-training distributions and semantic biases, they may fail to capture faithful visual details on out-of-distribution domains. Observing that low-dimensional latents naturally form a smoother, generation-friendly manifold, we propose dual-manifold VAE (DM-VAE) to leverage internal representations as a topological regularizer. Specifically, DM-VAE pairs a high-dimensional reconstructive branch with a low-dimensional branch that extracts a clean topological skeleton, anchoring the high-dimensional manifold to this smooth subspace. Building upon this framework, we further introduce topological representation alignment (TRA) to supervise intermediate generator features during training, and internal guidance with topological skeleton (IG_TS) to guide structural components while preserving high-frequency details at inference. On ImageNet-1K (256x256), our foundation-model-free DM-VAE achieves a state-of-the-art rFID of 0.12 and a generation FID50K of 1.28 (w/o CFG) and 1.20 (w/CFG), and further reaches 1.11 when orthogonally combined with DINOv2.

articles.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.24025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. Code validates the contract, and a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and writes the tool call itself. Provided the validation and dispatch code is correct, every executed call is written by the trusted model, the planner's influence on a call is confined to a contract logged before it, and the trusted side decides how much of a request to carry out. We compare contracts with two reviewers of planner-written commands: one sees only the user's words and the command, the information boundary of a reasoning-blind permission classifier, and one also sees the planner's goal and a checked quotation. With gpt-6.1-terra as planner and GLM-5.3-Flash as the trusted model on three AmPermBench task families, every object changed under contracts is named in the goal of the contract that produced the change; under review the planner names objects in its commands and rarely in its goals. When the planner adds work the user never asked for, contracts complete the user's task in 27/30 runs and the intent-visible reviewer in 16/30, because a reviewer can only refuse a whole command. Contracts do not reduce unauthorized actions. They are indistinguishable from blind review, and once the benchmark's environment terms are clarified, every condition that changes state hits a wrong target in 40-49% of those runs. That error is the planner's choice of objects for an ambiguous reference, which no trusted model here can see the environment to check; telling the executor to decline when unsure does not change it. We evaluate benign over-reach with one pair of models, not adversarial planners. We release the plugin and run records.

articles.title: Isolation, Purification, and Characterization of Solvent-Tolerant Lipase from Geobacillus stearothermophilus PS11
articles.abstract: An organic solvent-stable lipase secreted by Geobacillus stearothermophilus PS11, a solvent-tolerant strain, was purified and characterised. Purification raised the specific activity 8.04-fold, with 22.6% of the activity recovered. The purified enzyme had a molecular weight of roughly 27.5 kDa. It held its activity well in the presence of organic solvents such as toluene, benzene, propanol and methanol, retaining 745 EU/ml even after 72 h of incubation. Activity peaked at 764 EU/ml at 50°C and pH 10.0, and the enzyme remained stable across a broad temperature range of 10°C to 60°C. Given this tolerance to solvents, heat and alkaline conditions, the lipase shows promise as a useful biocatalyst for the biodiesel industry.

articles.title: Conceptual design and first-order performance assessment of a tri-source hybrid (solar– hydrogen–battery) long-endurance UAV for extreme climates
articles.abstract: Small long-endurance unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for hot-desert and polar operation face conflicting requirements: solar power is intermittent, hydrogen fuel cells need clean, temperature-conditioned air, and dust, sand, rain, and icing threaten every air-breathing subsystem. This paper presents the conceptual design of Eastern Hornet, a 60 kg tri-source hybrid UAV that combines a photovoltaic array covering 85% of the wing area, an air-cooled proton-exchange-membrane fuel cell, and a lithium-ion buffer battery on a common DC bus. The fuel cell is fed by a ram-air intake on the lower wing surface near the root, which does not shade the solar array and contains a passive inertial particle separator with electrothermal anti-icing. A common battery-powered heating subsystem supports fuel-cell cold start and sensor thermal management over a design operating range of − 50°C to + 50°C. First-order sizing gives a wing area of 7.5 m², an aspect ratio of 14 and a span of 10.25 m. A low-fidelity aerodynamic assessment gives a zero-lift drag coefficient of 0.021–0.028, cruise and loiter electrical power of 1.70–2.27 kW and 0.77–0.98 kW, and hydrogen-only endurance of 5.3–7.1 h and 12.2–15.6 h, bracketing the design estimates. Two-dimensional RANS simulations confirm the section lift data and give exit flow angles of 23–46° and loss coefficients of 0.03–0.07 for separator vane angles of 30–60°; a three-dimensional RANS simulation gives a lift-curve slope of 5.6 per radian, a loiter angle of attack of about 2.0° and, with the baseline internal arrangement, a static margin of about 14%.

articles.title: Understanding Hydrogeological Connectivity: Linking Groundwater Processes to Environmental Consequences
articles.abstract: Hydrogeological connectivity governs the movement of groundwater, hydraulic signals, dissolved constituents, and environmental pressures through subsurface systems. Although connectivity is central to groundwater assessment, it is commonly interpreted only as hydraulic communication between locations. This review synthesises the broader concept of connectivity and distinguishes four interrelated dimensions: structural, hydraulic, transport, and environmental connectivity. A connectivity-based framework is proposed linking sources, pathways, receptors, and environmental consequences across multiple spatial and temporal scales. The review examines the geological, hydraulic, hydrological, and environmental controls that influence connectivity and evaluates methods used for its assessment, including hydrogeological characterisation, tracer studies, groundwater monitoring, modelling, and particle tracking. The analysis shows that hydraulic connectivity alone is insufficient for assessing environmental risk because contaminant migration and environmental consequences depend on transport processes, travel times, and receptor vulnerability. Connectivity is presented as a unifying framework for understanding groundwater flow, recharge, groundwater recovery, groundwater-surface water interaction, contaminant transport, ecosystem response, and environmental management. Incorporating connectivity into groundwater investigations can improve environmental assessments, water-resource management, mine-closure planning, and climate-resilience strategies.

articles.title: Cutting Power, Surface Roughness and Sound Pressure in Circular Saw Ripsawing of Radiata Pine Plywood
articles.abstract: Direct measurement of cutting power and surface roughness is often impractical in plywood production. This study evaluated whether mean-square sound pressure could serve as a low-cost indicator of cutting power and roughness in plywood ripsawing. Two circular saw blade configurations (Saw A, 80 teeth; Saw B, 48 teeth) were tested on radiata pine plywood of three thicknesses (12, 15, 18 mm) at three feed speeds (7.5–11.8 m/min), giving 18 conditions with cutting power, roughness (Ra, Rz) and sound pressure recorded. Cutting power was associated with blade configuration, feed speed and panel thickness, with a blade × thickness interaction (R² = 0.98; leave-one-out Q² = 0.96, repeating the choice of the interaction within each fold); thickness was confounded with panel, and modulus of elasticity did not explain variation (p = 0.30). Roughness did not differ between blades; only panel thickness was significant (p < 0.03). Sound pressure discriminated blade configuration (p < 0.001) but, pooled across blades, not thickness or feed speed. Its overall correlation with cutting power (r = 0.89) reflected separate blade clusters: within Saw A it was strong (r = 0.81), whereas within Saw B none was detected (r = − 0.35; n = 9). Sound pressure was not correlated with roughness, overall (|r| < 0.06; n = 18) or within each blade (|r| < 0.49, p > 0.18; n = 9). An exploratory single-predictor model estimated cutting power moderately within Saw A (Q² = 0.54) but failed within Saw B (Q² = −2.8); general use requires validation.

articles.title: A fractional-order Eulerian dispersion model with a single fractional order: formulation and evaluation against five tracer data sets
articles.abstract: An Eulerian dispersion model for the planetary boundary layer is presented in which the vertical turbulent flux is written with a Caputo fractional derivative and, in three dimensions, the lateral flux with a symmetric Riesz operator. Dimensional consistency is provided by the vertical Lagrangian length scale of the turbulence, so that a single fractional order, common to all experiments, is the only quantity selected with reference to concentration data; all other parameterisations keep their published constants. The model, solved with a conservative finite-difference scheme, is evaluated against five tracer data sets (Copenhagen, convective and stable Prairie Grass, Hanford 83 and Kincaid) with statistical indices, bootstrap confidence intervals and the results of established models. In the classical limit the model performs at the level of those models. With a fractional order of 0.91 the fraction of predictions within a factor of two rises from 0.72 to 0.94 in convective Prairie Grass. A constant rescaling of the classical diffusivity reproduces this gain only in part and does not remove the growth of the residuals with distance. Copenhagen and Hanford 83 are statistically unchanged, while stable Prairie Grass and Kincaid deteriorate. The benefit is therefore restricted to surface releases in convective conditions.

articles.title: Effects of 0.15% Sodium Hyaluronate and 0.5% Sodium Carboxymethylcellulose Eye Drops on Schirmer Tear Test I Values in Shih Tzu Dogs During Bathing
articles.abstract: Routine bathing is an essential component of canine grooming but may expose the ocular surface to chemical, thermal, and mechanical stimuli capable of disrupting tear film homeostasis. This study evaluated the effects of prophylactic administration of eye drops containing 0.15% sodium hyaluronate or 0.5% sodium carboxymethylcellulose on aqueous tear production in Shih Tzu dogs undergoing routine bathing and drying. Forty clinically healthy Shih Tzu dogs were randomly allocated into four groups (n = 10): 0.15% sodium hyaluronate, 0.5% sodium carboxymethylcellulose, sterile saline solution (placebo), and an untreated control. Tear production was assessed using the Schirmer tear test I (STT-I) immediately before treatment and immediately after bathing. Data were analyzed using the Shapiro–Wilk test, paired t-test, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). Mean STT-I values increased after bathing in all experimental groups. However, statistically significant increases were observed only in dogs receiving sodium hyaluronate (P = 0.0092) and sodium carboxymethylcellulose (P = 0.0396), whereas no significant changes were detected in the placebo (P = 0.1264) or untreated control group (P = 0.1126). No significant differences were observed among groups after bathing (ANOVA, P = 0.134). These findings indicate that prophylactic ocular lubrication with sodium hyaluronate or sodium carboxymethylcellulose was associated with significant within-group increases in aqueous tear production following bathing, without evidence of superiority over placebo or no treatment. Further studies incorporating complementary ocular surface assessments are needed to determine whether prophylactic lubrication provides protective benefits during routine grooming.

articles.title: Surface-mediated reduction of Cr(VI) on aged polyamide microplastics: Leaching behavior and interaction mechanisms
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) can interact with toxic heavy metals, thereby altering their environmental behavior and ecological effects. This study investigated the adsorption–transformation and leaching behavior of Cr(VI) by UV-aged polyamide microplastics (UV-PA) under the combined effects of light irradiation and dissolved oxygen (DO). SEM-EDS and XPS analyses demonstrated that photo-oxidative conditions increased the surface roughness of UV-PA, promoted amide bond cleavage, and generated more oxygen-containing functional groups, thereby enhancing Cr(VI) adsorption. CV, EIS, pH, and ORP analyses further confirmed that UV-PA possessed Cr(VI) reduction capability, with the highest electron transfer efficiency observed under UV+aerobic conditions. Probe compound experiments revealed that the generation of O was maximized under these conditions, effectively promoting Cr(VI) reduction. In the presence of Cr(VI), dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and total nitrogen (TN) concentrations increased to 15 mg/L and 6 mg/L, respectively, indicating that Cr(VI) accelerated the leaching of UV-PA. EEM-PARAFAC analysis showed that the leachates were mainly composed of protein-like and humic-like substances, while NO was detected only in Cr(VI)-containing systems. LC–MS results further indicated that Cr(VI) could selectively cleave PA molecular chains and promote the formation of specific organic compounds. These findings provide new insights into the interaction mechanisms and environmental behavior of combined microplastic–heavy metal pollution systems.

articles.title: Bridging policy and practice in public e-recruitment: a workflow-integrated speech framework for people with visual impairments
articles.abstract: Public e-recruitment platforms increasingly mediate government employment, yet candidates with visual impairments often cannot complete application and interview workflows independently when interfaces are visual, text-intensive, and time-bound. This study examined the policy-to-practice gap in Tanzania's Public Service Recruitment Secretariat (PSRS), using its Online Aptitude Test System (OATS). Analysis identified architectural, interaction and systemic barriers that compromise privacy and increase dependence on third-party assistance. Using Design Science Research, the study developed a workflow-integrated speech framework as a browser-based accessibility layer for existing systems, combining structured workflow definitions with speech recognition, synthesis, validation, read-back confirmation, localisation and error recovery. User Acceptance Testing with twenty visually impaired participants produced one hundred task attempts, all completed independently without third-party assistance despite twenty-two minor errors and eight non-blocking incidents. Despite no control condition, the results offer preliminary evidence that workflow-aware design can translate accessibility policy into practical, privacy-preserving interaction support, and they extend the design-actuality gap by identifying the workflow as the operative unit for high-stakes public services.

articles.title: The Poverty Cost of Greenhouse Gas Emissions
articles.abstract: Economic growth reduces current poverty but increases greenhouse gas emissions, which will increase poverty in the future. To quantify the combined effect of these two mechanisms, we introduce emissions-adjusted poverty, a new measure that sums a country’s poverty today with the future global poverty that the country’s emissions will create in the future. The key parameter of this measure is a human-centric analogue to the social cost of carbon, quantifying how current emissions increase future global poverty. We estimate that each kiloton of carbon dioxide emitted today adds two person-years of extreme poverty globally by 2100. Despite large uncertainties, we identify two robust insights. For poor countries, poverty reduction from economic growth outweighs future global poverty added from the emissions associated with this growth, even with historical carbon intensities. Conversely, for many rich countries, the climate-related poverty cost of growth outweighs the benefits unless the carbon intensity of growth falls.

articles.title: Exact Spin Elimination for Quadratic and k-Local Ising Optimization
articles.abstract: Ising solvers have a finite spin budget. Quadratization uses auxiliary spins to replace higher-order interactions by pairwise ones. We show that removing spins while allowing more complex interactions can fit larger problems within the same spin budget and improve optimization. Walsh elimination minimizes over one spin at a time, writes the resulting interaction as a sum of spin products in the Walsh basis, and stores a rule for recovering the removed spin. Explicit resource limits control which eliminations are accepted. In a held-out test with the protocol frozen before instance generation and one annealing schedule shared by both formulations, mean observed success rises from 10.4% to 97.5% on sparse quadratic spin glasses and from 16.9% to 87.5% on three-body problems. Observed success increases on every instance with a verified reference minimum, and pooled time-to-solution estimates decrease by factors of about 34 and 11, respectively, with preprocessing included. For zero-field pairwise models on connected simple cubic graphs with more than four vertices, we prove that a fixed spin budget accommodates 50% larger inputs while retaining pairwise interactions, zero fields, residual degree at most six, and no increase in coupling count. These results establish exact spin elimination as a controlled trade between active-spin capacity and interaction complexity.

articles.title: Entangled Photons, Gravitational Records, and Correlated Kerr Horizon-Area Changes
articles.abstract: We examine how local gravitational interactions redistribute information initially encoded in the paths of an entangled photon pair. A controlled-recoil model relates the surviving two-photon coherence to the overlap of the alternative mass records. Replacing the masses by rotating black holes gives a distinct area-response problem: the Kerr first law predicts unequal horizon-area increments for equal-energy deposits with opposite axial angular momenta. In a symmetric two-hole geometry the joint alternatives exchange these increments, producing anticorrelated area responses with a common total. An effective capture map connects the two alternatives to conditional absorption amplitudes and external records. For identical local responses, unequal prograde and retrograde capture efficiencies do not unbalance the postselected joint branches; the surviving two-hole coherence depends on the distinguishability of the remaining records. We derive the area-outcome covariance and an operationally motivated phase-sensitive witness, showing why area correlations alone cannot distinguish a coherent state from a diagonal mixture. The calculation combines a classical Kerr benchmark with an explicitly conditional quantum model; the absorption amplitudes and physical access to the proposed phase observable remain dynamical questions.

articles.title: Optical connectivity governs the loss cost of multiphoton parity correlations
articles.abstract: Pairwise Hong-Ou-Mandel overlaps and purities determine the cyclic interference invariants of qubit-encoded photons up to a common complex conjugation, which mirrors their configuration. We determine how many photons must survive loss to read correlations between mirror labels under restricted optical connections. Each of d groups in a separable source carries such a label, for example a polarization handedness or a chirp sign, redrawn every shot; the labels' only correlation is the parity bias h. If the label-dependent parts of the states commute between groups within each set, every measurement that acts separately on prescribed readout sets without resolving internal states needs at least d + 2o survivors, where o counts sets containing an odd number of groups. This holds in any finite internal dimension, including mixed states. Beam splitters on disjoint group pairs, with a tritter on the remaining group of each odd set, attain this minimum, r* = d + 2o, when their signals are nonzero. For fixed source, accuracy and confidence, the number of shots scales as Θ(η⁽−r*⁾) with transmission η. A fixed source of six eight-photon groups needs 18 survivors with separate readout and 6 with paired or joint readout. For a known three-photon configuration mixed with its conjugate, we derive the external-state quantum Fisher information for |h| < 1 and the exact condition for tritter charge counting to attain it. The thresholds identify which optical connections improve the loss exponent.

articles.title: An Open Nonequilibrium Effective Quantum Field Formulation of the Corneal High Entropy-Production Zone
articles.abstract: The cornea maintains transparency through nonequilibrium regulation of hydration, solute transport, and collagen organization. The High Entropy-Production Zone (HEZ) hypothesis proposes that spatially organized dissipation in the anterior stroma may couple microscopic relaxation to useful gradient-driven transport. We reformulated this hypothesis as a spatially resolved open nonequilibrium effective quantum field theory linking a coarse-grained hydration/proton collective field and collagen order with classical solute and temperature variables. Local Lindblad channels and Schwinger–Keldysh kernels provided a formal description of dissipation, response, fluctuations, and correlations, while Marangoni-like transport coupling remained phenomenological. The conceptual HEZ was represented as an anteriorly biased, quasi-two-dimensional dissipative field without a fixed anatomical depth. We distinguished Spohn-type relative-entropy relaxation from physical entropy production and introduced a classical flux–affinity entropy-production expression, a connected density-correlation observable, and prospective transport-efficiency measures, including the Endothelial/HEZ Transport Index (EHTI) and a localization-dependent gain functional. In illustrative local-Markovian calculations using a prescribed Gaussian reference profile, increased damping produced broader spectral linewidths and shorter first-order field-amplitude correlation times.
