Increasing the number of ECAP cycles enhances the ductility of the UFG steel at 750-900C. Increasing the ECAP temperature results in a simultaneous decrease in ductility and flow stress. Heterostructured steel exhibits minimal values of the activation energy of SP deformation. Increasing the number of ECAP cycles and increasing the ECAP temperature lead to an increase in the activation energy of SP deformation.

articles.title: Remark on internal relaxation in large number qubit systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21681v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a time tc of calculation in an N qubit quantum computer that is much shorter than the intrinsic Heisenberg time t_H, t_cll t_H, the dynamics of the system is effectively irreversible and the couplings between the qubits give rise to a relaxation time scale τᵣ. If t_Hgg t_c >sim τᵣ one looses quantum coherence exponentially fast. Since t_H scales exponentially with N there is a threshold N_c such that for Ngg N_c one must be aware of possible intrinsic relaxation during calculation. As an order of magnitude estimation we find N_capprox ln(τᵣ/T) where T is a typical system specific oscillation time of a single qubit. τᵣ can be estimated as the typical inverse transition rate between two parts of the system, one of which is treated as an environment of the other.

articles.title: Cyclic Boson Stars with Quantum Vortex Molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We find a new type of stationary boson star with cyclic rotational symmetry in the minimal model of complex scalar field coupled to gravity. Unlike conventional axisymmetric spinning boson stars, these configurations can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle in units of the reduced Planck constant, revealing a new way for boson stars to carry angular momentum. We identify the vortex assemblies within these stars as self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules, in which gravity supports a stationary vortex arrangement despite internal circulation. These structures provide a relativistic realization of quantum vortex molecules studied in condensates and motivate possible laboratory analogues.

articles.title: Simple Models of Thermal Order in 2+1 Dimensions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21842v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Heating need not destroy order. We show that it persists to arbitrarily high temperatures in simple quantum field theories in 2+1 spacetime dimensions. In a mathbb Z₂×mathbb Z₂ model of two real scalar fields, a sufficiently negative mixed quartic coupling drives one field to condense, spontaneously breaking its mathbb Z₂ symmetry. When coupled to massless Dirac fermions through a Yukawa interaction, this condensate generates a fermion mass, thereby spontaneously breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries. We extend this construction to a mathbb Z₂× O(n) scalar model, in which the Mermin-Wagner theorem precludes spontaneous breaking of the continuous O(n) symmetry at finite temperatures. Nevertheless, for n=2, a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless superfluid phase persists to arbitrarily high temperatures. In this phase, spatial correlations decay algebraically, with an exponent that approaches zero as the temperature increases. For n≥ 3, we uncover a further unexpected feature of these models: the characteristic size of ordered domains grows asymptotically with temperature, revealing an unusual enhancement of spatial correlations upon heating. We establish our results using a controlled high-temperature expansion, with selected findings corroborated by numerical functional renormalization group analysis. The simplicity of the field content in these models provides a promising starting point for exploring experimental realizations of persistent thermal order in thin-film materials.

articles.title: Bandwidth-tunable thermal emitter via dynamic resonator coupling and loss
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21934v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate a dynamically tunable omnidirectional thermal emitter that can be switched from a narrowband emission state to a broadband state. The structure is a metal-backed multilayer with subwavelength thickness across the mid-infrared, which forms an angle-insensitive (up to 60deg) optical cavity with one input port. We used an ultrathin VO2 layer to dynamically switch the coupling and loss coefficients of this optical cavity, resulting in narrowband emission from the vibrational mode of a polar dielectric layer that is part of the multilayer stack when the VO2 is in its insulating phase, and broadband emission from a nearly impedance-matched cavity when the VO2 is switched to its lossy metallic phase. We fabricated the structure around a free-standing silicon membrane and integrated it onto a printed circuit board (PCB), which enabled electrical switching of the emitter at the ten-to-hundred millisecond scale, and can be used for free-space identification, tagging, or communication.

articles.title: Strong eigenstate thermalization in Singer-cycle Clifford circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) provides a central framework for understanding thermalization in isolated quantum systems. Recently, the infinite-temperature ETH has been established for almost all Floquet eigenstates in linear feedback shift register quantum circuits. Here we introduce brickwork Clifford circuits with L qubits where the induced transformation of Pauli operators is represented by an irreducible symplectic matrix over the finite field mathbb F₂ of the maximal order 2^L+1, known as a Singer cycle. For these Singer-cycle Clifford circuits, we prove a strong version of ETH: all Floquet eigenstates are thermal at infinite temperature without exceptions. We derive uniform bounds on both diagonal deviations from thermal expectation values and off-diagonal matrix elements of arbitrary observables supported on a fixed number of sites. The results indicate that long-time averages of observables approach the infinite-temperature values in the thermodynamic limit for arbitrary initial states. We also show that the temporal fluctuation of expectation values of observables is exponentially suppressed in the thermodynamic limit, implying that each observable remains close to the infinite-temperature value for almost all times.

articles.title: Quantum Codes for Distributed Quantum Fault Sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22530v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Targeted recovery in modular quantum processors requires identifying the component affected by a fault. Independent qubits can monitor faults through repeated preparation and measurement. Bell-pair probes improve the guaranteed correct-site probability for unknown local channels, but require partners kept away from the fault. Can entanglement among exposed probes supply this advantage without protected storage? We establish a quantum-code criterion for optimal distributed fault sensing of one unknown local qubit channel with strength in a prescribed positive range. For one interrogation with zero false alarms and no background noise, suitable code states attain the optimal worst-case correct-site probability, improving on independent probes by 50% with every qubit exposed. Exact attainment is equivalent to mutually orthogonal input and single-qubit Pauli error subspaces. Pairwise entanglement gives no improvement, and entanglement depth at most four cannot exceed 95.54% of the optimum without protected ancillas. Approaching the optimum without protected ancillas also requires a number of probes proportional to the array size to participate in larger entangled factors. For a persistent fault under memoryless depolarizing background of fixed strength 0 < eta < 1, independent probes already attain the optimal logarithmic interrogation scaling at fixed success between zero and one and a positive false-alarm budget. In three 1000-site comparisons with specified readouts, an encoded-probe protocol certifies fewer interrogations than independent probes and only one more than optimally decoded ideal Bell pairs, while storing no protected qubits.

articles.title: Predicting Quantum Mpemba Effects from Quantum Speed Limits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22547v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can anomalous Quantum Mpemba Effects be anticipated before a system comes close to its stationary state? We employ Quantum Speed Limits as geometric indicators of Quantum Mpemba Effects, arguing that Mpemba physics is already imprinted in speed limits by benchmarking dissipative qubits and open spin chains. Our results show that short-time speed limits can predict Quantum Mpemba Effects at low cost and with reasonable precision over broad parameter regimes. This predictive power implies a useful application of speed limits for open many-body quantum systems.

articles.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22615v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincaré algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.

articles.title: What Do LLMs Use to Judge Synthesis Recipes? An Experimental Analysis on 240 Solid-State Syntheses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inorganic materials discovery is increasingly limited by synthesis rather than by material design. Large language models (LLMs) are being adopted to propose synthesis conditions with little experimental evidence of their capabilities and biases. Here, we carry out an experimental synthesis benchmark of 240 experiments across eight known and unknown inorganic oxides and subsequently evaluate an LLM as a zero-shot ranker over fixed banks of solid-state synthesis recipes. For each pair of recipes for the same oxide target, `GPT-5.6-Sol` selects the recipe expected to yield higher target-phase purity. We aggregate these pairwise preferences using a regularized Bradley-Terry model to obtain a ranked list of synthesis recipes for a given target material. By comparison with the actual purity, obtained through X-ray diffraction, we measure `GPT-5.6-Sol`'s performance as a zero-shot ranker (0.72 pairwise accuracy). By selective removal of the information exposed to the model during this ranking, we conclude that ranking is driven predominantly by thermal features, with reaction chemistry modulating the effect. Ranking accuracy tracks the purity-temperature correlation by target (Spearman ρ = 0.91), (p = 0.002), and on the six thermally-driven targets withholding all chemical identity hardly impacts performance (0.68) compared to withholding temperature (0.56). Ranking performance was higher on known than unknown targets, but the group-level difference was not statistically conclusive. The methodological choices highlight the need for more experimentally validated synthesis benchmarks and position LLMs as a thermally informed prior.

articles.title: Thermal and Acoustic Measurements of Hybrid Bonding Stacks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermal and structural characterizations of hybrid bonding structures are essential for understanding heat transport in three-dimensional integrated circuits (3D-ICs). In this work, we investigate the effective thermal conductivity of the Cu/dielectric HB layer using time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) combined with picosecond ultrasonic technique. Shallow-angle polishing enabled depth-resolved thermal measurements by exposing hybrid bonding layers with different remaining thicknesses, while acoustic echoes were used to identify buried interfaces and determine the thickness. The distinct waveform of the bonding interface echo compared with the Cu/dielectric interface echo suggests that its acoustic response may also reflect the interfacial bonding conditions. The extracted thermal conductivity ranges from 1.14 to 1.75 Wm-1K-1 for the bottom pad layer and from 1.76 to 4.34 Wm-1K-1 for the top pad layer. The difference in thermal conductivity is consistent with the different Cu area fractions of the two layers. Furthermore, the thermal conductivity of the top pad layer increases significantly with the remaining thickness, possibly due to the thermal boundary resistance at the bonding interface, low thermal conductivity of SiCN interlayer, and increased electron scattering in thin Cu structures. Our work demonstrates a practical approach to investigate the thermal properties of buried hybrid bonding layers, providing experimental data for thermal design and modeling of 3D-ICs.

articles.title: W-SLDA Toolkit: A simulation platform for ultracold Fermi gases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.08982v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the W-SLDA Toolkit, a general-purpose software package for simulating ultracold Fermi gases within the framework of density functional theory and its time-dependent extensions. The toolkit enables fully microscopic studies of interacting superfluid systems across the BCS-BEC crossover, including spin-imbalanced configurations and arbitrary external geometries. It provides both static and time-dependent solvers capable of describing a broad range of phenomena in one-, two-, and three-dimensional settings. In addition, the toolkit incorporates functionality for solving the standard Bogoliubov-de~Gennes equations for fermions, extending its applicability to other physical systems such as superconductors. The code is implemented in C with GPU acceleration and is optimized for hybrid CPU/GPU execution on modern high-performance computing platforms. It ensures scalability on leadership-class supercomputers, enabling fully three-dimensional simulations with large atom numbers, and allows for direct benchmarks of ultracold-atom experimental setups. Its modular architecture facilitates straightforward extensions, user customization, and seamless interoperability with other scientific software frameworks. Furthermore, an extensive collection of practical usage examples is provided through the integrated reproducibility packs functionality, ensuring transparency and reproducibility of computational results.

articles.title: Suppression of Grain Boundary Nitrogen Degradation by Boron in Superalloys
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30451v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Superalloys enable the hottest sections of jet engines to operate at high temperatures, but environmentally assisted degradation limits their lifetime. In polycrystalline alloys, nitrogen penetrates beneath the protective surface oxides, to produce embrittling grain boundary nitrides. Boron is added in trace amounts to improve grain boundary strength, yet its role, if any, in oxidation-related degradation remains unclear. Here we show that boron segregates to an internal nitride--matrix interface in a Ni/Co-base γ/γprⁱme strengthened superalloy. Both B-free and B-containing alloys develop stratified chromia/alumina scales at 800~cⁱrcC in SI100hour, but the B-free variant produces larger, deeper and more elongated Ti/Nb-rich subsurface grain boundary nitrides. Correlative 4D S/TEM and atom probe tomography identify the particle as a chemically complex B1 nitride and reveal interfacial boron segregation. This shows that trace alloying as an alloy strategy can control damaging internal reaction product precipitation and growth by core-shell segregation.

articles.title: Frustrated Interlayer Coupling Creates a Higher-Order Helical Superstructure in a Twist-Bend Smectic Phase
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18347v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bent liquid-crystalline dimers provide a model system for studying the spontaneous emergence of chirality from achiral molecules. Depending on terminal-chain length, these materials exhibit a competition between heliconical, synclinic, and anticlinic packing tendencies in tilted smectic phases. In short homologues, the tendency to form twist-bend phases dominates, leading to two distinct helical phases: the SmCTB-SH phase, with a helical periodicity of four molecular lengths, and at lower temperatures, a double helical structure - the SmCTB-DH phase, with progressive rotation of the four-layer unit. With increasing terminal chain length, this twist-bend tendency is gradually suppressed, favoring phases with simple synclinic and anticlinic tilt arrangement in successive layers. Remarkably, in the regime where these tendencies become comparable, a new modulated smectic phase, SmCTB-mod develops; a double helical structure in which the internal four-layer unit undergoes a periodic modulation. This additional level of structural organization provides a means of accommodating competing heliconical and synclinic/anticlinic tendencies and produces a characteristic splitting of the resonant x-ray diffraction peaks into four signals symmetrically located around a signal of four-layer periodicity. These results reveal how bent dimers resolve local-packing-mode frustration through complex spontaneous hierarchical structural organization.

articles.title: New Agegraphic Dark Energy in Braneworld Cosmology: A Higher Dimensional Perspective on Dark Energy Evolution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we investigate the new agegraphic dark energy model within the context of braneworld cosmology. A higher dimensional viewpoint on the evolution of dark energy is examined. A combination of cold dark matter and dark energy, is explored within the frameworks of RS-II and DGP brane as the underlying gravitational theories. Both the possibilities involving interaction and non-interaction between dark energy and cold dark matter are investigated. A range of cosmological parameters, including the equation of state parameter, deceleration parameter, and statefinder parameters, are examined. The squared velocity of sound is examined to assess the system's stability. A data analysis based on observations, utilizing contemporary cosmological data and the Markov chain Monte Carlo method, is conducted to constrain the parameter space of the model. Our research suggests that the interplay between higher-dimensional phenomena and agegraphic dark energy provides a theoretically robust and observationally consistent framework for the universe's late-time acceleration.

articles.title: Radiation Response of NbN Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors Under ²¹⁰Po Alpha-Particle Irradiation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) are attractive for space applications because they combine high detection efficiency, low noise, and fast timing, but their radiation tolerance remains less established than that of conventional semiconductor detectors. Here we study NbN SNSPDs exposed to alpha-particle ²¹⁰Po irradiation by combining cryogenic electrical and photon-counting measurements with SRIM and Geant4 radiation-transport calculations. For the estimated fluence corresponding to the 200-hour ²¹⁰Po exposure, the air-inclusive Geant4 calculation predicts an average ionizing dose of 8.49 Mrad in the active NbN layer and a displacement-damage estimate of 5.67 × 10⁻⁷ displacements per atom. Measurements before and after irradiation show no systematic degradation of the superconducting transition, switching current, retrapping current, dark-count behavior, or photon-count response. These results indicate radiation resilience of thin-film NbN SNSPDs under a multi-Mrad alpha-particle exposure and support their use in photon-counting systems for radiation environments.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal programming of shape memory polymers for tunable vibration responses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stimuli-responsive materials offer a promising route to dynamically tailor material behavior, enabling adaptive functionalities in changing environments. However, simultaneously implementing spatial and temporal control in active material systems remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we present a photothermally programmable shape memory polymer (SMP) metamaterial platform that enables dynamic control of elastic wave propagation through reconfigurable spatiotemporal temperature distributions. By projecting user-defined light patterns onto carbon-doped SMP (C-SMP) surfaces, spatial thermomechanical property landscapes are generated, enabling a wide range of elastic wave functionalities, including tunable transmission spectra and programmable vibrational modes. By treating both space and time as design parameters, we access an expanded design space that allows a bulk C-SMP surface to function as a highly adaptive metamaterial platform. This work establishes spatiotemporal property modulation as a powerful framework for adaptive vibration control, tunable phononic systems, and other advanced dynamic applications.

articles.title: Photonic Maxwells demon as an energy resource
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new realization of Maxwells demon for photons and its use as an energy resource. The starting point is a multilayer dielectric mirror that transmits photons within a certain wavelength band but reflects photons at longer wavelengths, followed by a material that irreversibly converts the wavelength. A 3D box constructed from these one-way mirrors is a self-acting Maxwells demon for photons. The first case considered is a one-way mirror for visible photons, converting blue to red as an example. The next case is a one-way mirror that transmits visible light but reflects infrared light, followed by a perfect blackbody. We analyze a 3D box with such mirrors as walls to accumulate and store blackbody radiation. Applications include solar-powered thermal energy and solar-powered thermophotovoltaics. The latter case would combine the 3D box with an ultra-low bandgap semiconductor photovoltaic cell inside. In the ideal optical limit, radiation can enter the box but cannot return through the entrance channel after conversion, allowing repeated photon recycling and nearly complete optical utilization. This can in principle move the conversion efficiency toward the thermodynamic limit for solar-energy conversion, the Landsberg limit of 93.3%.

articles.title: Accelerating auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo with mixed-precision random propagators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an algorithm to propagate auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) wavefunctions in mixed precision. We target NVIDIA Tensor Cores using the TensorFloat-32 (TF32) format. We approximate each full-precision array by a TF32 leading term and a TF32 residual, and each full-precision matrix product by three TF32 products accumulated in full precision. Benchmarks on hydrogen chains show that mixed-precision propagation is consistently faster than double-precision GPU propagation, with an increasing advantage as the system size grows. The resulting local-energy deviations remain small over the propagation windows considered here. These results identify the stochastic two-body propagator as a particularly effective target for reduced precision, while our method allows higher precision to be retained for accuracy-sensitive operations. Hence, our algorithm provides a practical way to speed up AFQMC calculations and demonstrates where reduced precision can be applied without adverse effects on the method's accuracy.

articles.title: Microwave hinge states in an all-dielectric woodpile photonic crystal insulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher-order topological states are studied in a woodpile photonic crystal (PhC) having a large complete photonic bandgap. According to theoretical predictions, we fabricate a three-dimensional all-dielectric PhC with a millimeter-scale lattice period. The structure consists of two distinct lattice types that coincide through a structural displacement, where their interface intersection gives rise to hinge states. Microwave transmission measurements reveal transmission peaks and spatial localization at the intersection, demonstrating the hinge states. Furthermore, we confirm the absence of hinge states at a specific intersection. As theoretically predicted, hinge states emerge at intersections where the localized boundary polarizations are topologically different, whereas they are absent at intersections where the boundary polarizations are equivalent.

articles.title: Intraband vs. interband optical nonlinearities of transparent conducting oxides
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the intraband thermo-optical response to ultrashort intense infra-red illumination of transparent conducting oxides is much stronger than the nonlinear response associated with resonant and non-resonant interband transitions in typical experimental setups. This finding rules out several speculative explanations of recent measurements.

articles.title: Stability of Homochiral Peptides in Capillary Environments: Implications for the Origin of Biological Homochirality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The homochiral proteins in living organisms are rather stable, but they tend to lose their secondary conformations and homochiral order over time. This instability is found in all living organisms, from bacteria to humans. The aging of living organisms, with the destruction of their vital homochiral order, raises the questions about the emergence of homochirality and how the homochiral order in the building molecules was ensured in prebiotic times before life evolved. Based on thermodynamic arguments, we propose that the homochiral order was achieved by a ``Frank-synthesis'' of homochiral peptides from racemic amino acids and in a capillary environment in the vents in the Earth's crust, perhaps at crystalline chiral surfaces, and that the peptides are stable over long times in such an environment. The hypothesis can be confirmed by experimental analysis of the stability of the secondary structures in proteins as a function of water activity and in a capillary environment.

articles.title: Dual-Comb Spectrometry Enabled by Gain-Assisted Electro-Optic Fiber Ring Resonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broadband dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) with widely tunable repetition rates and simplified frequency stabilization is desirable for diverse sensing applications. Here, we demonstrate DCS using two gain-assisted fiber ring resonators that share a continuous-wave (CW) laser and incorporate intracavity electro-optic (EO) phase modulation. Intracavity gain compensates for round-trip losses, sustaining repeated phase modulation and enabling flat-top comb spectra with a 20-dB bandwidth exceeding 1.8 THz. Harmonic-order selection provides widely tunable repetition rates from approximately 5 to 0.2 GHz without substantially compromising the spectral bandwidth. The comb phase noise closely follows that of the radio-frequency (RF) drive at low offset frequencies. Without active frequency stabilization, the two combs exhibit an instrument-limited beat-note linewidth of 2 Hz, indicating high mutual coherence. The generated dual combs enable high-speed DCS at the single-interferogram rate, providing a platform for dynamic spectroscopic measurements. This all-fiber architecture, together with its simplified operation, offers a promising route towards compact and readily integrable dual-comb instruments.

articles.title: Quantum differential interference contrast microscope
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical sensing and imaging of transparent unstained biological and material specimen makes use of optical interference to translate phase shifts into intensity measurements, that are readily available in the optical domain. This is the case of Differential Interference Contrast (DIC) microscopes. However, environmental disturbances such as acoustic vibrations, air currents, temperature shifts, and mechanical drifts cause random phase noise that degrades the precision attainable in the estimation of the unknown phase shift. Although there are tools to compensate for these random phase drifts, such using common path interference techniques or phase stabilization systems, these are not always an option and its introduction is generally at the expense of device simplicity and robustness. Here we introduce a quantum version of Differential Interference Contrast microscopy (qDIC), that makes use of quantum interference for polarization analysis. When compared with standard schemes that make use of coherent light, our approach shows that the transfer of classical DIC microscopy into the quantum domain offers a route towards quantum-enhanced resilience to environmental disturbances, allowing the enhancement of phase sensitivity without sacrificing the simplicity and robustness of the optical setup.

articles.title: A variational multiscale rotational pressure-correction method for incompressible flows with open boundaries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotational pressure correction improves pressure accuracy near open boundaries in incompressible flow simulations, but equal-order finite element discretizations can still develop spurious pressure oscillations. We develop a residual-based variational multiscale rotational pressure-correction scheme (RPCS-VMS) that stabilizes both the pressure-increment and pressure-recovery equations. By constructing stage-specific momentum residuals using a common intermediate-velocity acceleration, the scheme retains four sequential linear solves per time step. For a reduced BDF1 Oseen model with frozen stabilization coefficients, we establish augmented-energy decay and a conditional bound on the pressure gradient. Manufactured-solution tests demonstrate suppression of pressure oscillations at small time steps and reduced near-boundary pressure errors. With (P₁/P₁) and (Q₁/Q₁) elements, the observed spatial (L²) convergence rates are 2 for velocity and approximately (1.5) for pressure, while first- and second-order backward differentiation formulas attain their expected temporal orders. Branched-pipe and two- and three-dimensional cylinder benchmarks assess outlet flow partitioning, transient forces, and pressure differences, with results agreeing closely with reference solutions. In the three-dimensional cylinder test, RPCS-VMS achieves a 2.41-fold wall-time speedup over the tested monolithic VMS solver.

articles.title: A regime dependent parameterization of the refractive-index structure parameter Cₙ²
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vertical profiles of the refractive-index (RI) structure parameter, Cₙ², are required in atmospheric-optics calculations. The Hufnagel--Valley (HV) model is a useful reference profile and it is widely used however, it is difficult to say that it produces consistent results at the observed altitude, magnitude, and thickness of all turbulent layers and it can diverge from realistic measurements in particular height ranges, sites, and stability regimes. This study develops a regime-dependent RI structure parameter considering meteorological conditions and, more importantly, it provides a structure that can be calibrated against measured Cₙ² throughout the surface layer (SL), atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), and free atmosphere. The formulation combines SL including distinct unstable, near-neutral, and stable limits; convective ABL; and free-atmospheric turbulence when kinetic-energy and temperature-variance dissipation rates are available. The Cₙ² is formed by weighting the contribution of different layers. We use representative, physically plausible meteorological profiles to examine the model's limiting behavior, transitions between atmospheric regimes, continuity, sensitivity to its parameters, and propagation-related differences from the HV 5/7 model. The intended outcome is a measurement-calibrated model that remains physically interpretable across meteorological regimes.

articles.title: Non-Intrusive Rubin Substructuring for Geometrically Nonlinear Structures via Nonlinear Manifolds
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Component mode synthesis enables modular reduction of large structural models, but its extension to geometrically nonlinear systems remains challenging. This work generalizes the Rubin method by introducing a cubic displacement manifold that statically condenses high-frequency free-interface modes onto the retained low-frequency modes and residual attachment modes. The reduced equations of motion, with cubic polynomial restoring forces, are derived by Galerkin projection onto the manifold tangent subspace. The consistency of the reduced forces is guaranteed by the cubic expansion of the component-level reduced manifold. We further present a non-intrusive procedure that combines elastic-force identification with finite-difference estimates of tangent-stiffness derivatives, which allows the reduced model to be constructed from the linear Rubin model and tangent-stiffness evaluations. In the proposed numerical tests, the reduced assembled models accurately reproduce the nonlinear responses of the full finite-element models, including internal resonance and modal coupling. Scalability and significant computational gains are demonstrated with an industrial scale model of a wing-box tip tank assembly, for which an online speed-up of about 24,666 was obtained.

articles.title: Generating Circularly Polarized and Chiral Cathodoluminescence from a Single Plasmonic Nanoantenna
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The generation and control of circularly polarized and chiral light is important for a wide range of applications, from sensing to optical communication and catalysis. Generally, the generation of chiral light emission from plasmonic nanostructures relies on the use of nanoantennas with predefined chiral shape, which requires complex nanofabrication. In this work, we show how localized electron excitation controls the generation of circularly polarized- and chiral cathodoluminescence from a single achiral plasmonic nanoantenna. We exploit the π/2 phase difference between the transverse and longitudinal components of the electric field that is carried by 30 keV electrons, to coherently excite degenerate dipolar modes of which the far-field radiation interferes in the far field, thereby creating a strong optical spin-Hall effect. Using angle-resolved cathodoluminescence polarimetry we measure the angle-resolved Stokes parameters for selected positions of the electron beam near the nanoparticle and show how the precise location of the electron beam controls the generation of the circularly polarized and chiral electric field components. Our findings represent an elemental form of generation of circularly polarized light, by synthesizing the circularly rotating electric fields characteristic for CPL from interference of orthogonal dipolar modes with controlled phase lag.

articles.title: Giant and sign-tunable spin Hall effect of light in a nonlocal nonlinear Rydberg medium
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that long-range Rydberg atom interactions provide a tunable mechanism for generating the giant spin Hall effect of light (SHEL) in a cold atomic medium. For a coherently driven 87Rb medium with Rydberg S states, we derive the linear, local, and nonlocal Kerr susceptibilities for the two orthogonal probe polarization components and evaluate the resulting spatial and angular SHEL shifts. The nonlocal third-order susceptibility reshapes the complex birefringence of the medium, and drastically enhances the y-polarized SHEL shift by about one to two orders of magnitude. Furthermore, it can reverse the direction of both the spatial and angular shifts relative to the predictions of linear response. The effect is controllably tuned by the laser detuning, the quantization-axis orientation, the atomic density, and the principal quantum number of the Rydberg state. In the 87Rb medium, we find that the spatial and angular shifts reverse sign when the principal quantum number of the Rydberg state are around n=40 and 60, respectively. At high-lying excited Rydberg states, the spatial shift can be enhanced to several tens of micrometres-a magnitude that should be directly observable in experiment. These results demonstrate that Rydberg-mediated nonlocal optical nonlinearity is an efficient mechanism for spin-dependent light transport and for future photonic sensing applications.

articles.title: Optical rectification and Pockels effect in the organic nonlinear crystal MBI for quasi-discrete THz time-domain spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organic nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals offer efficient nonlinear frequency conversion for broadband THz spectroscopy. Unfortunately, only a subset of NLO crystals is compatible with the telecom (~1.5 μm) pump wavelength region, where convenient MHz-rate femtosecond fiber lasers are available. Here, we present ultra-broadband (1-30 THz) THz generation and detection using a benzoindolium iodide (MBI, C₂₄H₂₄NOI) crystal illuminated by a 1.5 μm MHz-rate fiber laser. At 200 mW of average pump power, the crystal delivers ~1 μW of THz radiation as quasi-discrete peaks covering the whole emission region with a prominent peak at 11.8 THz. High-dynamic range (>40 dB) time-domain spectroscopy is demonstrated within minutes of integration.

articles.title: Quantum-classical dynamical density functional theory for solvation dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a unified modeling framework for thermalization and non-equilibrium spectroscopy in overdamped polar environments. This framework extends dynamical density functional theory to describe the coupled quantum-classical evolution of a molecular electronic subsystem and an overdamped polar solvent represented by a reaction-field coordinate. The nonadiabatic dynamics is formulated in terms of an operator-valued distribution obeying a quantum-classical Ehrenfest--Smoluchowski equation which exhibits nonlinear classical diffusion and non-increasing free energy, thereby retaining detailed balance. In contrast, a quantum-classical Liouville--Smoluchowski model with quantum-classical linear diffusion develops unstable long-time behavior and fails to reach a stationary thermal state. The method is applied to a two-level model of a polar dye in three different solvents: chloroform, dichloromethane, and dimethyl sulfoxide, each differing in polarity and dielectric relaxation time. Absorption and time-resolved emission spectra are obtained from dipole-dipole correlation functions, capturing the solvent-induced spectral broadening, the dynamic Stokes shift, and the time evolution of the emission bandwidth. The calculated solvent spectral response agrees well with the experimental relaxation trends of the three solvents.

articles.title: Oblique incidence and non-commuting limits: a remark on the convergence of Fresnel integrals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Gaussian integrals of quantum mechanics and of paraxial optics are oscillatory and only conditionally convergent. Textbooks usually make them converge by adding a small imaginary part to the time or by analytic continuation. We point out that the one-dimensional Fresnel integral converges by itself, while in two dimensions the result depends on the shape of the expanding domain: over squares it converges, over discs it oscillates for ever. The second case is the field of a uniformly excited plane of dipoles, which Feynman uses to explain the refractive index. Lai, Lau and Wong showed that at oblique incidence the integral converges and that normal incidence is recovered in the limit; we note that the two limits do not commute, and that this provides a transparent introduction to the regularization of the time-sliced path integral, where the ordering of the integrations in time plays the role of the physical prescription.

articles.title: Surface-muon production for ultraslow-muon sources of μ⁺-based colliders
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anti-muon colliders based on ultraslow muons, such as μTRISTAN and the μ^+p collider LHμC, need muon intensities well beyond those of present facilities. We study surface-mup production by 3~GeV protons in graphite, molybdenum and tungsten targets with Geant4, for single, tilted and multi-layer target geometries. As single targets, molybdenum and tungsten give comparable yields, more than twice that of graphite, because a larger fraction of the beam interacts. Tilting a target with respect to a narrow beam and splitting it into several layers both raise the yield substantially: five-layer Mo and W targets give 6--8 times the surface-muon yield quoted for the J-PARC MLF graphite target, counted at the production target before capture and transport.

articles.title: Stokes flow in a wedge with a moving contact point: well-posedness with a fixed contact angle and Navier slip
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study 2D Stokes flow in a wedge-like region bounded by a solid substrate with Navier slip and by a free surface driven by surface tension. The two meet at a moving contact point with a fixed contact angle. This is the model of a moving contact line at scales below the slip length, in its simplest setting. The slip length is the only length scale, and nothing is prescribed at the contact point beyond the angle: no relaxation law for the angle, and no contact-point dissipation. Slip removes the paradox found by Huh and Scriven, the infinite dissipation at a contact line that moves without slip, but in this model a weaker singularity remains. We give, to our knowledge, the first rigorous characterisation of this singularity for solutions of the free-boundary problem near the stationary state. For small contact angles and small initial data satisfying two compatibility conditions, we prove local existence, uniqueness and Lipschitz dependence on the data. The compatibility conditions are the price of the fixed angle for solutions regular in time up to the initial time. Rather than hiding the singularity, the solution class carries it explicitly in corner expansions. The velocity is continuous up to the contact point. The pressure has a logarithmic singularity, the slip-regularised version of that of Huh and Scriven. Its coefficient is proportional to the contact-point velocity. The slope of the free boundary has a corresponding logarithmic correction, the slip-scale counterpart of the Cox-Voinov relation. The linearised problem combines terms of different scaling, which prevents a direct treatment by the Mellin transform. We solve it by a Lax-Milgram argument, and an auxiliary test function problem shows that the variational solution satisfies the equations. Explicit Mellin representations then yield the corner expansions, and the nonlinear problem is solved by a contraction argument.

articles.title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22897v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum chemistry relies on general-purpose software, whose generality leaves many large-scale calculations beyond practical resource budgets. Coding agents make task-specific programs cheap to write, but not efficient ones easy to find: whether a computational strategy is accurate and fast enough becomes clear only after it actually runs at the target scale. We introduce BORN, a foresighted agentic computing framework that synthesizes high performance quantum chemistry programs on demand. BORN anticipates the behavior of each strategy before execution, extrapolating its error from representative small systems and predicting its runtime from the target-scale workload and measured hardware throughputs. Building on these predictions, BORN unfolds the preset schemes of existing packages into independently configurable algorithmic components, selects the fastest strategy within the error tolerance from the predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier, and guides coding agents to compile it with component-level performance predictions. For a Hartree-Fock calculation with 50,024 basis functions, BORN finishes in 1.41h on a single CPU node, 77× faster than the estimated runtime of a general-purpose baseline and still 9.8× faster with development time included. On a single GPU, BORN completes the ubiquitin calculation in 2.1,h, the same order of runtime as the GPU-accelerated package Mako on 64 GPUs, and shortens the B-DNA duplex calculation from an estimated two months to 8.1,h (173×).

articles.title: Variable-length MDI QKD under source imperfections and local randomization over horizontal links
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides security guarantees that hold despite device imperfections and finite-size effects. We address these challenges in measurement-device-independent (MDI) QKD, combining its intrinsic untrusted detection with an imperfection model for Alice's and Bob's sources via fidelity bounds. We establish variable-length general security under the Marginal-constrained Entropy Accumulation Theorem (MEAT), estimating the relevant Rényi entropies through conic optimization. We evaluate our model under a horizontal channel link, reporting secret keys for blocks as small as n~3x10⁴ rounds under atmosphere-free conditions, and show that compensating for unequal channel attenuation through appropriately chosen transmitted amplitudes improves performance in asymmetric configurations, enabling communication distances beyond 80 km for commercial satellite systems.

articles.title: Energy calibration of bulk events in the BULLKID detector
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.17423v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: BULLKID is a cryogenic, solid-state detector designed for direct searches of particle Dark Matter candidates, with mass lesssim 1 GeV/c², and coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering. It is based on an array of dice carved in 5 mm thick silicon crystal, sensed by phonon-mediated Kinetic Inductance Detectors. In previous works, the array was calibrated with bursts of optical photons, which are absorbed in the first hundreds nanometers of the dice and give rise to surface events. In this work, we present the reconstruction of bulk events through the 59.5 keV γ-ray generated by an ²⁴¹Am source, which emulates more closely the interaction of Dark Matter and neutrinos. The peak resolution is 5%~(σ) and its position is shifted by less than 10% with respect to the optical calibration. We observe that the resolution is further improved by a factor 2 combining the signal from neighboring dice. These results confirm the performance of the detector in view of the physics goals of the BULLKID-DM experiment for dark matter search.

articles.title: Plane partitions and spin adapted quantum states
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.06295v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe an explicit basis for the SU(2)-invariant space of the exterior power wedge₂ₖ C²m via the combinatorics of plane partitions. In quantum chemistry, this is the space of spin adapted quantum states of an electronic system with m spin orbitals and k electron pairs. We construct our basis by identifying the invariant space with an Artinian commutative ring called the excitation ring. We compute a Gröbner basis and enumerate its standard monomials via an explicit bijection to Dyck paths counted by the Narayana numbers.

articles.title: Inventa: Decentralized Self-Improving Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can generate research ideas and improve scientific discovery through iterative experimentation. However, increasing the number of agents or iterations does not automatically translate to producing more diverse or feasible ideas. Agents may converge on similar candidates, propagate unsupported claims through shared memory components and repeatedly apply search strategies that no longer yield any improvements. We introduce Inventa, a framework for automated scientific discovery that employs autonomous research units and verified shared knowledge. Each unit creates a lineage of candidate ideas using a mutator agent. A local orchestrator agent periodically adapts the mutator's harness. When progress stalls, the orchestrator agent replaces its model or restarts the idea evolution process. Verifiers evaluate each candidate idea and record verified improvements, useful components and constraint violations in a shared knowledge, the only channel between units. We evaluate Inventa on five benchmarks spanning the research cycle, covering retrieval (ScholarCatalyst), ideation (IdeaBench), proposal writing (IdeaScientist), and scientific law discovery (EurekaBench, SciLaws-Bench). It leads all five, achieving 73.6% on EurekaBench versus 56.2% for CORAL. On IdeaBench, it discovers 26.0 novel ideas per paper, compared with 18.6 for ResearchAgent, with 82% fewer model calls.

articles.title: PromptPack: Training-Free Augmentation of Diffusion Editors for Intent-Aligned Spatial and Semantic Control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many image-editing tasks require confining changes to intended spatial regions while exactly preserving user-designated source content. Instruction-driven editing pipelines often leave such user-intent underspecified, while inpainting editors condition generation on explicitly defined edit support but not on the spatial assignment of individual edit concepts. PromptPack addresses both limitations by equipping diffusion editors with two explicit 'Edit Guides': an edit-role partition that labels each pixel as 'Keep,' 'Permit,' or 'Modify' to specify where edits may occur, and a regional-prompt assignment that maps spatial regions to text prompts to specify which concepts apply where. These guides may be manually specified or, for source-object edits, automatically derived from a text-grounded SAM 3 mask. Without retraining, PromptPack injects independently embedded regional prompts into the editor's fixed-length text sequence and uses the Edit Guides to spatially mask attention, gate flow updates, and restore protected source pixels. We integrate PromptPack into FlowEdit FLUX, FlowEdit SD3, and FLUX Kontext and demonstrate improved requested-concept placement and protected-content preservation across all three integrations on PIE-Bench++. In a pairwise user study, PromptPack achieves an 87% preference rate over FlowEdit FLUX, establishing PromptPack as a practical, training-free interface for intent-aligned diffusion editing.

articles.title: HADVQ: Hessian Aware Directional Vector Quantization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultra-low-bit quantization of large language models is a challenging task because aggressive compression severely distorts model parameters and disproportionately harms a small number of highly sensitive channels. We present a vector quantization method tailored for this regime. Our approach begins with random preconditioning, which regularizes the weight space and makes it more amenable to quantization. We then represent weights in polar coordinates and decouple the quantization of directions and magnitudes. To quantize directions, we leverage the structure induced by random preconditioning and design a structured codebook based on the E₈ lattice, yielding a compact yet expressive representation. To further reduce degradation, we detect extremely important channels using a proxy Hessian and preserve them with an additional cost of only 0.16 bits. Together, these components provide an effective quantization pipeline for LLMs in the extremely low-bit regime. Empirical results demonstrate improved accuracy, highlighting the benefit of combining geometric structure, lattice-based codebooks, and selective channel preservation.

articles.title: Token Commitment as a Control Surface for Steering Masked Diffusion Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Masked diffusion models repeatedly predict provisional tokens before a sampler decides which predictions become permanent. Existing inference-time steering methods primarily modify activations, logits, or denoising trajectories, while treating this commitment policy as a fixed decoding detail. We instead study token commitment as a diffusion-specific control surface and separate it into two decisions: which tokens to commit and how many tokens to commit at each step. For the first, we introduce counterfactual target-aware commitment, which ranks unresolved positions by a mixture of model confidence and leave-one-token-out target contribution. For the second, we introduce calibrated adaptive budgets driven by target progress and confidence. Across language and vision-language settings in the LLaDA family, multiple targets, two activation-steering methods, and an unsteered control, both mechanisms yield empirically monotonic target-quality trade-offs in every configuration we evaluate. Adaptive schedules also recover competitive operating points relative to scorer-free stochastic schedules matched in average denoising cost. Because both mechanisms require only a scalar score evaluated on a provisional completion, they apply unchanged when the target is an automatic proxy for task success rather than an output attribute: NLI entailment for dialogue summarization and CLIPScore for captioning, neither of which corresponds to a single reusable steering direction. We reproduce the behavior of both mechanisms on a second masked-diffusion family, Dream-7B, for one control target and one task-success target. These results characterize commitment--which provisional predictions become irreversible, and how rapidly--as an interpretable control surface for steering masked diffusion generation under the conditions we test.

articles.title: Edge-Adaptive Hiera-Seg Model for Building-Integrated Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building integrated photovoltaic power forecasting is challenging because facade orientation, rooftop geometry, nearby buildings, vegetation, cloud movement, module temperature, inverter status and edge device reliability jointly affect power generation. This paper proposes an edge-adaptive HieraSeg model for short term BIPV power forecasting with multi-orientation visual-irradiance fusion. RGB facade images, optional thermal cues, irradiance measurements, module temperature, facade orientation, rooftop masks, shading labels, sky condition, historical power and edge device state are aligned into synchronous forecasting windows. HieraSeg extracts hierarchical regions from facade, rooftop, sky, shadow and background images, while the edge-adaptive module changes feature weights under missing frames, latency shifts and local shading changes. The segmentation branch identifies occluded module areas and separates facade, rooftop, sky and background evidence before the forecasting head estimates future BIPV output. Experiments are designed on a simulated multibuilding BIPV dataset with unseen building and unseen orientation tests. The model reports predicted power, confidence interval, dominant evidence, occlusion contribution, orientation contribution and energy-management review priority. This output is intended to show whether the forecast is driven by irradiance change, visible shading, orientation response, stale edge information or recent power history. The framework supports local forecasting at edge controllers with limited communication delay and computing resources, linking visual occlusion, irradiance dynamics and power history to traceable forecasting results for building energy management, microgrid scheduling and BIPV operation planning.

articles.title: Quantum-Classical Separation in Probability Distribution Transport via Nonlocal Games
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21840v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In many-body physics and generative artificial intelligence, locality provides a natural notion of phase equivalence: two quantum states or classical probability distributions are regarded as in the same phase when local dynamics can reversibly transform one into the other. This raises a fundamental question: can local quantum dynamics transport classical probability distributions in ways that local classical dynamics cannot? We establish a quantum-classical separation in distribution transport: two classical distributions can be connected exactly and reversibly by a constant-depth local quantum circuit, whereas classical stochastic transport requires a substantially larger spatial range. We demonstrate this separation explicitly on a one-dimensional chain and develop a general construction principle on graphs, based on nonlocal games. Moreover, the source distribution can itself be generated by a simple local classical process, establishing a quantum advantage in distribution generation as well. Our results reveal a fundamental distinction between classical and quantum local reversibility, even when both the initial and final states are entirely classical.

articles.title: Bias-Reduced and Parallel Heavy-Tailed Stochastic Convex Optimization in ellₚ Geometries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the fundamental problem of parallel stochastic convex optimization (SCO), whose aim is to approximately minimize a convex objective when given the ability to query a moment-bounded stochastic gradient oracle multiple times in parallel per round. Whereas most previous results have focused on the variance-bounded Euclidean (ell₂-norm) setting, meaning the objective is Lipschitz with respect to the ell₂-norm over an ell₂-bounded feasible set in R^d, in this work we study parallel SCO in ellₚ settings for 2 le p < infty under a heavy-tailed noise model. We begin by introducing a new class of ellₚ-optimal-distance-convergence (ODCₚ) algorithms, drawing on prior stochastic bias-reduced techniques [ACJ+21], which combine with multilevel Monte Carlo methods to efficiently estimate the optimum of uniformly convex objectives. As a consequence of our ODCₚ algorithms, we first establish rates for projection-efficient ellₚ-Lipschitz optimization, composite convex minimization, and efficient ellₚ-proximal point estimation. Combining our ODCₚ algorithms with a new ellₚ-generalized Gaussian-based stochastic gradient estimator (p-GREG), we provide two efficient ellₚ parallel algorithms, EpochDA and ellₚ-AC-SA, which achieve optimization error ϵ > 0 with at most tildeO(dfracp²p ⁺ ² ϵ⁻fracpp ⁺ ¹) query depth, improving upon the sequential heavy-tailed stochastic query depth of O(ϵ⁻p) for ϵ ≤ tildeO(d⁻¹/⁽²p⁾). We also establish dimension-dependent lower bounds of Ωbigl(minϵ⁻p,dp/⁽³p⁻²⁾bigr) adaptive rounds for nonsmooth convex optimization over a subset of the unit ellₚ ball. Our results improve upon the Ω(minϵ⁻p,ϵ²/³d¹/³) bounds of [DG19], when adapted to the same feasible set.

articles.title: ThermLeT: Transformer-based Temperature Prediction for 2.5D Chiplet Architecture
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The drive toward heterogeneous 2.5D chiplet packages promises unmatched performance and customization, yet the resulting density amplifies thermal challenges. To facilitate rapid design space exploration, we present ThermLeT, a multimodal transformer-based, scale invariant surrogate that integrates power density maps, spatial coordinate embeddings, material properties and heat transfer rate to predict steady state temperature in 13 ms, about four orders of magnitude faster than conventional finite element solvers such as ANSYS. To train the transformer model, we also create a dataset of 6,221 chiplet layouts perturbed from three representative architectures. On a 150 sample test set, ThermLeT achieves an RMSE of 3.16degC and an MAE of 2.24degC, improving accuracy by 35% over ThermEDGe and by 71% over HotSpot, while running approximately 6x and 11x lower inference latencies respectively. Ablation studies confirm robust generalization to unseen floorplans. Code and dataset available at https://github.com/MicroSystemsDesignLab/ThermLeT

articles.title: High-Dimensional Tail Index Regression
articles.abstract: arXiv:2403.01318v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the empirical observation of power-law distributions in the credits (e.g., ``likes'') of viral posts on social media, we introduce a high-dimensional tail index regression model and propose methods for estimation and inference of its parameters. First, we propose a regularized estimator, establish its consistency, and derive its convergence rate. Second, we construct a debiased version of the regularized estimator to facilitate inference and prove its asymptotic normality. Monte Carlo simulation studies corroborate our theoretical findings. We apply these methods (1) to the text analysis of viral posts on X (formerly Twitter) and (2) to the analysis of abnormally high health expenditures.

articles.title: CorrectCast: Selective Multimodal Context for Scale-Aware Residual Correction in Precipitation Nowcasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precipitation nowcasting models suffer from errors in intensity, location, and spatial structure. Addressing these errors by retraining nowcaster backbones can be computationally expensive and requires architecture-specific modifications. To overcome these limitations, we propose CorrectCast, a decoupled residual correction framework that refines completed nowcasts while keeping the base nowcaster frozen. By operating on predicted precipitation fields, CorrectCast requires training only a lightweight corrector, reducing computational overhead while providing a unified correction interface across different nowcasting models. Conditioned on the base nowcast and historical quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) and precipitable water vapor (PWV) observations, the corrector selects multimodal context and employs scale-aware modulation to estimate residual corrections. On the Mississippi River Basin (MRB) and contiguous United States (CONUS) datasets, CorrectCast improves six base nowcasters spanning extrapolation-based, deterministic, and generative approaches, with absolute gains in mean CSI averaging 0.0233 and 0.0290 across the six models, respectively.

articles.title: Harnesses That Improve Themselves: A Unifying Framework for Self-Improving Agent Harnesses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether a foundation model succeeds as an autonomous agent depends as much on its runtime software as on its weights. This runtime, the agent harness, manages context and memory, steers multi-turn control, executes tool actions in sandboxes, and verifies work before stopping. Because models differ in how they use tools and how they fail, a static harness tuned for one model or task often stalls, wastes tokens, or regresses on another. This bottleneck has driven a shift from prompt tuning to self-improving agent harnesses: systems that inspect their own execution traces, separate runtime bugs from model limits, and rewrite their own code. We present a unifying architectural and design framework for self-improving agent harnesses. The framework pairs four editable runtime components (context and state, agent control, action interfaces, and verification and recovery) with a four-stage loop that diagnoses failures, proposes code patches, validates candidates, and deploys updates. Using this framework, we show how optimizers trace errors across long trajectories and discover reusable runtime mechanisms such as pre-stop verifiers, loop breakers, and persistent memory. We further show why full-harness rewrites overfit or break across modules, and how modular updates with validation gates generalize across models while bounding token cost. To keep self-modification safe, we establish practical defenses against recurring failure modes including prompt bloat, benchmark gaming, and evaluator tampering. Finally, experiments on SWE-bench Lite validate this framework, showing that gated modular evolution outperforms prompt reflection and full-harness rewrites across models and repositories at a fraction of the token cost.

articles.title: Efficient Wide-Beam Generative Retrieval with Model-Native Trie Decoding and Shared-Context Attention
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) predicts catalog entries as short semantic identifiers (SIDs). Trie-constrained beam search keeps these identifiers valid, but wide beams expose two serving costs: vocabulary-wide score tensors that are mostly discarded, and repeated attention over the same prompt. We present Trie-Head, a model-native output interface that stores the identifier trie as validated GPU tensors. Compared with a Python custom logit processor (CLP), it reduces CPU--GPU coordination and memory traffic by avoiding Python constraint callbacks and vocabulary-wide candidate buffers. It scores compact codebook candidates and streams the full-vocabulary normalizer, preserving the original model's valid-token scores in real arithmetic without retraining. Shared-context attention complements this output path by reusing prompt key/value blocks across beams while preserving their private decode tails. We implement both mechanisms in SGLang and evaluate candidate sourcing for LinkedIn Hiring Assistant and qualification retrieval for the Qualification Retrieval Platform. The combined system improves closed-loop throughput by up to 5.57x over the CLP baseline and up to 2.63x over BF16 FlashRec at a common beam width of 200 on the Qualification Retrieval Platform workload.

articles.title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification. Given a boundary-representation part, stock, and material, a locally hosted, mid-sized open model proposes operations and cutting parameters for indexed three-axis machining. A geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, and returns feedback for plan refinement. Setup planning accounts for what the available cutters can physically reach, rather than visibility alone. We evaluate the resulting programs by the fraction of the target surface area within the specified tolerance after simulated machining. With Qwen3.8-27B, MillBill outperforms frontier-model approaches that construct their own geometry and toolpath workflows on the evaluated machining tasks. Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/millbill

articles.title: EvoSkill-S1: Evolving Reusable Skills with Genetic-Inspired Operators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reusable skills allow language-model agents to accumulate and reuse problem-solving experience. However, most existing methods improve a skill bank only indirectly through rollout-driven accumulation and heuristic reflection, often resulting in shallow and weakly controlled updates. We present EvoSkill-S1, an RL-driven framework that instead treats reusable skills themselves as the direct objects of evolution. Given hard-negative failures, EvoSkill-S1 selects parent skills and transforms them into candidate child skills through five genetic-inspired operators: revision, cross-revision, mutation, dual-reflection, and crossover. Downstream task rewards train the skill evolver to generate more effective child skills, while evaluator-guided write-back selectively retains beneficial updates. Complementary Skill Bank Fusion consolidates operator-specific banks to exploit their distinct recovery patterns, while a Procedural Skill Interface supports transfer to unseen problems. Across all reported math and code benchmarks, EvoSkill-S1 improves the corresponding initialized skill banks under both Qwen and GPT-family solvers, with relative gains of up to 12.39%. Compared with the strongest external baseline without direct skill evolution, the largest relative improvement reaches 20.39%.

articles.title: Structured AI ideation yields physical strategies for epithelial barrier repair
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems increasingly support literature analysis, candidate evaluation and hypothesis refinement, but enabling researchers to explore research directions beyond established disciplinary approaches remains challenging. We developed Abelio, an AI system designed to generate novel research directions by expanding investigators' avenues of inquiry. Abelio reformulates research objectives, uses these alternative formulations to identify relevant elements outside conventional disciplinary boundaries, and refines the resulting hypotheses. Each stage integrates divergent exploration with convergent selection through a dedicated subsystem. In quantitative evaluations, proposals generated by the Ideation Core (Abelio's hypothesis-generation core) outperformed those of four frontier large language models in scientific soundness and hypothesis diversity, and three of four in distance from existing literature. Subsystem ablation showed that each subsystem contributes to the property it targets, with the contribution of Element Selection measurable before Refinement. To investigate intestinal epithelial barrier restoration, Abelio proposed physical interventions involving membrane-tethered poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) and cholesterol-anchored complementary DNA. Both proposals were archived before experimentation and subsequently tested independently in damaged Caco-2 monolayers. PEG preserved barrier function in a membrane-surface-dependent manner, whereas complementary DNA enabled sequence-specific restoration that was reversible on demand. These findings demonstrate how structured research ideation can identify experimentally testable approaches beyond established disciplinary conventions.

articles.title: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. Here, the central question is how efficiently a problem class can be solved through a prescribed information interface and what costs no admissible algorithm can avoid. The gap between achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits defines the frontier recorded in its Complexity Atlas, a living map of frontier settings and the current state of knowledge. Self-Organization turns unresolved gaps into adaptive research programmes, coordinating conjecture formation, mathematical investigation, and replanning as evidence accumulates. Adversarial Co-Ascent develops algorithms and hard families through reciprocal challenge, exposing mechanisms of information use and concealment that guide stronger methods and proofs of unavoidable costs. Independent review and Lean-based formal certification check mathematical claims, while the Long-Term Memory carries supported findings and research experience across settings. To date, Colombo has established optimal or near-optimal rates for more than fifty settings in the Atlas. Colombo thus takes a concrete step toward Autopoietic Science: a scientific process whose validated advances regenerate the conditions of its own progress, continually reshaping how inquiry is organized and what it can discover.

articles.title: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speech applications require decisions about term presence, turn completion, and language within an audio window. We present Marimba, an interface for typed speech decisions built on frozen Qwen3-ASR 0.6B features. Lexical questions use zero-shot scoring of ASR transcripts; non-lexical questions use a question-conditioned head and a separate layer-18 turn-end readout. Language identification uses the ASR model's own language scores. On private conversational test sets, decoder AUROC is 0.80-0.92; on public read speech it is 0.92-0.97. Speech Commands four-way accuracy is 0.93; binary lexical ECE is at most 0.08. Personal-information detection, which passes the greedy transcript to a private, curated PII pipeline, reaches item-level F1 0.904 on synthetic Brazilian Portuguese speech (1.000 on reference transcripts). Layer-12 speaker readouts detect speaker change with AUROC 0.966-0.980 on AMI and VoxConverse, above an ECAPA baseline, and count speakers (0, 1, 2, or 3+) more accurately than pyannote 3.1. The turn-end readout reaches AUROC 0.930 versus Smart Turn v3.2 at 0.982 on Smart Turn's own test set. On a subset of ICSI meetings labeled by next speaker, AUROC is 0.716 versus 0.712; the paired confidence interval includes zero.

articles.title: An AI-Driven Assistant for Human-Centric Building Digital Twin Systems: Design, Implementation, and Comparative User Evaluation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22350v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Smart buildings generate streams of operational data, yet this richness rarely translates into accessible, decision-ready information for stakeholders who inhabit and manage them. Current Building Digital Twin Systems (BDTS) often remain oriented toward technical specialists and rely on static, one-size-fits-all interfaces. This paper presents the design, implementation, and comparative user evaluation of an AI-driven conversational assistant integrated into a human-centric BDTS for Indoor Environmental Quality monitoring, combined with adaptive information presentation and auto-suggest functionality. The prototype was deployed at New York University Abu Dhabi. A controlled, two-arm, between-subjects, quasi-experimental study with wave-based, non-randomized assignment compared the Baseline interface with the Experimental interface. Results showed significant reductions in task-completion time and perceived workload, while accuracy and usability improved but did not meet the adjusted significance criterion. The study contributes an implemented and empirically evaluated architecture that separates generative interaction from deterministic environmental assessment and coordinates conversational responses with adaptive visual presentation.

articles.title: Validation of the REBEL - BioMedix Listeria Test Kit for Rapid Detection of Environmental Listeria
articles.abstract: Background The persistence of Listeria species in food processing establishments is a serious food safety concern, highlighting the need for prompt and effective monitoring systems of environmental samples. A novel method using the one-step Rapid Enrichment Broth for Environmental Listeria (REBEL Media) followed by screening with the BioMedix Listeria Test Kit and/or CHROMagar™ Listeria were investigated and its effectiveness in detecting Listeria from swabs collected from multiple food contaminated surface materials was compared to the USDA reference method. Findings Our results show that the REBEL Method with BioMedix Listeria Test Kit is statistically equivalent to the reference method for detecting Listeria in swabbed samples from food contaminated plastic, stainless steel, or tile surfaces. In addition, CHROMagar™ Listeria was used as an alternative screening method for the tile-swabbed samples, showing that the REBEL Method with CHROMagar™ Listeria is statistically equivalent to the reference method. Detection specificity was determined using the randomized inclusivity and exclusivity panels and the results show that the REBEL Media and the BioMedix Listeria Test Kit successfully enriched and detected 100% of the 52 Listeria strains and 0% from the 35 strains in the exclusivity panel. Conclusions Our study demonstrates the effectiveness of the REBEL Method using the BioMedix Listeria Test Kit and the CHROMagar™ Listeria for rapid and specific detection of Listeria on various surface materials. The REBEL Method with the BioMedix Listeria Test Kit requires minimal setup and significantly reduces the testing time to less than 24 hours. This cost-effective and rapid method for detecting environmental Listeria could be readily integrated into food safety systems across Europe and worldwide.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Rule-Based, Fuzzy Logic and PSO-Tuned Energy Management Strategies for a Standalone Hybrid Renewable Microgrid: A Simulation Study
articles.abstract: Energy management systems (EMS) determine how much diesel, battery wear and capital an off-grid hybrid renewable microgrid consumes, yet rule-based, fuzzy and metaheuristic strategies are rarely compared on one plant with common safeguards, aging-aware economics and statistical testing. This simulation study compares an expert-set rule-based controller, a 27-rule Mamdani fuzzy logic controller (FLC) in untuned and particle swarm optimization (PSO)-tuned form, and a PSO-tuned version of the rule-based threshold policy on a photovoltaic (PV)–wind–battery–diesel microgrid, with equal tuning budgets for the tuned strategies. Hourly weather and load are synthetic, generated from assumed West-African coastal climatology; no field data were used. A Python framework couples component models, diesel forced outages, rainflow- and temperature-aware battery aging, and net present cost (NPC) and levelized cost of energy (LCOE) accounting. Strategies are tested out of sample on 100 simulated years, 12 PV–storage sizings, three stress scenarios and three economic sensitivities. In the baseline plant (100 kWp PV, 400 kWh battery), PSO tuning lowered mean LCOE from 0.467 to 0.429 /kWh (8.2%) and diesel consumption by 28% relative to the expert-set controller; the PSO-tuned FLC reached 0.431 /kWh (7.7% lower) with less unserved energy, whereas the untuned FLC cost 1.8% more than the baseline. The PSO saving did not depend on the number of training years (1–10). Savings grew from 0.8% for generously sized plants to 16.1% for undersized ones. Results are conditional on the assumed climate, cost and aging parameters and require validation with measured data.
