articles.title_zh: 由于超导微晶和晶间边界的磁响应，织构化Bi2223超导体的低磁场磁化各向异性反转
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A detailed study of the magnetic anisotropy of a bulk textured high-temperature superconductor Bi2223 has been carried out. In the range of moderate and high fields (up to 1 kOe), the difference ΔM between the upper and lower branches of the magnetization hysteresis loop is larger when the external magnetic field H is parallel to the normal of the texturing plane (H||NTP) than when H is parallel to the texturing plane (H perp NTP). This magnetic anisotropy is typical for such textured superconductors. However, at small values of the maximum applied field Hmax (up to 15 Oe at a temperature T = 78 K), an anomalous inversion of anisotropy has been found: ΔM(H||NTP) < ΔM(H perp NTP). It has been established that in the field range up to ~30 Oe (the first penetration field into Bi2223 crystallites is about 30 Oe at T = 78 K), the magnetic hysteresis is determined only by the magnetic flux trapped in the intercrystallite boundary subsystem. The pronounced platelet shape of the Bi2223 crystallites leads to partial screening of the external field inside the sample when the field is oriented parallel to the crystallite c-axis. The observed inverse anisotropy ΔM(H||NTP) < ΔM(H perp NTP) has been explained by the fact that the effective magnetic field into the intercrystallite boundaries is smaller for the H||NTP orientation than for H perp NTP. Therefore, when the field is oriented H||NTP, a larger external field is required for magnetic flux to penetrate into the sample inner than for the H perp NTP orientation.
articles.abstract_zh: 对大块织构高温超导体 Bi2223 的磁各向异性进行了详细研究。在中强磁场（最高1 kOe）范围内，当外部磁场H平行于纹理平面法线（H||NTP）时，磁滞回线上下分支之间的差异ΔM比H平行于纹理平面（H perp NTP）时更大。这种磁各向异性对于这种织构超导体来说是典型的。然而，在最大施加场 Hmax 较小时（温度 T = 78 K 时高达 15 Oe），发现了各向异性的异常反转：ΔM(H||NTP) < ΔM(H perp NTP)。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 对大块织构高温超导体 Bi2223 的磁各向异性进行了详细研究。在中强磁场（最高1 kOe）范围内，当外部磁场H平行于纹理平面法线（H||NTP）时，磁滞回线上下分支之间的差异ΔM比H平行于纹理平面（H perp NTP）时更大。这种磁各向异性对于这种织构超导体来说是典型的。然而，在最大施加场 Hmax 较小时（温度 T = 78 K 时高达 15 Oe），发现了各向异性的异常反转：ΔM(H||NTP) < ΔM(H perp NTP)。已经确定，在高达约 30 Oe 的磁场范围内（T = 78 K 时，Bi2223 微晶中的第一个穿透场约为 30 Oe），磁滞仅由晶间边界子系统中捕获的磁通量决定。当场平行于微晶 c 轴取向时，Bi2223 微晶的明显片状形状会导致样品内部外部场的部分屏蔽。观察到的反各向异性 ΔM(H||NTP) < ΔM(H perp NTP) 已被解释为 H||NTP 取向进入晶间边界的有效磁场比 H perp NTP 更小。因此，当磁场取向为 H||NTP 时，与 H perp NTP 取向相比，磁通量穿透到样品内部需要更大的外场。

articles.title: Molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and anomalous Hall effect in a trimerized kagome antiferromagnet
articles.title_zh: 三聚戈薇反铁磁体中弱轨道铁磁性和反常霍尔效应的分子轨道起源
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reveal the molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by noncollinear spin order in a trimerized kagome lattice. By transforming to the molecular-orbital basis of an isolated trimer in the double-exchange regime, we derive an effective low-energy model for the states with opposite orbital angular momenta m= ± 1 subject to an effective Zeeman field arising from spin chirality and spin-orbit (SO) coupling. In this representation, the kagome-lattice problem maps onto a triangular lattice of trimers, while the nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hoppings of the original lattice generate complex hopping amplitudes between neighboring trimers. This formulation provides a transparent picture of how spin chirality and SO coupling can be recast as an effective Zeeman field that lifts the degeneracy of the m= ± 1 states, breaks time-reversal symmetry, and thereby gives rise to weak orbital ferromagnetism and the AHE. The resulting phase diagram includes metallic phases, topologically trivial insulating phases, as well as several topological phases characterized by nonzero Chern numbers and the quantum anomalous Hall effect. We further identify an alternative route to time-reversal-symmetry breaking and orbital magnetization, driven by an emergent gauge field arising solely from complex inter-trimer hoppings and requiring no effective Zeeman field.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们揭示了弱轨道铁磁性和三聚化kagome晶格中非共线自旋有序诱导的异常霍尔效应（AHE）的分子轨道起源。通过变换到双交换机制下孤立三聚体的分子轨道基组，我们推导出了具有相反轨道角动量m= ± 1的态的有效低能模型，这些态受到由自旋手性和自旋轨道（SO）耦合产生的有效塞曼场的作用。在这种表示中，kagome晶格问题映射到三聚体的三角晶格上，而原始晶格的最近邻和次近邻跃迁会在相邻三聚体之间产生复杂的跃迁振幅。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们揭示了弱轨道铁磁性和三聚化kagome晶格中非共线自旋有序诱导的异常霍尔效应（AHE）的分子轨道起源。通过变换到双交换机制下孤立三聚体的分子轨道基组，我们推导出了具有相反轨道角动量m= ± 1的态的有效低能模型，这些态受到由自旋手性和自旋轨道（SO）耦合产生的有效塞曼场的作用。在这种表示中，kagome晶格问题映射到三聚体的三角晶格上，而原始晶格的最近邻和次近邻跃迁会在相邻三聚体之间产生复杂的跃迁振幅。该公式清晰地展示了如何将自旋手性和SO耦合重铸为有效塞曼场，从而解除m= ± 1态的简并性，打破时间反演对称性，进而产生弱轨道铁磁性和AHE。所得相图包括金属相、拓扑平凡的绝缘相，以及以非零陈数和量子反常霍尔效应为特征的若干拓扑相。我们进一步确定了时间反演对称性破缺和轨道磁化的另一种途径，该途径由仅源于复杂三聚体间跃迁的涌现规范场驱动，且不需要有效的塞曼场。

articles.title: Role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in noncentrosymmetric tetragonal magnets
articles.title_zh: 非中心对称四方磁体中方形和矩形斯格明子晶格中晶体场自由度的作用
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in stabilizing square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in a noncentrosymmetric localized-moment model on a square lattice. The magnetic phases are determined using self-consistent mean-field calculations. We first consider a single crystal-field doublet with exchange and polar-type Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions. We find square skyrmion lattices with distinct magnetic periods, as well as a rectangular skyrmion lattice that spontaneously breaks the in-plane fourfold rotational symmetry. Their stability and field-induced phase sequences are strongly controlled by the crystal-field wave function, including reentrant behavior of the rectangular phase. Second-neighbor exchange further modifies the competition among these states. When a second crystal-field doublet is retained, additional rectangular skyrmion lattices with distinct modulation patterns emerge, together with axial single-Q states and various double-Q states. These results demonstrate that crystal-field degrees of freedom provide a microscopic mechanism for tuning the stability, spatial symmetry, and topology of multiple-Q magnetic states.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们研究了在方格上的非中心对称局域磁矩模型中，晶体场自由度在稳定方形和矩形斯格明子晶格方面的作用。磁性相通过自洽平均场计算来确定。我们首先考虑具有交换和极性型Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya相互作用的单个晶体场二重态。我们发现了具有不同磁周期的方形斯格明子晶格，以及自发破缺面内四重旋转对称性的矩形斯格明子晶格。它们的稳定性以及磁场诱导的相序受到晶体场波函数的强烈控制，包括矩形相的重入行为。次近邻交换进一步改变了这些态之间的竞争。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们研究了在方格上的非中心对称局域磁矩模型中，晶体场自由度在稳定方形和矩形斯格明子晶格方面的作用。磁性相通过自洽平均场计算来确定。我们首先考虑具有交换和极性型Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya相互作用的单个晶体场二重态。我们发现了具有不同磁周期的方形斯格明子晶格，以及自发破缺面内四重旋转对称性的矩形斯格明子晶格。它们的稳定性以及磁场诱导的相序受到晶体场波函数的强烈控制，包括矩形相的重入行为。次近邻交换进一步改变了这些态之间的竞争。当保留第二个晶体场二重态时，会出现具有不同调制模式的额外矩形斯格明子晶格，以及轴向单Q态和各种双Q态。这些结果表明，晶体场自由度为调节多Q磁态的稳定性、空间对称性和拓扑结构提供了一种微观机制。

articles.title: Intertwined Spin Chirality and Weyl Topology Driven Giant Hall Responses in Nd₄Sb₃
articles.title_zh: Nd₄Sb₃中由交织的自旋手性和外尔拓扑驱动的巨霍尔效应响应
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic Weyl materials offer a unique platform for coupling magnetic order with real- and momentum-space topology, yet their simultaneous manifestation in a single material remains uncommon. Here, Nd₄Sb₃ is established as a highly spin-polarized magnetic Weyl semimetal exhibiting intertwined anomalous and topological Hall responses. Nd₄Sb₃ orders ferromagnetically below TCsim72 K and undergoes spin reorientation near 42 K into a non-coplanar magnetic state. A large topological Hall resistivity of sim3.9 μΩ cm and anomalous Hall conductivity reaching sim1170 S cm⁻¹ are observed. First-principles calculations identify an energetically preferred non-coplanar state with finite local scalar spin chirality, providing a microscopic route to the real-space Berry phase underlying the topological Hall effect. Calculated exchange interactions reveal dominant ferromagnetic exchange together with anisotropic exchange and finite Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions, while Monte Carlo simulations yield a magnetic transition near 78 K, close to the experimental TC. Concurrently, magnetic reconstruction profoundly reshapes the reciprocal-space topology, increasing the number of Weyl-point pairs from 42 in the collinear ferromagnetic state to 115 in the non-coplanar state. Berry-curvature calculations yield an intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity of sim983 S cm⁻¹ at the experimentally determined carrier concentration, closely reproducing the experimental intrinsic contribution of sim990 S cm⁻¹. These results establish Nd₄Sb₃ as a compelling platform where magnetic reconstruction intertwines real-space spin chirality with momentum-space Weyl topology.
articles.abstract_zh: 磁性Weyl材料为磁有序与实空间和动量空间拓扑的耦合提供了一个独特的平台，但它们在单一材料中的同时表现仍然罕见。本文将Nd₄Sb₃确定为一种高自旋极化的磁性Weyl半金属，其表现出交织的异常霍尔效应和拓扑霍尔效应。Nd₄Sb₃在低于TCsim72 K时呈铁磁有序，并在接近42 K时发生自旋重取向，进入非共面磁态。观察到约3.9 μΩ cm的大拓扑霍尔电阻率和约1170 S cm⁻¹的异常霍尔电导率。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 磁性Weyl材料为磁有序与实空间和动量空间拓扑的耦合提供了一个独特的平台，但它们在单一材料中的同时表现仍然罕见。本文将Nd₄Sb₃确定为一种高自旋极化的磁性Weyl半金属，其表现出交织的异常霍尔效应和拓扑霍尔效应。Nd₄Sb₃在低于TCsim72 K时呈铁磁有序，并在接近42 K时发生自旋重取向，进入非共面磁态。观察到约3.9 μΩ cm的大拓扑霍尔电阻率和约1170 S cm⁻¹的异常霍尔电导率。第一性原理计算确定了一种能量上优选的非共面态，该态具有有限的局部标量自旋手性，为拓扑霍尔效应背后的实空间Berry相位提供了微观途径。计算出的交换相互作用揭示了占主导地位的铁磁交换以及各向异性交换和有限的Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya相互作用，而蒙特卡洛模拟显示在接近78 K的温度下发生磁性转变，该温度接近实验TC。与此同时，磁性重构深刻地重塑了倒空间拓扑结构，使外尔点对的数量从共线铁磁态的42对增加到非共面态的115对。在实验测定的载流子浓度下，Berry曲率计算得出的本征反常霍尔电导率为约983 S cm⁻¹，与实验测得的本征贡献约990 S cm⁻¹非常接近。这些结果确立了Nd₄Sb₃作为一个引人注目的平台，其中磁性重构将实空间自旋手性与动量空间Weyl拓扑交织在一起。

articles.title: Unconventional Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect beyond Magnetization Scaling Driven by Pulse-Field-Induced Metamagnetism in Fe₂Mo₃O₈
articles.title_zh: 由脉冲场诱导的Fe₂Mo₃O₈超顺磁性驱动的超越磁化标度的非常规磁光克尔效应
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: First-order phase transitions often proceed through metastable states and complicated phase coexistence, yet such nonequilibrium processes are obscured in bulk measurements. The magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) probes the local off-diagonal optical response, offering access to local magnetic dynamics beyond bulk measurements. Here, we investigate the magnetic-field-induced antiferromagnetic (AFM)-ferrimagnetic (FRM) transition in the polar insulator Fe₂Mo₃O₈ using pulsed-field MOKE measurements extended for the first time up to 60 T and down to 1.4 K. The MOKE response exhibits unexpected and huge nonmonotonic transient behavior across the metamagnetic phase transition. The MOKE behavior does not show any scaling with the bulk magnetization, pointing to an MOKE analogue of the unconventional anomalous Hall effect. This is a new class of off-diagonal response emerging exclusively at the boundary between competing magnetic orders. At low temperatures, MOKE profiles are highly reproducible in detail, whereas at elevated temperatures they depend strongly on magnetic-field history and pulse protocol, suggesting changes in the driving mechanism of the phase transition. We infer that the excess MOKE anomaly originates from AFM-FRM phase interfaces in real space. Our results, extending MOKE into the 60 T regime, establish pulsed-field magneto-optics as a novel probe capable of uncovering transient and hidden field-induced phenomena through unconventional off-diagonal optical responses.
articles.abstract_zh: 一级相变通常通过亚稳态和复杂的相共存进行，但此类非平衡过程在体测量中并不明显。磁光克尔效应（MOKE）探测局部非对角光学响应，从而能够了解超越体测量范围的局部磁动力学。本文研究了极性绝缘体Fe₂Mo₃O₈中磁场诱导的反铁磁（AFM）-亚铁磁（FRM）转变。我们首次将脉冲磁场MOKE测量扩展至高达60 T和低至1.4 K的范围。MOKE响应在超磁相变过程中表现出出乎意料的巨大非单调瞬态行为。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 一级相变通常通过亚稳态和复杂的相共存进行，但此类非平衡过程在体测量中并不明显。磁光克尔效应（MOKE）探测局部非对角光学响应，从而能够了解超越体测量范围的局部磁动力学。本文研究了极性绝缘体Fe₂Mo₃O₈中磁场诱导的反铁磁（AFM）-亚铁磁（FRM）转变。我们首次将脉冲磁场MOKE测量扩展至高达60 T和低至1.4 K的范围。MOKE响应在超磁相变过程中表现出出乎意料的巨大非单调瞬态行为。MOKE行为未显示出与体磁化强度的任何标度关系，这表明MOKE是与非常规反常霍尔效应类似的现象。这是一种新型的非对角线响应，仅在竞争性磁序的边界处出现。在低温下，MOKE谱的细节具有高度可重复性，而在高温下，MOKE谱则强烈依赖于磁场历史和脉冲方案，这表明相变的驱动机制发生了变化。我们推断，过量MOKE异常源自实空间中的AFM-FRM相界面。我们的研究结果将MOKE扩展到60 T的强度范围，确立了脉冲磁场磁光学作为一种新型探测手段的地位，能够通过非常规的非对角光学响应揭示瞬态和隐藏的磁场诱导现象。

articles.title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
articles.title_zh: 通过图神经网络对镍纳米颗粒上离解水吸附进行无吸附质筛选
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dissociative water adsorption is a key step in heterogeneous and electrochemical catalysis, but on finite Ni nanosystems the OH^* and H^* fragments can occupy many combinations of surface sites, making exhaustive density functional theory (DFT) screening impractical. We introduce a graph neural network (GNN) framework with an adsorbate-free representation: candidate O- and H-binding sites are defined by sets of Ni atoms (anchors), and each site pair is encoded as a graph constructed solely from these anchors and their local Ni environment. Using only MACE-relaxed bare Ni geometries as input, separate GNNs predict the DFT-reference adsorption energies of OH^*+H^* configurations and whether the proposed binding sites would be retained upon DFT relaxation, eliminating the need to construct or relax adsorbates during screening. Trained across Ni nanoclusters and Ni(111)/Ni(100) surfaces, the energy model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.031 eV on the internal validation set and demonstrates transferability to unseen Ni₅₅, Ni₉₁, and Ni₁₃₀ clusters and larger surface cells, particularly for relative-energy ranking, although quantitative accuracy varies across systems. These independent tests also support the retention classifier's use as a conservative filter for selecting configurations likely to preserve their proposed binding sites. Application to Ni nanoparticles containing up to sim3000 atoms identifies favorable co-adsorption motifs and shows that lower O-site coordination generally stabilizes the dissociated state, whereas H-site coordination has a weaker influence. The framework thus offers an efficient route to screening adsorption energetics, with potential extensions to other metals and adsorbate combinations.
articles.abstract_zh: 离解吸水是多相催化和电化学催化的关键步骤，但在有限的镍纳米系统中，OH^*和H^*碎片可以占据表面位点的多种组合，这使得穷举密度泛函理论（DFT）筛选不切实际。我们引入了一种具有无吸附物表示的图神经网络（GNN）框架：候选O和H结合位点由一组Ni原子（锚点）定义，每个位点对被编码为仅由这些锚点及其局部Ni环境构成的图。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 离解吸水是多相催化和电化学催化的关键步骤，但在有限的镍纳米系统中，OH^*和H^*碎片可以占据表面位点的多种组合，这使得穷举密度泛函理论（DFT）筛选不切实际。我们引入了一种具有无吸附物表示的图神经网络（GNN）框架：候选O和H结合位点由一组Ni原子（锚点）定义，每个位点对被编码为仅由这些锚点及其局部Ni环境构成的图。仅使用MACE弛豫的裸Ni几何结构作为输入，独立的GNN预测OH^*+H^*构型的DFT参考吸附能，以及所提出的结合位点在DFT弛豫后是否会保留，从而消除了在筛选过程中构建或弛豫吸附质的必要性。该能量模型在镍纳米团簇和Ni(111)/Ni(100)表面上进行了训练，在内部验证集上实现了0.031 eV的平均绝对误差，并展示了对未见过的Ni₅₅、Ni₉₁和Ni₁₃₀团簇以及更大表面单元的可迁移性，特别是在相对能量排序方面，尽管定量精度在不同体系之间存在差异。这些独立测试也支持将保留分类器用作保守筛选器，以选择可能保留其拟议结合位点的构型。将其应用于含有多达约3000个原子的镍纳米颗粒，可识别出有利的共吸附基元，并表明较低的O位配位通常能稳定离解态，而H位配位的影响较弱。因此，该框架为筛选吸附能提供了一条高效途径，并有可能扩展到其他金属和吸附质组合。

articles.title: Detecting False Self-Consistency in Density-Functional Calculations
articles.title_zh: 检测密度泛函计算中的虚假自洽性
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Density-functional calculations feed materials databases and machine-learning models, and are declared converged when energy changes and residuals fall below thresholds. We show that these criteria, and even the agreement of independent optimizers, can accept a state from which the energy still descends or whose Hamiltonian is inconsistent with the energy. A variational formulation of self-consistency in the space of Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians yields a descent probe that exposes lower states accessible from a returned solution, and a frozen-orbital Janak test detects such an inconsistency. Both apply to any code without modification. In VASP, a UO₂ PBE+U calculation converges 1.46 eV above a lower state, and CoO and FeO converge as metals 0.8-0.9 eV above insulating states. In a census of 339 converged calculations on tungsten-free Materials Project structures, recomputed with a modified static protocol, 57 (16.8%) show energy decreases above the threshold, 49 without an initial energy rise exceeding the tolerance.
articles.abstract_zh: 密度泛函计算为材料数据库和机器学习模型提供数据，当能量变化和残差低于阈值时，即宣告收敛。我们表明，这些标准，甚至独立优化器的一致性，都可以接受能量仍在下降或其哈密顿量与能量不一致的状态。在Kohn-Sham哈密顿量空间中，自洽性的变分形式产生了一种下降探测器，该探测器揭示了从返回的解中可达到的较低态，而冻结轨道Janak检验则检测到这种不一致性。两者均适用于任何代码，无需修改。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 密度泛函计算为材料数据库和机器学习模型提供数据，当能量变化和残差低于阈值时，即宣告收敛。我们表明，这些标准，甚至独立优化器的一致性，都可以接受能量仍在下降或其哈密顿量与能量不一致的状态。在Kohn-Sham哈密顿量空间中，自洽性的变分形式产生了一种下降探测器，该探测器揭示了从返回的解中可达到的较低态，而冻结轨道Janak检验则检测到这种不一致性。两者均适用于任何代码，无需修改。在VASP中，UO₂ PBE+U计算收敛于比较低态高1.46 eV的位置，而CoO和FeO作为金属收敛于比绝缘态高0.8-0.9 eV的位置。在对339个针对无钨材料项目结构的收敛计算进行普查时，使用修改后的静态协议重新计算，其中57个（16.8%）显示能量降低超过阈值，49个没有初始能量升高超过容差。

articles.title: Multiple moiré polarization textures in twisted trilayers
articles.title_zh: 扭曲三层结构中的多重莫尔偏振织构
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twisted van der Waals layers exhibit nontrivial polarization textures from moiré-modulated stacking and the inherited sliding ferroelectricity. However, in any twisted bilayer, the topology of polarization texture is essentially fixed due to the inherent twist-stacking landscape for a given material. Here, this constraint is overcome in some twisted trilayers, where the relative moiré phase emerges as an additional structural degree of freedom. Using CrI₃ and BN as representative sliding ferroelectrics with distinct symmetries, it is clarified how the relative moiré phases reshape the trilayer stacking landscapes and tune the net polarization texture by layer sliding. The multiple moiré polarization textures can be attributed to the interference of original moiré patterns of the two bilayer subsystems.
articles.abstract_zh: 扭曲范德华层因莫尔调制堆叠和遗传的滑动铁电性而呈现出非平凡的极化织构。然而，在任何扭曲双层中，由于给定材料固有的扭曲堆叠格局，极化织构的拓扑结构基本上是固定的。在这里，在一些扭曲三层结构中克服了这一限制，其中相对莫尔相成为额外的结构自由度。以具有不同对称性的代表性滑动铁电体CrI₃和BN为例，阐明了相对莫尔相如何通过层滑动重塑三层堆叠形貌并调节净极化织构。多重莫尔极化织构可归因于两个双层子系统的原始莫尔条纹的干涉。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 扭曲范德华层因莫尔调制堆叠和遗传的滑动铁电性而呈现出非平凡的极化织构。然而，在任何扭曲双层中，由于给定材料固有的扭曲堆叠格局，极化织构的拓扑结构基本上是固定的。在这里，在一些扭曲三层结构中克服了这一限制，其中相对莫尔相成为额外的结构自由度。以具有不同对称性的代表性滑动铁电体CrI₃和BN为例，阐明了相对莫尔相如何通过层滑动重塑三层堆叠形貌并调节净极化织构。多重莫尔极化织构可归因于两个双层子系统的原始莫尔条纹的干涉。

articles.title: Noise-induced manifolds: reduction of slow--fast SDEs to switching processes
articles.title_zh: 噪声诱导流形：慢-快SDEs向切换过程的简化
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When constituents copy one another, as in reaction networks, collective behaviour and opinion dynamics, the noise of copying vanishes at consensus and can make a system bistable. More generally this noise vanishes on whole manifolds, along which slower variables keep moving and set the switching rates, yet no general method derives these switching dynamics. Here we reduce slow--fast stochastic differential equations whose fast noise acts in a single direction to a switching diffusion or piecewise-deterministic Markov process (PDMP), using the absorption probabilities of the fast noise in place of an invariant measure, and derive a first-order correction for the finite duration of switches. For the two-species Togashi--Kaneko model the reduction recovers our earlier PDMP, and the correction captures how the stationary composition depends on the timescale separation. In a model of foraging ants with a depleting food source, the hazard of leaving a source rises through every stay, which makes the colony unlikely to leave a source soon after arriving there.
articles.abstract_zh: 当组成部分相互模仿时，例如在反应网络、集体行为和意见动态中，模仿的噪声在达成共识时消失，并可能使系统呈现双稳态。更一般地说，这种噪声在整个流形上消失，沿此流形，较慢的变量持续运动并设定切换速率，但尚无通用的方法来推导出这些切换动力学。在这里，我们使用快速噪声的吸收概率来代替不变测度，将快速噪声沿单一方向作用的慢-快随机微分方程简化为切换扩散或分段确定性马尔可夫过程（PDMP），并推导出针对有限切换持续时间的一阶修正。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 当组成部分相互模仿时，例如在反应网络、集体行为和意见动态中，模仿的噪声在达成共识时消失，并可能使系统呈现双稳态。更一般地说，这种噪声在整个流形上消失，沿此流形，较慢的变量持续运动并设定切换速率，但尚无通用的方法来推导出这些切换动力学。在这里，我们使用快速噪声的吸收概率来代替不变测度，将快速噪声沿单一方向作用的慢-快随机微分方程简化为切换扩散或分段确定性马尔可夫过程（PDMP），并推导出针对有限切换持续时间的一阶修正。对于双物种Togashi--Kaneko模型，降阶还原了我们早期的PDMP，而修正则捕捉到了稳态组成如何取决于时间尺度分离。在一个食物来源正在枯竭的觅食蚂蚁模型中，每次停留都会增加离开食物来源的风险，这使得蚁群在抵达食物来源后不太可能很快离开。

articles.title: How Elasticity and Chiral Damping Shape Domain-Wall Creep
articles.title_zh: 弹性和手性阻尼如何塑造畴壁蠕变
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Asymmetric domain-wall expansion in the creep regime provides an experimentally accessible probe of the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI) and, in principle, chiral damping. However, severe discrepancies with complementary measurement techniques and the lack of a model describing the full experimental phenomenology of the creep of chiral domain walls, limits the application of these measurements. Here, using a symmetry decomposition of the velocity curve, we derive an analytical model describing the coupled influence of domain-wall stiffness and chiral damping in the creep regime. Their interplay generates the antisymmetric distortion that shifts the velocity minimum away from the DMI field. Applied to Co-based magnetic multilayers, the model yields iDMI values consistent with BLS and flow-regime benchmarks and identifies the reasons for the longstanding discrepancy. The model provides insights for possible strategies to measure chiral damping via creep dynamics of domain walls.
articles.abstract_zh: 蠕变状态下的非对称畴壁扩张提供了一种可用于实验的探针，用于探测界面Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya相互作用（iDMI），原则上还可用于探测手性阻尼。然而，与互补测量技术存在严重差异，以及缺乏描述手性畴壁蠕变完整实验现象的模型，限制了这些测量的应用。在这里，我们使用速度曲线的对称分解，推导出一种分析模型，该模型描述了蠕变状态下畴壁刚度和手性阻尼的耦合影响。它们的相互作用产生反对称畸变，使速度最小值偏离DMI场。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 蠕变状态下的非对称畴壁扩张提供了一种可用于实验的探针，用于探测界面Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya相互作用（iDMI），原则上还可用于探测手性阻尼。然而，与互补测量技术存在严重差异，以及缺乏描述手性畴壁蠕变完整实验现象的模型，限制了这些测量的应用。在这里，我们使用速度曲线的对称分解，推导出一种分析模型，该模型描述了蠕变状态下畴壁刚度和手性阻尼的耦合影响。它们的相互作用产生反对称畸变，使速度最小值偏离DMI场。该模型应用于钴基磁性多层膜时，得出的iDMI值与BLS和流动态基准一致，并指出了长期存在差异的原因。该模型为通过畴壁的蠕变动力学来测量手性阻尼的可能策略提供了见解。

articles.title: Altermagnetism in moiré quasicrystals
articles.title_zh: 莫尔准晶中的交替磁性
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnetism is a collinear compensated magnetic phase with zero net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin polarization. Quasicrystalline altermagnetism extends altermagnetism beyond periodic crystals, with noncrystallographic symmetries allowing high-order spin polarization patterns. Here, we propose a symmetry-based approach to realizing quasicrystalline altermagnetism by twisting collinear magnetic layers. Specifically, we demonstrate that the 30cⁱrc-twisted honeycomb lattice bilayers form the dodecagonal quasicrystals supporting an i-wave altermagnetic phase. We further find that 45cⁱrc-twisted bilayers preserving fourfold rotational symmetry support a mirror-driven l-wave phase with eight nodal lines. We characterize these altermagnetic patterns through plane-wave-projected spin-resolved spectral functions and spin-resolved conductances. Our work provides a systematic route to high-angular-order quasicrystalline altermagnetism through twist engineering.

articles.title: Global bound-state spectrum and spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement in an inverse-3/2 magnetic quantum dot
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the bound-state spectrum and confinement thresholds of a two-dimensional electron governed by the Schrödinger--Pauli equation in an inverse-3/2 radial magnetic-field profile. The radial problem reduces to the biconfluent Heun equation, but instead of restricting the solution to the quasi-exact polynomial sector, we impose the bound-state condition globally through a spectral Wronskian between the endpoint-selected Frobenius solution and the subdominant asymptotic solution. The resulting spectrum contains continuous nonpolynomial bound-state branches on which the known quasi-exact solutions appear as isolated exact points. In this global description, the polynomial index N remains a termination index within the quasi-exact sector but does not uniquely label the spectral branches. An independent exact analysis of the continuum edge yields spin- and angular-momentum-dependent critical couplings that can lie below the quasi-exact restriction U₀a>4, where U₀ is the Coulomb-strength parameter and a is the magnetic-profile length scale. These results establish quasi-exact solvability as a set of special analytic points embedded in a broader biconfluent-Heun spectrum with spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement thresholds.

articles.title: A tunable multi-gated platform for superlattice engineering in bilayer graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodic potentials with length scales much larger than crystal lattice constants can generate low-energy electronic minibands. While small-angle twisted van der Waals heterostructures have been widely used to realize such physics, correlated phases are often limited by twist-angle inhomogeneity, strain, and disorder. Here, we investigate high-quality Bernal bilayer graphene placed on a patterned graphite gate, featuring a triangular array of holes, forming a new class of "gate-engineered" superlattices tunable through three independent electrostatic gates. Near the charge neutrality point, we observe insulating states characteristic of miniband formation. Temperature-dependent transport reveals activated gaps consistent with theory, and Hall measurements indicate charge-carrier inversion. Notably, the superlattice can be reconfigured electrostatically using various gate combinations, enabling flexible band-structure design without mechanical twisting. The results highlight a new route to band engineering, potentially extendable to complex periodic structures that are untenable in natural materials.

articles.title: Hund physics in the quarter-filled two-band Hubbard-Kanamori model: Crystal-field splitting and non-local Correlations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the effect of crystal-field splitting and non-local correlations in the quarter-filled two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model. The role of the Hund's coupling in this configuration is not obvious since the atomic ground state has only one electron per site. Yet, previous works identified fingerprints of the Hund's coupling defining a weak Hund's metal at least at finite temperature. Using single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) and two-site cellular DMFT based on a selected configuration-interaction solver we investigate the zero-temperature properties of the weak Hund's metal. Within DMFT we draw the boundary for the weak Hund's metal, which is consistent with previous finite-temperature results. Interestingly, we find that the fingerprints of the Hund's coupling are quite robust to the lifting of the orbital degeneracy and they survive up to splittings of a quarter of the bandwidth, well beyond those at which a two-stage Kondo screening disappears. Including non-local correlations in cluster DMFT demonstrates the robustness of the single-site DMFT picture, even if Mott localization occurs at smaller interactions. In the metal the intersite correlations are weak and insensitive to J, while in the localized state we find nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic, antiferro-orbital correlations that are manifest also in the mutual information between sites.

articles.title: Bias Conditioning and Long-Range Electrostatics for Consistent Machine-Learning Potentials of Electrified Interfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) of electrified interfaces need the bias as input, but it is unclear whether a scalar electrode charge suffices and whether short-range models capture the non-local response. We add charge and field conditioning to short- and long-range MLIPs. State-of-the-art field-conditioned short-range models overpolarize thick water films nearly twofold and miss work-function shifts at stepped Pt. Our long-range model captures both, needs only the electrode charge at metals as input, and reproduces ab initio simulations of the Pt(111)--water interface.

articles.title: Large pseudo-orbital magnetic moment of magnons in CrI₃ nanotubes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently discovered CrI₃ nanotubes are expected to host unusual radial magnetic order states, on account of the strong out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy of the two-dimensional parent material. The detection of these peculiar magnetic states is challenging, and motivates the quest for unique features that can be probed experimentally. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show that an axial magnetic field tilts the radial phase into a conical one that threads the tube with an Aharonov-Bohm flux for magnons. This flux endows magnons with a pseudo-orbital magnetic moment, reaching approximately six Bohr magnetons, three times conventional magnon spin moment, and therefore detectable through magnon spectroscopy, providing a smoking gun for the radial and conical magnetic order in CrI₃ nanotubes.

articles.title: Large-scale Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations with Atomic Cluster Expansion potentials in LAMMPS
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics (MCMD) simulations are widely used to study the properties of materials at the mesoscale. Simulations with hundreds of thousands of atoms usually rely on empirical potentials because MCMD with machine-learning interatomic potentials is impractical at this scale in existing implementations. Here, we introduce a hybrid MPI/OpenMP scheme for MCMD with Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) potentials in LAMMPS. Monte Carlo moves are evaluated from local energy changes and carried out in parallel over MPI ranks, while molecular dynamics is parallelized over OpenMP threads. At a fixed number of CPUs, the wall time of the Monte Carlo moves decreases by a factor equal to the number of MPI ranks. Larger simulation cells also reduce the statistical errors of free energy calculations because thermal fluctuations decrease with system size. We demonstrate the scheme by calculating free energies of the HCP and BCC phases in the strongly anharmonic Hf--Ti system and by simulating zirconium segregation in a nanocrystalline copper sample of 670,000 atoms. For Cu--Zr, an ACE potential and an empirical potential predict similar grain boundary compositions but different amounts of zirconium dissolved in the grains. The scheme makes MCMD simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials practical at the length scales of microstructure.

articles.title: Interaction Landscapes of Structurally Distorted Toroidal Classical Spin Textures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a classical discrete magnetostatic model of localized magnetic moments arranged in a toroidal texture, where the moments are represented by static current loops and study the behavior of the magnetic dipole-dipole interaction under several types of structural deformations. The purpose is to disentangle effects due to geometric and magnetic deformations, including elliptical, lopsided, alternating, and tilted configurations. In particular, we investigate how distortions modify the toroidal moment and the interaction energy between pairs of toroidal structures. The resulting interaction landscapes exhibit characteristic symmetry patterns and anisotropies that are highly sensitive to the underlying deformation. As a separate proof-of-concept comparison, first-principles calculations on a molecular spin-toroidal system reveal qualitatively similar orientation-dependent behavior. The calculated interaction is microscopically the conventional pairwise magnetic dipole-dipole interaction between localized moments arranged in a spin-toroidal texture; the toroidal moment characterizes the collective texture and should not be interpreted as introducing an additional elementary interaction term. Our results provide a platform for exploring orientation-dependent interactions of spin-toroidal textures in molecular magnets and related nanoscale magnetic systems that are essential to understand the role of toroidal order.

articles.title: Torsional Hall Viscosity of Massive Chern Insulators: Finite Temperature and Chemical Potential
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the torsional Hall viscosity ζᵣₘ H of Chern insulators at finite temperature and chemical potential. Our analysis considers the massive Dirac fermion and two deformations: a constant out-of-plane magnetic field and a momentum-dependent mass described by the single-block Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hamiltonian. For the massive Dirac theory, we show that temperature and chemical potential lead to UV-finite corrections and that a chemical potential outside the bulk gap modifies ζᵣₘ H even at zero temperature. In a constant magnetic field, the response of massive Dirac fermions is dictated by the relativistic Landau-level spectrum, leading to a plateau structure at zero temperature that is smoothed at finite temperature. The jumps are proportional to the Dirac mass and inversely proportional to the squared magnetic length and the newly occupied Landau-level energy. Finally, we present a detailed study of the correction to ζᵣₘ H in the single-block BHZ continuum model due to temperature and chemical potential. For parameters relevant to (Hg,Mn)Te quantum wells, the magnitude of the jump across a mass domain wall retains its vacuum enhancement due to the BHZ deformation as long as the chemical potential lies sufficiently deep inside the gap compared with the thermal energy. Our results extend the theory of torsional Hall viscosity to experimentally relevant conditions and may facilitate its future detection.

articles.title: Moiré Excitons in a Chern Ferromagnet
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent experiments have established excitonic optical resonances as powerful probes and control knobs of moiré Chern ferromagnets. However, the microscopic nature of excitons formed on such interaction-driven, time-reversal-symmetry-broken ground states remains largely unexplored. In this paper, using a Gutzwiller plus Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, we investigate twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling νₕ=1 and identify two near-infrared Chern-ferromagnet excitons (CFEs) selectively coupled to opposite circular polarizations. Strong electron-hole interactions markedly enhance their energy separation and drive a pronounced momentum-space reconstruction of the emergent X- state, beyond the quasiparticle-transition picture. We further find that this reconstruction enhances the interlayer electron-hole character of X-, giving rise to a giant quadratic Stark response. These findings reveal the nontrivial interplay between electron-electron correlations and electron-hole interactions underlying CFE formation, providing optical fingerprints of moiré Chern-ferromagnetic order and a microscopic basis for its optical control.

articles.title: Low-energy states of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain connected perpendicularly to a metallic lead
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains (SSHCs) coupled to metallic leads have attracted attention. In particular Martínez it et al. [Phys. Rev. Res. bf 8, 043118 (2026)] studied a topological SSHC connected at one of its ends perpendicularly to a metallic lead modeled by a tight-binding chain. Here, we extend their results by incorporating the finite-size splitting of the end modes of the isolated SSHC, which are determined analytically with high accuracy. We also derive simple analytical expressions, valid in the low-energy regime, for the zero-temperature conductance through the lead and the relevant spectral densities. We find that, when the chemical potential coincides with that of the half-filled SSHC, the conductance reaches its maximum value, equal to that of the lead in the absence of the SSHC. By contrast, the conductance vanishes when the chemical potential is shifted by an amount equal to half the end-mode splitting.

articles.title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the Z₂ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

articles.title: Vortex states in submicron titanomagnetite particles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Numerical simulation is used to study the magnetic properties of spheroidal titanomagnetite particles Fe(3-x)TixO4 (0.4 < x < 0.6) with semi-axes ratio ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 and transverse diameters D = 100 - 480 nm. It is shown that various vortex micromagnetic states can emerge in the titanomagnetite particles depending on the titanium concentration, aspect ratio and particle diameter. The single-domain particle diameters are determined using the energy diagrams for stationary uniform and vortex states. The remanent magnetization of dilute assemblies of titanomagnetite particles with varying titanium content are calculated as a function of the transverse particle diameter D. It is demonstrated that for submicron-sized titanomagnetite particles, D ~ 500 nm, the normalized remanent magnetization of the assembly reaches very low values, M/Ms < 0.01, where Ms is the saturation magnetization of the particles.

articles.title: Accessing Electrode Edges: Upright Mounting for Site-Specific Cryogenic Atom Probe Tomography of Lithium-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cryogenic atom probe tomography (cryo-APT) is increasingly being used to map the three-dimensional distribution of highly reactive species in heterogeneous materials, including those found in battery systems. However, site-specific preparation of localised features and liquid-solid interfaces remains challenging, particularly when regions of interest (ROIs) are concentrated along electrode edges that are difficult to access using conventional mounting geometries. Here, we present a cryo-APT workflow incorporating an upright-mounting procedure that enables targeted specimen preparation of localised regions using plasma focused ion beam (PFIB) microscopy and milling under cryogenic conditions. We first demonstrate the approach using an electrolyte-wetted graphite electrode, successfully preparing and analysing a specimen containing both an edge-localised electrolyte deposit and the underlying graphite and Cu current collector. We then apply the workflow to a cycled graphite electrode, targeting Li dendrites concentrated around the electrode perimeter and successfully preparing and analysing the targeted Li-rich region. Beyond battery systems, this approach offers potential for site-specific cryo-APT of edge-localised features across a broader range of material systems, where conventional specimen preparation geometries may limit access to ROIs.

articles.title: Self-attention is a Dyson equation for many-body machine learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Why does symmetric sum-pooling (DeepSets) predict ground-state potentials to sub-meV accuracy, yet fail for correlated wavefunctions and excited states? Sum-pooling is a mean-field (Hartree) model: its O(1/N) off-diagonal Jacobian suffices for nearsighted ground-state energies, but erases nonlocal two-body correlations. We show that self-attention is a real-space Dyson iteration whose Boltzmann (softmax) kernel acts as a two-body self-energy. Because physical Hamiltonians act pairwise, Löwdin's 2-RDM theorem and the Galitskii--Migdal relation guarantee that iterating a two-body propagator captures the full energetics of correlated matter. When fitting a fractal backflow determinant, DeepSets blurs the nodal surface onto a mean-field envelope, whereas self-attention recovers the fractal attractor. Seen through this lens, the unreasonable effectiveness of attention is not an accident; in a universe built from pairwise interactions, two-body attention is all you need.

articles.title: Atomistic Insights into the All-Optical Switching of GdCo Alloys with Minimal Gd Concentration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-pulse all-optical helicity-independent switching (AO-HIS) is most commonly observed in Gd-based ferrimagnets near magnetization compensation. Recent experiments, however, demonstrated switching in Pt/Co/Pt-based heterostructures containing only a small amount of Gd at a Co/Pt interface. Here, we use atomistic spin-dynamics simulations to test an effective interfacial GdCo-alloy picture and to determine how species-dependent spin-bath coupling controls the minimum Gd concentration required for reversal. We compare a three-monolayer Co film with Gd confined to the surface layer and a three-dimensional uniformly alloyed GdCo model. Within the present uniform-heating model, robust transient toggle-like reversal is obtained far from compensation when the Gd coupling to the thermal bath is substantially weaker than that of Co; for λCo = 0.02 and λCo = 0.001, reversal occurs down to 1.5 at. % total Gd for selected pulse parameters. Increasing the Gd content accelerates reversal, consistent with the interpretation of Gd as an angular-momentum reservoir, whereas dilute interfacial Gd produces slower and more stochastic dynamics. These results show that compensation is not a fundamental requirement for ultrafast AO-HIS and identify the effective Gd spin-bath coupling as a key control parameter. Quantitative comparison with experiment will require explicit optical absorption, stack-dependent heat flow, dipolar fields, and a stable-final-state switching criterion.

articles.title: Energy spectrum of trions in semiconductors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. On the one hand, we construct the finite-element solution of the Schrödinger equation in the total angular momentum representation. On the other hand, we use the Gaussian expansion method (GEM), applied to each of the three Faddeev components of the wave function. The results for the total angular momenta J=0 and J=1 of the trion were obtained for a wide range of the hole-to-electron mass ratios covering most existing semiconductor compounds. The dependencies of the energies on the mass ratio for trions in a bulk crystal qualitatively agree with the results for a simplified model of a trion in a 1D quantum wire, for which the three-body energies can be calculated with arbitrary precision as well as easily approximated using Born-Oppenheimer potential-energy curves. A comparison of our results with data from other publicly available three-body codes as well as with the energies of well-known atomic counterparts, in particular, with vibrational energy levels of the molecular hydrogen ion, shows a good agreement and confirms the accuracy of the numerical data. We found that GEM significantly improves the precision of the obtained trion energies compared to previous calculations. Our calculations demonstrate that, for most semiconductor compounds, only one trion state with zero total angular momentum exists.

articles.title: Failure of Mean-Field Critical Scaling and Two Distinct Dissipation Regimes in La₂SmNi₂O₇₋δ
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, superconductivity with an onset transition temperature (Tcoⁿset) up to 96 K has been observed in the La₂₋ₓSm₁₊ₓNi₂O₇₋δ system under pressure, providing an attractive platform for investigating superconducting mechanisms in nickelates. Here, we systematically analyzed the critical scaling and vortex dynamics for the La₂SmNi₂O₇₋δ single crystal with Tcoⁿset=92.5 K under pressure. Within the Ullah--Dorsey framework, neither the two-dimensional nor three-dimensional scaling provides a good collapse near TcMF. This failure may be associated with the multiband composite order parameter of bilayer nickelates, in which pairing is mainly driven by antiferromagnetic exchange in the dz^₂ orbital, whereas the superfluid stiffness is mainly governed by the dₓ^₂₋y^₂ orbital. The two-step decrease in the logarithmic resistivity reveals two distinct dissipative regimes. The low-temperature regime is well described by the thermally assisted flux flow (TAFF) model, whereas the high-temperature regime cannot be explained by the vortex dynamics involved with the superconducting fluctuation. The crossover between the two regimes may be associated with the orbital-dependent evolution of vortex cores. These results suggest the significant role of the composite order parameter in critical fluctuations and vortex-motion dissipation in nickelates.

articles.title: Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.

articles.title: Hyperkagome antiferromagnetism in the iron garnet Almandine Fe₃Al₂Si₃O₁₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Antiferromagnets on the hyperkagome lattice provide a three-dimensional route to strong magnetic frustration, but experimentally accessible realizations with well-established microscopic Hamiltonians remain scarce. Garnets are a broad family of materials in which magnetic ions can form two interpenetrating hyperkagome lattices, giving rise to spin glass, spin-liquid and hidden-order physics. Here we identify the iron aluminosilicate garnet almandine, Fe₃Al₂Si₃O₁₂, as a spin-2 hyperkagome antiferromagnet. Using density functional theory energy mapping, we determine a Heisenberg Hamiltonian for the high-spin Fe²⁺ moments and find dominant nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange, as well as significant longer-range interactions. Classical Monte Carlo simulations of this Hamiltonian, combined with quantum-to-classical rescaling of the spin length, show a transition to antiferromagnetic order at Tᵣₘ Napprox9.8K̃, in excellent agreement with specific heat experiments. The resulting non-collinear magnetic state is naturally described by magnetic toroidal octupolar order, which we connect to known results for the highly frustrated hyperkagome antiferromagnet gadolinium gallium garnet, Gd₃Ga₅O₁₂. We also calculate magnetic neutron diffraction amplitudes as well as static and dynamic structure factors using semiclassical dynamics, providing quantitative predictions for future neutron scattering experiments. Our results establish almandine as a chemically accessible realization of frustrated hyperkagome magnetism in the garnet family.

articles.title: Automating literature screening and knowledge synthesis with large language models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scientific literature is expanding rapidly, yet much of its knowledge remains difficult to organize and reuse due to the substantial workload needed to navigate large, heterogeneous literature corpora. Here, we develop a generalizable large language model (LLM)-powered framework that automates literature screening, structured information extraction, and knowledge synthesis within a unified workflow. We benchmarked 11 state-of-the-art proprietary and open-weight LLMs across three materials science screening tasks differing in scope, corpus size, and class imbalance. Seven LLMs achieved balanced accuracies above 0.90 across all tasks, with the best-performing LLM reaching 0.96--0.98, demonstrating the potential of LLMs to accurately screen large, highly imbalanced scientific corpora. The framework also substantially reduces manual effort, screening 10,000 records within four minutes compared with approximately 83 person-hours for manual screening. Beyond literature screening, the framework extracts structured information from full-text articles, enabling content-level quantification of research landscapes that extends traditional bibliometric analysis based on publication metadata. This capability reveals methodological trends and underexplored directions, as shown for machine learning in concrete materials science. We further demonstrate its utility for information and data discovery by identifying publications containing silicate glass density data that are difficult to retrieve using conventional search strategies, which can support downstream hypothesis development, research design, and data-driven scientific discovery. Overall, these results demonstrate the broad applicability of LLM-powered literature analysis across scientific domains and its potential to transform large, unstructured literature corpora into structured, analyzable knowledge at scale.

articles.title: Dissipative many-body theory of electron-phonon-photon systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18748v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical cavities offer opportunities to control quantum materials, but radiative leakage and vibrational relaxation call for microscopic theories that treat interactions and dissipation on equal footing. We develop a Keldysh-Lindblad nonequilibrium Green's function framework for interacting electrons coupled to quantized photon and phonon fields. The formulation accommodates boson-number-nonconserving Hamiltonians and dissipative channels that combine electronic transitions with bosonic processes. We derive the mixed electron-boson diagrammatic expansion and the corresponding Kadanoff-Baym equations, retaining environmental noise, initial correlations, and interaction-induced memory. The equal-time equations govern the electronic density matrix and the bosonic covariance. As an illustration, we construct jump operators that preserve a semiconductor with filled valence bands and an empty photon field. Within a mean-field treatment, this state remains stationary although its two-time propagators exhibit dissipative broadening. The framework opens new avenues for studying correlated dynamics in lossy cavities and vibrational environments.

articles.title: Real-time dynamics with bead-Fourier path integrals. III. Atomistic condensed-phase simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurately accounting for nuclear quantum effects (NQEs), including zero-point energy and nuclear tunneling, is essential for a reliable prediction of the structural, thermodynamic, and dynamical properties of chemical systems, particularly those involving light atoms. However, incorporating NQEs could render simulations of large-scale chemical systems computationally prohibitive, particularly when combined with expensive electronic-structure calculations. One potential avenue for reducing cost is to use bead-Fourier path integrals (BF-PIs). In Paper I, we introduced the BF centroid molecular dynamics (BF-CMD) method, in which BF-PIs were used to compute an effective potential for CMD, and in Paper II, we introduced BF ring polymer MD (BF-RPMD), taking the BF-PI and using it for approximate real-time dynamics. Both papers featured a series of model systems and were able to reduce the number of beads needed to converge dynamical properties by a factor of 2 to 4, depending on the system. In this work, we report the first implementation and application of the BF-PI framework to atomistic simulations using liquid bulk water and hexagonal ice as test cases. As in our previous papers, we find that adding just a single Fourier component to the path yields a 4- and 8-fold reduction in the number of beads while achieving results that agree with reference PI simulations for liquid water and ice, respectively. We also demonstrate that we can reduce simulation costs by up to 5.5x compared to standard PIs by reducing the number of force calculations and normal-mode transformations.

articles.title: Non-Topological Chiral Anomaly: The Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive the chiral anomaly in a thermal medium and show that, in addition to the well-established topological piece, the anomaly acquires a previously overlooked non-topological contribution, relevant for non-gauged axial symmetries. Remarkably, this modification of the continuity equation is independent of the electromagnetic fields, thereby giving rise to novel transport effects in relativistic hydrodynamics. We further propose an experimentally accessible new effect in Weyl semimetals which we call the Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect: an electric field proportional to the magnetic field is generated by the non-topological anomaly, even in the absence of an externally applied electric field. Beyond this concrete prediction, our results establish a broader hydrodynamic framework for non-topological chiral anomalies, opening the door to a range of previously unexplored anomaly-induced transport phenomena across condensed-matter and high-energy systems.

articles.title: Gate tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits in Ge quantum well heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ge-based super-semi heterostructures are a promising platform for implementing Andreev spin qubits (ASQs). For example, they can be isotopically purified to eliminate nuclear spins that cause decoherence. However, spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which is a key ingredient for ASQs, is cubic in momentum for hole-based materials like Ge, in contrast with more-conventional ASQ materials (e.g., InAs wires), for which the SOC is linear in momentum. In this work, we study the interplay between geometrical properties like the channel width, and gate-tunable properties like the chemical potential, on ASQ operations. Intriguingly, we find that the spin splitting in a planar Ge Josephson junction does not depend on the junction width, in contrast with InAs nanowires. We explore the possibility of exploiting this property to suppress the harmful effects of charge traps. However, this prospect is spoiled by the fact that charge traps also affect the chemical potential, in addition to the channel width. Our results provide insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing spin splitting in ASQs and offer guidance for optimizing ASQs in other materials with cubic SOC.

articles.title: Hidden Momenta due to Magneto-Electric Coupling in Non-Reciprocal Media
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: From a canonical quantisation approach of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics, we derive the interaction Hamiltonian due to a dipole emitter interacting with a time-symmetry-broken topological insulator (TSB-TI), described by an axionic coupling Lagrangian. This provides an additional interaction term dependent on the magneto-electric coupling strength inherent to the TSB-TI which will modify measurements on related observables. The spontaneous decay rate is calculated in the Born-Markov approximation for a general electromagnetic Green's tensor, and then specifically for the case of a planar parallel-plate cavity.

articles.title: Tunable Multi-Frequency-Band Generator and Detector of AC Signals Based on a Spin Hall Device with Two Antiferromagnetic Layers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin Hall oscillators offer an electrical route to compact terahertz sources, while AFM spin Hall diodes can be used as a promising detectors of terahertz signals, however, their attainable frequency and the redout efficiency are constrained by the dynamics of a single AFM layer. We theoretically and numerically investigate a spin Hall multilayer junction Pt/AFM/Pt/AFM/Pt comprising two canted AFM layers, driven by independent drive DC currents flowing in the outer platinum (Pt) layers. Using a model based on the coupled Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equations for four AFM sublattices and a phase-dependent two-interface spin Hall magnetoresistance model, we show that the device manifests itself as a DC current-driven oscillating spin Hall magnetoresistance. When an additional DC (AC) signal current is applied to the junction, the device generates an output AC (DC) voltage. Our model predicts current-driven, locked, co- and counter-rotational states of the net magnetization at Neel-vector frequencies in the top and bottom AFM layers, respectively. These states result in a multi-frequency response of the spin Hall magnetoresistance at the sum and difference frequencies. The counter-rotation regime additionally activates the phase-sensitive mixing contribution, producing a fourth harmonic. In contrast, the co-rotation regime provides a difference-frequency channel on the order of 100 GHz, although mutual locking prevents this output from being tuned continuously toward zero. Our estimations show that the device matched to an external load can generate output AC power of 1.2 nW at the second harmonic and 0.8 pW at the fourth harmonic, and can produce a DC voltage of about 1 mV for a 6 mA input signal current.

articles.title: Finding Low-Energy States of the Bernasconi Model via Simulated Transverse-Field Quantum Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Low-Autocorrelation Binary Sequence (LABS) problem, the ground-state problem of the Bernasconi model, has a rugged landscape with deep, isolated local minima. We study real-time transverse-field dynamics initialized in these minima as a means of reaching lower-energy configurations. Using GPU statevector simulation for N = 20-30 spins, we compare the escape probability per verified quantum sample with the success rate per energy evaluation of steepest-descent kicks, random restarts and tabu search. Using the same field and sampling window across all system sizes, we find that, relative to the best classical baseline, the sampler achieves a factor of 11.9-35.2 for the deepest traps and 13.4-27.2 for the next energy tier. These ratios describe a constant-factor improvement in sample efficiency over the sizes studied. At the adopted field, broad Hamming-space spreading coexists with a strong preference for low-energy states. This regime follows a sharp increase in displacement as the field is raised. To connect this behaviour to the landscape, a short-time expansion relates the onset of escape to target distance and intermediate energies. Bounds on isotropic spin flips and on the free transverse mixer quantify the role of the Bernasconi potential in the observed transfer. At N = 28, the ground-state probability at t = 30 exceeds a canonical cost prediction fitted to the same mean energy by a factor of about 1.9. The cost of generating each quantum sample is assessed separately through a hardware estimate, which places a direct circuit implementation two to three orders of magnitude beyond present processor capabilities.

articles.title: The Goldstone--Wilczek Charge on the Rim
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A solenoid flux Φ=2πα threaded through the center of the Kaplan--Sen lattice disk binds a ground-state charge Qᵣₘ cₒᵣₑ=α-round(α), and the edge carries exactly the opposite charge. The edge charge is the Goldstone--Wilczek charge of the edge ladder, Qᵣₘ ₑdgₑ=-tfrac12η, with η its spectral asymmetry. At Φ=π one unit of charge crosses the disk. We ask how the rim operator, the Schur complement of the disk Hamiltonian on its boundary sites, registers this transfer. Its count of negative eigenvalues never changes over the flux cycle. Instead, the unit of charge enters the rim through a simple pole: the extremal eigenvalue of the rim operator passes through infinity in the same flux interval as the charge jump, with Δ Qᵣₘ ₑdgₑ=tfrac12Δ,sign,λᵣₘ ₑₓₜ. The residue factorizes into the coupling of the inner edge mode to the rim and the inverse slope of that mode's level, and grows linearly with the radius. All statements are checked numerically on disks of radius R=11, 19 and 34.

articles.title: Formulation of Brownian chain molecular dynamics and the path-resolved quasi-density operator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Brownian chain molecular dynamics (BCMD) [M. Shiga, J. Comput. Chem. 43, 1864 (2022)] was introduced as a practical path-integral-based approach to approximate quantum vibrational dynamics in molecular and condensed-phase systems. Its equations of motion combine Newtonian dynamics of the centroid variables with overdamped Brownian dynamics of the non-centroid path variables. Here, we introduce a path-resolved quasi-density-operator (path-QDO) representation by extending the QDO construction underlying centroid molecular dynamics to the full discretized imaginary-time path. For two position-diagonal observables, this representation gives an exact expression for the Kubo-transformed correlation function in the fine-discretization limit, without requiring either observable to be linear. BCMD can be viewed as a phenomenological, time-homogeneous Markov approximation to the exact reduced propagation in these path variables, although its generator is not derived from the path-QDO formulation. We also formulate and validate a multiple-time-step algorithm that allows pseudo-Hamiltonian errors in the deterministic propagation to be controlled by separating the Brownian refresh interval from the inner integration time step. We test the path-QDO representation on one-dimensional models and present BCMD infrared spectra of q-TIP4P/F ice, ambient water, and hot water, comparing them with published results from other approximate quantum-dynamics methods.

articles.title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can capture the nanoscale physics of fracture at the atomistic level, but their computational cost prohibits predictions at the length scales and time scales needed for many applications. Machine learning approaches, on the other hand, have been proposed as heuristic surrogates for material fracture, yet they cannot guarantee the physical consistency of the predicted response. To address this shortcoming, we propose the mesoscale neural operator (MNO): a data-driven nonlocal constitutive model that is learned directly from MD loading and displacement data. After training, it can be used in continuum fracture simulations on much larger domains and grid sizes. The key idea of the MNO is to exploit the built-in characteristic length of a nonlocal model, called the horizon, to travel across scales. Physical consistency across scales is obtained by building two structural ingredients into the MNO: a normalized kernel that renders the strain energy density invariant under horizon rescaling, and a rescaled critical bond stretch that keeps the energy release rate consistent across scales. Through tests on synthetic data, we show that the MNO and its learning workflow indeed discover the nonlocal continuum multiscale model in the form of the nonlocal kernel and the nonlinear constitutive relation. We then apply the framework to coarse-grained MD data and find that in a test problem, the learned model matches the MD strain energy density and critical energy release rate within 3%. It also predicts the peak transmitted forces within 6% in out-of-distribution tension tests. As a further demonstration, the model is applied to a plate with 4000 times the area of the training specimens and containing an initial defect. In this problem, the model reproduces the main features of dynamic brittle fracture, including branch and cascading branch networks.

articles.title: U-HamGNN: a universal model for magnetic Hamiltonians conditioned on spin and Hubbard U
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20035v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The electronic structure of a magnetic crystal depends jointly on its spin configuration and the on-site Hubbard correction U, requiring a separate DFT+U calculation for each combination. We introduce U-HamGNN, an equivariant network that takes these two inputs directly and predicts spin-resolved Hamiltonians across diverse crystal chemistries. A spectral-hybrid optimizer that weights each update direction by how consistently the gradient points along it reaches 8% lower Hamiltonian error than Muon and 26% lower than AdamW in a ten-epoch benchmark. The predicted bands reproduce U-dependent gap opening and altermagnetic spin splitting within the trained window and beyond it; exchange couplings and magnetic-order calls derived from the Hamiltonian agree with DFT+U on a calibration set. This universal model provides a new tool for magnetic research.

articles.title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20084v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying Lüscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.

articles.title: Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute SO(5) CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector φ, singlet s, and traceless symmetric scalar t, we characterize the bootstrap cone whose tip lies remarkably close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC. We extract an extensive spectrum across SO(5) irreducible representations, together with operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients. We study a fuzzy-sphere realization of the SO(5) nonlinear sigma model with a level-1 Wess--Zumino--Witten term. Using the special conformal generators, we identify 52 conformal primaries in a system with (N=10) Landau orbitals, including 31 not previously classified as primaries in the earlier fuzzy-sphere study. Symmetry projection extends fuzzy-sphere exact diagonalization to N=12. The bootstrap spectrum and OPE coefficients show close agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, including 16 of the newly identified primaries in channels accessible to the mixed-correlator bootstrap. The lowest SO(5) singlet scalar is relevant in the bootstrap and QMC results; its fuzzy-sphere data is Δₛ=2.816 at N=12 and decreases with system size. Our results suggest that the mixed-correlator bootstrap solution represents a unitary CFT with a relevant SO(5) singlet scalar and is closely connected to the QMC and fuzzy-sphere data for the DQCP. The conformal bootstrap, fuzzy-sphere, and QMC together provide comprehensive evidence for an SO(5) multicritical CFT and critical data to decode the phases in two-dimensional quantum magnets.

articles.title: Multi-output neural network surrogate for double-pulse femtosecond optothermal control of thin silicon films on fused silica
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a multi-output feedforward neural network surrogate trained on a coupled multiple-reflection and two-temperature model to map double-pulse femtosecond laser excitation (1030 nm) of crystalline silicon films on fused silica across film thicknesses (50-500 nm) and inter-pulse delays (0-10ps). Trained via Levenberg-Marquardt optimization on 2000 physical simulations, the dual-hidden-layer network ([40,30] neurons) simultaneously predicts six strongly coupled optothermal observables, peak electron temperature, peak lattice temperature, peak carrier density, minimum and maximum absorptivity and minimum refractive index achieving coefficients of determination R2 larger than 0.9998 across all targets. Evaluating a dense 200 by 200 design grid in milliseconds resolves pronounced thin-film interference fringes and carrier-induced index modulation, identifying an optimal optothermal coupling regime at d=156 nm and Dt=4.572 ps. This unified machine-learning workflow eliminates computationally expensive multi-physics runtime bottlenecks for real-time laser processing control and inverse photonic thin-film design.

articles.title: FiuMD: Heterogeneous Batching for Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics with Neural Network Potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: FiuMD is a GPU molecular dynamics engine that advances many independent biomolecular simulations as a single batch, even when the systems differ in size, topology, force-field parameters, periodic box, timestep, or thermostat parameters. All systems are concatenated into global tensors, so the classical interaction terms and a shared TorchMD-Net neural network potential are evaluated for the whole batch at once, while each system keeps its own integration and thermostat. FiuMD started as a fork of TorchMD and reworks its system representation, force evaluation, and integration to handle such heterogeneous batches. We test it with coarse-grained Cα models of chignolin, Trp-cage, BBL, and λ-repressor. In double precision, forces within a heterogeneous batch agree with isolated FiuMD and TorchMD evaluations to within the precision of repeated evaluations, with a maximum relative difference of 7×10⁻¹⁶ across 60 systems. Over 1000 steps without a thermostat, batched trajectories deviate by at most 2.5×10⁻¹¹ Angstrom from isolated ones, even when periodic images lie within the neural network cutoff. With a different target temperature for each system of the ensemble, the mean and width of each system's kinetic temperature match the values expected from its own thermostat. We show that when individual simulations are too small to fill the GPU, batching can improve throughput several-fold over TorchMD. On a single GPU, batching four different protein systems achieves a 4.6-7.8-fold speedup per step compared with sequential TorchMD simulations. Compared with sequential homogeneous FiuMD batches, heterogeneous batching provides up to a 4-fold speedup for smaller batches while maintaining comparable performance for larger ones.

articles.title: Quantum geometric spectroscopy with Schrödinger cat states
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a spectroscopic approach that reads out the quantum geometry of matter from the quantum decoherence of Schrödinger-cat light, in the same way that optical absorption reads out the energy structure of matter. For a cat-state probe comprising a superposition of two coherent states, the interbranch coherence of the outgoing light encodes the overlap between the matter states driven by the two branches. We show that, when the electromagnetic fields of the two branches differ only slightly, cat-branch decoherence is quantified by dynamical quantum geometry, which characterizes infinitesimal displacements on the matter-state manifold. For frequency-selective kitten probes of equilibrium matter, we further establish a partition law for the quantum geometric tensor between light and matter, enabling optical readout of matter quantum metric and Berry curvature through, for example, the brightening of a stellar zero in the outgoing Husimi function. For nonequilibrium matter in a pure state, short-pulse cat probes also provide a time-resolved witness of multipartite entanglement through the transient quantum metric, which can be extracted from homodyne measurements of the outgoing light. By turning cat-state decoherence, conventionally regarded as a loss of quantum information, into a carrier of information about matter, this approach establishes a spectroscopic principle that directly probes quantum-state geometry and fluctuations alongside conventional response-based spectroscopy.

articles.title: GPRidge: Gaussian-process Accelerated Calculations of Minimum Energy Paths and First-order Saddle Points
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20591v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GPRidge, a Gaussian-process (GP) library for accelerating calculations of minimum energy paths and first-order saddle points with compiled-language and Python bindings, is presented. An evaluation controller uses GP predictions to iteratively adjust the Cartesian coordinates of the atoms. The fitted GP energy surface and measured energies and forces pass from the path calculation to local refinement of the saddle point. New evaluations improve the surrogate and check the candidate geometry. For the molecular calculations, acceptance requires measured-force convergence and an independent Hessian with only one negative eigenvalue. A second negative eigenvalue triggers an escape and renewed refinement. The controller supports a joint inverse-distance GP for molecules and local GP residuals on periodic systems. Applications to the 24 Baker-Chan and 20 Birkholz-Schlegel molecular reactions using the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA-S-1.1), and to 72 Pt heptamer and island rearrangements on Pt(111) using a Morse potential, are presented. On matched Baker-Chan reactions, GPRidge uses 7.8- and 7.0-fold fewer energy-and-force evaluations than climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) and off-path climbing-image nudged elastic band (OCI-NEB), respectively, reducing validation-inclusive CI-NEB time by 41%. All 20 Birkholz-Schlegel saddle points pass the independent index-one check, compared with 17 for the classical dimer method started from the same path maxima; on those 17 reactions, the GP dimer stage uses 6.4-fold fewer evaluations. All 72 Pt(111) paths meet the OptBench force criterion, with median evaluation counts of 30 and 23 for the heptamer and island problems, against 778 and 443 for CI-NEB.

articles.title: Cavity Control of Emission Dynamics from Spin Defects in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optically addressable negatively charged boron vacancy (V_B⁻) defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are promising for quantum sensing at room temperature. The two-dimensional structure of hBN allows direct access to the local environment, enabling proximal sensing of target materials. However, its broadband emission and low quantum yield hinder efficient light-matter interaction, and the coupling of V_B⁻ optical dipoles to confined cavity fields remains poorly understood. In this study, we integrate V_B⁻ defects with a tunable plano-concave microcavity, achieving three-dimensional optical confinement. This approach yields photoluminescence (PL) enhancement and cavity-modified optical decay dynamics, providing insights into the orientation of the V_B⁻ defect dipole. Time-resolved PL measurements identify a distinct fast decay component, suggesting a complex dipole geometry for the defects. Therefore, a tilted optical dipole model is considered to attribute the fast and slow decay components to in-plane and out-of-plane dipole contributions, respectively. Additionally, optically detected magnetic resonance and excitation-polarisation-dependent PL measurements provide further insights into local symmetry breaking and potential optical dipole configurations. These results highlight the role of optical dipole orientation in V_B⁻ defect-cavity coupling.

articles.title: Solubility and Diffusion of Hydrogen Isotopes and Helium in Molten FLiBe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tritium produced in molten 2LiF-BeF₂ (FLiBe) may dissolve as T₂ or as TF, which differ greatly in solubility. Permeation experiments give a solubility close to that of HF and a flux proportional to the square root of the T₂ pressure, which has usually been taken as evidence of dissociation. We have developed a fixed-charge classical potential for FLiBe containing atomic tritium, T₂, TF, the hydride ion T⁻ and helium, fitted only to periodic DFT calculations for hydrogen. The nuclei are classical, so the solubilities apply to all hydrogen isotopes. The host reproduces the measured density and neutron structure factor but is too fluid close to the liquidus. The calculated solubilities of T₂ and TF agree with experiment, and neither molecule dissociates in the melt. Because TF is much more soluble, it holds most of the dissolved tritium unless the salt is strongly reducing, and at constant redox potential its concentration varies with the square root of the T₂ pressure, which accounts for the permeation results without dissociation. Helium does not change the solubility of T₂: a helium bubble in the melt takes up T₂ as its Henry constant predicts, while TF is enriched at the bubble surface. T₂ diffuses somewhat faster than measured, and TF and T⁻ two to three times more slowly than T₂.
