articles.title: Will it bend? Modelling hydrogel box hinges with a gel Lattice Spring Method
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20857v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hydrogels are biocompatible smart materials comprised of a hydrophilic polymer network which can absorb a large volume of water (swelling). The changes in shape the gel undergoes as it swells or de-swells can be utilised in the design of actuators. This is of particular interest for many applications whereby hydrogel actuators would be combined into a complex origami-inspired structure which can fold and unfold according to application needs. In this paper, we therefore focus on one such actuator design, the bilayer hinge, which can induce bending (for potential use in a fold/unfold mechanism). We develop a model using the gel lattice spring method (gLSM) which can be used to simulate composite structures comprised of hydrogel and elastomer and compute the equilibrium bending angle of bilayer hinges for a range of geometries and material properties.

articles.title: A simple solvable Z_N Hamiltonian in any dimension
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20874v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct local Z_N clock Hamiltonians from Baxter-Fendley chains coupled according to an arbitrary finite oriented simple transverse graph. Bounded edge lengths and vertex degrees give finite-range multispin interactions, with 2d-site bulk terms on a d-dimensional rectangular lattice. For open longitudinal boundaries, an explicit nonlocal unitary transformation decouples the chains and gives a free parafermion spectrum. On rectangular lattices this holds for any combination of open and periodic transverse boundaries. For periodic longitudinal boundaries, neighbouring chain charges fix the closing-bond twists. In each joint charge sector, the energies are sums of the corresponding twisted periodic-chain energies. As an example, we construct a three-dimensional array of chains perpendicular to a Penrose rhombus tiling.

articles.title: Reconfigurable Dysprosium Isotope Mixtures with Selectable Quantum Statistics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21028v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dipolar quantum mixtures offer new opportunities to explore many-body phenomena shaped by long-range anisotropic interactions, intercomponent coupling, and quantum statistics. Here we develop a reconfigurable platform for bosonic and fermionic dysprosium isotope mixtures using a single-isotope-like optical layout. We time-multiplex the 421-nm light to generate isotope-selective slow-atom fluxes, while spectrally engineered 626-nm light provides simultaneous common-path narrow-line cooling and trapping. By reconfiguring optical frequencies, we prepare seven isotope pairs spanning Bose--Bose, Bose--Fermi, and Fermi--Fermi combinations, with continuous population-balance control through the 421-nm dwell-time allocation. Systematic comparisons with sequence-matched single-isotope references, from magneto-optical-trap loading and compression to optical-dipole-trap transfer, reveal nearly single-isotope-like performance for most combinations. The larger deviations occur only for certain isotope pairs and preparation stages, with controlled measurements revealing optical sensitivities during loading and additional losses under high-density conditions. Our results make isotope composition and quantum statistics selectable within a strongly dipolar system while largely preserving single-isotope preparation simplicity and performance, opening new possibilities for exploring multicomponent dipolar quantum matter.

articles.title: Experimental Evidence of Elastic Instability in Viscoelastic Kolmogorov Flow
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21087v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inertialess elastic instabilities can profoundly affect transport in complex-fluid flows, from mixing in microfluidic devices and displacement through porous media to polymer processing. While such instabilities are well understood in flows with curved streamlines, their origin in rectilinear flows like the prototypical Kolmogorov flow remains unresolved. Here, we report the first experimental evidence of the center-mode elastic instability, at vanishing inertia, in a confined quasi-two-dimensional viscoelastic Kolmogorov flow, driven by electromagnetic forcing. The instability is characterized by the emergence of "arrow-shaped" structures in the velocity field, which fluctuates chaotically as the forcing strength increases. We reproduce these observations in simulations of the Oldroyd-B model and trace the dynamics in the confined flow to the travelling arrowhead structures that emerge from the center-mode instability of unbounded Kolmogorov flow. Our work establishes a generic route to purely elastic instability in rectilinear flows, broadening the conditions under which elastic turbulence and enhanced mixing can arise.

articles.title: Application-Oriented Evaluation of CPU/GPU Quantum Simulators: From Foundational Circuits to Quantum Chemistry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing simulators underpin the development and prototyping of quantum algorithms, yet the practical choice between competing software stacks and their CPU and GPU backends is rarely guided by application-oriented evidence. We present a systematic, quantum hardware-agnostic evaluation of two widely used stacks, CUDA-Q and Qiskit, selected as the simulators closest to production execution paths, across CPU and GPU backends, and across single- and double-precision arithmetic. The evaluation spans foundational utility circuits (GHZ-state preparation and QFT/QFT^dagger mirror circuits) through applied quantum chemistry (Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) energy estimation with standard UCCSD and a depth-reduced LCNot-UCCSD ansatz, and direct sampling on hydrogen chains up to 32 qubits). The results yield concrete selection guidance: GPU-accelerated double precision delivers consistent speedups, typically 2× to 10× for tractable application workloads and substantially larger at the widest circuits up to 100× or more, and governs the maximum simulable system size under fixed compute memory, while CPU statevector backends and Qiskit Aer remain competitive, and at times preferable, at low qubit counts and wide but shallow circuits. We demonstrate the practical payoff of this guidance by extending an in-house developed QSCI(LCNot-UCCSD)-RBM electronic-structure workflow, previously constrained to a 16-qubit active space on a CPU, to a 32-qubit (10 electrons, 16 orbitals) active space with GPU acceleration, completing a 20-point potential-energy-surface scan of N₂ in the cc-pVDZ basis. This end-to-end evaluation establishes that the principled simulator selection translates directly into expanded scientific reach and faster algorithmic prototyping.

articles.title: On Quantised Magnetic Monopoles in the Nonlocal Electromagnetic Field
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Maxwell electrodynamics in the presence of both electric and magnetic charges when the fields are made nonlocal by the prescription of the Moffat-Thompson nonlocal quantum field theory. The symmetry between the electric and magnetic equations is preserved, while a point magnetic charge is a finite distribution and its field energy becomes finite. When Dirac's quantisation condition eg=2π n is imposed, the magnetic self-energy is found to be much greater than the corresponding electric one. We conclude that magnetic monopoles may be permitted by the theory and yet require a very large energy for their production, thus making their abundance and detection a difficult feat.

articles.title: Relativistic and quantum fluid dynamics: nonlinear momentum evolution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an alternative framework for nonlinear momentum evolution in fluid dynamics, in which relativistic effects are proposed as an underlying mechanism for nonlinear behavior, even in the low-velocity regime. By interpreting the second-order velocity diffusion equation from a quantum-mechanical perspective, we establish a connection between higher-order viscous transport and the reduced Planck constant, identifying the second-order viscosity coefficient with (hbar). Furthermore, we show that the coupling of second-order velocity diffusion and nonlinear momentum evolution leads to a Dirac-type equation for quantum fluids. These findings reveal a potential connection among relativistic effects, higher-order fluid transport, and quantum wave dynamics.

articles.title: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized circular piece
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized circular piece, i.e. the part of a finite cylinder that is cut off by two planes parallel to the coordinate axes, is determined. The field is expressed as the product between the demagnetization tensor describing the geometrical part of the problem and the magnetization. All nine components of the tensor are expressed in closed form in terms of elementary functions and incomplete elliptic integrals of the first, second and third kind. The complementary geometrical piece, bounded by the same arc from the outside, is obtained from the same expressions. The solution, implemented in the open source magnetic framework MagTense, is verified against direct numerical integration and against a finite element calculation of the magnetic field, showing excellent agreement.

articles.title: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized cone
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized right circular cone is determined. The field is expressed as the product between the demagnetization tensor describing the geometrical part of the problem and the magnetization. Additionally, its magnetic scalar potential is expressed as the product between a demagnetization vector and the magnetization. All nine components of the tensor and three components of the vector are expressed in terms of elliptic integrals of the first, second and third kind, and a single scalar function of the field point. This function is given as a one-dimensional integral and as a series, and it reduces to the known logarithm on the axis of the cone. The demagnetization tensor and vector for the truncated cone and the annular cone are given by simple superposition. The magnetometric demagnetization tensor is also derived in closed form. The tensors are verified against direct numerical integration of the surface charges and with a finite element model, showing excellent agreement.

articles.title: What explainable deep learning reveals about wall-bounded turbulence: insights from conditional surprisal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Explainable deep learning (XDL) has identified regions of wall turbulence important for prediction that are only partly captured by classical coherent-structure criteria. We examine turbulent channel flow at friction Reynolds numbers Re_τsimeq125 and 550 by comparing SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) with conditional surprisal, which quantifies how unexpected an observed velocity transition is given its initial state. Although SHAP selection favours energetic fluid and largely overlaps classical masks, selected fluid outside these masks is less energetic but exhibits higher surprisal. Near the wall, at comparable fluctuation energy and wall distance, high-surprisal voxels outside classical masks are approximately 11 and 5 times more likely to be selected by SHAP than low-surprisal voxels, respectively. Within classical masks, the factor is about 1.3. SHAP-selected structures containing paired high- and low-speed regions exhibit surprisal maxima near their internal u=0 interfaces, where transverse velocity fluctuations remain nonzero. These interfaces contain vortical and SHAP-only regions, with the latter accounting for more than half of their reconstructed area. In part of the buffer layer, the SHAP-only portions have higher mean surprisal than the vortical portions. However, comparison with generic u=0 surfaces indicates that much of the raw interfacial surprisal excess is associated with surrounding fluctuation energy; after energy matching, the equally weighted surface comparison is statistically compatible with unity on the retained common support. Together, these results show how state-conditioned velocity transitions complement instantaneous structure-identification criteria in characterizing SHAP-selected flow.

articles.title: Adiabatic Electronic Momentum and the Continuity Equation with Nonlocal Effective Core Potentials in an Electronic Phase-Space Hamiltonian
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adiabatic electronic momentum and current density provide fundamental information about electronic motion induced by nuclear motion under the Born-Oppenheimer separation. In practical electronic structure calculations, core electrons in heavy atoms are commonly replaced by effective core potentials (ECPs), whose nonlocal components introduce additional contributions to electronic momentum and the continuity equation. Here, using a phase-space electronic Hamiltonian approach, we investigate these nonlocal components on adiabatic electronic momentum and the continuity equation in small molecules with moving nuclei. We demonstrate that this approach efficiently describes adiabatic electronic momentum and the divergence of electronic current density when the nonlocal contributions to the corresponding electronic operators are properly accounted for. We find that the nonlocal correction to electronic momentum is important when the ECP-centered atoms move but is small otherwise, reflecting the spatial locality of the electronic response and ECP. We further examine the implications of moving ECPs, which account for the motion of nonlocal pseudopotentials with the nuclei to restore Galilean covariance, for adiabatic electronic transport. We show that, for nondegenerate systems with time-reversal symmetry, moving ECPs do not modify the coordinate space adiabatic evolution of time-reversal even observables through second order in nuclear velocity, although they can alter the electronic momentum operator and its feedback on nuclear dynamics.

articles.title: Reflective Spin Wave Filtering Limiters with Bandpass to Bandstop Bifurcation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin wave (SW) filters using thin-film yttrium iron garnet are an attractive technology for reconfigurable and software defined radio (SDR) systems in which parameters such as channel frequency or transmit power are adjusted in real time to efficiently utilize constrained spectrum resources. Operating in congested electromagnetic environments leave communication systems vulnerable to damage or disruption from strong interference and jamming. Therefore, frequency tunable filters and power limiters are needed to support SDR operation on the physical layer. Here, we report a frequency tunable bandpass filtering limiter which reflects excess above threshold power using a network of nonlinear SW resonators in a ladder filter topology. The reported devices show insertion losses as low as 3.29 dB, isolation above 14.22 dB, center frequency tuning over more than two octaves from 4.75 GHz to 21.08 GHz, fast transient response of 14.01 ns, and low transient spike leakage. A physics-informed nonlinear SW model is discussed and a method to simulate and design networks of nonlinear resonators is introduced.

articles.title: Accelerating Atomistic-Continuum Simulations of Multilayer 2D Materials with Functional Principal Component Analysis-Based Machine Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomistic-continuum simulations of complex wrinkling deformations in large-area multilayer two-dimensional (2D) materials are computationally expensive. To accelerate these simulations, this work presents a machine-learning (ML) framework that first constructs a low-dimensional representation of the deformation field, then learns the deformation in this reduced space. Dimensionality reduction of deformed 2D membranes is challenging because of the extremely high dimensionality of discretized deformation fields, the need to preserve surface continuity and prescribed geometric constraints, the stochastic nature of wrinkling patterns, and the limited availability of training data. We address these challenges using two-dimensional functional principal component analysis (FPCA). The proposed FPCA representation reduces deformation fields containing millions of degrees of freedom to latent spaces with only tens of dimensions while preserving the continuity of the deformed surface. In addition, prescribed homogeneous boundary constraints are satisfied exactly through an appropriate choice of basis functions in the FPCA representation. A neural network is then trained to predict the principal components from the system and loading parameters. The resulting ML-predicted deformation fields are used as high-quality initial configurations for the atomistic-continuum solver, which subsequently performs energy minimization to obtain equilibrium solutions. The framework is demonstrated for multilayer graphene subjected to uniaxial compression, biaxial compression, and combined biaxial compression and simple shear. For the most computationally intensive large-strain cases, the proposed approach achieves speedups of at least 6.8 times while converging to final energies comparable to, and in some cases lower than, those obtained using conventional atomistic-continuum initialization.

articles.title: Parity nonconservation in hyperfine transitions of hydrogen-like muonic atoms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate parity nonconservation (PNC) in the 2s₁/₂(F=0)↔ 2s₁/₂(F=1) hyperfine transition of hydrogenlike muonic ¹³C⁵⁺ and ¹⁵N⁶⁺. Finite-nuclear-size effects and the Uehling potential are incorporated directly into the Dirac equation, whereas the leading kinematic-recoil and Fermi--Breit hyperfine corrections to the energy levels are treated to first order in perturbation theory. The spin-independent PNC amplitude is evaluated using hyperfine-resolved energy denominators and is proportional to the weak charge Q_W. The spin-dependent amplitude is proportional to κ=κₐ+κ_Z, where κₐ and κ_Z denote the nuclear-anapole and direct neutral-current couplings, respectively. For absorption we obtain the PNC degree mathcal Pᵣₘ ₐbₛ(¹³C)=-5.9×10⁻⁸Q_W +1.3×10⁻⁵κ and mathcal Pᵣₘ ₐbₛ(¹⁵N)=-8.8×10⁻⁹Q_W -8.1×10⁻⁶κ. Nuclear-structure calculations indicate that ¹³C has enhanced relative sensitivity to direct Z⁰-boson exchange, whereas the spin-dependent interaction in ¹⁵N is expected to be dominated by the nuclear-anapole contribution. In an idealized cavity-polarimetry model, a column density of order 10¹⁵~mathrmcm⁻² is required; however, the production of metastable hydrogenlike muonic ions remains the principal experimental challenge.

articles.title: Latent Molecular Rollout Towards Causal World Models: Direction is Learnable, Amplitude Control is Readout-Dependent
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A molecular world model should predict how structural changes alter physical properties, not merely assign labels to static molecules. We build a latent molecular rollout system on an 8B Qwen3 backbone, trained on 9,202 aqueous experimental pKa pairs from iBonD, and assess its progress toward causal control by auditing three often-conflated capabilities: predictive fidelity through the intended molecular pathway, directional learnability versus amplitude calibration of target-conditioned displacements, and transfer of latent control to decoded structures. After removing textual shortcuts, continuous latent inference achieves a test MAE of 2.087, significantly outperforming direct molecular feature readout (MAE difference -0.276, 95% CI [-0.352, -0.203], p<0.001). A target-conditioned policy reliably learns displacement directions, with a median cosine of 0.577 and 62.8% of 43 held-out pairs exceeding the 0.3 threshold. Amplitude conclusions are strictly readout-dependent. A frozen linear readout yields near-zero amplitude correlation (-0.020), while a nonlinear gradient-based readout recovers relative amplitude ordering (correlation 0.585, sign accuracy 0.744-0.767) with compressed absolute scale. At the decoded structure level, neither input-slot editing nor direct final-state injection produces meaningful changes across 80 test sources, bounding the tested control surfaces rather than indicating a universal decoder bottleneck. Generation fine-tuning shows relative improvement under internal oracle evaluation but does not surpass a simple constant baseline in single-sample settings. These results delineate the capability frontier of fixed-scale latent molecular interfaces: directional control is robustly achievable, but calibrated amplitude control and decoded structural transfer remain open challenges on the path to causal molecular world models.

articles.title: Simulations of turbulent heat and particle transport in stellarator plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving sustained energy production in magnetic confinement fusion reactors requires a deep understanding of turbulent transport of heat and particles. This thesis investigates turbulent transport with a particular emphasis on stellarators, using simulations with the δ f gyrokinetic code stella for the W7-X, LHD, TJ-II and NCSX stellarators, the ASDEX Upgrade (AUG) tokamak and the Cyclone Base Case (CBC). It addresses two questions: how do density gradients affect turbulent heat transport, and can turbulence help retain particles in the plasma core? In the first part, an inter-machine study shows a strong reduction of the ion heat flux in NCSX and W7-X with increasing density gradients, attributed to the stabilization of ion-temperature-gradient-driven modes without significantly destabilizing trapped-electron modes or universal instabilities. This beneficial effect is absent in tokamaks, where the heat flux increases with the density gradient, highlighting the role of magnetic geometry. The ion heat flux in stellarators does not follow the growth rate of the fastest-growing linear mode, underscoring the importance of nonlinear effects. Trapped-electron modes dominate in CBC, AUG, TJ-II, LHD and NCSX, while passing-particle-driven universal instabilities contribute significantly in W7-X. The second part addresses the long-standing discrepancy between the strongly hollow density profiles predicted by neoclassical theory in large stellarators and the flat or weakly peaked profiles measured in W7-X. Nonlinear simulations and a particle balance analysis show that turbulence provides a robust inward particle flux, driven by finite ion and electron temperature gradients, that can account for the observed profiles: the sign of the turbulent particle flux matches the sign of the discrepancy between the experimental and neoclassical fluxes across the entire plasma radius of W7-X.

articles.title: NAP-Wave: A Neural Adaptive Plane-Wave Architecture for High-Frequency Helmholtz Problems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training neural networks to simulate highly oscillatory wavefields presents optimization challenges, often hindered by spectral bias and poorly conditioned physics-based loss landscapes. To address these challenges and enhance convergence, we propose NAP-Wave, a joint neural architecture and training strategy that expands the target scattered wavefield in an adaptive neural plane-wave basis. The basis functions are extracted from all hidden layers and modulated by trainable plane-wave carriers, embedding the high-frequency oscillatory physics directly into the network's trial space. NAP-Wave is trained on a physics-informed loss built from the Lippmann-Schwinger integral equation, so no differentiation of the network with respect to its input is required. We develop a decoupled optimization strategy in which Adam updates the parameters of the neural plane-wave basis, while the linear combination coefficients are computed exactly by a least-squares (LS) solver. We couple this with an adaptive-depth training strategy in which the network starts shallow and grows progressively layer-by-layer. At each growth step, we avoid the loss spikes typical of dynamic network growth using the LS-computed coefficients, the warm-started parameters, and the preservation of the first- and second-order optimizer moments of the previous stage. Ablation studies confirm that the plane-wave basis, the exact coefficient solve, and the progressive schedule independently accelerate convergence and improve accuracy. Validated on exact-solution benchmarks, NAP-Wave achieves relative L2 errors of order 1%. On highly heterogeneous geophysical benchmarks, it achieves relative errors of 5%, 9%, and 10%, significantly outperforming published PINN methods in both accuracy and convergence time. To ensure reproducibility, the code is available at https://github.com/Hamza-Kamil/NAP-WAVE.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Influences of Magnetic Field Inputs on Simulating the 2017 September 10 Solar Energetic Particle Event
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-based solar energetic particle (SEP) models simulate the ambient solar wind, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and SEPs using photospheric magnetic field maps as the inner boundary condition. In this study, we select the 2017 September 10 SEP event, which produced the first ground level enhancement observed on the surfaces of both Earth and Mars, to examine how these inputs influence the modeled results. We use the SOlar wind with FIeld lines and Energetic particles (SOFIE) model suite, driven independently by the GONG and ADAPT-GONG magnetic field maps, to simulate the solar wind, CME, and SEPs from the low corona to beyond Mars' orbit. The two maps yield different open flux regions and hence different solar wind conditions, both globally comparable to in situ observations at Earth, STA, and Mars, with the GONG-driven results performing slightly better. We find that in the ADAPT-GONG-driven run, a more energetic CME flux rope propagates into a slower, wider stream, producing broader CME expansion and a more extended shock, which reaches both planets within ~4 hours of the observed arrival, while the GONG-driven run misses both arrivals. Both simulations reproduce the observed SEP fluxes at Earth within a factor of ~3, while the ADAPT-GONG-driven results compare better with observations at Mars, which connects magnetically to the shock flank. Therefore, for this event, the relative performance of the two simulations depends on the observer and observable, with SEP fluxes shaped by CME propagation through the ambient solar wind and by magnetic connectivity to the evolving shock.

articles.title: Quantum Startup, Recoil Statistics and Collective Gain in Free-Electron Lasers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the conditions under which quantum signatures can be distinguished from classical dynamics and statistical fluctuations in a free-electron laser. Starting from minimal coupling and the Bambini--Renieri frame, we derive the momentum-photon exchange Hamiltonian and its Raman-Nath ladder. An interaction-picture expansion retains detuning exactly and organizes recoil corrections through the mismatch between neighboring orders. Its validity depends on the accumulated recoil phase over the populated ladder, rather than on elementary recoil alone. Numerical checks and Gaussian entrance packets illustrate the effects of preparation and resonance averaging. We distinguish number-state exchange amplitudes from predictions for a coherent optical seed, and joint electron-field coherence from reduced radiation coherence. The Wigner representation connects finite recoil translations with classical transport and identifies the information required for bunching. A cavity channel then provides the basis for comparison with the recoil-resolved oscillator proposed by Kling and Giese, including the optical-undulator preparation, stimulated back-action and narrow resonance acceptance. Space charge, spontaneous diffusion and FEL-induced energy spread are compared with recoil and high-gain bandwidth scales. The coherent undulator pump is essential to exclude artificial zero-recoil antibunching from a number-state preparation. Startup and excess photon variance alone do not establish a quantum signature: the specified observable must remain distinguishable from a classical stochastic baseline under compatible preparation, propagation and detection conditions.

articles.title: Magnetic control of hydrodynamic spin coupling between rotors: Ferrohydrodynamic effects in the two-rotor problem
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hydrodynamic spin coupling between two rotors ("fluid gears") is investigated numerically for a magnetic fluid in non-uniform magnetic fields. An active cylinder drives a torque-free passive one inside a circular corral, with one rotor heated. The model combines magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and ferrohydrodynamics (FHD), with the full Kelvin force and temperature-dependent Langevin magnetisation. For the oil-based ferrofluid EFH1 the Lorentz force is negligible, and the Kelvin force drives thermomagnetic convection from the heated rotor. Steady torque-free states are computed with Taylor-Hood finite elements, the gear ratio Γ being an additional unknown. Without a field the results agree within 1-8% with published planar simulations up to Reapprox 50. About 17,000 steady states cover 34 arrangements of wires, NdFeB rods and magnet cores, gaps G=0.1-0.7, Re=10-40 and heating of 5-20 K. Because the coupling is weak, fields of 1-2 mT change Γ by an amount comparable to Γ itself. At 2 mT it is reversed, strengthened or weakened in nine cases out of ten. The outcome is set by the source position: at the experimental gap and Re=20 a source below the corral or behind the active rotor strengthens the gear-like counter-rotation up to 2.7-fold, and a source above the corral reverses it into belt-like corotation. Several sources do not act additively, and a magnet core inside the active rotor raises |Γ| at small gaps to seven times the largest hydrodynamic value. At fixed geometry and Reynolds number, field strength and heating act approximately through a single thermomagnetic source parameter.

articles.title: GPROF V08: Improving Satellite Precipitation Estimates Across a Heterogeneous Constellation of Passive-Microwave Sensors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precipitation estimates from the passive microwave observations (PMW) of the Global Precipitation Measurements (GPM) mission serve a wide range of scientific, societal, and economic applications. The Goddard Profiling Algorithm (GPROF) is the operational retrieval used to produce the precipitation estimates for all GPM PMW sensors. This study presents the implementation GPROF V08 -- the most recent version of GPROF and a major update aimed at improving the accuracy of precipitation estimates from the GPM constellation. GPROF V08 replaces the conventional Bayesian scheme used by earlier GPROF versions by a convolutional neural network (CNN). The first part of this two-part study described a novel ML framework for generating synthetic observations required for training CNN retrievals for all GPM sensors. This second part describes the final, operational implementation, which adds a second finetuning stage to the training.Retrievals from the new GPROF V08 algorithm for all principal GPM sensors are validated against reference precipitation estimates from various sources. Our results show that, while the magnitude of improvements vary by sensor and surface type, they are robust across sensors and metrics and can be as high as 40 % for the linear correlation coefficient for precipitation estimates from SSMIS and ATMS over ocean compared to combined radar and radiometer retrievals from GPM. While some challenges remain -- such as an increased sensitivity to sensor degradation and the persistence of climatological biases, which remain of the same order as for GPROF V07 -- GPROF V08 constitutes a substantial advancement in spaceborne precipitation monitoring. Since the improvements are robust across all sensor of the constellation, the update is expected to improve the full record of GPM precipitation estimates and thus benefit a wide range of downstream datasets and applications.

articles.title: Physics-Spawned Neural Integration of Rotating Shallow-Water Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Equation-derived neural integration can execute prescribed dynamics without training, while informative ensemble learning can estimate uncertain parameters and identify governing interactions without requiring differentiability. Together, these approaches motivate Physics-Spawned Informative Networks (ΦSpIN), a framework for prescribed and adaptive hybrid dynamical systems. As a first step toward flood modeling applications, we present ΦSpIN-SW, its prescribed-physics realization for the rotating shallow-water equations. Compatible C-grid operators on spherical Voronoi meshes define a computational graph that retains non-polynomial operations and advances the state through recurrent neural integration compiled with JAX. Analytical benchmarks characterize numerical errors, and global and coastal experiments closely reproduce reference solutions generated using the Model Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) model. At approximately 14~km global resolution, A100, H200 and B200 GPUs attain 9-, 19- and 34-fold higher timestep throughput than a 96-core MPAS-SW CPU reference under matched workloads. These results extend training-free neural integration beyond polynomial dynamics to complex geophysical simulation, establishing a computational foundation for subsequent adjoint-free ensemble estimation of physical and neural parameters and informative adaptation of operator structure.

articles.title: Solver-consistent learned curvature for algebraic volume-of-fluid simulations of rising bubbles: symmetry-preserving networks, closed-loop data aggregation and a posteriori benchmarks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Curvature reconstructed from compressed volume fractions exhibits a persistent force-weighted bias in the tested algebraic volume-of-fluid formulation. In OpenFOAM interFoam, face curvature is underestimated by 11-22% for radii of 2.5-40 cells, explaining the 14-17% static Laplace-pressure deficit. This bias is consistent with approximately 2% rise-velocity underprediction in the first Hysing benchmark. We estimate curvature from 5 x 5 volume-fraction stencils using a two-hidden-layer perceptron with exact phase-exchange antisymmetry and invariance under all eight square-grid symmetries. Training uses solver-generated profiles of periodic translating bubbles, droplets, and flat films with exact analytical curvature labels. Iterative data aggregation incorporates model-solver feedback and resolves deployment instabilities found in 15 of 76 periodic cases with the initial model. Band-weighted face interpolation supplies the same capillary force to momentum prediction and pressure correction. Independent tests show static pressure-jump errors of 2-6% and reductions in time-averaged maximum capillary numbers by factors of 2.8-16. Across three grids, time-integrated rise-velocity errors decrease from 2.06-2.76% to 0.65-1.04% in the first Hysing benchmark and from 5.64-8.72% to 4.72-7.61% in the second. Tuned curvature smoothing gives smaller static pressure-jump errors, but its first-benchmark accuracy deteriorates with refinement and second-benchmark gains remain marginal. A separate interface-gated dissipative momentum closure achieves a held-out coefficient of determination of 0.47 on Favre-filtered targets but changes rise velocity by less than 0.03% of its peak. Capillary-force discretisation is therefore the more influential correction target for the tested laminar bubbles.

articles.title: A Gravitomagnetic Bootstrap: from Newtonian gravity to general relativity via localizing rotational and conformal symmetries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Newtonian gravity, in the light of the Equivalence Principle, is best understood as a localization of Galilean inertial structure --- or at least, of the part of Galilean inertial structure that defines rectilinear acceleration. I consider what kind of theory can be constructed if we also localize rotational inertia and spatial and temporal scales. The resultant theory, given weak assumptions, is unique up to a constant with the dimensions of velocity and an overall sign. For an appropriate choice of these, it coincides with the first post-Newtonian approximation to general relativity, so that this construction gives a method to bootstrap from Newtonian gravity to general relativity without explicitly presupposing special relativity.

articles.title: Detection of minimum ionising particles with internal gain in the first Silicon Electron Multiplier demonstrators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Silicon Electron Multiplier (SiEM) is a novel sensor concept for minimum ionising particle (MIP) detection that uses internal gain achieved through a composite electrode structure embedded within the silicon bulk. Unlike conventional gain sensors (LGADs, APDs), the SiEM achieves amplification through applied electric potentials rather than doped gain layers, potentially offering superior radiation hardness above 10¹⁶,nₑq/cm². Following initial conceptual studies and simulation work, several fabrication approaches were explored, including Deep Reactive Ion Etching (DRIE) at Centro Nacional de Microelectrónica (CNM) and Metal Assisted Chemical Etching (MACEtch) at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI). This paper reports the first experimental results from functional SiEM demonstrators produced by Hamamatsu Photonics K. K. (HPK) using a single-electrode configuration with modified geometry. Electrical characterisation through I-V measurements and test beam studies with minimum ionising particles demonstrate clear evidence of charge multiplication, with gains comparable to simulation predictions.

articles.title: Resolvent-based modeling of turbulent flow over multilayer compliant surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compliant coatings offer a passive approach to modifying near-wall turbulence and potentially reducing skin-friction drag, but high-fidelity exploration of the coupled parameter space is costly. We develop a two-way coupled resolvent-Galerkin framework for turbulent channel flow over finite-thickness, layered viscoelastic coatings. The fluid is modeled using the Navier-Stokes equations linearized about a turbulent mean state, while the solid is represented by a through-thickness Galerkin discretization of the elastodynamic equations. The solid response is condensed into a spectral surface-impedance operator at the fluid-solid interface. At Re_τ = 180, stiff panels approach the rigid-wall response, whereas more compliant panels modify the low-rank response associated with the near-wall cycle. A Reynolds-number study shows that panels with fixed nondimensional material stiffness can produce different responses depending on whether their thickness scales with inner or outer flow length scales. The influence of viscoelastic damping is examined across low- and high-frequency regimes, where stiffness-proportional damping alters the high-frequency fractional-energy distribution, while the low-frequency distribution remains relatively insensitive to damping. For multilayer panels, the fluid-facing material determines the interfacial wave speed, while the subsurface stiffness distribution modifies the panel's effective thickness. Temporal stability analysis identifies regions of parameter space where a steady harmonic response is relevant and regions where instabilities grow. Finally, a leading-order, covariance-based drag-estimation framework relates the coupled response to changes in the mean flow and to the estimated skin-friction drag. Together, these tools provide a basis for screening coating designs and selecting candidates for high-fidelity simulations and experiments.

articles.title: Optimization Framework for Full-Skyrmionic Polarimetry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical skyrmionic beams hold considerable potential for applications in quantum information and weak-intensity detection. These applications require accurate measurements of full topological observables using imaging Stokes polarimetry, with measurement states optimized in advance to limit the effect of stochastic error sources. However, the optimization framework for general Stokes polarimetries is based on a linear reconstruction chain for Stokes vectors and cannot quantitatively evaluate the nonlinear reconstruction of topological observables. Here, we define full-skyrmionic polarimetry (FSP) and construct its optimization framework from the reconstruction chain for full topological observables. Based on existing polarization evaluating functions (PEF), we introduce topological evaluating functions (TEF) and develop a multi-stage FSP optimization methodology. Numerical results confirm that topological optimization can further improve the reconstruction of topological observables, even when the measurement states are already optimal for polarization. Increasing the redundant projection number also effectively suppresses the effects of all stochastic error sources, providing a low-cost methodology to improve the reconstruction of both polarization and topological observables. The FSP optimization framework can identify topologically optimal configurations for arbitrary FSP structures, providing a guideline for high-precision full-skyrmionic measurements at weak-intensity levels and potential skyrmion ellipsometry.

articles.title: Broadband Absorption Bounds for Coated PEC Spheres: Curvature, Angular Momentum, and Localized Sources
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate fundamental limits on broadband electromagnetic absorption by a material-coated perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) sphere. Exact reflection coefficients are derived for the transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) spherical modes. Their long-wavelength asymptotics, combined with causality and contour integration in the complex wavelength plane, yield sum rules relating the wavelength-integrated modal reflection to the static material parameters, coating thickness, curvature, and complex reflection zeros. For the dipolar modes (n=1), known passive spherical-wave sum rules establish analytically a material-dependent lower bound on the weighted logarithmic reflection integral. Extension to higher-order modes requires a nonnegativity condition on higher odd moments of the reflection zeros; we formulate this condition as a conjecture and provide extensive Monte-Carlo evidence for passive dispersive coatings. The resulting bounds establish a per-channel absorption--bandwidth tradeoff and reveal the spherical-harmonic order as a discrete transverse-wavenumber variable, recovering the familiar planar attenuation factor in the locally planar limit. Finally, we show how the modal bounds can be combined for a localized external source. For a radial electric dipole outside the sphere, the near-field excitation is decomposed into TM spherical channels, leading to a source-weighted broadband absorption bound. As the source approaches the surface, progressively higher angular momenta contribute, directly linking near-field spatial localization to the hierarchy of modal absorption constraints.

articles.title: Lock-in phase evidence for the electro-optic effect of interfacial water on ITO electrodes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attribution to the Pockels effect of interfacial water, reported at interfaces between transparent electrodes and aqueous solutions, has relied on using an optical model to estimate the contribution of changes in the electrode's own carrier density to the electromodulation spectrum and subtracting this contribution. In this study, we test this attribution using the phase, without subtracting the electrode contribution with an optical model. Because the carrier response of the electrode follows charge modulation at several hundred hertz without delay, it has a common phase at all wavelengths apart from sign reversals of the response. However, the measured transmission modulation spectra at the interface between indium tin oxide (ITO) and 0.1 mol L⁻¹ aqueous NaCl show a phase peak near 420 nm, where the ITO response becomes small. This peak cannot be explained solely by a step-like change due to sign reversal of the response. This peak appears even when the working-electrode potential, the modulation frequency, or the electrode is changed. Furthermore, this phase peak can be explained by a thin-film calculation assuming that a uniform refractive-index change on the electrolyte side contributes with a phase different from that of the electrode response. This result, an observation independent of the estimate of the electrode contribution, supports the attribution to the electro-optic effect of interfacial water.

articles.title: Embedded Trigger Control System for Wave--Plasma Interaction Experiments in Large Volume Plasma Device
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: {Magnetic-field control and synchronization are essential requirements in laboratory plasma experiments investigating wave propagation and plasma instabilities. In this work, an Embedded Trigger Control System (ETCS) has been designed and implemented for synchronized operation of a pulsed Helmholtz coil system and a broadband whistler-wave exciter in the Large Volume Plasma Device--Upgrade (LVPD-U). The experimental configuration employs an electrostatically shielded loop antenna driven by a thyratron-switched pulse-forming network to launch broadband whistler waves in the frequency range of approximately 150~kHz to 5~MHz. Simultaneously, a pulsed Helmholtz coil capable of generating magnetic fields up to ±150~G is used to modify the local magnetic topology and create transient magnetic-null configurations. The developed ETCS utilizes the controlled evolution of the Helmholtz circuit L/R time constant through the introduction of a lumped series inductor, enabling precise magnetic-field ramping and dynamic timing control. A microcontroller-based trigger architecture determines the desired firing instant from the calibrated current evolution of the Helmholtz circuit and synchronizes wave excitation with a prescribed magnetic-field amplitude. The system extends the effective circuit time constant by more than an order of magnitude, allowing accurate and repeatable wave launching during controlled magnetic-field evolution. The implemented approach provides a simple, reliable, and versatile synchronization platform for wave--plasma interaction studies requiring precise temporal coordination between pulsed magnetic-field generation and wave excitation.

articles.title: Breaking the Fixed-Substrate Limitation of Deep Learning Ellipsometry with Pseudo-Substrate Spectra
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A machine learning method, deep learning ellipsometry (DLE), enables direct and rapid estimation of the optical constants and structures of thin films from spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) spectra. However, conventional neural-network-based DLE models are restricted to the specific substrate used during training, and applying them to a different substrate requires ~100 h of retraining. Here, we propose a framework that overcomes this fixed-substrate limitation by introducing a two-input feature-wise linear modulation DLE (FiLM-DLE). In this model, the SE spectra of a thin-film structure are input together with those of the substrate measured before film deposition, which we term the pseudo-substrate spectra. Any substrate, including a multilayer stack, is thus represented solely by its measured SE response, analogous to the pseudo-dielectric function, so that no prior knowledge of the substrate structure is required. Trained on a virtual dataset of 165 million samples representing metal, glass, and SiO2/Si substrates with different SiO2 thicknesses, a single FiLM-DLE model, trained once, extracts thin-film optical constants and structures with high accuracy and shows strong applicability to substrates not included in the training datasets. Experimental validation on 47 thin-film samples across diverse substrates yielded sample-averaged mean absolute errors, relative to conventional manual analysis, of 0.047 for refractive index, 0.030 for extinction coefficient, and 1.52 nm for thickness, with each analysis completed in under 2 s. FiLM-DLE thus eliminates the need for a separate DLE model for each substrate and enables rapid, high-accuracy optical characterization of thin films on diverse substrates.

articles.title: Oxirane Ring-Opening Dynamics Mediated By The First Singlet Excitation Using Time-Dependent GW Molecular Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oxirane (ethylene oxide, ceC2H4O) is a prototypical system for investigating photoinduced bond cleavage and ring-opening dynamics. Previous time-dependent density functional theory studies identified the initial HOMO → LUMO (ceS1) excitation as nonreactive and attributed ring opening to higher-energy excitations. Subsequent constrained density functional theory simulations, however, reported ring opening following an ceS2 → ceS1 transition. Here, we investigate photochemistry of oxirane using time-dependent GW molecular dynamics (TDGW-MD), a many-body approach based on extended quasiparticle theory [J. Chem. Phys. 160, 184102 (2024)]. Our simulations reveal ring opening initiated by asymmetric ceC-O bond cleavage following direct HOMO → LUMO (ceS1) excitation. Following the selected surface hop, separate conditional trajectories on the broken-symmetry open-shell singlet and triplet potential energy surfaces lead to distinct products. The singlet trajectory yields acetaldehyde via intramolecular hydrogen transfer, while the triplet trajectory produces formaldehyde and methylene via ceC-C bond fragmentation. These products are consistent with those identified in previous photolysis experiments. Our results demonstrate that direct excitation to the lowest singlet excited state can initiate ring opening within the present TDGW-MD framework. They further reveal distinct subsequent reaction pathways under the selected spin conditions. This study highlights the potential of TDGW-MD for elucidating photoinduced reaction mechanisms from a many-body perspective.

articles.title: Material Tailored Multispectral Magnetization via the Inverse Faraday Effect in Tunable Coaxial Nanoantenna
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All-optical control of magnetization via the Inverse Faraday Effect presents a transformative pathway for ultrafast high-density data storage and nanoscale spintronics. However, unlocking its full potential requires moving beyond traditional gold-centric, narrowband constraints. In this study, we present a comprehensive theoretical framework evaluating IFE-driven static magnetic field generation across a diverse library of plasmonic materials, including gold, silver, copper, aluminum, and titanium nitride. Using a dimensionally tunable coaxial nanoantenna, we map the optomagnetic response across the deep-ultraviolet to near-infrared spectrum. Our findings reveal highly distinct, material-dependent behaviors: aluminum uniquely sustains robust magnetization in the deep-UV, whereas silver, copper, and gold exhibit superior efficiency at longer wavelengths. Crucially, we demonstrate that shifting the excitation to the near-infrared regime amplifies the generated magnetic field by several orders of magnitude, establishing these frequencies as critical for helicity-dependent all-optical switching. Furthermore, by resolving the local optical spin density, we elucidate how extreme subwavelength confinement drives synchronized drift currents, enabling efficient multispectral magnetization through localized surface plasmon resonances and higher-order Fabry-Perot modes. Strikingly, comparing these distinct modes reveals that structural geometry tunes the resonant wavelength, while the maximum achievable optomagnetic amplitude is fundamentally governed by the metal's intrinsic properties.

articles.title: Communication-Efficient Hamiltonian Evaluation for Massively Parallel Tensor-Product Bitstring Selected Configuration Interaction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme-scale selected configuration interaction (SCI) requires coordinated Hamiltonian evaluation, distributed CI-vector storage, and interprocess communication on massively parallel computers. Our previous work [J. Chem. Phys. 164, 194103 (2026)] introduced the tensor-product bitstring selected configuration interaction (TBSCI) framework, combining on-the-fly Hamiltonian evaluation with fully distributed CI-vector storage and enabling parallel diagonalization of trillion-determinant spaces on up to 54,000 Fugaku nodes. Here, we introduce FLIP, a new Hamiltonian evaluation algorithm within TBSCI that reorganizes the CI-vector layout and excitation-link data to replace remote CI-coefficient transfers for α-electron double excitations with local coefficient access and link retrieval from nearby MPI ranks. In communication-intensive full configuration interaction (FCI) benchmarks on Fugaku, no exposed communication waiting time was recorded on the slowest process across all 32 measured Hamiltonian-vector multiplications. For N₂/cc-pVTZ with 2.62×10¹² determinants, the multiplication achieved 91.3% strong-scaling efficiency from 18,000 to 81,000 nodes (more than 3.8 million compute cores). We also obtained an FCI reference potential-energy curve for N₂/cc-pVTZ. At all six bond lengths, spin bitstrings selected by their collective weights in reference SCI wavefunctions yielded variational TBSCI energies within 0.1 mEₕ of FCI using fewer than 1% of the FCI determinants, demonstrating the compactness of the tensor-product bitstring representation. Finally, we discuss local construction of double-excitation links to substantially reduce communication volume and eliminate persistent storage of precomputed double-link tables for future second-order perturbation theory calculations with large external determinant spaces.

articles.title: Experimental observation of higher-harmonic generation of whistler waves in magnetized plasma of Large Volume Plasma Device
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the higher-harmonic generation of whistler waves using a loop antenna in the Large Volume Plasma Device (LVPD). The antenna is energized using a pulse-forming network (PFN), and the excited magnetic fluctuations are measured using a three-axis B-dot probe. Experiments are performed in a moderate-density (nₑ sim 1-2 × 10¹⁷ m⁻³), low-temperature (Tₑ sim 2-5 eV) argon plasma in a uniform axial magnetic field (B_z sim 6.2 G). A Helmholtz coil is employed to investigate the dependence of the wave response and propagation on the local magnetic-field configuration. A clear distinction between wave characteristics is observed in the absence and presence of plasma: in plasma, the excited wave shows a significant δ B_y component along with δ Bₓ, indicating polarization. In addition to the fundamental frequency, distinct spectral peaks are observed at 300 kHz, 450 kHz, and 600 kHz. These harmonics indicate nonlinear wave-plasma interactions, and bicoherence analysis further provides evidence of nonlinear coupling between the observed frequency components. The spatial propagation of the wave was systematically diagnosed using a linear array of five identical B-dot probes. Spatial cross-correlation analysis reveals strong structural coherence during wave propagation, allowing the explicit experimental determination of the wave phase velocity (Vₚₕ) and parallel wave number (kₚₐᵣₐₗₗₑₗ) for the generated higher harmonics. The measured propagation is oblique at an angle of approximately 48^circ with respect to the background magnetic field, and the experimental dispersion relation agrees with the cold-plasma oblique whistler dispersion relation within experimental uncertainty.

articles.title: Condensation-related expansion work of water vapor as a major pathway for kinetic energy generation in the lower atmosphere
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Earth's atmosphere operates a steam cycle: water evaporates from the surface, expands as vapor, condenses in colder air, and returns as precipitation. Yet its power and relationship to atmospheric mechanical power remain poorly quantified. Applying the Clausius--Clapeyron relation between saturated vapor expansion work and latent heat converted at Carnot efficiency to vertically distributed condensation, we derive the steam-engine power as a sum of the gravitational and condensation-related contributions, Wᵥ=W_g+W_c; it is not the net power of a complete moist-air cycle. Using twelve years of GPM/DPR spectral latent-heating profiles and MERRA-2 fields, we estimate Wᵥsimeq4.1 W m⁻², with W_csimeq2.8 W m⁻². Separately, we diagnose total atmospheric mechanical power W=W_P+W_Ksimeq4.3 W m⁻², comprising gravitational power of precipitation W_Psimeq1.1 W m⁻² and kinetic energy generation W_Ksimeq3.2 W m⁻², including 2.4 W m⁻² below 500 hPa. Both correspondences Wᵥsimeq W and W_csimeq W_K lie within 20--30% uncertainty estimates. To explain these correspondences, we propose that W_c generates the potential energy associated with surface pressure gradients. Cross-isobaric flow in the frictional lower atmosphere converts this energy into kinetic energy. In a horizontally isothermal atmosphere, this positive pressure work would be nearly cancelled by compression aloft. An idealized circulation illustrates how differential heating can offset compression, allowing nearly isobaric upper return flow. In the proposed mechanism, condensation-driven circulation unlocks this thermal compensation thus providing a major pathway for lower-atmospheric kinetic energy generation. We discuss how changes in the coupling between condensation and differential heating could test this proposed causal relationship.

articles.title: Particle Identification Studies using a Highly Granular Crystal Electromagnetic Calorimeter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A proposal for the Circular Electron Positron Collider electromagnetic calorimeter is a highly granular scintillating crystal design that uses silicon photomultipliers to measure physics signals from photons. The potential to develop particle identification methods using deep and traditional machine learning is explored. A contrastive machine learning technique was found to enable the separation of showering and 'punch-through' pions without explicit labels. A supervised particle identification method was then trained using the results, using both a graph neural network and a boosted decision tree to distinguish electron, showering hadron, and minimum-ionizing-particle-like events. The classifier achieved an area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.996 for both cases. A Shapley additive explanations analysis showed the boosted decision tree classifier matched expectations for each event type. The particle identification capability is then demonstrated on experimental data taken from the CERN Proton Synchrotron T9 beamline.

articles.title: Reconstruction and Forecast of Extreme Waves from a Single Observation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The state space of a dynamical system can, under suitable conditions, be reconstructed from a single observational time-series through delay-coordinate embedding. However, reconstructing the spatiotemporal evolution of nonlinear water waves from highly sparse measurements remains a considerable challenge. Here, by combining deep learning, compressed sensing, and the self-similarity properties of unidirectional nonlinear water wave evolution equation, we show that the evolving surface elevation of a highly nonlinear wave field can be reconstructed from observations collected at a it single measurement location. We subsequently use these reconstructions to forecast rogue waves associated with self-focusing soliton dynamics from point observations obtained in controlled water wave tank experiments, demonstrating excellent agreement with measurements of the fully evolved wave field. Our results show that extreme wave events can be forecast from remarkably sparse observations and provide a framework that may be extended to other nonlinear dispersive systems governed by the interplay of dispersion and nonlinearity.

articles.title: Subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic waves for enhancing Brillouin gain in a planar waveguide structure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a planar waveguide structure consisting of two layers separated by a gap that provides subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic modes and a large overlap integral between them. This, in turn, leads to an increase in Brillouin gain. Using the structure of two Si₃N₄ layers with a subwavelength gap from SiO₂ as an example, we demonstrate that a hybridized transverse-magnetic (TM) optical mode exhibits strong field confinement in the SiO₂ gap. Simultaneously, a high-frequency acoustic mode can be confined in the same gap, providing a high spatial overlap between the optical and acoustic fields. This provides a high opto-acoustic interaction with a Brillouin gain up to 5 W⁻¹m⁻¹. The proposed structure is compatible with planar photonic integration and offers a promising platform for compact, low-threshold Brillouin lasers and coherent phonon generation.

articles.title: Out-of-training properties in frozen interatomic potential embeddings are decodable and ordered by physical scale
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on energies, forces and stresses, yet their frozen representations can predict other materials properties. We probe ORB-v3 and UMA-S across layers, read-outs and equivariant channels for nine properties of 154,875 Materials Project crystals. Both models outperform composition-only descriptors on all targets, including five outside their training objectives; errors in physical units help assess potential screening applications. Optimal depth varies by property, consistent with a physical-scale ordering. Random-weight controls reveal strongly property-dependent benefits of pretraining. UMA-S's rotation-invariant angular channels improve crystal-system classification, while higher scores from its full tensor disappear under rotation; matched-model controls do not isolate equivariance as the explanation. Accuracy varies across different probes, but nearest-neighbour prediction often approaches XGBoost performance, even though materials do not form distinct clusters according to their properties. We also test whether a linear predictor trained on one model's embeddings can predict properties using the other model's embeddings after a learned linear transformation. Predictive accuracy is largely preserved, despite differences in which atoms the two models place close together. These results guide the reuse of frozen MLIP representations for materials prediction.

articles.title: An Alternative Explicitly Correlated Approach for Describing Strongly Correlated Systems within a Single-Determinant Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an alternative explicitly correlated single-reference approach for strongly correlated systems within a single-determinant framework, providing a balanced description of strong and weak electron correlations by integrating singlet-paired coupled-cluster singles and doubles with explicitly correlated theory. While the singlet interactions are captured via standard explicitly correlated terms, the triplet correlation omitted during regularization is recovered through a newly formulated explicitly correlated pseudo-excitation operator that satisfies Kato's cusp condition and integrates a full virtual space to retrieve the missing triplet-paired correlations based on the interelectronic distance. We show that CCSD0 [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 11, 3171 (2015)] is structurally related to the complex molecular orbital framework, an orbital theory that addresses the stability dilemma by yielding an energy lower than that of restricted Hartree-Fock in the presence of imaginary spin-singlet instabilities, while the symmetry dilemma is resolved via projection [J. Chem. Phys. 69, 4535 (1978)]. Prompted by this structural correspondence, we introduce the explicitly correlated "CCSD0-F12Pi" and perturbative triples methodologies. The performance of these new single-reference frameworks has been evaluated for the bond-breaking processes of N2 and CO2, and benchmarked against Mukherjee's multireference coupled-cluster method for the strongly correlated regimes of linear singlet methylene and cyclobutadiene. Our results show that the new framework systematically avoids unphysical artifacts along the potential energy surfaces while accelerating convergence toward the complete basis set limit, offering a single-reference alternative to multireference methodologies for closed-shell molecules.

articles.title: Observation of Crossover from Repulsive to Attractive Interactions between Two nS-Rydberg Atoms in Dual-Species Atom Arrays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dual-species Rydberg atom arrays provide a flexible platform for engineering long-range interactions beyond the conventional isotropic blockade regime. We spectroscopically study interactions between different s-state Rydberg levels in a ⁸⁷Rb--⁸⁵Rb optical-tweezer array. By varying the principal-quantum-number difference Δ n around 61S₁/₂, we observe a crossover from repulsive to attractive interactions. We identify a distinct regime at Δ n=2 in which Förster-enhanced electronic spin exchange dominates over orbital exchange and produces a strongly bond-orientation-dependent pair spectrum. Time-domain collective-excitation measurements reveal this geometry-dependent spin exchange through a pronounced anisotropy of the double-excitation probability. For Δ n=1, by contrast, orbital exchange dominates and the interaction is nearly isotropic. These results establish the principal-quantum-number difference and bond orientation as complementary control parameters for tailoring Rydberg interaction spectra and collective excitation dynamics, opening new opportunities for engineering spin-dependent Hamiltonians in programmable atom arrays.

articles.title: Radiofrequency disorientation in migratory birds: radical pairs or a separate sensory system?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alongside other directional cues, migratory songbirds use the Earth's magnetic field to help them navigate the hundreds or thousands of kilometres between their breeding and over-wintering sites. If it seems surprising that an animal can extract information from a magnetic field a hundred times weaker than a small refrigerator magnet, it should be astounding that this ability can be disrupted by radiofrequency magnetic fields thousands of times weaker still. Magnetic fields with strengths between 1 and 100 nT and frequencies between 0.1 and 100 MHz have been found to prevent captive night-migratory songbirds from orienting in the geomagnetic field (25-65 microtesla, depending on geographic location). Remarkably, the frequency dependence of this disruption agrees closely with predictions for radical pairs in cryptochrome (the leading hypothesis for the mechanism of the avian magnetic compass), whereas the extraordinarily weak fields that cause disorientation are difficult to reconcile with conventional radical-pair theory. This perspective examines the evidence for radiofrequency-induced disorientation and its relationship to the cryptochrome hypothesis. It concludes by considering a suggestion that birds may possess a distinct radiofrequency-sensitive system based on electromagnetic induction.

articles.title: Rotation-Invariant Machine Learning for Highly Symmetric Molecular Configurations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomistic machine learning can approximate expensive quantum mechanical calculations at a fraction of their computational cost, but accuracy depends strongly on how the three-dimensional atomic environments are represented. Invariant representations enable fast computation but can fail to distinguish geometrically distinct configurations, especially in highly symmetric environments. We introduce a lightweight benchmark to evaluate expressivity on n-fold symmetric configurations, and use it to expose degeneracies in both invariant and equivariant architectures. Guided by these results, we construct a new invariant basis for HIP-HOP which resolves most of the identified failures. On a methane simulation dataset, the extended basis achieves the lowest error among the HIP-HOP variants and has similar accuracy to EquiformerV3 while running 3.2× faster at inference. These results show that carefully constructed invariant representations can mitigate key expressivity limitations while balancing accuracy and computational efficiency.

articles.title: Multilevel AlScN Ferroelectric Diode Crossbar Arrays with Sub-200 nm Cells for Selector-Free Nonvolatile Memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Passive crossbar arrays are a leading route to high-density nonvolatile memory and in-memory computing, but without a selector the memory element itself must supply the nonlinearity that suppresses sneak-path currents. Here we scale aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) ferroelectric diodes (FeDs) in both dimensions that matter - the ferroelectric is thinned to 10 nm and the junction diameter is reduced to 100 nm. We further integrate 200 nm cells into a 2-kilobyte (128 * 128) passive crossbar. At a junction area of 0.0314 um2 this is a ~625 reduction in cell area, at equal array capacity, relative to kilobyte-scale AlScN FeD crossbars built on 5 μm cells. The 10 nm Al0.64Sc0.36N layer reverses its polarization under pulses of 50 ns full width at half maximum at a pulse-energy density of ~16 pJ μm-2, corresponding to ~0.5 pJ per 200 nm cell. Pulsed programming at 17.5 V and 1 kHz yields an ON/OFF ratio of 4.2 * 103 in a 200 nm cell, while DC characterization of 283 randomly addressed cells of the 2-kB array gives ON/OFF and rectification ratios at 5 V of 43 33 and 61 74, from which we derive the sub-array size that selector-free reading currently supports. Eight conductance levels (three bits) written into a 200 nm array cell remain resolvable for 103 s, and the two extreme states are stable beyond 5 * 104 s. Mapping the measured, nonuniformly spaced levels onto a ResNet-20 network recovers 91.7 +- 0.1 % CIFAR-10 accuracy after quantization-aware training, against a 92.2 +- 0.1 % full-precision baseline. AlScN FeDs thus combine nanosecond switching, three-bit storage and sub-0.05 μm2 cells in a BEOL-compatible, selector-free crossbar.

articles.title: Shared-State Inverse Synthesis of Dual-Mode Conformal Metasurfaces for Low Scattering and Telemetry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A conformal surface that alternates between sectoral low scattering and directive telemetry poses a shared-hardware inverse problem when both modes must use one finite passive impedance alphabet, although their spatial codebooks may differ. This paper formulates and solves that mixed continuous--discrete problem at the effective impedance-boundary level. Reference-centered Tikhonov preimages prescribe restricted radiation data; inverse-source null-space freedom then moves each current within its data-equivalent class toward impedance profiles quantizable by the same alphabet. A line-searched Gauss--Newton update, common-state assignment and projected-centroid updates, and exact forward refinement determine the currents, two codebooks, and one passive library. Data invariance, the current-to-impedance differential, the optimal state update, monotonic mismatch reduction, and a forward perturbation bound are derived. A full-mutual-coupling two-dimensional TM study of a 4λ₀-diameter cylinder uses 64 physical cells and one shared eight-state library. On a 256-unknown validation model, the worst power ratio over ±10cⁱrc monostatic sectors and incidence angles from -30cⁱrc to 30cⁱrc is -11.6~dB relative to a PEC cylinder; telemetry directivity is 13.1~dB with -13.6-dB peak sidelobes and a 1cⁱrc pointing error. A separate Fourier--Galerkin formulation, converged through 513 complex modes without reoptimization, gives -11.36~dB and 13.02~dB for the corresponding worst-sector and directivity metrics. The results establish feasibility at the effective impedance-boundary level; they do not establish unit-cell, bias-network, or platform-level realizability.

articles.title: Variational and geometric time-dependent density-functional theory of electronic systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central problem in time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) is to construct a time-dependent many-electron wave function that reproduces a prescribed time-dependent electron density. This problem admits a natural geometric interpretation, which in turn leads to at least two distinct formulations of TDDFT. The first is the usual variational formulation of TDDFT, in which the density constraint is enforced with a real-valued local potential. The second is geometric TDDFT, introduced in recent works, in which the same density constraint is enforced with an imaginary local potential, or equivalently with a Hermitian nonlocal potential. In this work, we develop this unified viewpoint for continuous electronic systems and systematically compare the two formulations. We formulate the corresponding time-dependent Kohn-Sham schemes and derive a number of exact conditions for geometric TDDFT, including conditions associated with causality, time-reversal symmetry, uniform-coordinate scaling, translational invariance, energy and momentum equations of motion, one-electron self-interaction, and the adiabatic limit. The paper also contains a mathematical section where we provide a fully rigorous justification of some parts of the text. We particularly discuss the mathematical properties of two operators underlying the two formulations of TDDFT and establish sufficient conditions for their invertibility. We explain the functional-analytic subtleties underlying the geometric interpretation of TDDFT and the two formulations of TDDFT. This unified perspective clarifies the mathematical and conceptual relation between variational and geometric TDDFT and provides a foundation for the development of approximations within geometric TDDFT.

articles.title: Controlling Mode-Locking in Liquid Light
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mode-locking is the process by which the phases of many cavity modes organize collectively into a stationary state. In lasers, mode-locking originates from the interplay of gain, loss, dispersion and nonlinearities, most commonly resulting in the emission of short pulses. However, pulse formation is prevented when the gain recovery is fast enough to suppress amplitude fluctuations. Mode-locking then produces an extended state of nearly constant intensity, whose dynamics is governed by the phase. Yet, a general framework for designing the phase of such extended photonic states remains lacking. Here we introduce a hydrodynamic approach to designing extended photonic states, in which the phase dynamics are understood and controlled as a flow of liquid-like light. The intensity, clamped by fast gain, plays the role of a constant density, the instantaneous frequency that of a flow velocity, and the programmable radio-frequency modulation applied to the laser acts as a potential landscape that controls the flow. We derive analytical solutions connecting the applied modulation to the instantaneous frequency and hence to the spectrum emitted by the laser. We further provide experimental evidence for the liquid light shaping framework by measuring the frequency comb spectra emitted by a fast-gain semiconductor laser around SI1.6microm under the control of a programmed modulation, and comparing them to the ones predicted by the analytical solution. The hydrodynamic picture of mode-locking provides a predictive design principle for frequency combs, pointing toward a programmable synthesizer of light, and establishes fast-gain lasers as an accessible, electrically driven platform for nonequilibrium fluids of light.

articles.title: A spherical body in plasma simulated with adaptive mesh and algorithm refinement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An absorbing sphere in a weakly ionized plasma is the oldest kinetic problem of probe theory. It presents key difficulties in plasma simulation: disparate velocity scales, orbital motion, phase-space regions that no characteristic of the plasma reaches, a boundary set by a kinetic flux balance, and collisions that qualitatively change the answer. We use this problem to demonstrate the Plasma Adaptive Mesh and Algorithm Refinement (PAMAR) framework introduced in a companion paper. Electrons and ions have separate solvers on their own adaptive (r,v,μ) octrees, or on reduced phase spaces at the angular-moment level (Fokker-Planck and two-stream models), coupled through a radial Poisson field solver. Two exact references, a method of characteristics for the collisionless problem and integration along the orbits for elastic scattering, audit the solvers. We compute the current-voltage characteristic of the probe on both electron and ion branches, and the profiles of the potential and of the moments of both species agree with the exact solution. Far from the sphere, the potential follows the Coulomb law in neither limit: it falls as r⁻² without collisions and as r⁻¹ only beyond the ion mean free path. With elastic electron scattering, the kinetic solver follows the exact dependence of the collected current on the mean free path, from free flight toward diffusion, to 1 percent.
