Finally, we demonstrate the ion model selection cell by cell, using a fluid model coupled to the kinetic solver, with the interface set by the pressure anisotropy; with charge exchange, a sensor of ion trapping is also needed. According to exact solutions, the ion anisotropy extends to several probe radii, much farther than the electron loss cone.

articles.title: A conditional quadrature method of moments for populations of oblate spheroidal particles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-spherical particle populations are encountered in numerous industrial processes, where particle size, shape, and velocity jointly influence transport, breakage, and classification dynamics. The resulting coupled distributions of geometric and kinematic particle properties evolve within a high-dimensional phase space whose accurate representation remains a significant challenge. We present a conditional quadrature method of moments (CQMOM) for oblate spheroidal particles described by a five-dimensional phase space that includes their size, aspect ratio, and velocity. The dimensionality of the problem is reduced by assuming that the particles continuously adopt their drag-maximizing orientation. In the solution algorithm, the resulting conditional quadrature representation of the particle phase space is combined with a Strang splitting of the continuous and discontinuous mathematical operators governing the moment transport. We verify this CQMOM framework against Monte Carlo simulations of the same particle model for representative test cases of increasing complexity, including drag, breakage, recoil, and attrition, at different Stokes numbers. With two nodes per coordinate, the particle number, the mean size, and the mean aspect ratio agree with the Monte Carlo solution within its statistical uncertainty, and the velocity statistics to within 7 %. Time-step and quadrature resolution studies identify the conditional velocity quadrature as the main source of the remaining deviations, for which we discuss potential remedies. Overall, the results demonstrate that the conditional quadrature representation preserves the geometric-kinematic correlations of the particle population in a five-dimensional phase space, at a cost more than 60 times lower than that of a single Monte Carlo realization.

articles.title: Local topology hallucinations in universal machine-learned interatomic potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting metastable states with universal machine-learned interatomic potentials requires that they preserve the minima and saddles of the reference potential-energy surface. Here we identify local topology hallucination, in which distinct model minima relax into the same reference basin. This failure arises from mode-selective curvature-sign errors shared by MACE, CHGNet and M3GNet. Curvature signs predicted by two of the three models agreed with density-functional calculations in 55 of 57 positive but only 5 of 56 negative cases. In LiGe₂S, two MACE minima connected by a verified saddle relaxed into one density-functional basin. Reference relaxation likewise returned nine of ten selected model minima to their reference basins. A directional test with two displaced reference calculations rejected 9 of 12 prospectively tested model instabilities. Model agreement alone therefore cannot establish that predicted minima are distinct metastable states.

articles.title: Run it Back: Autoregression vs. Video Diffusion for Final-Conditioned Weather Trajectories
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-likelihood, high-impact extremes are projected to increase in severity and frequency in a warming climate. Sampling the precursors that lead to these events traditionally requires massive ensembles that scale poorly with lead time and rarity, and typical rare-event sampling and ensemble-boosting methods do not show how a single extreme might arise from diverse synoptic precursors. Recently, Lin et al. (2026) showed this is possible with final-conditioned 66-hour trajectories (trajectories constrained to end at an observed state) from cBottle-video, a pre-trained, off-the-shelf video diffusion climate emulator not explicitly fine-tuned for this task (Brenowitz et al., 2025). However, its ensembles were underdispersed and geostrophically inconsistent, and it reproduces conditioned frames only approximately, hindering autoregressive rollout. Here, we train Rewind-AR, a backward-in-time probabilistic autoregressive model with a FourCastNet~3 backbone (Bonev et al., 2025), and generate final-conditioned ensembles for the same three cases: the 2021 Pacific Northwest heatwave, Hurricane Ian, and Superstorm Sandy (in the Supplementary Information). The leading modes of Rewind-AR's antecedent 500 hPa geopotential height explain far more of the across-member variance than cBottle-video's for both hurricane position and heatwave surface temperature, and Rewind-AR better reproduces the day-over-day heatwave intensification observed in ERA5. Finally, geostrophic inconsistencies close to the conditioning frame seen in cBottle-video are not reproduced by Rewind-AR. Nevertheless, up to 22% of Rewind-AR members become numerically unstable within 66 hours, so improving rollout physical consistency and stability over long lead times is a natural next step.

articles.title: Drift of a Charged Particle in a Black Hole Magnetosphere: the Effect of Black Hole Spin
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sparse plasma immersed in a strong magnetic field is common in astrophysical scenarios, for which a collisionless description is more appropriate. The guiding-center approximation serves as an effective tool for describing the motion of charged particles in a strong magnetic field, revealing the drift, a sub-leading order motion that causes particles to deviate from the magnetic field lines. It is widely accepted that the charged particles drift under the induction of gravity in Newtonian framework. However, a covariant formulation of the guiding-center approximation, as well as the drift of a charged particle induced by strong gravitational field, has yet to be fully explored. As a preliminary study, we aim to analyze the drift of a single charged particle in a black hole magnetosphere via a covariant approach. Particularly, we focus on the effects of black hole spin. We first examine the drift caused by the rotation of a massive object in the Newtonian regime using the language of gravitoelectromagnetism. A covariant formula of drift is derived, which is confirmed to reduce to the Newtonian results in the weak gravitational field and low speed limit. The impact of BH spin on the drift is analyzed in detail in Kerr spacetime specifically, for which we define the drift rate whose value quantifies the significance of the drift. Our results indicate that the impact of BH spin on the drift of a charged particle in a BH magnetosphere can be comparable to that of other factors in some extreme cases.

articles.title: A Hybrid State Space-Attention Architecture for Forecasting the Trajectories of Battery Degradation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Early-life battery degradation trajectory forecasting aims to predict a battery cell's full state-of-health (SOH) trajectory from its initial charge-discharge cycles, potentially reducing cell qualification and evaluation time from months to days. Despite recent advances, accurate forecasting remains challenging for emerging battery chemistries, data-scarce domains, and cells exhibiting degradation behaviors beyond those observed during training. Existing state-of-the-art approaches increasingly rely on model scaling, large language model-derived aging-condition embeddings, and extensive fold-specific hyperparameter tuning, raising concerns about computational efficiency, reproducibility, and generalization. This work introduces DecayFormer, a compact hybrid state-space and attention architecture designed for early-life degradation trajectory forecasting. DecayFormer combines cycle-level selective recurrence, using a single scalar state per channel, with an attention mechanism queried by the recurrent state. It further incorporates state-of-charge (SOC) interval statistics and a master curve head that jointly estimates a scalar lifetime and a monotonically non-increasing SOH profile parameterized by normalized lifetime. We evaluate DecayFormer on the BatteryLife benchmark using all 22 aging-condition-exclusive folds, with a single run per fold and one fixed configuration across all folds, without fold-specific tuning. DecayFormer achieves mean test MAPE values of 2.25% on Li-ion, 2.76% on CALB, 0.95% on Na-ion, and 7.19% on Zn-ion. These results demonstrate the potential of compact sequence models to deliver accurate early-life degradation forecasts across diverse battery chemistries and aging conditions, without relying on extensive model scaling or per-fold optimization.

articles.title: Radial Evolution of a Corotating Interaction Region from a High-Resolution MHD Simulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19438v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are large-scale structures formed by fast--slow solar wind interaction, playing a crucial role in heliospheric dynamics and space weather. However, the evolution of individual CIRs and their full three-dimensional morphology remain poorly understood. We investigate the radial evolution of a single CIR using a high-resolution simulation combined with a backmapping method. The simulation reproduces the major plasma and magnetic signatures observed by Wind at 1~AU and by MAVEN and Tianwen-1 at sim1.6~AU. The CIR exhibits a warped, shell-like spiral structure tilted relative to the heliospheric current sheet, consistent with theoretical predictions. During its developing stage, geometric changes are modest, and the radial scalings of velocity (Vᵣ propto r⁰.⁰²), density (N propto r⁻².⁰⁰), magnetic field (Bᵣₘ ₜₒₜₐₗ propto r⁻¹.⁷⁴), and temperature (T propto r⁻⁰.⁹⁷) are comparable to those of the background solar wind. In the mature stage, the CIR drifts in longitude and expands toward high latitudes, while its longitudinal and latitudinal widths decrease with distance. The full-domain scalings change markedly to Vᵣ propto r⁰.¹³, N propto r⁻¹.⁹¹, Bᵣₘ ₜₒₜₐₗ propto r⁰.³⁵, and T propto r⁻⁰.⁵², differing from both the background wind and the ecliptic-plane CIR. This study quantifies the radial evolution of a CIR from formation to maturity and highlights the importance of its three-dimensional structure in characterizing its morphology and dynamics.

articles.title: Federated versus Centralized PV Capacity-Factor Forecasting: A Non-Inferiority Study Across Seven Stations in North Macedonia
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Background: Photovoltaic (PV) forecasts inform energy commitments by PV operators and aggregators and guide charge-discharge scheduling in solar-plus-storage systems. Federated learning enables collaborative model training through model updates when local operators cannot pool raw operational data. This study evaluated whether federated training was non-inferior to centralized training for PV capacity-factor prediction across seven stations in North Macedonia. A common multilayer perceptron was used in an offline forecasting comparison with a 24-hour timestamp lag. Exploratory validation compared local, centralized, Federated Averaging, and Federated Proximal (FedProx) training. FedProx (E = 1, mu = 1) was selected for a confirmatory comparison under a protocol fixed before test evaluation. The comparison used past-only offline inputs, five paired training seeds, macro-averaged mean absolute error (MAE), a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 0.005, and a paired day bootstrap with 10,000 repetitions over 49 test dates. Results: FedProx achieved a macro-MAE of 0.128397, compared with 0.133405 for centralized training. The paired difference (FedProx minus centralized) was -0.005008 (95% confidence interval: [-0.009926, -0.000537]). The upper confidence bound was below the prespecified margin, satisfying the non-inferiority criterion. All five seed-specific differences favored FedProx, and its mean MAE was lower at six of the seven stations. Post hoc calendar sensitivity analyses did not change the conclusion. Conclusions: These findings support further evaluation of federated forecasting for collaboration under data-pooling constraints. The study demonstrates predictive non-inferiority within the evaluated setting. Benefits for energy commitments and battery scheduling remain potential applications requiring operational evaluation.

articles.title: Sharp First-Hit Identification from Finite Depth Samples
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Which depths in a new camera view are determined by finitely many source-depth measurements? Pointwise uncertainty bounds do not answer this question: unobserved geometry between samples can change which surface is encountered first. We study a bounded Lipschitz class of continuous source inverse-depth fields with interval observations and known camera pose. Building on classical Lipschitz envelopes, we characterize the exact set of attainable first-hit depths and construct a globally admissible scene for every value in that set. The set can be disconnected. We also give a necessary and sufficient test for several proposed depths to be first hits of one shared scene. An epipolar reduction uses scalar cone inequalities without enumerating surfaces. In a rectified model with source spacing h, interval half-width ε, baseline b, and slope bound L, we prove a sharp worst-case inverse-depth diameter of maxLh+2ε,2ε/(1-bL) when bL<1, subject to sufficient depth and domain range for attainment. Exact samples still give the sharp bound Lh at bL=1, while above this threshold ambiguity need not vanish as sampling becomes arbitrarily dense. Any positive measurement uncertainty can destroy uniform stability at the critical threshold. We provide constructive examples, an exact rational validation oracle, and a frozen ten-scene evaluation using reference, stereo, and learned-depth observations. The experiments separate solver correctness under the scene assumptions from failure of those assumptions: fixed learned-depth bands often yield narrow but incorrect sets. The results identify what a specified scene class permits; they do not infer a continuum regularity or physical-scene guarantee from sampled predictions.

articles.title: Well-Log Reconstruction with Pre-trained Geological Knowledge: A Knowledge-Conditioned Large-Language-Model Generative Agent
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Missing well-log intervals make subsurface reconstruction ill-posed. Existing numerical regression models lack geological prior knowledge to constrain ambiguous inverse mappings. We propose GeoLog-Agent, a knowledge-conditioned generative agent using pre-trained large language models (LLMs) as a source of geological priors. A universal Geo-Harness translates LLM stratigraphic reasoning into formation-anchored petrophysical trajectories, feature-wise linear modulation, and conditional adversarial constraints. On the Norwegian North Sea benchmark, GeoLog-Agent achieves a mean R² of 0.9307 and a peak R² of 0.9713. It exceeds the nine-baseline average R² of 0.8387 by 0.0920, with a 30.97% average RMSE reduction, and exceeds the strongest baseline by 0.0274--0.0498 in R², with 16.25%--24.05% lower RMSE. Ablations confirm the effectiveness and synergy of geological prior reasoning, multi-scale dilated generation, and conditional adversarial modules. Transferring the coupling mechanism to six conventional deep learning models improves their R² by 0.0162--0.0789 with cross-well stability. These results demonstrate how foundation-model domain reasoning can constrain deep generative reconstruction of missing petrophysical measurements.

articles.title: Robust Well-Log Reconstruction Across Point Gaps and Whole Wells via Boundary-Gated Soft-Thresholding Kalman Fusion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Missing wireline logs hinder subsurface characterization. Deep reconstruction networks suffer from gap-boundary steps and cross-basin shifts, while interpolation and Gaussian smoothers struggle with long intervals and outliers. We propose boundary-gated soft-thresholding Kalman fusion (ST-KF), unifying multiresolution wavelet shrinkage, distance-gated residual prior learning, and closed-form robust Kalman smoothing with learning--inference decoupling. Across two public benchmarks totaling 263 wells in the Norwegian North Sea and New Zealand's Taranaki Basin, ST-KF ranks first over 0.15--100-m anchored gaps with 0.09% parameter overhead. Against the strongest of nine baselines, pooled RMSE falls by 5.0%--8.3% for bulk density and 6.4%--15.6% for compressional slowness; against the four strongest baselines, reductions are 0.7%--4.1% for neutron porosity and 1.3%--2.9% for photoelectric factor. Ablations and sensitivity analyses confirm operator synergy and stable performance: removing state-space fusion increases short-gap errors by up to 58.8%, while zero-shot transfer cuts anchored errors by 14%--68%. The results show that local borehole continuity transfers across basins whereas cross-property mappings shift with regional geology, supporting measurement-guided log reconstruction.

articles.title: Score-Based Stochastic Closure Modeling via Offline Indirect Learning and Online Data Assimilation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. However, learning stochastic closures typically requires closure data that are difficult to obtain from measurements or often prohibitively expensive to compute using first-principles simulations. In this work, we develop a stochastic closure modeling framework that builds on score-based diffusion models, leveraging indirect offline training and online data assimilation without requiring the direct data of closures. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional turbulent flows demonstrate that indirect offline learning captures key closure statistics and improves predictions of system state. In addition, combining the learned closure with known physical dynamics leads to better generalization capability across different regimes than purely data-driven models that directly predict system state. Compared to standard data assimilation methods with a Gaussian assumption, the posterior-score assimilation better represents non-Gaussian features of the learned closure, and its combination with state-level data assimilation further improves prediction of the system state. The proposed framework enables stochastic closure modeling in realistic and challenging scenarios of complex dynamical systems in mechanics and engineering problems, where non-Gaussian statistics of model-form uncertainties are non-negligible (e.g., due to the nonlinearities of the system dynamics and/or the observations) and true closure data are not available, for both offline learning and online assimilation.

articles.title: When Zero Is Competitive: A Descriptive Pilot of Transformer and Gate-Graph Surrogates on Random-Angle Quantum Circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine supervised classical prediction of all one-qubit Z and two-qubit ZZ expectation values on noiseless, layered 4-10-qubit RX/RY/RZ-CNOT circuits. In a 63-cell stratified workload with disjoint circuit-template tests, we evaluate one transformer encoder and gate-dependency graph neural networks against literal-zero and training-derived constant predictors. On the Arm K training labels, 44.89% of scalar targets have absolute magnitude below 0.05. The held-out-template zero predictor has equal-instance mean absolute error 0.193399, and none of the evaluated transformer checkpoints or final graph-network endpoints achieves a lower score. A separate product-state positive control achieves MAE 0.007755 versus 0.514811 for zero, but does not explain the failure on the entangled workload. The difference between zero and a training-fitted mean constant under training MSE is only 0.14%, a descriptive point estimate without uncertainty analysis. The transformer's 815,233-parameter source identity is locally verified; detailed packed-input semantics have not been independently audited. These results constitute a descriptive pilot, not a causal explanation, formal equivalence test, or impossibility claim. Comparable circuits can be regenerated from the workload specification, but exact frozen datasets and model-run evidence remain private.

articles.title: QA-CMIF:Accurate and Lightweight Cross-Modal Latent Imputation and Fusion for Fault-Tolerant sEMG-Inertial Hand Gesture Recognition
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fusing surface electromyography (sEMG) with inertial measurements is widely used for myoelectric prosthesis control and wearable human-machine interfaces. In daily wear, however, socket micro-displacement, electrode lift-off, and wire failures often corrupt an unknown subset of sEMG channels through burst artifacts, lift-off shocks, or open-circuit dropouts. Existing fusion networks mix all channels in the first convolutional layer, so a few corrupted electrodes contaminate the entire latent representation, whereas gate-only attenuation of corrupted channels discards the co-activation cues needed to separate fine-grained gestures. We propose QA-CMIF, a quality-aware cross-modal latent imputation and fusion framework that encodes each sEMG channel independently, scores its reliability with a soft gate, and protects intact channels via a confidence-weighted residual bypass, while a cross-attention imputer repairs degraded channels in latent space using the inertial stream and remaining reliable sEMG channels under a bad-channel alignment loss. Across within-subject evaluations on 29 participants from Ninapro DB3, DB2, and DB5 spanning 17-52 gesture classes, QA-CMIF outperformed the gate-only baseline under 50% channel corruption by 1.29-2.65 percentage points, denoted pp, across all three 17-class cohorts with paired-t Holm-adjusted p<0.002, widened this margin to 2.59-4.15 pp on the 40- and 52-class tasks, and surpassed corruption-augmented conventional fusion by 4.61-19.85 pp. Requiring only 0.175-0.185M parameters and 2.45-2.63M multiply-accumulate operations across the 2000 Hz and 200 Hz setups, QA-CMIF saves 46%-55% in parameters and 72%-81% in compute over recent baselines with a 1.44 ms 99th-percentile single-thread CPU latency.

articles.title: A Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-Head Attention Model: A Surrogate for Parallel DEVS Semiconductor Fab Simulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semiconductor factories process many kinds of wafers organized into lots of various sizes and configurations. Different kinds of machines, each with its own operations, process wafers for hours to days, and the wafers undergo many incremental fabrication steps (with re-entry) and flows spanning days to weeks across connected machines. Fast and accurate predictions of throughput (TH) and turnaround time (TA) dynamics for individual machines and their combinations are essential for factory operations. To use machine learning methods for this purpose, this paper presents a Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-head Attention (TCNA) architecture. It uses simulated datasets from a benchmark Parallel DEVS (PDEVS) semiconductor fabrication factory model. The factory processes configurable wafer lots with uniform and sinusoidal wafer arrival profiles and may undergo preventive maintenance. The wafer lot size, arrival profile, and factory maintenance policy are used as static covariates. TCNA is applied to a selected set of simulated discrete-event throughput and turnaround time trajectories. The TH and TA time series predicted by TCNA, evaluated with the common MAPE, MSE, and R² measures, show comparable or higher accuracy relative to other model architectures, with similar parameter counts and epoch times; the TCNA model size and execution time are similar to those of other architectures such as the Temporal Fusion Transformer. Although time series predictions are less accurate than high-resolution simulations, they can be deployed at a much lower computational cost. The TCNA achieves orders-of-magnitude speedup over PDEVS simulation with an acceptable loss of accuracy, enabling frequent product scheduling, capacity planning, and maintenance planning.

articles.title: Quantum Computing-Based Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks for Airfoil Parameterization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Airfoil geometry parameterization is essential in aerodynamic design optimization. Optimization search in the large space suffers from low efficiency and modest feasible region, which could further incur failures to convergence. Generative adversarial networks (GAN), aiming to learn the statistical distribution of existing data, pave a new avenue for shape generation and airfoil parameterization. GAN manages to implicitly reduce design space by generating only smooth, realistic airfoils. Meanwhile, quantum computing has been emergingly exhibiting great potential for achieving superior performance in specific types of engineering problems but has not been introduced to airfoil parameterization. To fill this gap, this work develops quantum computing-based Wasserstein GAN (Q-WGAN) and investigates the performance for airfoil parameterization. The Q-WGAN adopts parameterized quantum circuits as the generator to promote the generative performance, while the discriminator remains classical. The developed Q-WGAN is demonstrated on a dataset of optimal airfoils parameterized by free-form deformation (FFD) control points, resulting from 992 airfoil aerodynamic design optimizations. Results show that Q-WGAN achieves 92.1% mean fitting accuracy on the optimal FFD control points and 99.2% accuracy on airfoil coordinates, comparable with the classical WGAN performance of 92.28% on FFD control points and 99.26% on airfoil coordinates. Q-WGAN achieves lower Jensen-Shannon divergence, Fréchet distance, and Wasserstein distance than the classical WGAN, indicating an improved agreement with the reference airfoil distribution. Therefore, this work presents a convincing evidence that Q-WGAN makes a viable option for parameterizing airfoils and possesses a great potential for other relevant engineering applications.

articles.title: Newton-PINet: A fast physics-informed neural network with Newton linearization for meta-learning nonlinear PDEs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific machine learning has opened new avenues for solving parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs), enabling models to learn a family of PDEs and generalize to unseen instances. In this context, data-driven operator learning methods typically require large training datasets, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) suffer from difficult optimization and limited generalization, especially for nonlinear PDEs. We propose Newton-PINet, a physics-informed network enhanced by Newton linearization, offering an effective meta-learning framework for nonlinear PDEs. Newton-PINet (i) employs a physics-informed multilayer network with skip connections, where the output-layer weights are solved by least squares; (ii) adopts a two-stage learning strategy that first leverages gradient-based training to learn robust representations from the available training tasks, and then performs gradient-free fine-tuning on the output layer for fast task-specific generalization; and (iii) incorporates a Newton linearization method to speed up the least-squares iteration for nonlinear PDE problems. On a challenging nonlinear reaction-diffusion benchmark, Newton-PINet achieves up to three orders of magnitude lower relative error than recent neural solvers, while using 16x fewer training tasks and over an order of magnitude less training time (about 5 minutes versus several hours). This work advances the meta-learning of PINNs toward data-efficient, fast, and generalizable physics solvers. The code and datasets are publicly available at: https://github.com/fycAIwj/Newton-PINet.

articles.title: Hierarchical Regime-Conditioned Dynamics for Spatiotemporal Graphs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forecasting the behavior of spatio-temporal systems often requires more than accurate predictions: models should uncover the dynamical modes governing future evolution. Existing temporal graph and latent dynamical models achieve strong forecasting performance, but their latent representations often entangle multiple dynamical patterns, limiting interpretability. Conversely, regime-inference methods explicitly model such modes but typically do not support generative forecasting over graph-structured systems. We introduce HERON, a self-supervised regime-aware generative framework that unifies graph-structured trajectory generation with regime identification. HERON factorizes the latent state into discrete system-level regimes, capturing global dynamical modes, and continuous entity-level dynamics, yielding a modular regime interface compatible with existing spatio-temporal backbones. Crucially, the inferred regime actively conditions system dynamics, enabling regime tracking and controlled simulations under alternative dynamical modes. Without regime annotations, HERON jointly learns forecasts and regime dynamics in a self-supervised manner, recovering meaningful modes across controlled synthetic and real-world datasets while maintaining competitive forecasting performance. These results open a path toward interpretable, controllable generative modeling of spatio-temporal dynamics.

articles.title: Over-the-Air Semantic Alignment via Dual Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semantic communications enable task-oriented information exchange, but suffer from latent-space mismatch when transmitter and receiver employ heterogeneous machine learning models. Existing semantic alignment methods rely on digital processing, introducing computational and latency overhead. This paper proposes a dual stacked intelligent metasurfaces (dual-SIM) architecture that performs semantic alignment entirely in the wave domain. By jointly exploiting programmable metasurfaces at both ends of a link and the wireless channel, the proposed architecture realizes an end-to-end linear transformation between heterogeneous latent spaces. We show phase-only multilayer SIM can approximate both supervised linear aligners and zero-shot Parseval-frame equalizers. We investigate single-SIM, disjoint asymmetric and symmetric dual-SIM, and jointly optimized dual-SIM configurations, considering channel equalization and constructive channel exploitation. For joint design, we develop an alternating projected gradient algorithm with convergence guarantees to first-order stationary points. We further introduce a deep-unrolled network that unrolls gradient-based iterations to reduce computational cost of SIM reconfiguration under channel variations. Numerical results with heterogeneous vision transformer encoders show accurate semantic alignment from moderate to high signal-to-noise ratios. The joint and symmetric disjoint dual-SIM designs achieve the highest accuracy over compact channels, the joint design leads at shallow stack depths, and the advantage over single-SIM designs diminishes at equal depth.

articles.title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension. In the present work, we establish this acceleration simultaneously in both aspects for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. More precisely, for target measures μ(dx)propto e⁻U⁽x⁾dx with m-strongly convex, L-gradient Lipschitz, and L_H-Frobenius Hessian Lipschitz potentials, we show that the method mixes to ε-accuracy in total variation using mathcal Obigl((κ¹/²+L_H¹/²m⁻³/⁴),d¹/⁴bigr) gradient evaluations up to logarithmic factors, both uniformly over starting points in domains of high equilibrium probability and from warm starts. The proof incorporates ideas from previous studies by Bou-Rabee and Chen et al. that show either aspect of acceleration separately, into novel coupling technology. This new coupling technology for general Markov chains extends earlier frameworks aimed at capturing fast local equilibration in the presence of slow global mixing. Specifically, via a weak-(1,1) maximal inequality that follows from Hopf's maximal ergodic theorem, we uncover a stability mechanism in high-probability domains with respect to equilibrium. This enables straightforward localization to naturally arising domains of fast local mixing, and seamlessly fits broad local frameworks via Dobrushin contraction, Wasserstein contraction and local Harris' theorems. We develop the Dobrushin formulation.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Joint Source and Parameter Estimation in Advection-Diffusion Equations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.07755v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Source inversion problems under sparse measurements for parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs) are particularly challenging to solve using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), due to their severe ill-posedness and the multiple unknowns involved including the source function and the PDE parameters. Although the neural tangent kernel (NTK) of PINNs has been widely used in forward problems involving a single neural network, its extension to inverse problems involving multiple neural networks remains less explored. In this work, we propose a weighted adaptive approach based on the NTK of PINNs including multiple networks representing the solution, the unknown source, and the PDE parameters. The key idea behind our methodology is to simultaneously solve the joint recovery of these unknowns thereby using the underlying PDE as a constraint that couples multiple unknowns functional parameters, leading to more efficient use of the limited information in the measurements. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis of the approximation error of PINNs in a source inverse problem governed by the advection-diffusion equation (ADE) with known velocity and diffusion coefficients. In particular, we derive an error bound for the estimated source function in terms of the PINN's training error, the noise level and the discretization error. This analysis provides theoretical insight into the factors influencing the approximation accuracy. We present numerical experiments on 2D and 3D ADE using different types of measurements data reflecting practical engineering systems. Our results demonstrate the successful performance of PINNs in solving our source inversion problem and its robustness to noise in the measurements.

articles.title: Kähler landscapes for complex neural network descents and guarantees including a search and destroy of the Calabi-Yau manifold
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.19584v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study landscapes for complex-parameterized networks. Our approach is motivated with an information-theoretic manifold perspective of the parameter and via classical optimization guarantees although of complex geometric variety such as through Dolbeault asymptotics. The descent path admits a Kähler information metric under a cross-entropy via the Wirtinger Hessian on the log-likelihood potential. We descend according to a differentiated loss scaled by the inverse metric, so the descent path remains in the holomorphic tangent bundle. We emphasize information manifolds which profane theoretical guarantees via ill-curvature-conditioned, or lack thereof, landscapes. We focus on Calabi-Yau metrics specifically in a non-compact setting with a global potential, so defined geometrically rather than invoking the topological requirements of the Calabi conjecture. In non-compact settings, we can write the metric determinant with respect to a background in terms of a function, pluriharmonic or real. Using Yau's Liouville theorem, we get a small eigenvalue blow-up effect under nontrivial background interaction, geometric invariance of the endomorphism constant, and almost low rank assumptions. In an empirical setting, a Ricci-flat metric will not form, but large eigenvalues can be a local condition and hold empirically on open sets even in generalized Kähler cases due to lower bounds on the Ricci potential. Moreover, it has been discovered that negative curvature subverts the loss landscape, specifically sectional curvature, so we expand on this and draw interconnections to negative-definite Ricci curvature. Our arguments primarily exist via geometric modality, although we establish roots in deep learning theory such as through asymptotics at initialization and connections through failure modes of neural network guarantees under vanishing and negative Ricci curvature.

articles.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior. Following a watch-act-rewatch paradigm, the agent extracts procedural guidance from tutorial videos containing visual demonstrations and spoken explanations, executes tasks, and verifies its progress by rewatching its execution as video. We instantiate VEX with video-SALMONN-VEX, a 9B-scale audio-visual computer-use agent built on the video-SALMONN 2 architecture with a Qwen3.5-9B backbone. We further introduce Action-Grounded Guide Optimization (AGGO), a reinforcement learning method that optimizes video-derived guidance for downstream action prediction, and augment AgentNet, OSWorld, and CUA-Gym with over 24K real-world tutorial videos. Experiments on OSWorld and a complementary subset of CUA-Gym demonstrate consistent improvements, with video-SALMONN-VEX achieving a 22% relative increase in task success over its Qwen3.5 backbone on OSWorld. Moreover, its generated guidance improves Gemini-3.5-flash by 10% relatively on OSWorld. These results highlight the potential of audio-visual understanding as a unified interface for procedural learning and self-verification in computer-use agents.

articles.title: CLEAR: Legible and Steerable Recommendation via Grounded Natural-Language Interests
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern recommenders keep learned preferences in representations people cannot inspect or change. We present CLEAR (Controllable and Legible End-to-end Architecture for Recommendation), an end-to-end system deployed at Meta and built around an editable natural-language interest layer. CLEAR makes a ranked subset of inferred interests readable and stores accepted additions and suppressions as authoritative preference state. Behavioral grounding maps each inferred interest back to supporting events in the user's own history. The resulting interest object is also a serving address: its label and profile-conditioned rewrites drive lexical retrieval, its supporting events seed behavioral retrieval, its projection queries an embedding index, and its stable identity supports ranking, attribution, and exposure control. A fresh user declaration may precede behavioral support, so it enters through the same serving identity and initially draws candidates from topical retrieval. Ranking makes those candidates competitive, while a delivery controller observes attributable exposure and replenishes underexposed interests. Direct user review found that users rated about 88.5% of displayed interests accurate. In an offline benchmark using a shared evaluation protocol, the Specialized 3B generator reached 0.3967 mean-user F1@10, compared with 0.3633 for Gemini 2.5 Pro and 0.1911 for the prior generator. For a newly declared interest, a user-randomized cumulative ablation measured same-day delivery losses of 8.7 percentage points for added-interest ranking terms, 11.1 for reserved top-slot insertion, and 13.7 for interest-conditioned candidate sourcing, conditional on the tested removal sequence. CLEAR components have operated in production for over one year; the system spans four surfaces on Instagram and Facebook, with an interest layer people can inspect, correct, and use to direct recommendations.

articles.title: NI-ACT: A Neural Intent Interface for Brain-Embodied Manipulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intracortical brain-computer interfaces can drive robotic arms, but they keep the user inside the fast sensorimotor loop: every approach, correction, and grasp must be neurally specified. Whether intracortical population activity can instead serve as a task-level condition for a learned embodied policy, without symbolic commands or hand-designed skill libraries, remains unknown. NI-ACT addresses this question with a hierarchical brain-embodied framework: a brief motor-cortical signal is read once as a persistent intent, and a visuomotor policy then closes the perception-action loop from vision and proprioception. In a counterfactual grasping task where the scene cannot specify the target, the neural intent alone determined which object the robot grasped; replacing the intent changed the behavior accordingly. Passing the full population latent as a dedicated intent token, rather than a one-hot decoded direction, raised grasp completion from 69% to 81% over 132 held-out scenes, whereas a continuous direction alone did not improve on a one-hot label. Where the signal was read also mattered: in one dual-array session, with the readout window matched, premotor (PMd) intent completed more grasps than primary motor (M1) intent (77% vs. 53%), and the conventional post-cue M1 readout reached 42%. Preparatory activity was itself sufficient: in a center-out task, intent read only from PMd before the go cue (that is, before any movement) drove complete grasps, and in one recording it completed more grasps than the same animal's post-cue readout. These results show that how a neural signal is represented, and where and when it is read, jointly determine how effectively it conveys movement goals to an embodied agent.

articles.title: Interactive Structured Environment Scaling for Large Language Model Agentic Reasoning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning via environmental interaction is a cornerstone post-training paradigm for evolving large language models into autonomous agents capable of multi-turn tool use and exploration. Because the environment defines what the policy observes and how actions are verified, its structure directly bounds the capabilities an agent can acquire. Yet existing structured and retrieval environments rely on upstream pre-filtering---extracting a compact subgraph around the gold answer or retrieving fixed passages before the policy acts. We show that such pre-filtering introduces a fundamental measurement confound: because per-question subgraphs enclose ground-truth paths, they compress the candidate space by orders of magnitude and leak answer locations via local topology, allowing a question-blind degree heuristic to surface gold answers far above chance. To restore path selection, candidate pruning, and optimal stopping as genuine policy decisions, we propose RISE (Interactive Structured Environment), which transitions structured reinforcement learning from static subgraphs to full-scale interactive databases along two coupled axes. First, Decision-Space Scaling exposes the unpruned knowledge graph via a five-stage graph-agnostic typed intent adapter under a bounded call budget and a multiplicative grounding reward gate. Second, Learning-Frontier Scaling overcomes within-group variance collapse under group-normalized objectives by uniting model-independent structural tier progression with a self-evolving competence-frontier bandit. Across nineteen benchmarks and three model backbones, RISE substantially advances in-domain and unseen-schema knowledge-graph reasoning, transfers zero-shot to open-domain passage retrieval, and significantly enhances out-of-domain mathematical and logical deduction.

articles.title: Dynamic Shaping: Acquiring Interfaces and Constructing Execution over Frozen Pretrained Components
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Dynamic Shaping, a method for constructing executable neural arrangements through acquired response and partial-derivative interfaces over frozen pretrained components. The method learns local descriptions of available computation, ranks component rebindings using task-gradient alignment, transports the current interface across a rebinding, and retains changes through behavioral feedback. Continuous interface acquisition uses proximal policy optimization; the source coefficients remain fixed. We derive an exact identity relating transport error in component responses and partials to changes in action logits and their sensitivities. A pixels-only ViZDoom Basic study evaluates first task acquisition without a competent reference controller, demonstrations or intact response targets. Across three initializations and 100 shared held-out game seeds, initial arrangements succeed on 86/300 controller/episode pairs; joint interface-and-binding construction succeeds on 295/300. Fixed-binding interface acquisition also reaches 295/300. Each policy executes four source fragments, with 110 acquired interface values and fixed random visual and action projections. The artifact includes all candidate trials, interventions and costs; all 1,200 recorded initial/retained outcomes replay exactly. The contribution is an explicit profile, rebind, transport and retain procedure and a reproducible reference-free acquisition case over frozen pretrained computation.

articles.title: We Have All the Cards: Securing Agent Cards at the Operational Trust Boundary of the Agent2Agent Protocol
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agent interoperability protocols enable orchestrators to discover and invoke external agents using machine-readable metadata. In the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, Agent Cards contain attacker-controllable natural-language fields that may influence agent selection before a provider is invoked, creating a pre-invocation trust problem. We characterize this discovery-time attack surface through a taxonomy of ten Agent Card manipulation attacks and present SECCARD, a layered validation framework combining protocol checks, deterministic analysis, and LLM-based semantic reasoning. We measure the emerging public A2A ecosystem by probing 36.1 million Internet domains and collecting 310 deployed Agent Cards. Two annotators independently label the corpus with 96.8% agreement. We then construct a 660-card real-card perturbation benchmark with matched benign controls and a 260-card synthetic adversarial benchmark spanning all ten attack categories. On controlled attacks injected into real Agent Cards, the strongest semantic judge achieves 97.0% security recall at a 1.7% false-positive rate. Across nine LLM judges on the synthetic benchmark, security recall ranges from 25.8% to 92.3%, demonstrating substantial model-dependent variation. These results show that SECCARD effectively identifies Agent Card manipulations spanning all ten discovery-time attack classes while preserving benign Agent Cards, but also reveal that its effectiveness depends critically on the choice of the underlying LLM judge.

articles.title: Assessing the Effects of Design Complexity and Prompt Engineering on CAD Model Generation Using Microsoft Copilot
articles.abstract: The use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly increasing across various sectors, making tasks more accessible, efficient, and user-friendly. One emerging application is computer-aided design (CAD), where AI has the potential to enable users with little or no-prior CAD experience to create three-dimensional (3D) models through natural-language. Despite growing interest in AI-assisted design, the capability of publicly accessible generative AI systems to reliably generate CAD models across varying levels of design complexity remains insufficiently studied. This work benchmarks the performance of Microsoft Copilot for CAD model generation and investigates the influence of prompt engineering on model quality. A benchmark dataset comprising 60 design tasks was developed and categorized into easy, intermediate, and complex levels. The benchmark included primitive geometries, polygonal and polyhedral models, mechanical components, hollow structures, assemblies, lattice designs, and advanced engineering systems. For each prompt, the generated STL file was evaluated based on geometric accuracy, completeness of requested features, and overall structural validity using commercial software. The results revealed a strong dependence of generation success on design complexity, with easy-level tasks exhibiting high first-attempt success rates, while intermediate and complex tasks frequently required prompt refinement. Prompt length alone was found to have minimal influence on performance; instead, successful CAD generation depended primarily on clearly specified dimensions, geometric features, and functional relationships. Overall, the findings demonstrate that generative AI can lower the barrier to CAD modeling for non-expert users while improving productivity for experienced designers, thereby offering significant potential for engineering design, rapid prototyping, and additive manufacturing applications.

articles.title: From Reservoirs to Potential Vectors of Superbugs: Wild Birds Co-Harboring Extended- Spectrum Beta-Lactamases and Plasmid-Mediated Quinolone Resistance determinants in Enterobacteriaceae isolates in Pakistan
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a significant health issue of the 21st century. Wild birds are increasingly recognized as reservoirs of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria. They are ecologically important because they have travelling ability across globe, and with no direct antimicrobial interaction making them an important part of One Health interface to predict environmental contamination of MDRs and its dissemination. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and co-occurrence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) determinants in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from the gut of wild birds in Islamabad region. Using standard bacterial characterization techniques in total, 342 Gram-negative Enterobacteriaceae isolates were obtained from fresh fecal droppings collected seasonally at eight locations with various types of facilities in Islamabad Pakistan including hospitals. zoo, parks and other public areas. Disk Diffusion test was performed to confer quinolones resistance and double-disk synergy test (DDST) was used to confirm ESBL production. Multiplex PCR was used to detect PMQR genes (QnrA, QnrB, and QnrS), whereas aac (6′)-Ib-cr was detected using conventional PCR. Statistical analysis was used to assess inter-variable associations. A total of 342 isolates were obtained, of which 118 (34.5%) were ESBL producers. Among ESBL-positive isolates that were phenotypically co-resistant to ciprofloxacin and/or nalidixic acid (Quinolones), 73 (61.8%) carried at least one gene of the PMQR family. The most common PMQR determinants were QnrS (76.7%) and aac (6′)-Ib-cr (47.9) %. The co-harboring isolates were dominated by Escherichia coli (82.2%). K. pneumoniae showed a high carriage of aac (6′)-Ib-cr (90%) and QnrB (60%) genes. The highest levels were observed in autumn and winter. Multi-gene co-carriage patterns, where ESBL and PMQR genes occur on a single plasmid, were inferred and were similar to those found in other major plasmid families, IncF, IncI, and IncHI. Wild birds are important reservoirs and active spreaders of MDR Enterobacteriaceae carrying ESBL and PMQR determinants on transferable plasmids in the urban environment of Islamabad. Based on these results, the need to involve wildlife surveillance in One Health-based AMR surveillance programs and increase antibiotic stewardship in Pakistan is highlighted.

articles.title: Hydrothermally Synthesized BiOI/MWCNT Composite Flexible Thin Films for High-Performance Solid-State Supercapacitors
articles.abstract: High-surface-area two-dimensional (2D) bismuth oxyiodide (BiOI) nanoplatelets with abundant electroactive sites were synthesized using a simple and cost-effective hydrothermal method. Flexible BiOI/multiwalled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) composite thin films with varying weight percentages of BiOI and MWCNT were fabricated and evaluated for their electrochemical performance in a symmetric two-electrode configuration. Among the prepared composites, the film with a BiOI-to-MWCNT mass ratio of 60:40 exhibited superior electrochemical performance, delivering a specific capacitance of 218 F g⁻¹ and an energy density of 7.6 Wh kg⁻¹ at a power density of 0.136 kW kg⁻¹, using a PVA/H₂SO₄ gel as the solid-state electrolyte. The fabricated flexible solid-state supercapacitor device (FSSSD60) demonstrated excellent cycling stability, retaining 95% of its initial specific capacitance after 10,000 charge–discharge cycles. Furthermore, the device exhibited excellent mechanical flexibility, maintaining nearly constant electrochemical performance when bent at different angles. These results highlight the potential of BiOI/MWCNT composite thin films as promising electrode materials for flexible, high-performance solid-state supercapacitors.

articles.title: Bioinspired Design of Proximal Amine Boosts Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO 2 by Cobalt Tripyridine-Diamine Complex
articles.abstract: A bioinspired cobalt tripyridine–diamine complex (Co-NH₂) bearing an intramolecular secondary amine in the second coordination sphere was designed to mimic the hydrogen-bonding function of enzymatic active sites. A methyl-substituted analogue (Co-CH₃) was prepared as a control to probe the role of the pendant amine. Electrochemical measurements reveal that Co-NH₂ exhibits higher catalytic current for CO₂ electroreduction relative to Co-CH₃ in methanol-containing CO₂-saturated acetonitrile. Controlled-potential electrolysis confirms that CO and H₂ are the main products, with Co-NH₂ achieving a CO Faradaic efficiency of 57% after 30 min, about twice that of Co-CH₃ under identical conditions. In situ infrared spectroelectrochemistry identifies a metallocarboxylic intermediate and a cobalt–carbonyl species, indicating that C–OH bond cleavage occurs after CO₂ binding. Density functional theory calculations show that the pendant amine hydrogen-bonds to the bound CO₂ unit and assists intramolecular proton transfer during C–OH cleavage, thereby lowering the barrier for this step. Together, these results establish a clear mechanistic link between the positioned amine and the enhanced electrocatalytic performance, highlighting the value of second-sphere hydrogen-bond donors in the rational design of molecular catalysts for CO₂ reduction.

articles.title: Evaluating deep learning detectors for thermal photovoltaic fault localization using independent source families
articles.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based automated infrared thermography (IRT) offers a scalable approach to condition monitoring in utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) plants, but published deep-learning evaluations exhibit persistent methodological weaknesses: frame-to-frame data leakage, unaddressed class imbalance, inconsistent input resolutions, and unstandardized detector benchmarking. This work presents a controlled, source-family-independent benchmark comparing single-stage (YOLOv8s, YOLO11s) and two-stage (Faster R-CNN with ResNet-50-FPN) object detectors on 7,339 cleaned thermal images with 20,995 annotated defect instances from the Thermo-Solar dataset. To reduce evaluation bias, dataset partitioning enforces zero leakage across 2,431 unique source families defined by physical PV module identity, flight pass sequence, and camera telemetry. The single-stage anchor-free detectors clearly dominate the two-stage baseline in a Pareto sense. YOLOv8s and YOLO11s attain similar localization accuracy (0.6958 and 0.6876 mAP@0.50, respectively), with YOLO11s offering a 15.3% smaller parameter footprint (9.43M vs. 11.14M) and lower computational complexity (21.7 GFLOPs). Faster R-CNN achieved lower localization accuracy (0.6542 mAP@0.50), 7.3× slower forward-pass inference latency on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU (75.86 ms/image vs. 10.20–10.40 ms/image), and an 8× higher computational training runtime (7.86 hours for 20 epochs vs. ~1.1 hours for 50 epochs). Despite a raw 119.6:1 class imbalance, the single-stage models retained stronger robustness on minority fault classes (String Reversed Polarity: 0.5817 AP@0.50) than the Region Proposal Network baseline (0.2781 AP@0.50), while spatially dense Multi Hotspots caused severe bounding-box suppression problems (0.4342–0.4781 AP@0.50). This work provides a rigorous and reproducible baseline for operational UAV thermography.

articles.title: A Venus Cloud-Level Aerostat Colony as a Superior Offworld Settlement Strategy to a Mars Surface Colony: A Monte Carlo and Neural Network Analysis
articles.abstract: This study tests the proposition that a crewed aerostat colony floating within the Venus cloud deck at 54 to 60 km altitude represents a superior offworld settlement strategy to a crewed surface colony on Mars. The author constructed first-principles physical and economic models of both colonies and propagated the uncertainty in 367 input parameters through Monte Carlo simulation of 20,000 draws per test. An H2O deep learning surrogate was refitted on bootstrap resamples of each response to produce per-prediction perturbation sensitivities, while a paired permuted-refit null arm supplied per-variable p-values alongside permutational multivariate analysis of variance. Five research questions were evaluated as ten one-sided tests against an alpha test statistic of 0.05. The null hypotheses were rejected for radiation (p = 0.00015; median Venus advantage 143.8 mSv per year) as well as for colony net present value in both habitat configurations (p = 0.024 and 0.022; median Venus advantage approximately USD 228 million per colonist). The null hypotheses for water and oxygen cost, for four export lines and for a gravity health benefit were not rejected. These findings suggest a possible systemic Venus advantage arising from several moderate benefits acting together rather than any single commodity.

articles.title: Thermodynamic limits to secondary mineral formation from US enhanced weathering
articles.abstract: It has become increasingly accepted that carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategies will be necessary to prevent the worst impacts of climate change. As a result, CDR has been incorporated as a central component of climate policy frameworks and projections for climate impact in the coming century. Enhanced weathering (EW), the process of applying finely ground reactive rocks to croplands to accelerate chemical weathering and increase the conversion of atmospheric CO2 to dissolved bicarbonate, has emerged as a promising, scalable, durable CDR approach with clear co-benefits for agricultural systems. However, there remain questions about the extent to which secondary mineral formation may constitute a significant carbon leakage pathway downstream of agricultural deployment. Here, we use an EW field trial and groundwater data from the coterminous US to develop a framework to gauge the likely risk of carbon leakage due to secondary mineral formation. We demonstrate that there are regions across the US with a low risk of carbon leakage through secondary mineral formation, and that these are typically the same regions where the process has the potential to provide the greatest economic and agricultural benefits to farmers. We suggest that this framework can be used to help derisk carbon accounting and crediting through EW in managed lands.

articles.title: An Automated QGIS Plugin to Generate ENVI-met Traffic Emission Sources from Vehicle Trajectories
articles.abstract: Traffic-related particulate matter (PM) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) are critical urban health risks. Microclimate models such as ENVI-met can resolve their street-level distribution, but feeding them with traffic data remains a manual bottleneck, so modelers generalize traffic into polygons or uniform line sources. This study presents an automated method, implemented as an open-source QGIS plugin, that converts vehicle trajectories into street-segment-specific ENVI-met line sources with hourly emission profiles. The plugin discretizes the road network, counts trips per segment, aligns trip times with the model clock, groups segments with similar traffic and splits NOx and PM emissions into the model species. To evaluate the generated sources, the background concentration forcing of ENVI-met V6 is combined with an evaluation of the local concentration increment and a backward Lagrangian footprint analysis, which separate the local traffic signal from the regional background and trace deviations from observations to their cause. Tested with SUMO-generated trajectories at an official Berlin traffic station on six summer and autumn days, the method reproduced PM with high agreement (R² = 0.94 for PM2.5 and 0.82 for PM10), largely through the background, and 71% of the measured local NOx increment with passenger-car trajectories alone. The footprint confirmed that this signal originates almost exclusively from the adjacent street canyon, and the remaining deviations were traced mainly to the vehicle classes missing from the demonstration dataset rather than to the gas-phase chemistry. By replacing manual data entry, the method provides segment-specific emission input for exposure assessments and planning scenarios.

articles.title: Local Morphology Controls Fano Output Zeros and Nonlinear Chirality in Gold Helicoids
articles.abstract: Local changes to a chiral metal nanoparticle can alter its radiation without substantially shifting its principal resonances. We investigate this distinction in connected gold helicoids by varying the winding of one four-groove face while retaining the other five faces and the left-handed backbone. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations are combined with complex angular-channel and vector-spherical-harmonic decompositions, Argand trajectories, singular-value analysis, and a reduced pole/output-zero description. In the 560--610~nm band, a dominant mixed-multipolar channel interferes with a weaker predominantly electric-octupolar branch, producing fixed-channel amplitude minima and rapid phase rotation. The fitted pole positions vary modestly, while local face winding reorganizes the interference and circular dissymmetry. A two-step surface second-harmonic-generation calculation separates nonlinear source formation from radiation at the generated frequency. At a generated wavelength of 600~nm, the radiated dissymmetry changes from -0.131 to +0.986, whereas the nonlinear-source-norm dissymmetry remains below 0.09. For the counter-wound face, a source-norm ratio of 1.092 corresponds to a radiated-power ratio of 2.944. Mesh-refinement tests support the stability of the principal linear and nonlinear results. These findings identify local face winding as a control parameter for plasmonic interference and support a phase-sensitive, generated-frequency interpretation of nonlinear chiroptical amplification beyond scalar source-strength enhancement.

articles.title: A Distributed Learning Framework for Energy-Aware Cooperative Navigation in Multi- Robot Systems
articles.abstract: Cooperative Navigation Problem with Multiple Robots is known to be a quite challenging task, especially under unknown and dynamic traffic conditions. This happens since robots operating under these circumstances usually suffer from a lack of communication, inability to observe the whole environment, and a short lifetime due to a low level of available battery power. Traditional approaches to centralized control and planning for multi-robot navigation often fail here as they do not scale well and carry extremely large computational costs. A team of researchers has come forward to offer a new solution based on the concept of Energy-Efficient Distributed Deep Reinforcement Learning (ED-DDRL). In particular, their method involves developing a much-decentralized decision-making process, which means that each robot independently learns its own policy while communicating with other neighboring ones through the minimal amount of shared local data. To make sure all operations work smoothly without wasting too much electricity, the authors proposed a unique reward function taking into account various factors affecting robot movement. Thanks to an advanced lightweight communication scheme developed specifically for this system, ED-DDRL significantly reduces inter-robot bandwidth utilization levels. All in all, tests performed extensively within a physical prototype showed that compared with state-of-the-art solutions like DQN, PPO, MAPPO, and even MADDPG, ED-DDRL excels in several critical areas – achieving a higher overall success rate alongside enhanced energy efficiency metrics. The latter was most evident during trials involving environments packed with lots of bots where ED-DDRL easily managed to keep ahead.

articles.title: Expressivity limits in variational quantum portfolio construction
articles.abstract: A recurring construction in quantum portfolio optimisation obtains weights by normalising the Pauli-(:Z) expectation values (:⟨Zᵢ⟩) of a variational circuit. We show that its standard one-layer ansatz admits the closed form (:⟨Zₖ⟩=prod:ᵢₗₑ:ₖcosθ:ᵢ), verified to (:4×:10⁻⁸) against simulators and complete backtests. The result generalises: in the static case, any per-qubit readout normalised into weights reparametrises the (:(n-1))-simplex and therefore admits no expressivity advantage. It admits an expressivity deficit. Because the readout is a cumulative product, (:|⟨Zₖ⟩|) cannot increase along the chain, and reachability reduces to whether (:n-1) half-lines on a single scalar intersect: at nine assets the construction attains fewer than one portfolio in twenty thousand, and from twelve none we could sample in two million draws. Over forty training windows the circuit attains the matched classical optimum in every window where that optimum is reachable and in none where it is not ((:p=2.6×:10⁻⁷)), so what separates the circuit from its control is reach rather than optimisation dynamics. Depolarising noise contracts (:⟨Z⟩) by (:(1-4p/3)k) and therefore degrades the portfolio toward the equal-weight portfolio, not toward randomness. The failure is invisible to the usual metrics: with the circuit 95 % of the way to equal weighting, its Sharpe ratio still exceeds the benchmark. Across five universes and 1,313 accounted configurations, none of the twenty-five quantum variants survives Holm–Bonferroni, and the largest statistic in the sweep, (:3.12), falls short of the deflated threshold of (:3.83). In a pre-registered sweep over eight universe sizes, the construction beats the equal-weight portfolio at all eight and the best classical competitor at none. We give the evaluation protocol that follows.

articles.title: Comprehensive Modeling and Physical Analysis of Proposed FCC-ee Superconducting Solenoid System
articles.abstract: The Future Circular Collider electron–positron collider (FCC-ee), planned at CERN, requires an integrated detector-magnet system that produces a strong, well-controlled central field while suppressing fringe fields and limiting electromagnetic loads. Superconducting Magnet Division is designing magnets for the interaction region of FCC-ee including the main focusing quadrupole, correctors and compensations solenoids. This project focuses on the screening solenoid which annuls magnetic field generated by the detector solenoids at locations of the final focus quadruples. A primary detector solenoid and mirror-symmetric segmented screening coils are modeled using analytical finite-thickness solenoid fields. Differential Evolution optimizes the screening geometry, while bounded weighted least squares determine current densities that preserve the central field and suppress the axial field. The optimized configuration is exported to OPERA-3D for finite-element validation. The force methodology is first established using two identical coaxial solenoids, with analytical predictions compared against OPERA calculations over multiple separations to verify force direction, scaling, symmetry, and action–reaction balance. It is then applied to a more advanced optimized FCC-ee magnet model representing the logical next step of the inverse-design process. Forces on the main and screening coils are evaluated through conductor-level load distributions, mirror-pair residuals, and global force balance. An independent reconstruction is compared with full nonlinear and matched nonmagnetic OPERA models, validating the coil-only calculation and isolating the contribution of the iron yoke and calorimeter. The resulting workflow unifies inverse magnetic design, numerical force validation, and electromagnetic loading analysis for an optimized FCC-ee screening solenoid system. It supports Brookhaven and U.S. Department of Energy accelerator-magnet objectives while developing professional expertise in superconducting magnet design, optimization, finite-element analysis, and practical engineering interpretation skills.

articles.title: Periodic Parametric Modulation and Redistribution of Quantum Resources in a Kerr Cavity under Intrinsic Decoherence
articles.abstract: We investigate a two-atom Kerr cavity subjected to a periodically modulated degenerate parametric pump and intrinsic decoherence. The model is formulated in a common frame rotating at half the pump frequency for both the field and atoms, so the linear terms appear as detunings and the Kerr interaction is written in its standard form χ adagger ²a². A time-local extension of Milburn intrinsic decoherence is used for the driven problem and is compared with a second prescription in which only the static Hamiltonian generates the double-commutator dephasing. All principal numerical calculations use a converged Fock basis with photon cutoff n_c=9, and both photon-cutoff and time-step convergence are reported. The normalized quantum Fisher information (QFI) for the initial atomic angle, together with negativity and l₁ coherence, is analyzed. The normalization widetilde F_θ(t)=F_θ(t)/F_θ(0) makes every QFI trajectory start from unity while preserving the physical ordering and data-processing bound. Periodic modulation changes the timing and distribution of these resources, but for the baseline parameters it does not exceed the unmodulated case in late-time averaged normalized QFI. The raw initial-angle QFI remains below its analytically determined initial value, while the plotted normalized QFI satisfies widetilde F_θ(t)le 1, as required by data processing. The results therefore establish a numerically converged description of quantum-resource redistribution rather than a generic claim of modulation-induced protection.
authors: S. Abdul Khali S. Abdul Khali

articles.title: A new chemical network to explore the disequilibrium chemistry of silicates and iron in hot gas giants
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chemical equilibrium modeling of gas giant planet atmospheres has shown that the production and condensation of silicates plays an important role in shaping their final composition. However, no chemical kinetics network for these species are available, preventing the opportunity to analyze the impact of chemical disequilibrium processes. In this paper we present textttSILANE, a new chemical network that include Mg, Si, Fe and 15 carriers of these elements, including MgSiO₃ and Mg₂SiO₄, ready for use in the VULCAN code. We compare the results of our network with a chemical equilibrium model and discuss them in relation to previous results from literature. We then apply our new network to the analysis of a vertically mixed, Solar-composition atmosphere with equilibrium temperatures Tₑq in the [700, 1600] K range, finding that (i) rock-forming silicates disappears from the upper atmosphere already at 1100 K, (ii) SiH₄ reaches concentrations of 10⁻⁷ in the upper (Ple 1.0 bar) atmosphere for planets with Tₑqin [800, 1100] K and (iii) the amount of oxygen in refractories decrease from 21% at Tₑq=700 K to essentially zero already at 1000 K, while in the classical equilibrium framework it remains constant up to Tₑq=1300 K. By applying our network to the case of the young hot Jupiter YSES-1 c and comparing both the mixing ratios of volatile species and the enstatite fraction in the silicate mix, we find evidence of a well-mixed atmosphere, possibly with an average Kzz ge 10¹⁰ cm²s⁻¹ up to the 10⁻⁴ bar level.

articles.title: Transferable neural-network preconditioners for Wilson--Clover propagator inversions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate two single--layer neural-network architectures for accelerating four-dimensional Wilson--Clover propagator inversions on lattice ensembles in practical use; both transfer directly without retraining. The first is a gauge-covariant parallel transport convolution (PTC) network that directly reduces the number of generalized conjugate residual (GCR) solver iterations. The second is a CNN-like network used together with a multigrid-inspired algorithm. The two approaches can be combined to further reduce GCR iterations. PTC transfers without retraining across lattice volumes, lattice spacings, and pion masses while maintaining comparable acceleration, whereas the CNN-like network transfers directly from small- to large-volume ensembles with strong acceleration. A cost comparison accounting for both basis construction and solves shows that the proposed scheme is more advantageous for large-volume ensembles than for small-volume ones.

articles.title: A Hierarchically Compressed Immittance Operator Formulation for Fast Statics-to-Full-Wave Electromagnetic Simulation with the Boundary Element Method
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The boundary element method allows the electromagnetic simulation of three-dimensional problems with a two-dimensional discretization, using a surface integral representation of Maxwell's equations. For applications involving broadband simulations or multiscale geometries, the well-known low-frequency breakdown of conventional integral equation formulations must be addressed, while ensuring that dielectric, semiconducting, and lossy metallic regions are modeled rigorously, including the skin effect. In this work, a new boundary element formulation based on an immittance operator is proposed, where the underlying integral equations are inherently valid from statics to the full-wave regime. To enable efficient matrix assembly and solution, a hierarchical matrix compression strategy is devised, leveraging fast direct factorization as an intermediate step, and fast matrix-vector products for the iterative solution of the final system of equations. The proposed formulation is capable of electrostatic, magnetostatic, quasistatic, and full-wave simulations of dielectrics, semiconductors, and lossy metals. Representative numerical examples drawn from a variety of applications demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articles.title: Variational Monte Carlo for Quantum Excited States via Nested Low-Rank Approximation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The electronic Schrödinger equation encodes a molecule's electronic structure and quantum properties, but solving it scales exponentially with the number of electrons. Solving this equation with neural-network variational Monte Carlo (VMC) has reached chemical accuracy on the ground state of small molecules; extending this success to excited states is constrained by two existing paradigms. Penalty-based methods need K Laplacians per step but require tuning the overlap-penalty weights against the energy gaps they aim to compute. Natural excited states VMC (NES-VMC) is penalty-free, but it combines the K ansatzes into one determinant, whose local energy requires K² Laplacians per step. We resolve this trade-off via low-rank approximation (LoRA) reparameterization of the rank-K variational objective. The reparameterized objective admits a VMC-compatible stochastic gradient estimator via MCMC sampling from the per-state Born densities, and a sequential nesting scheme recovers the lowest K eigenstates in eigenvalue order. The resulting algorithm, NestedLoRA-VMC, inherits a global optimality guarantee from the LoRA principle. On the first-row atoms Li through Ne at K=10, its accuracy is comparable to that of NES-VMC and of a state-of-the-art penalty-based method.

articles.title: Emergent kagome-like electronic texture in epitaxial β-Sb on Al(111)
articles.abstract: arXiv:2112.05424v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report the epitaxial growth of β-Sb on Al(111) and the emergence of a kagome-like electronic texture with increasing Sb coverage. The surface evolves from disordered clusters through honeycomb and dice patterns before kagome-like regions appear. Diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, spectroscopy, and density functional calculations identify the ordered phase as β-Sb formed by AB stacking of two dice layers, with the honeycomb phase serving as a precursor. The kagome-like maxima occupy bridge positions within the same lateral lattice and differ in apparent height from dice regions by only about 25 pm.
