Our audit first screens for the claims that a risk-sensitive user would act upon, using the excess Wasserstein gap between the top two actions (which is equal to the mass by which first-order stochastic dominance is violated). Each claim is then tested against ground truth using permutation nulls, bootstrap refutation and FDR control. Across QR-DQN, C51 and IQN on MinAtar (33 runs), 40-95% of the strongest claimed risk trade-offs are refuted at 95% confidence, their placement is statistically indistinguishable from a truth-blind placement, and almost none of them can be confirmed. A similar pattern is seen for a pretrained full-Atari QR-DQN. On positive controls of known magnitude the same audit confirms 96-100% of real claims (correlation 0.89-0.92), so it is able to detect real risk when it is present. Acting on the learned CVaR advice at the most-flagged states gives results ranging from beneficial to significantly worse than chance. Ensembling, risk-sensitive training and recalibration do not fix the problem, and the recalibration experiment indicates that the learned spread has no usable information about the true risk. Based on these results, we suggest that uncertainty estimates, including those of learned world models, should be checked against realized outcomes at the decisions where they are used..

articles.title: Same Task, Different Statement: When and How Reformulation Helps LLM Problem Solving
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When people face a hard problem, they often restate it in a clearer way before solving it. We study whether the same habit helps large language models by rewriting the statement of a problem. A legal rewrite must keep the meaning, the constraints, and the correct answer unchanged. We test three kinds of rewrites. Decomposition makes hidden subgoals explicit. Typed Reformulation casts the task into a more suitable solving frame. Concept Reduction removes surface detail and exposes the task structure. We evaluate them on eight math, logic, and code benchmarks with eight models, all under the same chain-of-thought solving prompt. The effect is large but depends on the problem type. An oracle that picks the best rewrite after the fact raises accuracy by +27.6% on average. Yet no single rewrite helps every problem, and a mismatched rewrite can hurt. Still, the effect follows clear patterns. Each kind of rewrite fits certain problem types. A simple fixed rule learned from one set of problems transfers part of the gain to new problems. It gains +11.0% on the problems it chooses to rewrite, while blind rewriting loses 5.6% on a similar share of problems. Rewriting is therefore not a universal way to solve problems. The question is when and how to rewrite.

articles.title: Expanding the Decision Space of Pretrained Models through Structured Re-Decoding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Native decoders limit how pretrained models combine local predictions under new structural constraints. We introduce Structured Re-Decoding (SRD), a training-free framework that constructs local candidates from model scores, samples, or external specifications, jointly optimizes their selection, and verifies reconstructed outputs. We show that candidate recombination expands feasible support and can improve attainable reward under a fixed KL divergence budget. Across molecular generation, protein design, RNA structure prediction, and antibody modeling, SRD enables improved structured inference, including verified molecules absent from the original sample pool. External chemical templates further extend SRD to noncanonical amino acids, peptide cyclization, and grammar-guided molecular construction. Preliminary experiments on a physical coherent Ising machine demonstrate the feasibility of hardware-based optimization, suggesting broader opportunities for quantum and quantum-inspired approaches to structured inference and combinatorial optimization across scientific domains.

articles.title: One Fuzzer, Many Reasoners: Adaptive Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzing with Reliability-Calibrated and Context-Gated Guidance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural-symbolic AI (NSAI) combines learned perception with programs, constraints, and compositional reasoning, but remains difficult to test because small semantics-preserving changes can alter grounded symbols and trigger discontinuous reasoning failures. Existing neural fuzzers mainly rely on neural coverage or representation-space feedback and do not provide a common testing interface for heterogeneous NSAI systems. We introduce NSAI-Fuzz, a unified semantics-aware fuzzing framework that separates task-specific valid mutation from architecture-neutral guided search and represents each candidate using five availability-aware, rank-normalized risk signals: boundary pressure, grounding uncertainty, representation drift, constraint violation, and archive novelty. We further propose Reliability-Calibrated Weighting (RCW), which learns dataset-model-level signal allocations from calibrated reliability, and Contextual Signal Gating (CSG), which adapts signal weights to the current candidate pool. We evaluate four NSAI systems across four reasoning tasks, nine compatible dataset-model cells, 20 policies, and 1,800 on-policy runs. Fixed five-signal guidance outperforms Random and Uniform in every cell, while RCW and CSG further improve over Fixed in all nine cells. Under matched mutation and query budgets, RCW and CSG achieve 16.17% and 16.06% aggregate failure discovery, compared with 6.06% for the strongest neural-fuzzing baseline. Wall-clock evaluation further shows that TensorFuzz requires 1.11x the runtime of RCW while achieving only 0.45x its failure throughput. These results show that effective and efficient fuzzing of heterogeneous NSAI systems benefits from a common neural-symbolic risk interface with adaptive signal allocation.

articles.title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embodied agents make decisions by combining information from heterogeneous memory modules, including declarative memory for explicit knowledge, procedural memory for learned routines, and working memory for current observations. During interaction, the memory contents required for decision making change with the agent's state, goal, and task progress, while many contents remain shared across consecutive decisions. However, existing memory modules are typically accessed through separate interfaces, so each updated memory context is often processed as a new input to the foundation model. This prevents selective key-value (KV) cache reuse for unchanged memory contents and forces full KV cache recomputation even when much of the memory context remains valid. We introduce HeMeR, an inference framework that performs KV reconciliation between dynamically updated memory contexts and reusable KV states. HeMeR tracks declarative, procedural, and working memory contents across action decisions, preserves KV states for unchanged contents, and reconciles only the KV states affected by memory-content updates. This enables efficient and stable inference as memory contents evolve during interaction. We evaluate HeMeR on ALFWorld, Habitat, and real-world robotic deployments requiring coordinated use of heterogeneous memory contents. In the real-world setting, HeMeR achieves 83.20% task success and reduces per-step inference time from 2.94 to 1.87 seconds compared with MemRL, while preserving compatible KV states as task progress updates the memory context.

articles.title: SignRot: LLM Quantization with Massive Outlier-Aware Sign-Adjusted Rotation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While quantization compresses LLMs and accelerates inference, outlier activations impede efficient low-bit representation. In particular, massive outliers cause substantial performance degradation. Although rotation-based methods that rely on randomized Hadamard transforms for online inference aim to mitigate this, they can produce fragmented distributions with empty bins when a massive outlier dominates a token's activation. This fragmentation severely undermines uniform quantization performance. Moreover, massive outliers concentrate in the down-projection input, where the preceding nonlinearity requires the rotation to be applied at inference time. This constraint prevents training-based approaches such as SpinQuant from learning the online rotation at this position, as a learned dense matrix cannot use the Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform and would require a full matrix multiplication during inference. To address this, we propose SignRot (Sign-adjusted Rotation), which identifies massive outlier channels and constructs a sign adjustment vector that unifies the signs of the corresponding Hadamard row, collapsing the bimodal distribution into a unimodal profile amenable to quantization. Since the aligned outlier shifts the activation mean away from zero, we pair SignRot with asymmetric activation quantization, whose zero-point absorbs this shift. As a lightweight, drop-in improvement compatible with any Hadamard-based quantization method, SignRot requires only a single calibration forward pass and adds only element-wise sign flips at inference, without an additional matrix multiplication. Applying SignRot to QuaRot achieves a WikiText2 perplexity of 5.88 and an average zero-shot reasoning accuracy of 72.73, surpassing SpinQuant on the LLaMA3-70B model. Code is available at https://github.com/HYU-ARK-Lab/SignRot.

articles.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. We propose a two-branch architecture that combines an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification. The graph branch groups 61 EEG electrodes into anatomically informed regions and learns their spatial relationships, providing a direct representation of the regions emphasized by the model. We evaluate the proposed architecture using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb movement dataset. The model achieves a mean F1-score of 0.74 +/- 0.06 across subjects. Beyond classification performance, we analyze the learned graph structure to identify the regions with the strongest connectivity. Across all held-out subjects, the highest connectivity is consistently observed in the Parietal Left Low region, corresponding to electrodes P1 and P3. This region is opposite to the performed right-arm movements and lies within the posterior parietal area previously associated with upper-limb movement processing. These results show that incorporating a region-based graph into the decoder can provide an anatomically interpretable representation while maintaining effective movement classification, offering a practical approach toward more transparent EEG-based BCIs.

articles.title: QSim-Arena: an evolving developer for quantum simulation advantage
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Where practical advantage emerges in quantum dynamics simulation remains a central debate in quantum computing. Claimed advantages can be rapidly narrowed or overturned by stronger classical methods, while progress on both sides can outpace the journal publication cycle. We present QSim-Arena, a research framework in which AI agents combine a closed loop of verification and benchmarking with open exploration. Hamiltonians, initial states and accuracy targets for evolved states or observable expectation values provide explicit specifications for evaluating simulation methods. Agents translate published techniques into executable components, reproduce reported results and benchmark their performance across diverse Hamiltonian families. Competing classical methods are implemented and independently crosschecked, providing credible baselines for end-to-end quantum resource estimates based on rigorous error bounds and empirical calibration. Alongside this closed loop, agents recombine classical simulation techniques and co-design fault-tolerant quantum circuits using knowledge extracted from the literature. Initial applications improve baseline resource estimates through the integration of established techniques. QSim-Arena thus treats quantum advantage assessment as an evolving, reproducible research process that can respond to advances in algorithms, error analysis and hardware.

articles.title: Prototypes of the Mind: A Unified Framework for Probing the Visual Brain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning has driven substantial progress in modeling fMRI responses, yet most existing approaches are optimized for a single objective---such as neural encoding, stimulus decoding, or post hoc interpretation---making it difficult to obtain a coherent account of neural representations. We introduce a unified framework that connects vision foundation models to brain activity while supporting neural analysis from multiple complementary perspectives. Our approach replaces black-box features with a sparse, interpretable representation composed of visual prototypes, and links these prototypes to voxel responses through a linear readout. This design makes the model transparent at both levels: prototype activations expose the visual concepts present in the stimulus, while the learned linear weights characterize each voxel's selectivity. Using this interface, we identify which visual concepts drive neural responses and where they appear in the image, reveal cortical organization through voxel tuning in prototype space, and perform controlled stimulus synthesis to probe cortical selectivity through targeted interventions. Together, these results establish prototype-based representations as a unified and interpretable foundation for studying visual representations in the human brain.

articles.title: Where is My Mug? Training-Free Framework for Personalized Image Segmentation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Personalized Image Segmentation (PIS) aims to segment the specific object in a target image that matches a user-provided reference. Unlike category-based segmentation or few-shot segmentation, PIS must discriminate between multiple visually similar instances, a requirement central to deployed applications such as augmented reality, personalized content editing, robotics manipulation, inventory tracking, and fine-grained visual retrieval. We show that the strong numbers reported by existing PIS methods are largely an artifact of single-instance benchmarks: when evaluated on realistic scenes with several same-category look-alikes, prior point-prompt methods collapse, because the correct instance is frequently never surfaced as a prompt. We trace this to a recall bottleneck rather than a mask-quality one, and address it with a training-free, modular system. The pipeline first generates high-recall object proposals using an off-the-shelf class-agnostic detector, then matches each proposal to the reference using foundation-model features (e.g., BLIP-2), and finally refines the selected box with SAM. For robust matching we propose top-K Sinkhorn, a patch-level distance that scores each candidate only on its most confidently matched patches; trimming the Sinkhorn dual potentials recovers the robustness of partial optimal transport at more than 100× lower cost, keeping it inside the per-proposal candidate loop. To evaluate this regime, we introduce datasetname, a realistic multi-instance benchmark. Across datasetname, PerSeg, PerMIS, and DAVIS, our system surpasses PerSAM, P²SAM, and PDM by up to sim!48 mIoU while matching their runtime and using fewer parameters, establishing a strong, deployable training-free baseline for real-world personalized segmentation.

articles.title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the multi-head quantum neural network (QNN), a quantum module compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices that can replace transformer blocks inside pre-trained large language models (LLMs) with little loss in accuracy and with far fewer parameters than the blocks it replaces. Encoding a model's D hidden neurons into a qubit register is the obstacle: amplitude encoding scales poorly in circuit depth and angle encoding in qubit count, so neither is practical at production-scale width. We instead partition the hidden space into k disjoint heads, angle-encode each into an n_q-qubit register, process the heads in parallel, and couple them through constrained classical linear layers, the mixers. Performing surgery on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, we show that a single multi-head QNN with 145,281 trainable parameters (D=2048, k=32, n_q=8, L=4) can replace a contiguous span of eight transformer blocks, displacing 16.33% of the model's parameters. Ablations show that, for a single replaced block, the quantum heads (circuits followed by a learned readout), and not the classical mixers alone, recover the displaced function, whereas for fused spans the mixers alone come within 1-3% of the full module in perplexity. Whether this benefit is specific to trained, entangling quantum circuits is not established: controls that switch the entangler off (two seeds), or freeze the circuit at its initial or at uniformly random angles (one seed), beat the full module on held-out perplexity, and a parameter-matched classical multilayer perceptron remains a few percent ahead of the full module. We train classically with exact statevector simulation, then execute the quantum heads of our fusion checkpoints on a 156-qubit IBM Heron processor, showing that NISQ-scale quantum modules can be installed in a production-scale LLM and run on hardware.

articles.title: Quantum Recurrent Architectures for Financial Time Series Prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study evaluates quantum classical hybrid recurrent architectures for financial time-series forecasting: a Quantum Long Short-Term Memory (QLSTM) network and Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) with lag-based inputs. Classical lag vectors are encoded into quantum states via amplitude encoding, which compactly represents normalized observations but requires nontrivial state preparation; the QLSTM gates and the QRC reservoir are implemented with parameterized quantum circuits, while classical optimizers train the interface and readout layers. On a monthly revenue series extended to 1056 months by a Gaussian-process--hidden-Markov generator, with a fixed chronological 70/15/15 split and one-step-ahead forecasts, we compare both models against a full-size LSTM, a classical control matched in parameter budget and interface architecture, a small plain LSTM, and classical reservoir computing, over ten seeds and against persistence, seasonal-naive and SARIMA benchmark forecasts. The QLSTM, with 2,105 parameters, is statistically indistinguishable from an LSTM 126 times larger, but equally indistinguishable from the matched classical control and from a plain LSTM of the same budget, so its parameter efficiency cannot be attributed to the quantum circuits. The quantum reservoir is worse than a classical reservoir of equal feature dimension in all ten seeds and worse than SARIMA, whereas all recurrent models and both classical reservoirs improve on SARIMA by about 2% in RMSE. In a 24-month rolling-origin backtest the classical LSTMs degrade more slowly than the QLSTM. We find no evidence of a quantum accuracy or parameter-efficiency advantage in this low-dimensional setting.

articles.title: TopoST: Topology-Conditioned Node Specialization for Urban Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Urban spatio-temporal foundation models must share knowledge across diverse urban scenarios while accommodating heterogeneous node dynamics. Our analysis of 20+ datasets spanning diverse urban scenarios reveals recurring local graph structures across datasets alongside substantial node heterogeneity within local subgraphs. Motivated by these observations, we propose TopoST, which combines shared learning over local subgraphs with topology-conditioned node specialization. The key insight is to make node specialization itself transferable through a shared topology-to-parameter mapping. This mapping uses identity-independent topological representations to generate node-specific temporal and spatial dependency parameters, enabling direct specialization for unseen nodes without target-specific embeddings or model updates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TopoST achieves remarkable zero-shot generalization across unseen cities and tasks, highlighting topology-conditioned node specialization as an effective mechanism for transferable urban spatio-temporal foundation models. Code is available at https://github.com/weikaiyun/TopoST.

articles.title: GIS-Based Agricultural Potential Zoning Using Remote Sensing Indicators and the Analytic Hierarchy Process: A Case Study of Blida Wilaya, Northern Algeria
articles.abstract: Agricultural land suitability assessment is a critical instrument for sustainable land-use planning in Mediterranean semi-arid regions exposed to climate variability, land degradation, and expanding urban pressure. This study develops and validates a GIS–remote sensing–based agricultural potential zoning (APZ) model for Blida Wilaya, northern Algeria, by integrating five spatial criteria: the Soil Moisture Index (SMI), the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), Land Use/Land Cover (LULC), and a composite Agro-Physiographic Suitability factor derived from slope, elevation, and distance from water bodies. Multi-source datasets—Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS imagery acquired during the 2025 growing season, SRTM DEM, and OpenStreetMap hydrography—were harmonized to a 30 m grid on the Google Earth Engine platform and integrated within ArcGIS 10.8. Criterion weights were derived through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) eigenvector method, with SMI (0.4502) and NDVI (0.2502) exerting dominant influence; consistency ratios of 6.25% and 3.34% for the five-factor and three-factor matrices, respectively, confirmed the logical coherence of the elicited judgments. Weighted linear combination yielded a five-class APZ map covering 148,046 ha, of which 47.40% was classified as suitable, 22.53% as moderately suitable, 12.58% as highly suitable, 11.43% as marginally suitable, and 6.05% as not suitable. ROC validation produced an area under the curve of 0.935, indicating excellent discriminatory performance. The results delineate a suitable agricultural matrix across the Mitidja plain, a highly suitable belt along the Blidean Atlas front that should be interpreted as conservation-oriented rather than as a mandate for intensification, and an urbanized piedmont corridor whose 4,015 ha of residual suitable land constitutes a finite reserve requiring explicit protection against urban sprawl. The framework provides a transparent, reproducible screening tool for sustainable agricultural planning in semi-arid Mediterranean landscapes.

articles.title: Removal of Total Petroleum Hydrocarbons from Simulated Crude Oil Contaminated Seawater Using Plantain Stem Derived Biosorbent
articles.abstract: This study investigated the application of plantain stem biosorbent for the removal of total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) from simulated crude-oil-polluted seawater. The prepared contaminated seawater exhibited a slightly acidic condition (pH 6.47), salinity of 8.51 ppt, and an initial TPH concentration of 213.48 mg L⁻¹. The biosorbent was characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis to evaluate its surface properties and adsorption potential. The results confirmed the presence of oxygen-containing functional groups, porous morphology, and carbon-rich composition suitable for hydrocarbon adsorption. A three-factor Box–Behnken design was employed to optimize the effects of adsorbent dosage, adsorption time, and particle size on TPH removal. The quadratic model was statistically significant (F-value = 109.02, p < 0.0001) with a high coefficient of determination (R² = 0.9929), indicating good agreement between predicted and experimental values. The optimum conditions were obtained at an adsorbent dosage of 2 g L⁻¹, contact time of 20 min, and particle size of 70 µm, achieving a predicted TPH removal efficiency of 95.63%. Adsorption equilibrium analysis showed that the Langmuir model provided a better fit than the Freundlich model, suggesting monolayer adsorption on the biosorbent surface. The study demonstrates that plantain stem, an abundant agricultural residue, is a promising low-cost and sustainable biosorbent for petroleum hydrocarbon remediation in contaminated seawater.

articles.title: SHRX: a neural surrogate of turbulent transport in tokamak plasma and its comparison with TORAX against experimental data
articles.abstract: Integrated tokamak modelling needs fast surrogates of turbulent transport, but existing ones depend on JAX. We built SHRX, a neural network with 29,283 parameters that runs on NumPy alone, by distilling the QuaLiKiz neural network (QLKNN). A “bridge” converts the state of our one-and-a-half-dimensional simulator SINTEZ into the ten dimensionless QLKNN inputs. For stiff transport we introduce the error of the critical-gradient factor, (:δ:f), as a metric, and an ensemble of five networks gives an uncertainty estimate. We compare SINTEZ with SHRX against the TORAX code at three levels: identical local plasma states, an integrated ITER discharge with identical inputs, and 206 conventional and 41 spherical records of the H-mode database of the International Tokamak Physics Activity (ITPA). On machines held out of training, the median error of the heat diffusivity (:χ:) is 9% and the median (:δ:f) is 2.3%; the ensemble lowers the (:χ:) error to 5.9–6.5%. The ITER fusion power is 492 MW with SINTEZ and SHRX, 478 MW with SINTEZ and QLKNN, and 532 MW with TORAX. On experimental records the two codes agree with each other ((:r=0.995) in (:lnW)) better than with the measurements, and both are less accurate than the IPB98(y,2) regression ((:σ:ₗₙ) of 0.55 and 0.56 against 0.21). On spherical tokamaks SHRX overestimates the stored energy by a median factor of 28. SHRX is a faster, JAX-free copy of QLKNN, not a better model than TORAX: most of the experimental error comes from inputs that both codes share.

articles.title: Development, optimization, and functional characterization of a gelatin-based hydrogel biodegradable packaging film for sustainable food packaging and refrigerated cherry tomato preservation
articles.abstract: 27 This study aimed to develop and characterize gelatin-based hydrogel active biodegradable 28 packaging films formulated using the solvent casting method. Three formulations (S1-S3 films) formation. Mechanical testing showed that tensile strength decreased from 0.203 ± 0.012 MPa 33 (S1 film) to 0.091 ± 0.013 MPa (S3 film), while elongation ranged from 248.9 ± 4.33 % to 34 189.07 ± 3.68 %. Barrier studies indicated that WVTR reduced from 54.10 ± 1.51 to 46.06 ± 35 1.16 g·m⁻²·day⁻¹ and OTR from 210 ± 4.08 to 181.67 ± 6.24 cm³·m⁻²·day⁻¹·atm⁻¹ with 36 increasing gelatin concentration. DSC analysis exhibited dual glass transitions (Tg₁ = 39.09 37 °C; Tg₂ = 51.92 °C) and a melting point at 188.7 °C (ΔHm = 156.48 J·g⁻¹), indicating semi-38 crystalline stability. FE-SEM revealed a compact porous network (3.9–8.9 µm), while Total 39 Plate Count remained 95 % 40 biodegradation within 15 days, validating the film’s environmental compatibility for active and 41 sustainable food packaging applications. The selected S2 gelatin-based hydrogel film was 42 evaluated for packaging cherry tomatoes under refrigerated storage at 4 ± 1 °C. Visible surface 43 shrinkage was first observed on day 12 in the control and on day 15 in the S2 hydrogel-film 44 packaged cherry tomatoes, indicating a 3-day extension in apparent visual shelf life.

articles.title: Effect of Carbon Black Morphology on Electrical and Mechanical Properties of Filled Natural Rubber
articles.abstract: The balance between electrical conductivity and mechanical reinforcement is a critical challenge in the development of conductive rubber composites for aircraft tire applications. In this work, the electrical and mechanical behaviors of natural rubber (NR) composites filled with a conventional reinforcing carbon black (N234) and a high-surface-area conductive carbon black were systematically investigated. Compared with N234-filled NR, the conductive carbon black composite exhibits significantly lower volume resistivity and improved stability of electrical conductivity under cyclic tensile deformation, which is attributed to the formation of a more continuous and damage-resistant conductive network. These results demonstrate that electrical performance is primarily governed by the integrity of the carbon black network, while mechanical behavior is dominated by polymer-filler interfacial reinforcement. This work provides new insight into the independent evolution of conductive and reinforcing networks and offers guidance for designing balanced conductive rubber systems for tire applications.

articles.title: Conceptual design of a practical field-reversed configuration magneto- inertial fusion reactor
articles.abstract: Magneto-inertial fusion (MIF) is expected to offer the dual advantages of lower cost and a more compact reactor design than both magnetic confinement fusion (MCF) and inertial confinement fusion (ICF). However, existing MIF reactor designs either require destructively high magnetic fields (B. Wang et al., Phys. Rev. E 114, 015211, 2026) or unrealistically long plasma confinement times (T. Nicolas et al., J. Fusion Energy 45:24, 2026) to reach ignition. This article presents a practical MIF reactor design based on acceleration and compression of field-reversed configuration (FRC) plasmas. The most conservative scaling law for FRC plasma confinement time is used to ensure the physics design robustness, and an engineering limit of < 100 T is adopted to enable non-destructive repetitive operation. The unique structural design ensures FRC stability throughout the compression process, and a practical path to ignition is expected at moderate densities (~ 1024 m− 3). The simple relationship between the minimum required magnetic field for a given confinement time is also presented as “the D-diagram” which can be used as a guide for the design of any fusion reactors with the goal to achieve ignition. The effective kinetic wall compression method used in the design has higher plasma heating efficiency than traditional wall compression and avoids the impurity contamination problem.

articles.title: Design of a Triple-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction for Sub-6 GHz Applications
articles.abstract: The increasing demand for compact multiband antennas in 5G/6G communications, cognitive radio, and other modern wireless communication systems requires efficient and intelligent antenna design approaches. Conventional antenna optimization methods based on full-wave electromagnetic simulations are time-consuming and computationally expensive due to repeated design iterations. Machine learning (ML)-assisted methods provide a faster prediction of optimal design/geometry parameters for efficient multiband anttena for targeted Sub-6 GHz applications. Multiband microstrip patch antennas are attractive for compact sub-6~GHz radios, but placing several resonances with full-wave simulation alone is slow. Published ML based studies mostly address one or two bands. They rarely test whether the simulated antenna meets a matching requirement at the required centre frequencies, or whether the training data are themselves consistent. This paper presents an ML-assisted workflow for a compact dual-slot, inset-fed microstrip antenna with a defected ground structure on FR-4. It targets the 2.4~GHz ISM, 3.5~GHz 5G n78 and 5.8~GHz ISM bands. A Latin Hypercube plan of 805 geometries over five parameters was simulated in CST Studio Suite, giving 630 usable samples with 15 outputs each. A first campaign was discarded after a consistency check showed unrelated outputs for identical geometries. Random forest (RF), XGBoost, and a neural network (ANN) MODELS are trained and compared, with and without electrical-length features. On 95 held-out designs, XGBoost with engineered features reached the highest mean R² across all fifteen outputs (0.72). This compares with 0.70 for the raw ANN, 0.68 for raw XGBoost and 0.67 for RF. The surrogates also separated passing from failing designs well, with an AUC from 0.93 for the raw ANN to 0.99 for the engineered-feature ANN. Even so, the difference between XGBoost and the neural network was within statistical noise. A surrogate-guided search followed by 40 verification simulations produced a design that meets S₁₁le-10~dB at all three target frequencies (-11.4, -21.5 and -11.6~dB), where the baseline meets none. Six of eight tolerance variants still met all three targets. Gain, efficiency, VSWR, coverage of the standard bands and radiation patterns are reported for the final design. The design is narrow-band with modest gain and efficiency, and all results are from simulation.

articles.title: Groundwater Potential Assessment Using Ann-Rks Machine Learning Based Models in Part of Aule Community, Akure, Nigeria
articles.abstract: This study adopted an integrated approach combining hydrogeological, geophysical, and machine learning techniques to evaluate groundwater potential in Aule Community, Akure, Ondo State, Southwestern Nigeria. Remote sensing data, particularly the ASTER Global Digital Elevation Model (DEM), were processed in ArcMap 10.8.2 to derive key terrain conditioning factors such as slope and aspect, which influence surface runoff, infiltration, and groundwater recharge. The geophysical investigation involved electrical resistivity surveys using the Schlumberger array configuration, with 105 Vertical Electrical Sounding (VES) stations acquired across the study area. Interpretation of the VES data delineated five subsurface geoelectric layers: topsoil, lateritic layer, weathered layer, partially weathered or fractured basement, and fresh basement bedrock, providing detailed insight into aquifer geometry and subsurface conditions. These geoelectric and hydrogeological parameters were integrated as predictor variables within a supervised machine learning framework. A dataset comprising 40 matched well–VES control points were used for model training and validation, with hand-dug well measurements serving as the target variable. Two predictive models were developed: a conventional Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and an enhanced ANN integrated with Random Kitchen Sinks (ANN-RKS) to improve nonlinear feature representation. Using 5-fold cross-validation, the ANN-RKS model outperformed the standard ANN, achieving MAE = 0.056, MSE = 0.006, RMSE = 0.078, and R² = 0.910, compared to MAE = 0.082, MSE = 0.012, RMSE = 0.109, and R² = 0.801 for the ANN model. The optimized ANN-RKS outputs were subsequently spatially interpolated within a GIS environment to generate a detailed groundwater potential map of the study area.

articles.title: Roll-to-Plate Fabrication of Gold Nanopillar SERS Chips for Phthalate Detection and Classification
articles.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is a detection technique that enables rapid and non-destructive analysis of samples. To overcome the high cost and long fabrication time associated with conventional SERS substrate fabrication processes and to facilitate commercialization, extensive research has been conducted on the development of SERS substrates suitable for large-scale production. Although significant progress has been made in the mass production of SERS substrates using various fabrication methods, including lithography and nanoimprinting, high fabrication costs and long processing times are still required during pattern formation and subsequent metal deposition, remaining major challenges for commercialization. In this study, to address these limitations, a 6-inch scale Au Nanopillar SERS substrate (Au NSS) was fabricated by patterning nanopillar structures over a large area using a roll-to-plate process, followed by Au sputtering, thereby simplifying the fabrication process and enabling rapid and cost-effective production. The fabricated nanopillar structures induced localized electromagnetic field enhancement and exhibited SERS activity. The resulting Au Nanopillar SERS chip (Au NSC) achieved a limit of detection 1.53 x 10− 6 M for rhodamine 6G. In addition, the detection performance of the Au NSC was evaluated for four phthalates widely used in industrial applications confirming the feasibility of detecting each compound. Furthermore, AI-based analysis was applied to classify the four phthalates at a concentration of 50 ppm. These results demonstrate the potential of the developed Au NSC as a low-cost, large-area, and mass-producible SERS analytical platform for practical applications in industrial environments.

articles.title: Methane dynamics in wetland ecosystems: mathematical model, properties of the initial–boundary value problem and verification of the numerical scheme
articles.abstract: A one-dimensional vertical model of dissolved methane dynamics in water-saturated peat is formulated and analysed. The model accounts for methanogenesis, Monod-type oxidation, molecular diffusion, ebullition with a threshold determined by the atmospheric, hydrostatic and capillary pressures, and plant-mediated transport represented by a point sink at the root uptake level; mass exchange with the atmosphere is imposed on the total flux at the surface by a Robin condition. For the problem with a truncated bubble flux, a weak formulation is introduced, and the existence, uniqueness and non-negativity of the weak solution and its continuous dependence on the initial data and the source are proved. The point sink is shown to be well defined without regularization and to be equivalent to an interface condition with a jump of the diffusive flux. For the stationary problem, the existence of a non-negative solution is established, together with its uniqueness and exponential stability under a smallness condition, and a sufficient condition for a zero bubble flux through the surface is obtained. A conservative monotone finite-volume scheme with exponential fitting of the fluxes, upwind evaluation of the bubble velocity and the implicit Euler method is constructed. Its MATLAB implementation is verified against two analytical steady-state solutions and by the method of manufactured solutions: the scheme conserves mass to machine precision and exhibits second-order spatial convergence without active ebullition and first-order convergence with active bubble transport and in time.

articles.title: Polarization-encoded multifocal stitching imaging based on all-dielectric metasurface engineering
articles.abstract: The development of integrated microscopic imaging requires optical systems to simultaneously possess miniaturization, multi-channel control, and high-quality imaging capabilities, while traditional lens systems still have limitations in terms of structural compactness and functional reuse. This paper presents a polarization-coded multifocal stitching imaging system based on an all-dielectric metalens. By using polarization multiplexing and phase modulation, the designed metalens can achieve selective multifocal modulation of the incident polarization state: it generates 8 focal spots under left-handed circularly polarized light, 4 focal spots under right-handed circularly polarized light, and can simultaneously excite all 12 focal spots under linearly polarized light. The metalens was further used to perform multifocal imaging and stitching reconstruction on a resolution plate, verifying its multi-channel imaging capability. As a proof of principle, based on the experimentally measured multifocal PSF, convolutional coding, demixing, and stitching reconstruction methods were used to perform computational imaging processing on onion epidermal cell images, achieving effective reconstruction of complex biological sample images. This work demonstrates the application potential of polarization-multiplexed metasurfaces in integrated multifocal imaging and computational reconstruction.

articles.title: Graphene-interlayer-induced suppression of the longitudinal spin Seebeck effect in Pt/Y 3 Fe 5 O 12 heterostructures
articles.abstract: We investigate the influence of sequentially inserted graphene (Gr) interlayers on thermally driven spin transport in Pt/YIG, Pt/Gr/YIG, and Pt/Gr/Gr/YIG heterostructures through magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent longitudinal spin Seebeck effect (LSSE) measurements. The LSSE voltage exhibits a characteristic magnetic-field-dependent polarity reversal and increases approximately linearly with the applied temperature difference. Compared with Pt/YIG, the LSSE signal decreases to approximately 47% of the reference value upon insertion of a single Gr layer and is further reduced to approximately 22% of the original response with two Gr layers, demonstrating successive suppression of the measured LSSE response. The Pt/Gr/Gr/YIG heterostructure exhibits a nonmonotonic temperature dependence, with a maximum LSSE response near 150 K. To investigate the underlying interfacial electronic structure, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed for Pt/Gr/Gr/NiFe model heterostructures with AA- and AB-stacked bilayer Gr, using NiFe as a simplified ferromagnetic model. The calculated electronic structures reveal stacking-dependent changes in electronic states near the Fermi level, providing a possible microscopic framework for understanding Gr-mediated modifications of interfacial spin transmission. These findings highlight Gr layer number and stacking configuration as potential parameters for controlling interfacial spin transport in magnetic heterostructures.

articles.title: Adsorption of trans-cinnamamide on pristine and functionalized fullerene: A DFT study
articles.abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to determine adsorption energies (Eads), frontier molecular orbitals (HOMO and LUMO), charge transfer (Q), and partial density of states (PDOS) for the interaction of trans-cinnamamide (CM) with pristine C60 and TiO2-functionalized C60 (C60-TiO2). For pristine C60, these quantum-chemical parameters indicate weak adsorption or desorption, depending on the configuration. By contrast, functionalization markedly increases the magnitude of Eads relative to pristine C60 because bonds form between the Ti atom of C60-TiO2 and C or N atoms of CM in the two most favorable configurations. Charge transfer from the functionalized fullerene to CM further enhances adsorption. The energy-gap (Eg) values indicate that semiconductor-like electronic behavior is retained after adsorption for all systems analyzed. The contribution of “d” electrons is associated with the enhanced adsorption. Solvated Eads values are lower in magnitude than those obtained in the gas phase; nevertheless, the interaction remains sufficiently strong for potential sensing or storage applications. Overall, TiO2-functionalized C60 appears to be a promising system for capturing CM in both the gas and aqueous phases.

articles.title: Graph Neural Network and Fingerprint Attributions of Antibacterial Activity: Atom-Level Agreement Varies Across Random Seeds Reference distributions, topology controls and multi-instance replication
articles.abstract: ML models with different inductive biases are routinely used to prioritise compounds for antibacterial screening, and attribution methods are used to explain them. Circular fingerprints consumed by tree ensembles and message-passing graph networks share neither featurisation nor optimisation, so agreement between their explanations would carry information that neither method alone provides. Whether two independently derived attribution schemes identify the same atoms of the same molecule, and whether such agreement survives retraining, has received little quantitative examination. We curated a published Staphylococcus aureus screen (39,312 compounds, 512 actives) to 38,748 compounds by stereochemistry-aware deduplication and partitioned it by Bemis–Murcko scaffold into training (26,345; 123 actives), validation (4651; 31), and held-out (7752; 302; 3.90%) sets. Fingerprint Random Forest reached a held-out AUPRC of 0.1233 fitted on the training portion alone, and 0.1518 when refitted on training plus validation, with a 9.75-fold enrichment in its top 50; eight AttentiveFP networks differing only in random seed reached a median of 0.0834 (range 0.0587–0.0949). TreeSHAP attributions were verified for additivity (error 3.69 × 10⁻⁷) and projected onto atoms through Morgan bit environments with a coverage normalisation that reduced their correlation with atom degree from + 0.268 to + 0.069; readout attention was obtained by a forward-pass replication verified against the model's own output (logit error 1.91 × 10⁻⁶). Across 60 molecules the median per-molecule Spearman correlation between the two maps was + 0.0890, exceeding a size-matched cross-molecule reference in 6 of 8 instances. The agreement is not topological: the attention–degree association varies in sign across instances (− 0.2562 to + 0.1497) while the |SHAP|–degree association is invariant at + 0.0439. Across instances, the agreement spans − 0.1067 to + 0.1547, a range including both signs, and no prespecified antibiotic core survived Benjamini–Hochberg correction under either scheme. Cross-model atom-level attribution agreement in this low-data regime is small, exceeds a demanding reference in most but not all training runs, and is not attributable to atom connectivity. Because its across-instance range includes both signs, a single training run can misstate both the magnitude and the direction of the agreement it reports. Attribution comparisons in comparable data regimes should be reported as distributions over independently trained instances rather than as point estimates.

articles.title: Flexible polymer nanocomposite film of BiFeO 3 - MnFe 2 O 4 – PMMA for magnetoelectric device applications
articles.abstract: The electric, magnetic, and magnetoelectric characteristics of BiFeO3 - MnFe2O4 - PMMA (BMFO - PMMA) nanocomposite films were examined using the solvent-casting approach. The films' structural examination was carried out using XRD, SEM, AFM, and FTIR spectroscopy, confirming the existence of BiFeO3 and MnFe2O4 phases as well as the amorphous phase of PMMA. At room temperature, magnetoelectric coupling experiments show that the composite film is multiferroic, with considerable magnetoelectric coupling between BiFeO3, MnFe2O4, and PMMA. The coupling coefficient of the ceramic-polymer composite film with increased concentration of nanoparticles measured is 52.22 mV/cmOe, which is lower than the ME coefficient of PMMA alone. At room temperature, the hysteresis loop validates the composite's ferromagnetic characteristic. Improvements include a significantly greater dielectric constant (67), a huge dielectric loss, and a modest increase in ac conductivity. These unique nanocomposites' dielectric characteristics, magnetoelectric coupling, and ferromagnetic properties at room temperature make them highly appealing for magnetoelectric device applications.

articles.title: Enhancing PLA Crystallinity and Thermal Stability through Esparto Microfiber Reinforcement: Implications for Sustainable 3D Printing
articles.abstract: Natural fiber reinforcement offers a route to control polymer crystallization and improve the processability of sustainable materials for additive manufacturing. This study introduces a processing-dependent assessment of PLA reinforced with 1 wt% Esparto microfibers, focusing on thermal stability, crystallization behavior, and potential for fused deposition modeling (FDM). Thermogravimetric analysis showed that the fibers remain thermally stable up to approximately 200°C, with major degradation occurring between 225 and 350°C. Esparto addition increased PLA crystallinity from 28.9% to 36.7%, reduced the cold-crystallization temperature from 121.82°C to 115.41°C, and raised the melting temperature from 159.81°C to 167.12°C, indicating enhanced heterogeneous nucleation. Melt spinning reduced composite crystallinity to 25.3%, demonstrating the influence of processing on polymer structure. Despite this reduction, the composite retained the crystallization benefits of Esparto reinforcement relative to spun PLA. These results establish a link between natural fiber-induced nucleation and processing-dependent thermal behavior, demonstrating the potential of low-content Esparto reinforcement for developing renewable PLA filaments. The findings provide a basis for optimizing processing conditions and advancing Esparto/PLA composites for sustainable FDM applications.

articles.title: Genotype-dependent physiological markers for embryogenic callus induction in Korean pine
articles.abstract: The application of the established somatic embryogenesis (SE) system of Korean pine (Pinus koraiensis) has been largely limited by strong genotype dependence in embryogenic callus (EC) induction. To identify genotype-dependent markers for screening responsive genotypes, we compared physiological traits of one sensitive Korean pine EC-producing genotype and two recalcitrant genotypes: one that produces low-embryogenic callus (LEC) and another that produces non-embryogenic callus (NEC). At the early stage of embryogenic competence acquisition, the EC genotype was characterized by higher indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), methyl jasmonate (MeJA), peroxidase (POD), and malondialdehyde (MDA), coupled with moderate hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), while exhibiting lower abscisic acid (ABA) and catalase (CAT). During subsequent callus expansion without subculture, the EC genotype maintained moderate H2O2, elevated POD and superoxide dismutase (SOD), coupled with a reduced IAA/zeatin-riboside (ZR) ratio and decreased MDA. In contrast, the LEC genotype had lower ZR but higher IAA/ABA, MeJA/ABA, gibberellins (GA3)/ABA, brassinosteroids (BR)/ABA, and ZR/ABA ratios, with significantly reduced SOD, potentially explaining its late‑stage loss of embryogenic competence. In summary, this study identifies stage-specific physiological indicators, including phytohormone profiles, redox homeostasis, and oxidative damage, for early Korean pine genotype screening. Critically, embryogenic competence hinges on a two-phase transition: from "hormone-triggered oxidative signaling" during initiation to "hormonal equilibrium coupled with antioxidative defense" during maintenance, whereas failure (hormonal imbalance plus low SOD) may lead to loss of embryogenic competence in LEC. These findings identify physiological markers for early screening of Korean pine genotypes and provide insights into reversible transition between somatic and embryogenic cell states.

articles.title: Electro–elastic–thermal coupling in electroosmotic transport of viscoelastic fluids: Steric-induced elastic stress restructuring and heat transfer regulation
articles.abstract: Electroosmotic flow (EOF) is a fundamental actuation mechanism in microfluidic systems, where coupled electrokinetic and thermo-hydrodynamic processes govern microscale heat transfer. Under high surface potentials, steric effects and interfacial slip alter the electric double layer (EDL) structure and near-wall transport. In viscoelastic fluids, these interfacial effects further modulate the evolution of polymeric elastic stresses, leading to transport behaviors that deviate markedly from Newtonian EOF. Here, we develop a thermo-electrohydrodynamic model for electroosmotic transport of simplified Phan–Thien–Tanner (sPTT) fluids, incorporating finite ion-size effects and Navier slip. The coupled influences of the steric factor (:v), Debye parameter κ, slip length Ls, solvent viscosity ratio β, extensibility parameter (:ϵDe²), and Brinkman number Br on the flow and thermal fields are systematically investigated. The results reveal a previously unreported mechanism of steric-effect-induced elastic stress restructuring. Unlike Newtonian fluids, where steric effects primarily weaken the electroosmotic driving force through EDL modification, in sPTT fluids increasing (:v) leads to a reduction in near-wall peak normal and shear stresses while broadening their spatial distribution toward the channel core. This stress redistribution modifies the effective viscosity through the constitutive stress function, thereby reshaping velocity and temperature fields. Consequently, distinct thermal behaviors emerge, including enhanced sensitivity of temperature and Nusselt number in the low-κ regime, reversal of the Nu−(:v) response at sufficiently high Br, and slip-induced multi-stage enhancement of heat transfer. The combined action of steric effects and interfacial slip establishes a nonlinear competition between convective transport and internal heat generation, producing thermal responses absent in Newtonian EOF systems.

articles.title: Parametric Optimization of a Two-Dimensional Double Arc Star-Shaped Auxetic Unit Cell Using a Hybrid SEO Algorithm
articles.abstract: Auxetic structures are a class of mechanical metamaterials characterized by a negative Poisson’s ratio, which enables them to contract in the transverse direction when subjected to compression. Their mechanical response strongly depends on the geometry of the unit cell, making parametric optimization an important tool for improving their auxetic behavior. This study presents a procedure for optimizing the geometric parameters of a two-dimensional double arc star-shaped (2D-DASS) unit cell with the objective of minimizing its Poisson’s ratio while maintaining Young’s modulus, solid material volume, and total unit-cell volume within prescribed allowable deviations. The mechanical properties of the unit cell were determined analytically using Castigliano’s second theorem in conjunction with Euler–Bernoulli beam theory. The optimization procedure was applied to seven initial configurations, with the initial angle θ ranging from 35° to 65° in increments of 5°. Five geometric parameters, namely θ, l1, g, l3, and t, were considered as design variables. The results showed that the optimized angle reached 70° in all considered cases, while the constraints on Young’s modulus, solid material volume, and total unit-cell volume were satisfied within the prescribed allowable deviation of ± 0.5%. For initial angles of 35°, 40°, and 45°, the optimization procedure produced negative Poisson’s ratio values despite the positive values obtained from the initial analytical configurations. Furthermore, finite element analyses of structures composed of 3x3 unit cells demonstrated greater horizontal deformation in the optimized configurations under vertical compression. Comparisons between the analytical, optimization, and numerical results showed generally good agreement. The findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed procedure for improving the auxetic response of 2D-DASS unit cells while preserving their principal mechanical and geometric characteristics.

articles.title: Gallium induces an RNR-associated nucleotide crisis and sensitizes osteosarcoma cells to cisplatin
articles.abstract: Gallium (Ga) exhibits antitumor activity, but the mechanisms underlying its cytotoxicity in osteosarcoma remain incompletely defined. Here, we investigated gallium nitrate using LC–MS metabolomics, 13C2-glutamine tracing, iron-rescue experiments, DNA synthesis and damage assays, DepMap dependency analysis, and density functional theory (DFT) modelling. In MG-63 osteosarcoma cells, gallium depleted glycolytic and pentose phosphate pathway intermediates while increasing several ribonucleotide monophosphates and nucleosides and reducing dTTP, consistent with disrupted deoxynucleotide supply. DepMap analysis revealed broad RRM1 and RRM2 dependencies in osteosarcoma models. Gallium reduced EdU incorporation, increased DNA damage detected by alkaline comet assay, and expanded the low-DNA-content/sub-G1 population without clear phase-specific arrest. Iron supplementation rescued gallium-associated loss of viability, whereas cystine, selenium, and ferrostatin-1 did not, arguing against canonical ferroptosis as the dominant death mechanism under these conditions. 13C2-glutamine tracing showed depletion of glutamine, glutamate, and glutathione, with an increased fractional contribution of labeled glutathione driven largely by loss of the unlabeled pool. DFT cluster modelling supported the geometric feasibility of Ga accommodation within an RNR R2-like metal centre. Finally, gallium enhanced cisplatin cytotoxicity within defined concentration ranges, and exogenous deoxynucleosides partially rescued the combination effect. Together, these findings identify an iron-dependent, RNR-associated nucleotide-metabolic vulnerability that links gallium exposure to impaired DNA synthesis and enhanced cisplatin sensitivity in osteosarcoma.

articles.title: Quantum-Assisted Optimization for Ergonomics-Aware Human–Robot Task Allocation in Human-Centric Manufacturing - A QUBO Formulation, Quantum-Annealing and QAOA Benchmark Against Classical Baselines
articles.abstract: Industry 5.0 shifts the focus of manufacturing automation toward human well-being, not just efficiency or output. This means task-allocation systems now have to juggle production targets, ergonomic safety, and what the workforce can realistically handle. Here, we introduce what we call the Ergonomics-Aware Human–Robot Task Allocation (EA-HRTA) problem. Picture it as a complex assignment challenge: for every task, we have to consider execution cost, whether the person or robot has the right skills, the workload each can take on, and the total ergonomic strain humans can safely handle. We turn this challenge into a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model, so it runs on both quantum-annealing machines and gate-model quantum computers. We lay out three key contributions: first, we develop a penalty-based QUBO model and show exactly how to set penalty weights so it actually works. Second, we roll out a complete system where the very same QUBO gets sent both to a D-Wave-style simulated-annealing sampler and to our own lightweight, dependency-free QAOA statevector simulator. Finally, we’ve built and open-sourced a benchmarking suite that lets you see how quantum solutions perform next to a quick, greedy heuristic and a full-scale CBC integer programming baseline.. Across 60 runs spanning problem sizes from 9 to 240 binary variables, quantum annealing maintains a 100% constraint-feasibility rate at every scale tested, matching classical baselines closely on small instances (within 2% of the exact optimum at N = 9) but exhibiting a solution-quality gap that widens to roughly 140% at N = 240 under fixed penalty weights and a fixed annealing schedule. QAOA achieves competitive cost values only at the smallest instance tested (N = 9) and loses feasibility entirely by N = 16, consistent with known near-term gate-model scalability limits. We report a warm-start ablation seeding the annealer with the greedy solution, which does not yield a consistent improvement, and use this negative result to motivate an adaptive-penalty and problem-decomposition research direction. Rather than claiming a present-day quantum advantage, this paper contributes a reusable ergonomics-aware QUBO formulation, a transparent and reproducible benchmark methodology for the human-centric manufacturing community, and an honest empirical map of where current quantum optimization methods stand relative to classical practice at realistic shop-floor problem sizes.

articles.title: One-pot fabrication of durable antibacterial cotton fabric coated with silver nanoparticles via banana peel as a binder and stabilizer
articles.abstract: The development of sustainable antibacterial textiles using plant-derived resources offers a promising strategy for reducing the environmental and health concerns associated with conventional textile functionalization. In this study, a one-pot, in-situ approach was developed for the fabrication of silver nanoparticle (AgNP)-functionalized cotton fabric using banana-peel extract as a natural reducing, stabilizing, and binding agent. The formation and immobilization of AgNPs on cotton fibers were investigated as a function of reaction time (5–45 min) using FE-SEM, EDX, XRD, FTIR, and Raman spectroscopy. FE-SEM revealed a progressive transformation from a relatively clean cellulose surface to finely dispersed Ag-containing nanoparticles at 5 min, followed by increased surface coverage at 25 min and larger, partially aggregated particles at 45 min, demonstrating time-dependent nucleation, growth, and immobilization. EDX confirmed silver incorporation, with Ag contents of 4.22, 24.79, and 8.44 wt% at 5, 25, and 45 min, respectively. XRD confirmed the formation of crystalline metallic Ag⁰ while retaining the characteristic crystalline structure of cellulose; the Ag (111) reflection yielded an average crystallite size of 52 nm. FTIR and Raman analyses indicated modification of the cellulose surface and interactions involving cellulose and extract-derived constituents during AgNP formation. The functionalized fabrics exhibited antibacterial activity against both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, with maximum inhibition zones of 9.8 and 12.9 mm, respectively. Overall, the results demonstrate that banana-peel extract enables a simple, green, and efficient route for producing AgNP-coated cotton with promising antibacterial functionality for potential antimicrobial textile applications.

articles.title: Electricity-Secure Sustainable Closed-Loop Supply Chain Design at the Production-Land-Energy Nexus: A Data-Driven Co-Optimization Framework for the Steel Industry
articles.abstract: Energy shortages, resource scarcity, and limited industrial land can infeasible the attractive steelmaking locations. This study develops an integrated robust optimization framework for a sustainable closed-loop DRI-EAF steel supply chain in which facility location, production-line selection, scrap recovery, wastewater reuse, on-site electricity generation, and industrial-land allocation are co-planned. The central modeling contribution is the endogenous competition for a common, finite land resource between steel production, photovoltaic systems, and diesel-fueled CHP units of different capacities. This coupling allows electricity-constrained candidate locations to remain feasible when the economic and operational value of the site justifies appropriately sized on-site generation. A data driven approach is used to model polynomial regression based on historical temperature, solar-irradiance, and energy-consumption data to estimate location- and period-specific electricity conditions, natural-gas availability, and solar-generation potential; bounded uncertainty is then handled through robust optimization. The multi-objective MILP model proposed to minimize total system cost and CO2 emissions while maximizing surplus on-site electricity exported to the grid. In the case study, the selected design generates approximately 1.29E + 10 kWh of on-site electricity annually, including 6.94E + 9 kWh from solar PV, and exports 5.34E + 9 kWh to the grid. The associated circular-resource strategy avoids approximately 6.10E + 6 t of iron-ore extraction, mitigates approximately 2.80E + 9 kg of CO2 emissions, reuses approximately 2.15E + 8 m of wastewater, and creates 7,415 jobs. The results show that industrial land is an active coupling resource between production expansion and energy security, rather than a passive siting parameter, and that coordinated energy-land-production planning can preserve technically constrained but strategically attractive steelmaking locations.

articles.title: Partition of Unity Data-driven Finite Element Method for Anisotropic Diffusion in Magnetized Plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Numerical simulation of transport processes in magnetized plasmas is characterized by extreme anisotropy, where diffusion along magnetic field lines can be many orders of magnitude larger than in the perpendicular direction. This anisotropy leads to thin, steep boundary layers and numerical pollution that standard finite element methods struggle to resolve without prohibitive mesh refinement. In this paper, we introduce the Partition of Unity Data-Driven Finite Element Method (PU-DDFEM), a data-driven local model reduction approach, for anisotropic diffusion. The method utilizes a bottom-up construction to enable a complete offline-online splitting. We parametrize the local magnetic field and boundary conditions to generate a snapshot space that captures the essential physics of plasma confinement. Dominant modes are extracted via a local spectral problem to identify representative features. These modes are then mapped to the global domain using a partition of unity to form a conforming approximation space. This ensures that the basis functions are fully reusable across different global magnetic configurations, significantly reducing the online computational overhead for large-scale plasma simulations.

articles.title: Electron--phonon matrix elements for hybrid functionals in the projector augmented-wave method: Eigenvalue projection, nondiagonal supercells, and Wannier interpolation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2503.11013v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a finite-displacement approach to electron--phonon matrix elements that requires only eigenvalues and wave functions from the displaced calculations, for both norm-conserving pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave (PAW) method. Extending the eigenvalue-projectability approach, previously formulated for norm-conserving pseudopotentials, we reconstruct the displaced Hamiltonian from the displaced eigenvalues and from overlaps evaluated in the PAW metric of each displaced structure. Analytic terms constructed from the PAW dataset then yield the all-electron matrix element, without derivatives of the local potential or of the PAW strengths. The approach therefore applies in principle to any electronic-structure method available in PAW. To reduce the supercell cost, we combine it with nondiagonal supercells that sample the Brillouin zone equivalently to the primitive cell and recover the full matrix elements by crystal symmetry. Implemented in the ARES-EPC code, the method reproduces matrix elements from density-functional perturbation theory (DFPT) and from VASP+phelel for seven materials with mean absolute errors below 0.5 meV. Nondiagonal supercells reproduce the diagonal-supercell results to the same accuracy and reduce the cost of the displaced calculations by up to a factor of 23. Through an interface to EPW, the norm-conserving matrix elements give an electron mobility of Si within 0.9% of that from DFPT. The HSE06 hybrid functional increases the mobility of Si by 13% relative to the PBE functional, because the lighter conduction band and the harder phonons outweigh the stronger coupling.

articles.title: Quantum geometric ferromagnetism by singular saddle point
articles.abstract: arXiv:2505.01089v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose ferromagnetism that occurs in electrons at a saddle point with band touching, which we call the singular saddle point. At the singular saddle point, the divergent quantum metric induces ferromagnetic correlation, and the logarithmic divergence of the density of states ensures ferromagnetism within Stoner theory. This is a prototypical example of quantum geometric ferromagnetism. The two-dimensional t₂g-orbital model accommodates the ferromagnetism by this mechanism, which is continuously connected to the exactly proven flat-band ferromagnetism.

articles.title: Evidence for time-reversal symmetry breaking and glassy dynamics in superconducting (La,Pr,Sm)3Ni2O7 films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.16412v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Superconductivity and magnetism are generally distinct and competing orders, characterized by different broken symmetries and order parameters. Although they may coexist in some correlated systems, whether and how these orders can become inherently intertwined in unconventional high-transition-temperature (high-Tc) superconductors remains a central open question. Here, we report time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking and glassy dynamics in the superconducting state of nickelate (La,Pr,Sm)3Ni2O7 films. Magnetoresistance hysteresis and zero-field non-reciprocal charge transport, complementary evidence for broken TRS, are observed in the superconducting state, while absent in the normal state. Within the superconducting transition regime, logarithmically slow resistance relaxations following magnetic-field perturbations provide strong evidence for glassy dynamics. Remarkably, the reproducible temperature hierarchy across multiple films reveals that these novel phenomena emerge concurrently with developing superconducting phase coherence, preceding the zero-resistance state. Consistently, scanning superconducting quantum interference device (sSQUID) microscopy directly resolves the zero-field magnetic-flux patterns indicative of spontaneous TRS breaking, which emerge simultaneously with local superconducting diamagnetism and phase stiffness. Our observations suggest a frustrated multicomponent superconducting order parameter in the nickelate films, whose internal relative phases may carry TRS-breaking chirality and freeze into a textured phase glass. Collectively, our findings identify a distinctive form of superconductivity in which internal phase degrees of freedom may support additional broken symmetries and glassy order, offering a new perspective on intertwined ordering phenomena in unconventional high-Tc superconductors.

articles.title: Dynamics of CPN⁻¹ skyrmions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.17403v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive several exact results for the dynamics of CPN⁻¹ skyrmions with arbitrary N. Fractonic continuity equation is shown to hold for arbitrary CPN⁻¹ fluid implying the conservation of the topological charge and the dipole moment. Inclusion of the Gilbert damping modifies the continuity equation, resulting in the violation of the dipole moment conservation but not of the topological charge. Thiele's equation for the CPN⁻¹ skyrmion follows from the modified continuity equation. The Girvin-MacDonald-Platzman (GMP) algebra in the long-wavelength limit is derived for arbitrary CPN⁻¹ fluid. In the case of CP² skyrmions, we construct a finite-size skyrmion with dominant ferromagnetic moments. We find that its magnetic dipole texture carries a nonzero CP¹ charge equal to half the CP² skyrmion charge and argue that the topological Hall effect of electrons should exist due to their coupling to the ferromagnetic part of the CP² texture.

articles.title: Predicting Coherent B2 Stability in Ru-Containing Refractory Alloys Through Thermodynamic Elastic Design Maps
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.01326v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The development of next-generation refractory superalloys is fundamentally constrained by competing requirements of high thermodynamic stability and low interfacial energy. Ru-based B2 intermetallics possess strong intrinsic ordering, but their use as coherent reinforcing phases requires balancing formation enthalpy against elastic strain. Here, we present a physics-guided machine-learning framework that integrates high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), Random Forest screening, and symbolic regression to map this design space. The approach addresses the "binary paradox" observed in recent experimental studies, where strongly ordered Ru-refractory compounds do not necessarily achieve the highest solvus temperatures. The resulting closed-form relation, T_solvus ~ 0.11(Delta H/Delta S) - 20000|delta|, quantifies the competing effects of thermodynamic stabilization and lattice misfit. Because the electronic-structure calculations are static 0 K calculations, the relation is treated as an effective calibrated design equation rather than a directly calculated finite-temperature free-energy boundary. The model is benchmarked against published B2 solvus measurements, while calculated formation enthalpies and lattice parameters are independently compared with calorimetric and diffraction data. Within the fitted relation, a 1% lattice misfit corresponds to an effective solvus penalty of approximately 200 degrees C. Al/Si substitution further shows that improved lattice matching is accompanied by reduced thermodynamic stabilization, with zero misfit near 11 at.% Al and 7 at.% Si for Nb75V25.

articles.title: When does a lattice higher-form symmetry flow to a topological higher-form symmetry at low energies?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.20935v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the lattice version of higher-form symmetries on tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Interestingly, at low energies, these symmetries may not flow to the topological higher-form symmetries familiar from relativistic quantum field theories, but instead to non-topological higher-form symmetries. We present concrete lattice models exhibiting this phenomenon. One particular model is an R generalization of the Kitaev honeycomb model featuring an R lattice 1-form symmetry. We show that its low-energy effective field theory is a gapless, non-relativistic theory with a non-topological R 1-form symmetry. In both the lattice model and the effective field theory, we demonstrate that the non-topological R 1-form symmetry is not robust against local perturbations. In contrast, we also study various modifications of the toric code and their low-energy effective field theories to demonstrate that the compact Z₂ lattice 1-form symmetry does become topological at low energies unless the Hamiltonian is fine-tuned. Along the way, we clarify the rules for constructing low-energy effective field theories in the presence of multiple superselection sectors. Finally, we argue on general grounds that non-compact higher-form symmetries (such as R and Z 1-form symmetries) in lattice systems generically remain non-topological at low energies, whereas compact higher-form symmetries (such as Zₙ and U(1) 1-form symmetries) generically become topological.

articles.title: From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.06800v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behaviour of CaCO₃ in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. Here, we combine advances in machine learning and electronic structure theory to fully resolve the ion pairing free energy of CaCO₃ with explicit solvation. We show that achieving quantitative agreement with experiment requires going beyond density functional theory up to the ''gold-standard'' coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]. We generate a set of systematically improvable models, enabling reliable insights into the initial association mechanism of Ca and CO₃ ions prior to nucleation while fully quantifying enthalpic and entropic effects. These quantitatively accurate models further resolve a long-standing lack of consensus surrounding the hydration mechanism of the calcium ion in solution. Our results demonstrate that CCSD(T)-level thermodynamic predictions of complex aqueous systems can now be routinely achieved.

articles.title: Giant spontaneous Kerr effect and its self-doping dependence in altermagnetic MnTe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.21021v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Altermagnetism, a third class of collinear magnetism with spin-split bands and vanishing net magnetization, has emerged in hexagonal α-MnTe, a promising platform for ultrafast, stray-field-free spintronics. Whether MnTe's macroscopic symmetry-breaking signatures reflect ideal altermagnetic order or are activated by defects remains open. Here we report giant spontaneous Kerr rotations of up to 1500 rad in α-MnTe single crystals at the telecommunication wavelength of 1550 nm, onsetting precisely at the Néel temperature TN = 307 K. The signal appears in disjoint macroscopic patches whose amplitude tracks the sample conductivity, and a hole-conducting α-MnTe film reproduces this response together with an anomalous Hall effect. Within a single crystal, Kerr-active regions are optically distinct from their Kerr-silent surroundings in co-registered reflection maps. These observations indicate that carrier self-doping, rather than ideal altermagnetic order alone, governs the giant magneto-optical response, and establish telecom-wavelength Kerr imaging as a practical readout for altermagnetic spintronics.

articles.title: Evaluation of External Magnetic Flux Density in Piezo-Flexomagnetic Nanobeams Using a Hybrid 1D-2D Finite Element Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.19422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Most theoretical models of piezo-flexomagnetic nanostructures forcibly impose magnetic isolation at the structure-air interface, neglecting the external magnetic domain entirely. This mathematical compromise limits the model's capability to account for stray-field behavior in non-contact applications. To overcome this gap, our study proposes a fully coupled hybrid finite element formulation combining a 1D Timoshenko beam model with a 2D magneto-static problem, encompassing both the beam body and the surrounding air domain. By continuously mapping 1D structural kinematics into the 2D space to define the mechanically induced magnetic flux, and subsequently integrating the resulting 2D scalar potential back into 1D static generalized magnetic loads, this framework enhances the capability of the simple 1D beam model. The results present the distribution of an external magnetic flux in piezo-flexomagnetic structures and identify the material parameters driving this.
