Power-dependent and polarization-resolved measurements confirm the second-order nonlinear origin of the observed response and reveal anisotropic emission patterns. Our results demonstrate a direct correlation between spacer-induced center-symmetry breaking and nonlinear optical activity. These results establish quasi-2D halide perovskites as a promising class of symmetry-engineered materials for efficient frequency conversion and integrated nonlinear photonics.

articles.title: What Can Next Generation Ultrafast Light Sources Tell Us About Quantum Materials?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15997v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ultrafast spectroscopy of quantum materials has emerged as a principle application of modern ultrafast optical sources. Measurements made with ultrashort pulses allow the normally strongly coupled internal degrees of freedom inside these systems to be de-coupled in the time-domain, revealing the key interactions for the different orders that lead to dramatic emergent phenomena. This has naturally motivated a wide range of experiments, and quantum materials have now been studied with ultrafast sources spanning from the hard X-ray to the THz, with fields intense enough to create non-equilibrium states, and using pulses down to the attosecond duration. As the optical spectroscopist's toolbox becomes increasingly complete, it is worth pausing and reflecting on what are the capabilities that we currently lack for examining quantum materials, and what are the problems that require the next generation of ultrafast sources now coming on-line or being designed. Here I will offer an overview of the remaining missing capabilities in ultrafast optical sources as required for studying quantum materials, and identify some outstanding problems where I believe these new sources can provide decisive impact in our understanding of quantum and strongly-correlated materials.

articles.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed k₀ and k₁. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength k₁ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the k₁ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and g-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.

articles.title: Establishing Standards for Assessment and Reporting of SNSPD Performance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) can be made sensitive to single photons with near-unity detection efficiency, ultra-low dark-count rates, and sub-nanosecond timing jitter over a broad wavelength range. However, many studies report data inconsistently, often emphasizing a single performance metric without considering overall device performance. This inconsistent data reporting limits the field, as it makes it difficult to determine which device characteristics are most important. Different applications require functionalities that may conflict with one another; for example, longer-wavelength operation may require lower operating temperatures. Moreover, there is no universally accepted metric for defining the figures of merit of an SNSPD. In this work, we amass a dataset representing the state of the art of SNSPD fabrication, including operating temperature, operating wavelength, photon count rates (PCR), and dark count rates (DCR). We fit the PCR curves and suggest using the saturation plateau length to gauge the SNSPD's sensitivity. We then fit the DCR and compare the PCR and DCR. Using this approach, we establish a quantitative framework to determine the optimal biasing condition for a given device and to determine the device's sensitivity at that optimal biasing condition, enabling meaningful comparisons across disparate devices. Additionally, we offer concrete benchmarks for measuring device performance.

articles.title: Fragility of Aeolian Ripples
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sand surfaces exposed to the wind are covered by aeolian sand waves of diverse wavelengths, from centimetres for small ripples to decameters for dunes. Sand dunes can be said to be antifragile, since their growth is not prohibited by storms, whereas ripples and megaripples are fragile since they get flattened. The fluid-entrainment hypothesis attributes their fragility to a common cause: the spontaneous aerodynamic entrainment of grains. Here, we challenge this conventional view by revealing its major shortcomings and inconsistencies. An alternative framework, routed in the granular bed rheology, posits that impact ripples are erased when the two-phase flow of ballistically hopping grains on a solid sand surface gives way to a three-phase flow, featuring an intermediate, collision-dominated, fluid-like transport layer. Notably, both martian wind-drag ripples and terrestrial aerodynamic ripples, which emerge via a hydrodynamic instability, are insensitive to such "surface-melting". Their destruction is predicated on the transition from aerodynamically smooth to rough conditions, instead. Our theoretical arguments are well supported by a stability diagram in terms of Shields number and grain diameter, assembled from a carefully reassessed large body of literature, and backed up by dedicated control measurements.

articles.title: Turbulent velocity statistics in convective boundary layers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-eddy simulations (LES) of the convective atmospheric boundary layer (CBL) are used to investigate velocity variance statistics in turbulent sheared convection. The thirteen simulations span conditions from weak convection with longitudinal rolls to free penetrative convection with no mean wind. In the presence of thermal rolls, the near-surface streamwise variance profile exhibits an approximately logarithmic decay with a slope proportional to the friction velocity, u_*, and an added constant proportional to the convective velocity, w_star. After the structural transition to convective cells, both the streamwise and spanwise variances follow the empirical stability and height dependencies of Wilson (Boundary-Layer Meteorol., 2008, vol. 129, pp. 353--369). The near-surface vertical (wall-normal) velocity variance is well described by Monin--Obukhov similarity with improved agreement using local-in-height scaling. Within the mixed layer, the peak vertical variance initially decreases relative to w_star as shear diminishes, before increasing and shifting downward as the flow approaches free convection. In contrast, the total turbulent energy decreases relative to w_star across the parameter space. The spanwise velocity variance represents the dominant turbulent component under weak convection and exceeds the streamwise variance throughout most of the convective regime. These statistical trends are attributed to the role of pressure, evaluated through variance budget contributions. Large-scale buoyancy production in the mixed layer is transported downward by pressure and redistributed preferentially to the spanwise component, coinciding with the presence of longitudinal roll motions. The weakening of this pressure-transport pathway for convective cells coincides with greater retention of vertical variance within the mixed layer.

articles.title: Data-driven Reconstruction of the Phase Dynamics for the El Niño-Southern Oscillation Reveals Seasonality and Statistical Synchronization with the Annual Cycle
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we treat the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) as a rhythmic system periodically forced by the annual cycle. We examine ENSO event seasonality and synchronization between the annual and ENSO cycles. We compute phase time series for both cycles from sea surface temperature data using a data-driven Koopman operator approach. We then use Bayesian inference to reconstruct phase equations describing how the phases of the two oscillators evolve. The reconstructed two-variable phase equations show that the annual cycle modulates the instantaneous frequency of the fundamental ENSO mode. Stochastic simulations of these equations incorporating the estimated stationary noise indicate that El Niño and La Niña events tend to last longer when they start in boreal summer and that the variability of their durations is greater when they start in boreal spring. Furthermore, the averaged form of the phase equations indicates statistical 3:1 phase locking between the annual and ENSO cycles, whereas no statistical phase locking is found for the other m:n ratios.

articles.title: Effect of Gas Pressure and Molecular Structure in the Spatial-Mode Conversion of Terahertz Radiation from a Plasma Filament
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, the generation of terahertz (THz) radiation under single color filamentation of a femtosecond laser pulse in an optical cell with compressed gases (argon, nitrogen, CO2) in broad pressure range from 0.001 to 25 atm is experimentally studied for the first time. A nonmonotonic dependence of the integral energy of the THz signal on the gas pressure is revealed, which can be attributed to the competition between an increase in the plasma density and the development of plasma selfabsorption processes, multiple filamentation of the femtosecond pump, and collision induced absorption in the neutral medium. We show that the molecular structure of the gas critically determines the pressure optimum of generation, shifting the maximum of the THz energy yield to the region of elevated pressures (from 10 to 15 atm) for monatomic argon and to the region of subatmospheric pressures (approx. 0.1 atm) for molecular carbon dioxide due to strong vibrational rotational dissipation. On the basis of numerical 3D modeling, it is shown that the cylindrical metal waveguide insert used for signal collection operates in a strongly multimode regime and substantially transforms the angular spectrum of the THz source. We demonstrate that the conical structure of the THz radiation recorded in the experiment is a consequence of intermode interference and diffraction at the output end face of the waveguide, which transforms the true parameters of THz generation in the plasma channel.

articles.title: A Field-Deployable 2U Ultra-Stable Laser with Sub-Hertz Linewidth Based on Optoelectronic Oscillator Locking
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact, high-performance ultra-stable lasers that can operate outside the laboratory remain a long-standing goal. Here we report, to our knowledge, the most compact field-deployable ultra-stable laser, packaged in a standard 2U rack chassis. It is stabilized to a 50 mm-long, 19 mL optical reference cavity with low vibration sensitivity by optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) locking, an approach particularly suited to compact, transportable systems. The laser delivers an integrated linewidth of about 0.42 Hz and a fractional frequency stability of about 5E-15 at 1 s averaging time (about 2.2E-15 at 0.4 s). Measured phase noise approaches the cavity thermal-noise limit below 100 Hz and the theoretical OEO-locking limit from 100 Hz to 100 kHz. The system volume is roughly one quarter of the volume of previously reported integrated, transportable ultra-stable lasers of comparable performance, making it well suited for field applications in time-frequency metrology, quantum technologies, and environmental sensing.

articles.title: Melting Ice Activates Mechanical Forcing from Entrapped Air
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Natural ice commonly contains entrapped air, yet its dynamical role during melting remains unresolved. Using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis, we show that melt-front-released bubbles activate entrapped air as a mechanical forcing on the liquid. Bubble buoyancy disrupts density-anomaly-induced thermal structure and injects momentum into the melt-controlling boundary layer, producing melt rates more than twice the bubble-free value at percent-level gas fractions. The evolving interface and background convection regulate this coupling, which weakens again under sufficiently vigorous convection, producing a finite coupling window. A mechanical-power ratio comparing bubble-generated and background-flow power organizes this behavior. Recasting the bubble contribution as an effective near-boundary velocity extends standard ice-ocean melt closures, while reported field conditions can enter the mechanically significant regime. More broadly, a moving phase boundary can activate an embedded dispersed phase as an internal mechanical forcing.

articles.title: Data-driven non-contiguous photon-energy groups for fast multigroup radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Opacity of mid- and high-Z plasmas is dominated by thousands of overlapping spectral lines. Examples are laser-produced plasmas for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, inertial-fusion hohlraums, and stellar interiors. Radiation transport in such plasmas needs more than 1000 photon-energy groups in the EUV case, and this makes radiation-hydrodynamic simulations very expensive. We show that the accuracy of a small-group opacity model can be recovered by choosing properly emphwhich fine bins are put into the same group. We present a data-driven method that assigns the fine bins of a detailed opacity and emissivity table to K emphnon-contiguous groups. Each group has a fixed spectral shape inside it. The groups follow from one requirement: the reduced absorption operator must be diagonal for every plasma state. They are determined from a Gram matrix of spectra, taken from detailed-group solutions of a small part, for example 5% in this work, of the parameter space. The reduced model is a set of K uncoupled flux-limited diffusion equations. It can be used in an existing multigroup code by replacing the opacity table. For a Sn plasma with electron densities of 4×10¹⁵--1.1×10²¹~cm⁻³, electron temperatures of 5--250~eV, and scale lengths of 2.5--6900um, the model with K=100 reproduces the total flux of the 1500-group reference with a median error of 2% and a 90th-percentile error of 8%. The 90th-percentile error is ten times smaller than that of a conventional 100-group model at the same cost.

articles.title: Extension of the Renard-Deck Drag Decomposition to Compressible Rough-Wall Turbulent Boundary Layers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A generalized Renard-Deck (RD) drag decomposition is developed for spatially developing compressible turbulent boundary layers over rough surfaces. Derived from the locally resolved, time-averaged momentum equations, the formulation accounts for both viscous friction and pressure drag without requiring spatial averaging at the roughness-element scale. Eight direct numerical simulations are considered at freestream Mach numbers of 2.5 and 5.86, comparing smooth walls and two-dimensional transverse square ribs (λₓ/k=8) under adiabatic and cold-wall conditions. The decomposition reconstructs the total drag with errors below 5%. Mean-flow viscous dissipation and turbulent kinetic-energy production together account for approximately 90% of the drag work. While their contributions are comparable over smooth walls, turbulent production dominates over rough walls, contributing approximately 80%. More importantly, roughness substantially alters the wall-normal distributions of both contributions. Viscous dissipation becomes concentrated near the roughness crest, whereas turbulent production peaks above the crest, with both contributions decaying more gradually into the outer layer than over smooth walls. The resulting differences in their cumulative contributions persist across a substantial fraction of the boundary layer, demonstrating that the energetic influence of surface roughness extends well beyond the roughness sublayer.

articles.title: Hypersonic Flow Over an Axisymmetric Open Cavity: Effects of Segmentation Angle and Reynolds Number
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study investigates the influence of cavity segmentation angle (φ) on the flow characteristics of a cavity mounted on a cone under Mach 6 freestream conditions in a Ludwieg tunnel. Four segmentation configurations, corresponding to φ = 360^circ, 48^circ, 32^circ, and 16^circ, are examined for cavity length-to-depth ratios (L/D) of 1 and 6 over a range of Reynolds numbers (Re_D = 23000--74000). The flow field is characterized using surface pressure and heat flux measurements, complemented by planar laser Rayleigh scattering visualization. The results indicate that, for L/D = 1, the downstream Strouhal number (St) and mean pressure remain largely unaffected by the segmentation angle and closely agree with those of the axisymmetric configuration. In contrast, the flow parameters within the cavity are larger than in the axisymmetric case, which is attributed to the three-dimensional bounding effect. For L/D = 6, the mean pressure distribution exhibits a similar trend across the segmentation angles, whereas the downstream St increases with increasing φ, approaching the axisymmetric value. Flow-mode transitions are observed across all segmentation angles, consistent with the axisymmetric configuration. However, both the transition Reynolds numbers and the corresponding flow modes vary with the segmentation angle.

articles.title: An Analytical Model for Fast Design Optimization and Performance Studies of nuSTORM
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The concept of generating neutrino beams from stored muons (nuSTORM) has been explored for several decades. A few nuSTORM facilities have been designed for GeV muons, and a design of a sub-GeV nuSTORM, proposed for the European Spallation Source, is now underway. At low energy, the much larger beam divergence can significantly reduce the neutrino flux reaching the detector. Therefore, optimization of facility parameters is essential to avoid additional flux losses. This optimization, however, is not trivial due to the interdependency of the parameters. In this paper, we derive an analytical expression for the absolute neutrino flux incident on the detector front face and show how it can guide the optimization of a nuSTORM facility. The analytical expression is furthermore validated with published data and Monte Carlo simulations from five separate cases. In addition, we show how it can be extended to also predict the neutrino energy distribution at the detector, thus offering a convenient method to estimate the facility performance without time-consuming Monte Carlo simulations of particle transport and decay.
authors: J. P. A. M. de André

articles.title: Advancing global water cycle science with the upcoming MAGIC satellite mission through data assimilation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The GRACE and GRACE-FO missions provide unique global measurements of terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA) from space since 2003. However, in order to spatially downscale the GRACE/-FO resolution of 300 km further, and to vertically disaggregate TWSA into soil moisture, groundwater and other contributions, the TWSA observations were assimilated into hydrological and land surface models in the past while improving the realism of the models. With the upcoming MAGIC (Mass Change and Geosciences International Constellation) constellation consisting of two satellite pairs (NASA/DLR GRACE-C and ESA NGGM), significant advancements are expected for the monitoring of water mass changes, with improved temporal and spatial resolution, reduced latency, and with lower noise levels. In this study, we reviewed the capabilities and limitations of existing GRACE/-FO data assimilation systems. We then investigated the benefit of including data from the upcoming MAGIC constellation into existing assimilation frameworks to improve not only data sets for water and carbon cycle science but also in view of operational applications, within a closed-loop simulation. For example, we extended a global 17 years GRACE/-FO assimilation era to a long time series of 33 years with synthetic MAGIC data assimilated and show reductions in groundwater trends errors and errors in identifying hydrological extreme events. We further showed for Europe that both storage and river runoff simulations benefit from more frequent assimilation, which the integration of MAGIC data will enable due to the foreseen 5-daily (instead of monthly) TWSA product. Finally, we demonstrated for the Iberian Peninsula and for Eastern Europe that MAGIC TWSA data assimilation also improved simulated carbon cycle variables via coupling in the land surface model, especially in water-limited regions.

articles.title: Quantum-logic detection of rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collisions between molecules govern chemical reactions and energy transfer across a range of different environments from interstellar space to the Earth's atmosphere. Despite their fundamental importance, molecular collisions have traditionally been studied through ensemble-averaged experiments which obscure the dynamics of individual scattering events on the quantum level. Probing single molecular collisions with quantum-state resolution has thus far remained a major experimental challenge. Here, we demonstrate a method for detecting individual rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecular ions with neutral atoms using quantum-logic techniques. We prepare individual trapped N₂⁺ ions in their rotational ground state, subject them to a beam of helium atoms and detect isolated collision events through their effects on the motion of the trapped ions. Quantum-logic-spectroscopic measurements reveal changes of the molecular state upon collision enabling the determination of the probability of rotationally inelastic scattering. The experiments are analysed by comparison with quantum and classical scattering calculations yielding detailed insights into the underlying collision dynamics. By combining single-collision detection with non-destructive readout of the molecular quantum state, our approach establishes a new experimental framework for investigating molecular scattering beyond conventional ensemble measurements. It opens a route towards investigating state-to-state scattering in individual molecules and exploring molecular interactions at the level of single quantum-state resolved events.

articles.title: Laser-induced damage threshold of periodic plasmonic metasurfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Plasmonic metasurfaces enable strong nonlinear optical responses due to sub-wavelength field confinement, yet their performance is fundamentally limited by low laser-induced damage thresholds (LIDT). Here, we present a comprehensive experimental and numerical study of the interplay between surface lattice resonances (SLRs), second-harmonic generation (SHG), and LIDT in periodic gold nanobar metasurfaces. Angle-resolved measurements reveal that excitation of SLRs at the fundamental wavelength strongly enhances SHG efficiency while simultaneously reducing the LIDT. In contrast, excitation of an SLR at the second-harmonic wavelength does not affect the damage threshold, allowing the SHG signal to be maximized. Our findings establish a fundamental trade-off between nonlinear efficiency and optical robustness and provide design guidelines for optimizing periodic plasmonic metasurfaces for high-power nonlinear applications.

articles.title: Development of millikelvin scintillation photodetectors with CUPID
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: CUPID is a next-generation tonne-scale cryogenic experiment that will search for the neutrinoless double beta decay (0νββ) of ¹⁰⁰Mo. It will be located at the Gran Sasso National Laboratory (Italy) and will employ the cryogenic calorimetric technique to reconstruct the energy deposited in Li₂MoO₄ crystals, in which the isotope of interest is embedded. Preliminary measurements have been performed with the CUPID VSTT (Vertical Slice Test Tower), a prototype tower designed to test the detectors' response and the apparatus' mechanical and thermal stability. In addition, a key objective was to demonstrate the improved performance of germanium-based cryogenic light detectors. In CUPID, light detection is used for both particle identification and pile-up rejection. Li₂MoO₄ is a scintillating crystal, enabling particle identification by exploiting the dependence of light yield on particle type. This requires collecting the Li₂MoO₄ scintillation light, peaking at sim600 nm, with a sim300 μm-thick high-purity germanium wafer placed next to the crystal. The wafer is also equipped with concentric Al electrodes biased at a few tens of volts. This bias improves the signal-to-noise ratio by an order of magnitude thanks to the Neganov-Trofimov-Luke effect. This work presents preliminary results on the performance of the VSTT light detectors and of its Optical Injection System.

articles.title: Open Quantum System Embedded in an Optimized Reservoir of Molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-boundary Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics (QM/MM) simulation provides a direct way to test whether a quantum subsystem and its surrounding classical reservoir are physically consistent. Here we use this framework to replace a standard flexible TIP3P reservoir by a dipole-renormalized (DR) Amber-compatible three-site water model optimized against a full ab initio trajectory of liquid water. The renormalization targets the molecular dipole distribution and adjusts the atomic charges, bonded, and Lennard-Jones interaction parameters through a stochastic optimization procedure. In the case of a large QM region (langle Nrangleapprox 440), where the surface-to-volume ratio is small, the DR reservoir induces, as expected, Grand Canonical statistics for the quantum subsystem. In smaller subsystems (langle Nrangleapprox 190), where the surface-to-volume condition is deliberately less favorable, the same reservoir shows substantially improved molecular consistency with the QM region relative to the non-renormalized flexible TIP3P model. These results show that quantum information at molecular dipole level is crucial for the microscopic physics of liquid water. When this concept is transferred into a classical reservoir, it can be used to extend the reliable regime of adaptive open-QM/MM water simulations even beyond the physically dictated Grand Canonical conditions. end{abstract

articles.title: Radiation Hardness Assurance of Optical Coatings for the COMPASSO Iodine Reference
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The COMPASSO payload demonstrates compact iodine-based optical frequency references on the International Space Station (ISS), requiring optical windows and antireflective coatings that remain stable in the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) radiation environment. Radiation analysis was performed to quantify how trapped electrons, protons, and ions affect the fused-silica iodine cell and its coatings under mission-relevant shielding and exposure scenarios. The aim was to determine whether selected coatings meet the COMPASSO optical requirements after realistic LEO irradiation, identify degradation mechanisms linked to deposition technology and materials, and provide selection guidance for coatings used in spaceborne iodine spectroscopy and optical-clock payloads. Nominal and worst-case corpuscular environments for the ISS orbit were derived using AE8/AP8, CREME96, ESP, and ISO15390 models. Eight coating stacks produced by different deposition methods were exposed to proton and electron irradiation corresponding to the nominal and worst-case mission loads. Pre- and post-irradiation characterization included reflectance and transmittance measurements, together with visual and microscopic inspection. The tests led to the selection of a four-layer Ta₂O₅/SiO₂ stack for the iodine cell optical window. Total ionizing dose levels for all layers of the selected coating were derived with GRAS, showing that the coating will not be affected by corpuscular radiation for years in the LEO ISS environment, including the COMPASSO mission at the ISS Bartolomeo platform.

articles.title: Buffer-Gas-Assisted Fluorescence Spectroscopy of Molecular Ions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustained fluorescence detection of generic molecules has been challenging due to the lack of cycling transitions and limited photon budgets. We demonstrate a nondestructive method for continuous fluorescence of strongly rovibronically open molecular ions, ²³²ThF⁺. Effective quasi-cycling transitions are established by room-temperature buffer-gas collisions, which replenish the population back to the laser-addressed states. In situ images and rotationally resolved spectra are obtained without optical repumping or auxiliary atomic readout ions. Combined with low-background spectroscopic detection, this approach achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 6 in a 1 s exposure on the P(1) line of ²³²ThF⁺, despite a thermal population of only approximately 0.17% in the addressed state at room temperature. The ability to repeatedly interrogate trapped ions is particularly promising for scarce molecular samples, broadband spectroscopic searches, and in situ monitoring of molecular reactions.

articles.title: Flow Structure in Idealized Rotating Detonation Combustor with Supersonic Inflow
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The work presented investigates the flow structure and stability of an airbreathing rotating detonation engine (RDE) in an idealized combustor. The presented derivation of a modified pressure cutoff injection scheme allows for supersonic injection in an idealized two-dimensional RDE as a function of a specified design Mach number and the pressure ratio across the injection surface. Numerical simulations are conducted using a compressible reacting flow solver with finite-rate chemistry built on an Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) framework. The fuel mixture is set to a stoichiometric hydrogen-air mixture for all simulations. Stable operation occurs for a wide range of inflow conditions with inflow Mach numbers up to 4. The increased total temperature associated with increasing Mach numbers causes burning at the injection surface during the injector recovery process, resulting in unstable operation. Meanwhile, increasing total pressure facilitates sustained supersonic injection. Analysis of the steady flow structure shows a familiar structure with significant changes to the detonation structure when compared with a rocket RDE. With supersonic inflow, an oblique detonation wave (ODW) forms along the injection surface connected to the moving detonation through a slip line. Changes in the oblique detonation wave and normal detonation angle occur with changes in the inflow Mach number, however the overall detonation structure remains similar when supersonic injection occurs.

articles.title: Proliferating against the current: how multistep branching nucleation can sort microtubule polarity in the spindle
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spindle, which segregates chromosomes during cell division, is a paradigm of cytoskeletal self-organization: a highly ordered structure that persists for hours is assembled from dynamic microtubules that branch, grow, slide, and turn over within tens of seconds. Its microtubules point inward, with minus ends clustered at the poles and plus ends extending toward the chromosomes at the center of the structure. In large meiotic spindles this arrangement is puzzling, since microtubules nucleate near the chromosomes and grow at their plus ends much faster than motors slide them backward. One would therefore expect the plus ends, rather than the minus ends, to radiate outward. Here, we propose a resolution to this seeming paradox through a kinetic model that integrates the core filament-level processes. When branching complexes assemble with a sufficient delay, for instance through several sequential rate-limiting steps, they accumulate on old microtubule lattice sites near the backward-sliding minus ends of mother microtubules. Each generation is then born farther back than the last, so the self-renewing population drifts toward the minus ends even though each filament's center advances toward its plus end. For the sliding and growth velocities measured in Xenopus egg extract spindles, a multistep mechanism requires at least four rate-limiting steps. The kinetic theory has a surprisingly amenable structure: the filament length configuration variable can be eliminated exactly, yielding a finite space-time hierarchy, and the direction of population drift follows from a general criterion comparing the mean lattice age at branching sites with the ratio of plus-end advance to sliding speed.

articles.title: A linear stability method based on generalized hydrodynamics: application to high-speed plane Couette flow beyond continuum regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear stability analysis of compressible shear flows beyond continuum regime attracts increasing attention in recent years accounting for high-altitude applications. In this paper, the temporal stability of high-speed plane Couette flow in near-continuum regime is addressed. A novel linear stability method based on the generalized hydrodynamic equations (GHE) with slip boundary conditions is developed within the 13-moment framework. Meanwhile, the linear stability equations of the nonlinear coupled constitutive relations (NCCR) and the Navier--Stokes (NS) equations are also given. Based on the developed methods, the linear stability of plane Couette flows at Ma=2.5--10 and Kn=2.7× 10⁻⁵--0.07 are analyzed, and the rarefaction effects on the base flow, eigenspectrum, mode synchronization and least stable mode are investigated. The results show that the GHE with slip boundary conditions agrees well with direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) results in predicting base flow profiles of velocity, temperature, all stress and heat flux components, while the NS equations show considerable differences, especially for capturing the nonlinear normal stress and tangential heat flux. The GHE-based linear stability theory (LST) recovers to the classical NS-based LST in the continuum limit, while they show considerable differences when Kn reaches O(0.01). As rarefaction degree increases, the synchronization between acoustic modes and viscous modes becomes weak, and all modes become stable in rarefied plane Couette flow. The surface slip effect and nonlinear transport increase the disturbance phase speeds, while they have different effects on the growth rate of different modes. Generally, rarefaction effects increase the growth rate of the least stable Mode II at low wavenumbers, and show more pronounced effects on higher modes and high-wavenumber disturbances.

articles.title: Laser cooling of Th⁻: Revised bound-state structure and a more efficient cooling scheme
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The thorium anion (Th⁻) has been proposed as a candidate for laser cooling of negative ions. However, previous theoretical and experimental results exhibit significant discrepancies in both the excitation energies and lifetimes. Here we revisit the bound-state structure and transition properties of Th⁻ using two independent ab initio approaches. The two calculations agree well and improve agreement with measured excitation energies and lifetimes. Based on the present level structure, we reassign several observed levels and show that the previously proposed ⁴F^e₃/₂↔{}²S^o₁/₂ cooling transition is not closed and requires two repumping lasers. We therefore propose an alternative cooling scheme based on the ⁴F^e₃/₂↔{}⁴F^o₃/₂ transition, which requires only one repumping laser and has a transition rate approximately five times larger (Aapprox1.1×10⁵ s⁻¹), the fastest reported bound--bound E1 transition in atomic anions to date.

articles.title: Stable ring-polymer molecular dynamics without Fourier transforms: a linear-scaling bead-space Cayley propagator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) builds zero-point energy and tunnelling into classical trajectories and is widely used for bimolecular rate coefficients. At low temperature it requires many beads, and the stiff ring-polymer springs then limit the integrator. The Cayley modification of the free ring-polymer step removes this limit, but it has so far been formulated mode by mode, which requires Fourier transforms of every degree of freedom at every step. Here we show that, in bead coordinates, the Cayley step reduces to one cyclic tridiagonal solve for the midpoint of the step, with a matrix that depends only on the number of beads P, the temperature and the time step, and not on the atomic masses. The bead-space step is exactly the normal-mode Cayley map: it conserves the free ring-polymer energy, preserves the free ring-polymer Boltzmann distribution, and is stable for any P whenever ΩΔ t<2 for the highest physical frequency Ω. A Thomas recursion with a rank-two Woodbury correction solves it in about 18P operations per degree of freedom without pivoting, with a condition number bounded by 1+(ω_PΔ t)², and the inverse matrix decays geometrically with bead separation, so the step is local in bead index. Implemented in the open-source PyRPMD package, the propagator reproduces normal-mode Cayley to 1.5×10⁻¹⁵ for up to 2048 beads and its cost grows linearly with P. For direct RPMD (dRPMD), which has so far integrated the springs explicitly, these properties raise the stability limit on the time step 23--29-fold in published low-temperature settings; at SI20K with 3072 beads, the Cayley step conserves the ring-polymer energy as well as velocity Verlet does with a time step about ten times larger, while leaving the low-lying internal modes that govern spurious resonances essentially unchanged.

articles.title: Compensated Grid-Based Hybrid Exchange - A Simple, Accurate, Efficient, and Differentiable Recipe for Large-Scale Molecular Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A compensated grid-based approach is developed for hybrid exchange in large-scale molecular systems. The method uses a symmetrically overlap-fitted grid-based exchange approach, with fitting performed in the orthonormalized atomic orbital basis. This fitting is augmented with a superposition-of-atomic-densities difference-density (dSCF) partitioning of the exchange energy, yielding the finished compensated grid-based exchange approach. The complete method is found to have orders of magnitude reduction of absolute and relative error properties versus raw grid-based exchange, and remains analytically differentiable. The method is easy to implement and provides efficiency gains over GPU integral-direct techniques for high quality and/or augmented basis sets. Library functions to help users implement the method in their own quantum chemistry codes are provided in the recently-shipped cuEST v0.3 library.

articles.title: Speckle Angle: An Intrinsic Geometric Metric for High-Precision Speckle Metrology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speckle-based metrology exploits the extreme sensitivity of complex interference patterns to perturbations in wavelength, refractive index, displacement and other physical parameters. Existing approaches typically quantify speckle evolution using similarity-based correlation metrics, whose local sensitivity deteriorates near the operating point because their gradient vanishes as the similarity approaches unity. Here we show that normalized speckle patterns represent points on the surface of a high-dimensional unit sphere and introduce the speckle angle: the intrinsic geometric coordinate between speckle patterns. The speckle angle preserves the physical calibration of established similarity approaches while providing a linear response and maximal sensitivity in the small-perturbation regime. This geometric perspective enables discrimination of perturbation dynamics from measurement noise, enabling direct estimation of uncorrelated and fixed-pattern noise contributions and yielding a fundamental acquisition-limited resolution bound. Using speckle generated by an integrating sphere, we experimentally validate the framework and demonstrate quantitative noise analysis using angular coordinates. Beyond improving sensitivity characterization, the speckle angle establishes an original common metric for comparing disparate speckle metrology architectures and provides a foundation for multidimensional sensing based on trajectories through speckle-vector space.

articles.title: The landscape of quantum technology companies in 2026
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We update our 2022 mapping of 441 quantum technology (QT) companies and examine how the industry has developed. The principal dataset now includes 1,092 companies founded with a QT focus, of which 935 remain active. Public sources and archived company websites provide evidence on company formation, technology fields and geography, alongside acquisitions, closures, valuations and involvement in artificial intelligence, defence and space. Company formation continued beyond the apparent 2018 peak in the earlier study. Computing software and applications remain the largest field, with suppliers and supporting businesses accounting for almost a third of active companies. Countries with similar company totals can have different technological profiles, and regional comparisons reveal concentrations obscured by country rankings. The first companies generally preceded the selected national policy milestones. Supporting businesses usually followed technical companies in the same jurisdiction. AI is more prevalent than defence in current company activities, while defence shows the larger increase from the earliest assessed evidence. Space relevance is documented for more than a quarter of active companies, often alongside defence involvement.

articles.title: Inverse Design of an On-chip Phase-Change Switch Composed of Sparse Heterogeneous Metasurfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic switches are exploited for optical signal routing and control within optical communication systems. The integration of phase change materials with silicon photonic switches overcomes the drawbacks of the state-of-the-art photonic switches based on electro-optic and thermo-optic effects. In this work, a 1x2 on-chip switch with a footprint of 6.3umx31um based on on-chip one-dimensional metasurfaces is inverse-designed. The on-chip metasurfaces are heterogeneous, which their meta-atoms can be composed of either SiO2 or the phase-change material Sb2Se3. This helps to the realization of higher extinction ratio between the switch outputs, especially at the amorphous state which has a small refractive index contrast to that of the silicon. To benefit from structural, fabrication and switching simplicity, sparse parameterization is followed in the inverse design of the switch using ternary search (TS) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithms.

articles.title: Thulium- and Holmium-Doped Silica Fibres for 2 μm High-Power and Highly-Efficient Lasers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silica optical fibres, originally developed as a low-loss transmission medium for telecommunications, have evolved into a versatile platform for compact and efficient high-power lasers. This review discusses recent progress in thulium- and holmium-doped active fibres emitting within the 2 μm spectral band, with an emphasis on material and waveguide approaches that address power scaling through thermal-load mitigation and enhanced laser efficiency. In particular, the temperature dependence of absorption and emission cross-sections are reviewed, and their implications for spectral gain, amplified spontaneous emission and high-power laser operation are discussed. Structured-core thulium fibres are then considered as a route to combining the high local Tm3+ concentration required for efficient two for- one cross-relaxation with a reduced average dopant concentration, lower longitudinal heat load, and a pedestal-free waveguide design. Finally, recent results on holmium-doped silica fibres prepared by nanoparticle-assisted modified chemical vapour deposition are summarised. Crucially, the Al/Ho ratio is identified as a key compositional parameter governing laser efficiency, while a high absolute alumina content supports a long fluorescence lifetime and enables high Ho3+ concentrations without excessive clustering. These advances have enabled core-pumped holmium fibre lasers with slope efficiencies reaching 84% and output powers approaching 100W. Collectively, these development illustrate how control of spectroscopy, composition, and transverse dopant distribution can extend the performance of silica fibre lasers across the 1.7-2.2 μm spectral region.

articles.title: Development of a Cryogenic Anti-Coincidence System Based on Scintillating Crystals Read Out with Kinetic Inductance Detectors for BULLKID-DM
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The BULLKID-DM experiment has been proposed to search for WIMP-like dark matter particles with a mass of 1 GeV or lower and with a WIMP-nucleon interaction cross section down to 10⁻⁴³ cm². To achieve this goal, the experiment utilizes a detector consisting of a stack of 16 silicon wafers instrumented with phonon-mediated superconducting Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs), to be operated at the underground facility of the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), Italy. To reduce the residual background arising from γ-rays, neutrons, and muons, a cryogenic active anti-coincidence system (veto) operating at mK temperature, surrounding the main detector, is under development. The veto detector consists of segmented scintillating crystals read out by phonon-mediated KID light detectors. Current status and future developments of the veto system are presented. In particular, we focus on cryogenic tests of both bismuth germanate (BGO) and gadolinium aluminum gallium garnet (GAGG) crystals, which had been previously chosen as veto candidate crystals according to our preliminary studies on the dependence of their optical properties (i.e. light yield and scintillation decay time) on temperature. We finally present the operation and preliminary tests of a two-module veto prototype with multiplexed readout.

articles.title: Quantum Boltzmann Equation for Static Correlation with Cumulant Kernel Closure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a Quantum Boltzmann Equation for static correlation by mapping the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to discrete atomic-orbital matrix mechanics via the Wigner-Weyl isomorphism to evaluate scattering of the correlated two-body cumulant. This Quantum Boltzmann Equation converges to the active-space static correlation limit and preserves pure N-representability constraints during the kinetic relaxation. To resolve scaling bottlenecks of explicit two-body cumulant methods, we project the two-body cumulant onto its lowest unitary invariant and evaluate a susceptibility-windowed orbital scattering scale via a single Coulomb-exchange contraction. Relaxing onto a hyperbolic-tangent cumulant attractor through Markovian collisional relaxation yields a parameter-free Quantum Boltzmann Equation Cumulant-Kernel that regularizes derivative cusps without thermal smearing. Using the collinear H₃ exchange reaction, the symmetric D₄ₕ square H₄ dissociation, the non-adiabatic avoided crossing in BeH₂, the symmetric bond cleavage of H₂O, the triple-bond dissociation of N₂, the 11-molecule MR-MGN-BE17 dissociation test set, and the singlet diradical isomers of benzyne as case studies, we show that this kinetic relaxation resolves strong static correlation at zero electronic temperature.

articles.title: Active-space construction in single-fragment coupled-cluster embedding for chemical reactions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We benchmark single-fragment quantum embedding, in which electron correlation---at the level of coupled-cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]---is restricted to orbitals associated with a chosen molecular fragment, and the remaining orbitals are frozen at the Hartree-Fock level. We compare several methods for constructing fragment active spaces, and we test their performance on 60 organic reaction energies and three reaction profiles. A common fragment projection operator is used to relate several of the tested orbital constructions. Regional embedding, based on density matrix embedding theory, is shown to give accurate and robust performance when used for both the occupied and virtual active orbitals. For virtual orbitals, fragment-centered projected atomic orbitals and fragment natural orbitals (defined by eigenvectors of a fragment MP2 density matrix) also perform well, but the latter typically retains larger virtual spaces. Composite MP2 corrections yield the largest improvement: combined with fragment natural orbitals, they give average reaction energy errors below 0.3 kcal/mol relative to full-system CCSD(T), with all individual errors below 1 kcal/mol. Reaction profiles show that accurate endpoint energies can conceal substantial barrier errors, emphasizing the importance of approximating omitted correlation.

articles.title: Critical excited states in quantum metrology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15683v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate criticality-enhanced sensing near ground- and excited-state quantum phase transitions in a strongly coupled qubit-boson system. Accounting for finite-size effects, we design driving protocols that exploit diverging susceptibilities to enhance signal-to-noise ratios in parameter estimation using experimentally relevant generators. We show that the excited-state criticality provides a metrological advantage through single-mode bosonic squeezing in regimes that circumvent the 'death of adiabaticity', limiting conventional critical quantum metrology with ground-state criticality.

articles.title: C₂ Swan, CH and CN emission, surface temperature and luminous efficiency of the Hayabusa2 sample-return capsule from ground-based spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Hayabusa2 sample-return capsule entered the atmosphere over South Australia on 5 December 2020 at 12 km/s. A slitless spectral video, taken from the ground with a hand-tracked consumer camera, shows the capsule alone from 80 to 49 km. In the first ten seconds of heating the shock layer emits the CN violet system, the CH A-X band and the C₂ Swan bands, the latter for the first time in remote observations of a capsule entry. C₂ (Tᵣₘ ᵣₒₜapprox9200 K, Tᵣₘ ᵥᵢbapprox7800 K) and CN (about 7000 K) are far hotter than the surface. C₂ and CH disappear while the heat flux is still rising and CN persists, which we relate to the early pyrolysis of the carbon-phenolic ablator and to the changing boundary-layer chemistry. The colour temperature of the heat shield rises from 2720 to 3080 K, in agreement with airborne results. The radiated energy is one to two orders of magnitude below that of natural fireballs, because the light comes from the hot surface rather than from ablation vapour. A faint persistent train lights up about 1 s after the passage and fades within a few seconds, probably chemiluminescence in the cooling wake.

articles.title: Reply to the Comment by Hradil and Řeháček
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16716v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hradil and Řeháček argue that the quantum metrological advantage demonstrated in our squeezed-vacuum phase-sensing experiment disappears, when measurement repetitions and total photon resources are properly accounted for. We show that this conclusion is mathematically unfounded and that neither resource accounting nor finite-sample statistical considerations invalidate the demonstrated quantum-enhanced local phase sensitivity.

articles.title: Closing the Loop: Co-Evolving EM for Irregular Time Series Generation in Lifted Representations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regular time-series generation from irregular time series is typically reduced to one-shot imputation: complete each partial sequence once, freeze the completions, and train a generator on the resulting surrogate dataset. We show that this open-loop strategy is structurally flawed. Point imputers collapse ambiguous missing regions to conditional averages, while stochastic imputers become stale as the generator evolves; the binding constraint is therefore iteration, not imputer design. We introduce a co-evolving Monte Carlo EM framework that closes the imputer-generator loop. Each E-step samples missing values from the posterior of the current generator, and each M-step retrains the generator on these completions, preserving unconditional generator training. Since our diffusion prior operates in a lifted 2D representation while observations live in time-series space, we further introduce Posterior Sampling for Lifted Representations (PSLR), which enforces operator-consistent conditioning, uncertainty preservation, and manifold consistency during the E-step. Across ten datasets and four corruption regimes, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving over the strongest baselines by 59% in discriminative score, 15% in predictive score, 73% in Context-FID, and 71% in feature-correlation error. Ablations show that our approach reduces average discriminative score by 73% over single-step baselines, closing most of the remaining gap to the clean-data oracle. Code is available at https://github.com/azencot-group/PSLR.

articles.title: Recursive State-Augmented Language Models: Persistent Latent-State Adaptation of Pretrained Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models rely on finite token contexts, limiting access to earlier interactions. We introduce Recursive State-Augmented Language Models (Recursive SALM), a framework in which a persistent latent state evolves with each observation and generates adaptations of a pretrained language model. A modular read-transition-write architecture separates observation encoding, latent dynamics, and predictor adaptation. We develop deterministic and stochastic formulations. The experiments evaluate only deterministic SALM with frozen GPT-2 small and exclude earlier evidence from its decoder context. On a four-turn hypothesis-inference task, latent-gated LoRA reaches 89.1% accuracy, comparable to 88.0% for a trained full-context LoRA baseline, with earlier evidence available solely through a 64-dimensional state. Zeroing or shuffling the state substantially reduces accuracy. In a two-turn task with codewords unseen in training, several interfaces improve candidate ranking over chance, but rarely generate the exact codeword under the evaluated training schedule. These experiments show that persistent latent-conditioned adaptation can support sequential inference when earlier evidence is absent from the decoder context.

articles.title: Characterizing Local Breadth in Language Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models sharpen the validity--breadth trade-off: a generator should avoid hallucinations without collapsing onto a narrow set of valid outputs. We study generation from positive examples of an unknown target in the Kleinberg--Mullainathan model, with arbitrary, possibly adversarial order and no distributional or computational assumptions. Breadth is measured by lower Banach density, which rules out arbitrarily large sparse holes, unlike prefix-based lower asymptotic density. 1. Exact optima in one dimension: For each target K in a countable family, we characterize its optimal lower Banach density b(K) via equivalent combinatorial and topological formulations. One eventually valid generator attains all b(K) simultaneously. Every αin[0,1/2] occurs as b(K) in some countable family; finite Cantor--Bendixson point rank guarantees b(K)=1/2, even without a uniform rank bound. 2. Unavoidable trade-offs in higher dimensions: For dge2, there need not be a single best generator: optimizing density for one target may worsen the guarantee for another. An explicit family quantifies this intrinsically multi-objective trade-off. 3. Complete characterization of density profiles: We characterize the full region of simultaneously achievable guarantees, with equivalent combinatorial and topological formulations, after excluding geometrically degenerate rectangles. Every prescribed product prodᵢ[0,αᵢ], αᵢin[0,1/2] can occur as an exact achievable region for some language collection. 4. Near-half guarantees and the sharp endpoint: Under a near-logarithmic nondegeneracy condition, one generator achieves filtered density at least 1/2-ε at all finite-point-rank targets, for every ε>0, improving the previous polylogarithmic threshold. The exact 1/2 endpoint can fail even for a rank-zero singleton family.

articles.title: MIGRO: A Decoupled and Portable Long-Term Memory System for Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models evolve, but the observations, revisions, and context accumulated through user interactions should remain usable. Each new model must be able to retrieve past evidence, track revisions, and add new observations. We present MIGRO, a decoupled long-term memory system that treats experience as a persistent state shared across successive language models. MIGRO follows a simple principle: preserve historical evidence exactly, organize it approximately, and decide what to retrieve only when the question is known. We call this asymmetric fidelity with deferred selectivity. A shared semantic index supports retrieval, while exact records retain observations and their historical relationships. Because models differ in vocabulary and tokenization, host-specific interfaces convert selected evidence into inputs the receiving model can use. Reversible encoding reduces archival storage while enabling exact recovery. The shared state and its access interfaces let successive hosts read and extend the accumulated experience. On matched LoCoMo states, MIGRO scores 7.3% higher and uses 99.3% less private memory than the strongest quality baseline. After handoff, continued writing retains 99.9% of full-history rebuilding quality by extending the inherited state. On million-token BEAM histories, MIGRO uses 57.5% less private storage on average than the most compact baseline. MIGRO combines high answer quality, continued memory growth across hosts, and low storage cost. Code is available at https://github.com/zOUMINGXI/MIGRO.

articles.title: DISCERN: Preserve at Write, Resolve at Read for Persistent LLM-Agent Memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise agents accumulate memory across dozens of sessions in which facts contradict, get superseded, and blur as similarly named entities collide in embedding space. The field treats this as a retrieval problem; we show it is not. On ENT-310, a synthetic enterprise sales-agent memory benchmark of 310 queries (210 answerable, 100 unanswerable), a vanilla Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) reader over a memory store already matches strong memory systems on the recall pillars. Retention and currency are near-saturated, roughly 0.93 to 0.98 for every competent system, so recall is essentially solved. What remains unsolved is resolution: which entity a query refers to, which time-state is current, and whether to commit an answer at all or decline when evidence is insufficient. We propose DISCERN (DISambiguation and Cross-session Episodic memoRy Navigation), an agent-memory framework built on a single rule: preserve at write, resolve at read. At write time DISCERN builds a strictly additive bi-temporal provenance graph that never merges confusable entities and never drops superseded values. At read time a zero-LLM tool surface drives an agentic loop that navigates this graph and commits exactly one of four gated terminal actions. A four-judge LLM-as-a-Judge council scores two axes: answer correctness on answerable questions, and the answer-versus-abstain decision as a classification problem. On ENT-310, DISCERN is the best-calibrated system on abstention (F1 0.924 versus at most 0.802 across eight baselines) and leads macro answer correctness under equal pillar weighting (0.861 versus 0.806 for the strongest baseline), a lead driven by entity resolution (0.800, where no baseline exceeds 0.40). Applied with zero tuning to the full LoCoMo corpus, the same pipeline again leads macro answer correctness (0.663 versus 0.638) and stays among the best-calibrated on false-premise abstention.

articles.title: Controlling the Probability of Unknown Unknowns in Pre-Deployment Testing of AI Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.15835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In pre-deployment testing of AI systems such as AI agents, a developer can often deal with known failure modes (e.g., leaking API keys, deleting important databases, or installing a malicious package) by implementing fixes or making contingency plans for when the same issue might occur again. What is more challenging are the unknown unknowns: the unseen failure modes that haven't surfaced during testing. The decision to stop testing and deploy therefore faces an inherent tradeoff: continue testing to observe more behaviors, at the cost of time and resources, or stop testing and deploy, at the risk of failure modes remaining undiscovered. How then does the developer decide when they have tested enough? To answer this, we develop an algorithm that certifies when the probability of observing an unseen failure mode is sufficiently small. The algorithm constructs an anytime-valid upper confidence sequence on this quantity, so the developer can repeatedly test a system, inspect the bound, and decide to stop when it falls below a chosen threshold without invalidating the statistical guarantee. Our problem can be interpreted as a sequential variant of the missing-mass estimation problem which gave rise to the classic Good-Turing estimator (Good, 1953). On SWE-Chat, a dataset of real-world coding agent traces (Baumann et al., 2026), we implement our procedure and show that it achieves tighter upper bounds than a simple multiple-testing corrected Good-Turing baseline, and even dominates a fixed-horizon (non-multiple-testing-corrected) Good-Turing upper confidence bound, which is not anytime valid. Additionally, to better match realistic evaluation pipelines, we extend our method to handle sampling from a different task distribution and imperfect automated failure labeling.

articles.title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agents modify prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies using interaction histories. Yet a plausible modification is not necessarily suitable for persistent adoption: candidate selection is adaptive, evaluators may be imperfect, and local gains can hide degradation against an earlier baseline. We introduce Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for governing adoption of self-generated agent modifications. EGE separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, requires meaningful improvement on a prespecified primary objective, protects declared capabilities through reference-relative non-inferiority tests, and applies governance constraints before bounded canary deployment. We establish an evaluator-calibrated simultaneous lower-bound construction for a countable sequence of adaptively generated candidates. It combines candidate-wise Hoeffding bounds with independent calibration samples comparing the operational evaluator with a prespecified reference procedure. We also formalise reference replacement through bridge tests, derive a cumulative degradation bound along a versioned reference lineage, and provide an audit-planning condition relating effect-size margin, sample sizes, and acceptance probability. A Monte Carlo stress test illustrates calibration under candidate-dependent evaluator optimism; it is a stylised statistical experiment, not an evaluation of a deployed agent. The guarantees are conditional on bounded paired scores, fresh sampling, a valid reference-evaluation construct, and declared evaluation distributions; they do not establish universal agent safety or robustness to arbitrary distribution shift.

articles.title: AstroMemBench: A Benchmark for Memory Systems in Embodied Spacecraft Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term spacecraft autonomy requires embodied agents to use operational history under communication delays, time-critical operations, environmental uncertainty, complex physical interactions, power and computational constraints, and safety and reliability requirements. We introduce AstroMemBench and a Scenario-Challenge-Capability design method that maps these requirements to executable memory tests. The benchmark covers 16 memory subchallenges through 140 templates and 2240 instances across nine tasks in planetary surface operations, on-orbit servicing, and deep-space exploration. A deterministic environment scores actions for task completion, state changes, safety, and resource use. Ablations under nine conditions show that the benchmark is sensitive to how accurately agents recover and use historical information and to differences in memory-system design. Main experiments compare six configurations. Mem0, Chain-of-Memory, LightMem, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improve same-session mean scores over native Pi Agent, with no clear advantage of the three memory systems over RAG. After a session restart, Mem0 outperforms RAG by 12.25 points. Benefits favor instruction retention and result reuse over ongoing state tracking and energy reservation. AstroMemBench supports the design, development, and selection of memory systems for embodied spacecraft agents. AstroMemBench 1.0 and its evaluation code are publicly available: https://github.com/flyingView/AstroMemBench-v1.

articles.title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.16937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Typed System-1 (S1) decision models are increasingly deployed in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization to cut inference cost, yet untrusted context can still manipulate typed outputs and alter execution branches. Unlike autoregressive System-2 (S2) models, S1 interfaces score dynamic rules and options without token-by-token decoding, mismatching attacks targeting text continuation or explicit override commands. We propose S1-Evo, a self-evolving framework tailored to S1's contract-based option competition and margin feedback. S1-Evo perturbs untrusted fields via contract-aware evidence channels to induce emphevidence competition with original task evidence while preserving fact invariance. Offline on seed tasks, it optimizes candidates via feedback search guided by directional margins and re-verification, distilling verified flips into experience cards. At test time, S1-Evo retrieves relevant cards to construct perturbations for unseen tasks. Across four benchmarks and three S1 models, S1-Evo reaches 71.99% mean ASR and 57.47% high-confidence ASR on textttjev-1.14, and causes up to 24.00% E2E agent violations.

articles.title: Speed-to-Power Dominates Energy Costs for AI Data Centers: Technoeconomic Analysis of Powering AI in the Continental United States
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving demand for new data centers at large scale and on short deployment timelines. To power them, firms connect to the commercial grid or contract generation directly, but interconnection and gas-turbine delays now incentivize on-site generation. We compare grid-connected and off-grid data center energy infrastructure (AC- and DC-coupled solar-plus-storage, islanded natural gas, and grid interconnection) across the continental U.S. Using an open-source technoeconomic framework built on empirically calibrated AI training loads, climate-driven cooling, stage-by-stage power conversion, and physics-based battery degradation, we model designs providing equivalent energy services. Our central contribution is a speed-adjusted cost of energy that values the compute unlocked by faster construction, making options with different deployment timelines directly comparable on one physically consistent basis. We find DC coupling reduces lifetime energy costs by 18% (0.09/ kWh) on average versus AC counterparts by eliminating inverters and improving efficiency. Though rarely cheapest on unadjusted energy cost, DC-coupled microgrids' faster deployment makes them the lowest-cost modeled option in 85% of U.S. locations once foregone compute is valued, or 55% under accelerated natural gas timelines. For AI infrastructure, deployment speed rather than unit energy cost determines the economically preferred path to power.

articles.title: Benchmarking Multilingual Document Understanding in Vision-Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) perform strongly on multimodal tasks, Document Understanding (DU) among them, but the benchmarks that measure them mostly cover English documents and narrow problems. How well current VLMs generalize across languages, tasks, styles and layouts therefore remains unclear. We introduce MDU, a multilingual DU benchmark of 23146 examples spanning 13 tasks and five languages: English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish. The tasks isolate complementary capabilities, from surface-level text and Markdown extraction through summarization, classification and named-entity recognition to layout-sensitive passage and layout extraction. We evaluate 45 state-of-the-art open-weight VLMs from 1.7B to 235B parameters, plus one commercial system under the same protocol. The benchmark is far from saturated: the best average is 69.0, only eight of the 45 evaluated systems reach 65, and the two best results come from 27B models rather than from the largest systems we evaluate. Performance is uneven in ways that scale does not fix. The gap between the strongest and weakest language does not close as models grow, and it survives controlling for the domain composition of each language. Capabilities also do not improve together: once we partial out overall model quality, per-task scores are largely uncorrelated, and transcription ability in particular trades off against semantic extraction.

articles.title: When Safety Becomes an Attack Surface: Manipulating Abstention in Tool-Using AI Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An AI agent's decision not to act can itself become an attack surface. We study warning-induced over-abstention, an availability attack in which adversaries place fabricated risk warnings in low-trust content to prevent legitimate task completion. Our central premise is that safe abstention requires evaluating both the claimed risk and the authority of the evidence supporting it. We develop controlled counterfactual task variants that vary risk content, source provenance, and warning wording, and evaluate a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol that corroborates warnings against authoritative records or the underlying content. Across three model families and 51 injectable AgentAbstain task pairs, caution-first prompting amplifies the attack. For Gemini, induced over-abstention rises from 9.8% to 86.3%, despite unchanged clean-task completion. Matched wording comparisons further reveal sensitivity to warning language, with substantial variation across models and environments. Provenance-aware verification improves legitimate completion, while forgery and sensitive-content controls expose its dependence on authoritative evidence and its limitations in preserving confidentiality. These results motivate evaluating agent safety through the justification for restraint, alongside the safety of actions taken.

articles.title: Vibration-Based Mass Sensing with Functionally Graded Graphene-Reinforced Piezoelectric Microcantilevers in Air and Liquid
articles.abstract: Resonant microcantilevers are widely used for mass sensing, yet the effects of material architecture and operating medium remain unclear. This study develops an analytical model of a multilayer graphene nanoplatelet-reinforced composite (GPLRC) piezoelectric microcantilever with a narrowed tip. The formulation combines Euler–Bernoulli beam theory, a modified Halpin–Tsai model, a piecewise modal solution incorporating adsorbed mass, and a string-of-spheres hydrodynamic model. Uniform (U) and functionally graded (X, O, A) platelet distributions are investigated in epoxy, polyamide 6 (PA6), and polypropylene (PP) matrices. Validation against published measurements yields deviations of 2.2% in air and 0.3–2.3% in liquids. Adsorption of a 20ng particle decreases resonance frequency. The relative shift in water is nearly ten times smaller than in air and decreases with increasing glycerol concentration. O-GPLRC produces the largest frequency shift in both media. PP performs best in air, whereas PA6 performs best in liquids. Amplitude-based responses rank configurations differently from frequency-based metrics. Higher platelet content reduces relative frequency shifts through stiffening. Sobol’ analysis identifies platelet width and thickness as dominant parameters, contributing 52–54% and 41–44% of variance, respectively, while length contributes less than 5%. These findings support optimizing material architecture, matrix, medium, and readout metric.

articles.title: SST‑Gradient Driven Asymmetric Decline of Coastal Wind Power in Northwest Africa: Multi‑Model Attribution and Projections to 2100
articles.abstract: This study quantifies the asymmetric decline in wind power density along Morocco's Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts and develops a multi-model projection framework. Analysis of ERA5 reanalysis data (1981–2020), evaluated against independent NASA POWER, MERRA-2, and NOAA OISST datasets, reveals a pronounced north–south contrast: the southern coast exhibits wind power density approximately 1.6 times higher than the northern coast, whereas the northern region shows 1.9 times greater inter-annual variability and an 11% faster rate of decline. A Random Forest attribution model identifies the Mediterranean–Canary Current sea-surface-temperature gradient as a dominant predictor of the north–south wind-speed differential, with the two SST predictors accounting for approximately 68% of the total permutation importance. The statistical relationship is consistent with a physical mechanism involving differential ocean warming and associated changes in the regional pressure gradient. Comparative analysis of constrained linear, logistic, quadratic, and CMIP6-informed projection approaches indicates that methodological choice introduces a 10–20-year range in projected threshold-crossing times. Five CMIP6 models were used to characterize structural model uncertainty under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5. The results indicate substantially earlier loss of the 150 W m⁻² viability threshold in the northern region than in the southern region, although the precise crossing time depends strongly on the projection method and emissions scenario. These findings highlight the importance of physically informed, multi-model approaches for assessing climate-related risks to coastal wind-energy resources in Morocco.

articles.title: Siloxane-Containing Vinyl Ester Coatings for Cellulose-Based Substrates: Balancing Thermal, Saltwater-Barrier, and Mechanical Properties
articles.abstract: Developing multifunctional coatings that simultaneously provide thermal protection, moisture resistance, and mechanical integrity remains challenging for cellulose-based materials. Herein, siloxane-modified vinyl ester resin (SMER) composite coatings incorporating thermally stable inorganic fillers were developed for cellulose-based templates (CBTs). The effects of SMER content (10–40 wt%) on coating structure and protective performance were systematically investigated. Spectroscopic and microscopic analyses revealed the incorporation of silicon-containing components and composition-dependent morphological heterogeneity. Increasing SMER content enhanced the char yield at 700 °C from 35.91% to 53.46% and raised the final decomposition temperature from 600 to 642 °C. The 30 and 40 wt% coatings exhibited hydrophobic surfaces with water contact angles exceeding 90°. After immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution for 3 days, the 40 wt% coating reduced saltwater absorption to 7.66%, compared with 38.65% for uncoated CBTs. Notably, the 10 wt% coating exhibited the longest heat-resistance time of 327.4 s at 250 °C, whereas the 30 wt% coating achieved the highest engineering stress at break (6.69 MPa) and elongation at break (82.06%). These findings reveal distinct composition-dependent trade-offs among thermal response, moisture resistance, and mechanical performance, providing insights into the rational design of multifunctional protective coatings for cellulose-based materials.

articles.title: Direct Effects of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Ligands on Myocardial Function in Isolated Hearts from Streptozotocin-Induced Diabetic Rats
articles.abstract: Purpose Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor ligands are widely used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity and have demonstrated cardioprotective effects beyond glycemic control.
