articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moiré superlattices have recently been extended from electronic materials to photonic systems, enabling complex topological light fields such as skyrmion bags. However, these realizations remain confined to two dimensions. Here, we demonstrate 3D moiré superlattices formed by twisting multi-volume spatiotemporal optical lattices, giving rise to previously undiscovered 3D quasiparticle topologies, including hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and hopfion-hopfionium nested superlattices. By tailoring the interference polarization textures of the moiré spacetime lattices, we achieve controlled topological transitions among these states, and tailored topological numbers of hopfion bags. These spatiotemporal supertopologies offer a promising platform for high-capacity information encoding in higher dimensions.

articles.title: Investigation of the timing performance of double-sided p-type 3D silicon sensors produced by CNM
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the timing performance and spatial uniformity of double-sided p-type 3D silicon sensors produced by the Centro Nacional de Microelectrónica (CNM). Three sensor layouts are studied: hexagonal and square geometries with an inter-electrode spacing of SI30micrometer, and a hexagonal geometry with an inter-electrode spacing of SI50micrometer. The sensors are characterized using a SI1064nanometer infrared laser and a custom two-stage wide-band readout. Measurements with a ⁹⁰Sr source are used to establish a minimum-ionizing-particle-like reference for the laser signal. The timing resolution improves with increasing bias voltage for all three layouts. Two-dimensional laser scans are used to study the position dependence of the timing response and to quantify its uniformity. Among the investigated devices, the square SI30micrometer geometry shows the best overall timing performance at the highest measured bias voltage.

articles.title: Stress-controlled avoided-crossing evolution of an optical microresonator induced by inter-fibre side coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analogies between quantum mechanics and photonics provide a powerful means of transferring concepts and phenomena between the two fields. Photonic analogues offer a distinctive advantage by allowing us to engineer and continuously vary parameters fixed by the microscopic structure of quantum systems, revealing richer behaviour. Building on these analogies, the recent demonstration of widely tunable microresonators formed by side coupling between optical fibres marked a significant advance in the development of reconfigurable resonant photonic systems. However, those methods offered no direct way to reach the centre of the avoided crossing, where the uncoupled fibre cutoff frequencies coincide and the modes hybridise most strongly. Here, we introduce an additional tuning degree of freedom by axially stretching a straight fibre coupled to a bent fibre. At essentially fixed coupling geometry, this lets us sweep the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies through zero. As the avoided crossing is approached, the induced microresonator's resonance band widens. Beyond the crossing, the band narrows and, strikingly, appears to "hang" below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency. Our experimental results agree with coupled-mode theory and indicate the feasibility of 100 MHz-scale control of the straight-fibre cutoff frequency and the resonator spectral height over a tuning range of about 100 GHz, using a relative elongation of order 10⁻³.

articles.title: Time-Varying Photonics: A Review of Theory, Phenomena, and Experimental Platforms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-varying photonics opens new avenues for controlling waves through engineering material properties in time. In this review, we introduce the basic concepts and theoretical tools for describing temporal interfaces, time-periodic systems, and space-time media, as well as review representative experimental approaches across different photonic and wave platforms. We further discuss characteristic phenomena enabled by temporal modulation, including coherent wave control, parametric amplification, nonreciprocity, and topological effects. This review provides a unified pathway for understanding time-varying photonics and outlines its current challenges and future opportunities in both fundamental physics and practical applications.

articles.title: Analytic Solution to Cumulative Coulomb Scattering in Boltzmann Theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In plasmas, frequent soft Coulomb collisions gradually transfer energy and momentum, whereas a single close collision can change both abruptly and redirect a particle. This coexistence can shape runaway-electron avalanches in tokamaks and alpha-particle heating in inertial fusion, yet no first-principles analytic theory has determined how the cumulative statistics evolve under plasma conditions. Fokker--Planck and moment-matched models reproduce average transport but do not determine how scattering evolves from isolated events to cumulative relaxation across plasma conditions. Here we resolve this long-standing problem directly from Boltzmann theory. By asymptotically rescaling the exact angular expansion, we obtain the first quantitative map of the single-collision, core-tail coexistence, and low-order relaxation regimes within a unified Boltzmann framework. The rescaling also provides explicit analytic representations of the angular distribution across these regimes without empirical transition parameters. The theory further shows that small-angle models differ from the Boltzmann distribution even in the forward core, so appending a large-angle tail to a conventional core cannot recover the collision statistics. In fast-electron transport, this full-range redistribution leaves mean energy loss nearly unchanged yet counterintuitively enhances beam concentration and modifies the energy flux delivered to a finite region.

articles.title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases is essential for attosecond science. Improving conversion efficiency from the infrared driving laser to the extreme-ultraviolet high-order harmonic radiation requires balancing microscopic single-atom dipole responses with macroscopic phase matching. The resulting conversion-efficiency landscape exhibits complex structures, such as the hyperbolic ridge in the pressure-length space, which can be difficult to accurately reconstruct using conventional Bayesian optimization. Here, we introduce a physics-informed Bayesian optimization framework that incorporates known physical scaling relations through nonlinear transformations of the search space. We first demonstrate the approach in the two-dimensional pressure-length space, where a direct grid scan enables detailed validation of the reconstructed landscape, before extending it to four dimensions, where exhaustive scanning becomes computationally impractical. In four dimensions, incorporating the pulse-duration scaling and a square-root transformation of conversion efficiency further improves the accuracy of the reconstructed landscape, as validated against an independent reference dataset. We also employ a threshold-based acquisition strategy to identify extended high-efficiency operating regions rather than isolated optimal points. Together, these results demonstrate that incorporating physical knowledge into Bayesian optimization improves the exploration and reconstruction of multidimensional high-order harmonic generation landscapes, extending its capabilities beyond locating individual optima.

articles.title: Exponential Control of Adiabatic Time Reflection by Complex-Time Singularities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nearly identical temporal switching profiles can produce very different reflections even when both have small local adiabatic measures. In a lossless dielectric, we obtain this difference by adding a weak feature that changes the complex-time singularities while preserving monotonicity, endpoints, and central slope. A perturbation bounded by 0.6% of the total inverse-permittivity change raises the reflected mode amplitude from 8.02×10⁻¹⁰ to 1.28×10⁻³. The complex action and pole residue predict this amplitude to within 0.32%. Within this waveform family, deviation and monotonicity constraints select three design regimes. At fixed deviation bound, reoptimization keeps the central feature's time scale comparable to the inverse incident angular frequency. The optimal amplitude is then proportional to 1/T as the switching time T tends to infinity. Stretching a fixed profile gives exponential suppression. Full-wave Maxwell simulations resolve the backward packet, and filtering calculations quantify its sensitivity to modulation bandwidth.

articles.title: Intracycle Interference in Strong-Field Photoemission from a Tungsten Needle Tip
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrons photoemitted by strong laser fields can rescatter, generating attosecond high harmonics. Spectral peaks arise from inter- and intracycle interference of coherent electron wave packets. While intercycle interference is well known, intracycle interference of plateau electrons has not been observed. We present carrier-envelope phase-resolved photoemission spectra from a nanometric tungsten needle tip driven at 1570 nm revealing such interference, supported by quantum orbit and TDSE simulations that elucidate attosecond-scale electron dynamics.

articles.title: Nanostructuring Semiconductor Surfaces Using Self-Assembled Metal Nanoparticles for Optoelectronic Applications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semiconductor nanostructures are key light-management elements because their geometry can strengthen light-matter interaction, suppress reflection, and enhance optical coupling. Yet their adoption across material platforms is constrained by lithography, multistep pattern transfer, persistent masks, and material-specific etching. Here, we introduce a lithography-free two-step strategy in which thermally evaporated self-assembled Ga nanoparticles act as self-consuming masks during Ar inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etching. Correlated transmission electron microscopy on GaAs reveals the formation mechanism. Comparable erosion of the Ga nanoparticles and exposed substrate progressively converts Ga-capped pedestals into pure semiconductor nanocones while preserving crystalline order. Nanocone dimensions extend from tens to hundreds of nanometres, and surface coverage is tunable through Ga deposition and plasma power. The same process produces nanocones on GaP and Si and dense nanostructures on polycrystalline hybrid metal-halide perovskite without detectable PbI2 formation. During nanostructuring, the sun-weighted reflectance reaches minima of 11-15% on the monocrystalline substrates, whereas the perovskite achieves 0.5% after complete mask consumption. The approach therefore combines a self-assembled mask, its consumption, and pattern transfer in a single physical etching step, providing a simple route to light-coupling surfaces for III-V, Si, and perovskite optoelectronics.

articles.title: Experimental Investigation of Heat Transfer in Axisymmetric Open Cavities at Hypersonic Speeds
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An experimental investigation was conducted to characterize the heat-transfer behavior of an axisymmetric cavity mounted on a cone with a semi-apex angle of (48^ circ) under Mach 6 freestream conditions in a Ludwieg tunnel. The effects of cavity geometry, represented by the length-to-depth ratio (L/D = 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, and 6.0), rear-wall height-to-depth ratio (h/D = -0.25, 0, and 0.5), and Reynolds number (Re_D = 23000 - 74000) were systematically investigated. Flow-field characteristics and surface heat-transfer behavior were examined using schlieren and planar laser Rayleigh scattering visualization techniques, together with surface pressure and heat-transfer measurements. The results indicate that increasing the cavity length-to-depth ratio leads to a reduction in the downstream Stanton number (St_d). For the longest cavity L/D = 6, however, the downstream Stanton number was found to exceed the upstream value (Stᵤ) indicating enhanced heat transfer in the region downstream of the cavity.

articles.title: A fast two-phase model for PEM fuel cell impedance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a physics-based matrix model for PEM fuel cell impedance that takes into account liquid water transients in the cathode catalyst layer (CCL). This model is an extension of our previous single-phase matrix model for functionally graded CCLs. The solution to the boundary-value problem for the perturbation amplitudes is constructed from basic solutions to the respective Cauchy problem with constant coefficients on numerical cells. The single-phase model employed analytical solutions to this problem. Here, for a larger system of ODEs, the analytical solution does not exist and we used spectral decomposition of the ODE system matrix to obtain the basic solutions numerically. Our impedance model is two orders of magnitude faster than a model based on a standard, general-purpose boundary-value solver. Fitting the matrix model to an experimental spectrum takes about a minute on a laptop. The developed matrix method can be used to numerically solve high-order linear boundary-value problems with variable coefficients.

articles.title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. We describe the setup and its extensive characterization, together with the procedure used to measure the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of materials at various angles of incidence, for wavelengths from 128 to 500 nm, covering both the argon (128 nm) and xenon (175 nm) scintillation wavelengths. To illustrate the capabilities of the setup, we present results for rough aluminum and stainless-steel surfaces as reference materials. Fitting the measured angular profiles with the analytical GGX microfacet model allows us to extract the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index and the surface roughness parameter of each sample. These parameters are then used to extrapolate the in-plane measurements to the full hemisphere and from gaseous argon to liquid media, enabling the inference of the hemispherical reflectance in gaseous argon, liquid argon and liquid xenon.

articles.title: Thin-film lithium niobate integrated photonics at 493 nm
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visible and near-ultraviolet light underpins applications from biophotonics to quantum computing, which demand fast control of optical amplitude and phase. Integrated photonics offers scalable control, yet most visible-wavelength platforms lack gigahertz-scale modulation. We demonstrate a thin-film lithium niobate platform at 493 nm integrating grating couplers, beamsplitters, ring resonators, and modulators. Segmented traveling-wave modulators achieve a half-wave voltage--length product of 450 mV·cm, >20 dB extinction, and bandwidth beyond 50 GHz. Ring resonators show 2.9 ± 0.2 dB/cm propagation loss and quantify the platform's photorefractive response. This enables agile visible beam delivery for trapped-ion systems, although photorefraction and substrate uniformity remain key challenges to scaling.

articles.title: Observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between two atoms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13665v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We have prepared pairs of atoms at densities exceeding  10¹⁶/rmcm³ corresponding to nlambdabar³>10 and studied how they interact with light. In this regime, the coherent part of the electric dipole-dipole interaction is larger than the dissipative part, and a single photon emission can transfer large momenta (larger than ten times the single photon recoil) to the atoms. For off-resonant laser light, the atoms are dressed with an electric dipole moment of approx 1 Debye and interact coherently. This light-induced dipole-dipole interaction has been previously observed only in the far-field mean-field regime. For two atoms, the resonance is shifted by the two-body Lamb shift which is dominated by the near-field part of the dipolar interaction. Dipolar resonance shifts have been observed before only for many atoms interacting with the far-field part of the dipolar interaction. Our work sheds new light on photoassociation processes and paves the way for studying driven quantum systems with strong electric dipole-dipole interactions.

articles.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for higher-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data stay distributed, moved between slab layouts by collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. It is also an exact coarse solver. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a (p)-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-(p)MG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and deal.II span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for an octree generalized Poisson problem across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. The results guide solver selection by mesh structure and coefficients

articles.title: CV-TF-QKD
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution, using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Full-record reconciliation and a binary phase-disclosure protocol achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. At fixed weak input-referred excess noise per arm, both rates per relay use scale as sqrtη, where η is the end-to-end transmissivity. For phase disclosure, we establish composable security against general coherent attacks using a bounded test of preparation intensities and sign-parity complementarity. For specified apparatus parameters, finite-key calculations incorporating detector inefficiency, dark counts, phase fluctuations, and reference overhead predict rates exceeding the pure-loss and matched thermal-loss repeaterless bounds. These results extend the twin-field advantage to Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum cryptography.

articles.title: Classical phase unwrapping enables large-time-step unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For computing molecular energies on early fault-tolerant hardware, unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization (UQKSD) avoids both the deep circuits of quantum phase estimation and the Pauli-term sampling of variational methods by extracting the energies from a projected real-time propagator. At a small time step τ, nearly linearly dependent Krylov vectors make the overlap matrix ill-conditioned. Our tests at fixed total evolution time show that additional Krylov vectors then add no accuracy, while the thresholded energy becomes increasingly sensitive to the choice of cutoff. A larger time step improves the conditioning and reduces the Krylov dimension M needed for a target accuracy, but the energies are then known only modulo 2π/τ. We present Classical Unwrapping for Resolving Eigenvalues (CURE-QKSD), a classical post-processing method that leaves the UQKSD circuits and generalized eigenvalue problem unchanged and recovers the missing multiples of 2π/τ from phase-consistency landscapes of one or, when needed, two UQKSD runs. In noiseless tests on six molecules with 12--20 qubits, all 28 targeted energies are recovered in their aliased regimes with final errors of at most 1.1×10⁻⁷~Ha. Under Gaussian noise with σ=10⁻⁴, the median error of the ground or first excited state reaches chemical accuracy at large aliased time steps with M=20--65, whereas uncorrected principal-branch energies are off by 0.7--115~Ha. CURE-QKSD therefore makes aliased time steps usable for UQKSD calculations with smaller, better-conditioned Krylov bases.

articles.title: The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969. Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) still show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD. Regge exchange organizes the fragmentation region in triple-Regge form. It supplies the diffractive mass law of the excited systems, with the shrinkage of the Pomeron in its transfer dependence. Finite-energy sum rules and the two-component duality of Harari and Freund equate averaged towers of resonances with that exchange. Duality therefore motivates describing the excited systems in hadronic degrees of freedom. The review follows the cascade description through its predecessors, namely the fireballs of Niu, the novas of Jacob and Slansky, the clusters of Hwa, Good-Walker diffraction, and the two-stage dissociation of Hama. HEART (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions) assembles these pieces into an event-level cascade of two-body hadronic transitions. A companion paper (arXiv:2611.11570) defines it and tests it against the NA49 data. The review closes with the fragmentation-region measurements that would separate a resonance cascade from a string, namely the isospin of forward baryons, the local balance of strangeness in associated production, and forward resonance signals with their mass tails.

articles.title: Nucleation of water ice under weak ionization via clustering on negative ions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Water-ice grains are shown to form spontaneously in a cold, weakly-ionized laboratory plasma with trace water admixture when neutrals and ions are cooled below sim200 K. These conditions serve as an analog of ice nucleation in cold astrophysical and atmospheric environments. The ice grains form without the presence of particulate impurities, and do not form in the absence of ionization, indicating that nucleation is induced by ions. Time-resolved ion mass spectrometry provides separate detection of clusters of water molecules on both positive and negative ions. Hydrated negative ions, mainly OH⁻(H₂O)ₙ, grow to sim200 amu, while hydrated positive ions, mainly H⁺(H₂O)ₙ, remain small and short-lived. As the temperature is reduced from room temperature toward 200 K, negative ion clusters grow in size and then drop sharply in abundance, consistent with the onset of rapid growth into macroscopic ice grains below a critical temperature. This indicates that hydrated negative ions are key precursors to ice nucleation in cold, weakly ionized environments, such as the Earth's mesosphere and protoplanetary disks, providing a concrete pathway for ice formation in environments where the nucleation mechanism has remained unresolved. This negative ion pathway is estimated to dominate over ice deposition on pre-existing dust grains in protoplanetary disk locations where there is sufficient UV to partially dissociate water molecules, and in addition, where negative ions such as OH- can form readily through electron attachment at low temperature.

articles.title: Does quantum mechanics apply to macroscopic objects? How to define macro?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2410.17298v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: According to Quantum Mechanics a narrow wave-packet of the center of mass of any macroscopic object should smear out after some time. The problem is usually waved out by assuming that due to their heavy masses this occurs over astronomical times. Without a clear definition of macroscopic objects this remains ambiguous. On the other hand, Quantum Mechanics allows and energetically even prefers largely smeared out c.m. states that never been seen. Why is this the real state of the world we know? Does it suggest a micro-macro threshold with different theoretical descriptions? Does offer micro-miniaturization a hope for answering these questions?

articles.title: Exponentially enhanced sensing through non-reciprocal light propagation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.16895v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-reciprocity is a key resource for pushing the performance of photonic devices beyond the fundamental limits imposed by Lorentz reciprocity. Notably, it was predicted that sensor architectures implementing a bosonic analogue of the Kitaev chain can yield an enhanced signal-to-noise ratio. However, experimental demonstrations of such sensors have so far been limited to small chains. Here we show how this model can be implemented in a scalable optical platform, enabling the detection of weak perturbations with a signal-to-noise ratio, linked to the quantum Fisher information extracted per input photon, that grows exponentially with system size. Our approach encodes two coupled Hatano-Nelson chains---realizing an effective bosonic Kitaev model---within the resonant modes of an electro-optic frequency comb. Non-reciprocal propagation in frequency space is achieved via simultaneous phase and amplitude modulation of the intracavity field. We demonstrate the sensing of a weak modulation tone coupling the two chains, observing an exponential enhancement of the signal-to-noise over three orders of magnitude as the system is scaled to over 70 frequency modes per chain. These results establish a new regime of non-Hermitian sensing, highlighting how non-reciprocal dynamics can be harnessed to achieve exponentially enhanced measurement precision in photonic systems.

articles.title: Free Lunch Uncertainty: Sequence-Level Rényi Entropy from Particle Decoding for Adaptive LLM Reasoning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantifying uncertainty over an entire LLM completion is critical for selective prediction and adaptive compute. Zero-cost signals such as mean token entropy and log-probability are local to tokens or to one completion, and self-consistency needs many extra completions. We show that Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) decoding for power sampling already estimates the normalizing constant of the power distribution, which gives the sequence-level R'enyi entropy (SRE) of the model's completion distribution at zero marginal cost, with a guarantee at every particle budget. A R'enyi chain rule extends this readout to a family of stepwise entropies of any order. We prove that orders above one are tied to the most likely token of each step, which explains why they track log-probability, while the order-1/2 member accumulates the log of per-step search effort. This member is the best zero-cost selective-prediction signal in 10 of 13 settings. On MATH500 its AUROC is 0.022 to 0.044 above log-probability with all four models and within length quartiles, and the same order is selected when each setting is held out. An 8-particle probe identifies the problems that benefit from more particles, and a two-pass policy matches 64-particle accuracy on MATH500 with 34.2% fewer particles over three seeds.

articles.title: Target Selection with a Disappearing-Stimulus Mixed-Reality P300 Interface: Feasibility and Object-Distinguishable Versus Uniform Cues
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-reality (MR) P300 interfaces can register selectable destinations, such as wheelchair goals, directly in the user's surroundings. When the cues disappear between flashes, however, the user must retain an intended target that is no longer visible. We tested whether such an interface supports target selection and whether giving each cue a stable colour-shape identity improves it compared with visually uniform spheres. Six healthy adults completed four trials in each cue condition of a 5x5 row/column task on a head-mounted MR display, with EEG from Fz, Cz, and Pz. Shrinkage linear discriminant analysis was evaluated with nested validation in which complete trials were held out from class balancing, hyperparameter selection, and fitting. Both conditions evoked a parietal target-related positivity. The decoded cell was correct in 18 of 48 held-out trials, against 1.9 expected by chance (binomial p < 1e-12), and in three participants individually. Cue format made no detectable difference: complete-target accuracy was 9/24 in both conditions (paired difference 0.0 percentage points, 95% CI [-37, 37]), and held-out AUC was 0.609 for spheres and 0.585 for object cues. Disappearing-stimulus MR P300 selection is therefore feasible under strict trial-level evaluation, but the benefit of object identity, if any, is too small to resolve in a pilot of this size.

articles.title: One-Sided Expert-Parallel All-to-All for Mixture-of-Experts Inference over NVLink
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Expert parallelism (EP) shards the experts of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layer across GPUs, so every MoE layer requires two all-to-all communications, namely dispatch and combine. Compared with training, inference processes relatively few tokens per GPU at a time, and at small batch sizes fixed costs that do not grow with the number of tokens, rather than data movement, dominate the latency. We present NVLinkOneSided, a one-sided EP all-to-all for GPUs within a single NVLink domain. Each source rank pushes its tokens, without first exchanging metadata, into rank-major buffers on the target GPUs, and the grouped GEMMs read them in place instead of from a per-expert copy. We provide two protocols for the synchronization that the communication requires, namely Fence and Sentinel, for high-throughput and low-latency scenarios respectively. On Blackwell GPUs, NVLinkOneSided completes dispatch and combine 1.2-3.0× faster than DeepEP, with the largest speedups at small batch sizes. The resulting MoE layer is up to 2.4× faster than DeepEP with DeepGEMM. It even outperforms the fused DeepGEMM MegaMoE at up to 128 tokens per GPU, making it still competitive for decoding. We expose NVLinkOneSided through a modular interface, so that it is agnostic to the activation quantization format, decoupled from the MoE compute backend and easy to integrate into inference frameworks.

articles.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second. Every observation influences the estimate in two roles, through its own evaluation when it is held out and through the models it helps fit when it trains. The random splits determine its weight in each role. From this representation, we prove an exact finite-sample identity for the variance of the cross-validated estimate. For a given splitting scheme with a common training set size, the variance is a function of these weights, with constants of the model, the metric, and the population. It covers metrics averaged over observations, such as mean squared error, and over case--control pairs, such as the AUC. The identity shows which schemes to use. The variance decomposes into sampling variance, which depends only on the training size, and variance due to the random fold splitting, which arises when the weights change from one draw of the splits to the next. K-fold cross-validation, whose weights are equal across observations by design, is therefore variance optimal at first order; Monte Carlo and bootstrap cross-validation are not. The first-order variance of K-fold does not depend on K, and under reasonable conditions on the model leave-one-out has the smallest variance of any K-fold scheme. For the AUC the same holds for leave-pair-out, which evaluates every case--control pair. Finally, we show the cross-validated estimate is asymptotically normal with the identity's full variance. Together, these results provide a general theoretical foundation for inference on cross-validated performance and establish principles for selecting variance-optimal cross-validation designs.

articles.title: From Process Models to Composable Agentic Workflows: Combining BPMN, Agents and Enterprise Knowledge
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based agents can reason, use tools and collaborate. However, coordinating increasingly complex agentic applications becomes difficult to understand, monitor and improve. Decisions distributed across prompts, tool calls and application logic make workflows implicit. We introduce **Recursive Capability Composition**, enabling agents to execute business processes and expose them as reusable Agentic Tools. This paper presents a BPMN-based approach to Agentic Workflows, combining explicit orchestration with autonomous reasoning. SemTalk BPMN models are transformed into executable workflows using a LangGraph/Pregel runtime. Agentic Tasks introduce LLM reasoning at selected activities, while conventional BPMN controls process flows, deterministic decisions, system interactions and human approvals. Agentic Participants provide reusable interfaces for agent behavior or other executable processes. BPMN orchestration makes multi-agent systems more understandable and manageable. Explicit process models provide developers and operators with a shared view of workflow structures and execution progress, facilitating debugging, monitoring and optimization. Enterprise agents also need organization-specific context. Process Models and Knowledge Graphs describe activities, participants, information objects, decisions and relationships between processes. They provide structured knowledge of how an organization operates, supporting informed agent decisions and actions. Our contributions are threefold: 1. **Model-Driven Execution:** Transforming BPMN models into executable Agentic Workflows. 2. **Recursive Capability Composition:** Exposing agents and executable business processes as reusable tools for other agents. 3. **Enterprise Context:** Using Process Models and Ontologies to provide organization-specific knowledge for agent reasoning.

articles.title: ExpertCrowd-SWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Expert-Authored Engineering Tasks in Unfamiliar Codebases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ExpertCrowd-SWE (EC-SWE) is a benchmark of 100 expert-authored, multi-file software engineering tasks for evaluating autonomous coding agents in large, unfamiliar codebases. Each task is a change request written by a practising engineer against a pinned commit of a real repository, paired with a sealed reference solution and a task-specific grader whose weighted, mostly executable criteria award partial credit; must-pass blockers and pass/fail gates encode what a maintainer would refuse to merge. The tasks span 87 open-source projects and 11 languages. The median ticket is 148 words, while the median reference solution changes 471 lines. Every task image is calibrated before release so that the reference solution scores 1.0 and both the untouched repository and an inert change score 0; nearly half of the tasks also ship alternative, lazy and adversarial control patches that the grader must classify correctly. The final 100 tasks were selected for difficulty against current frontier models. We evaluate seven frontier models, five runs each (3,495 scored runs), in a single platform harness that gives each model its provider-native tool interface. Claude Opus 5.5 (67.3%) and GPT-6 Astra (63.7%) lead without a statistically significant gap, followed by Claude Fable 5.1 (46.5%), Gemini 3.8 Flash (40.0%), and a statistically indistinguishable group of Qwen 3.8 Max, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Grok 4.6 (32-34%). No task is fully solved by every model, and on 80 tasks no model earns full credit on all five runs. Scores span 35 points. Depending on the model, agents take a median of 33 to 166 steps per run, with little relation to score. We release 24 tasks with their environments, graders and results, and hold out 76 to limit contamination.

articles.title: Agent-Guided Discovery of Exchange-Correlation Functionals with Physics-based Validation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate, compact exchange--correlation functionals are central to predictive density functional theory. Symbolic search and language-model agents can propose new functional forms, but it remains unclear whether their gains survive self-consistency and external evaluation, whether the new terms carry physical content, whether agents outperform evolutionary search, and how language-model backbones compare. We connect frontier LLM agents to a GPU evaluator through the Model Context Protocol, with training-only fitting, persistent memory, and self-consistent and external evaluation. Opus-5.5 agents passed the screening gate with about 40-fold fewer tokens than Codex (GPT-6-Astra) agents and found a candidate with lower validation and held-out errors; only this candidate advanced to self-consistent evaluation. The resulting 13-parameter functional, O159, multiplies same-spin correlation by a smooth density window. Refitted controls favor a window that scales the entire same-spin factor, reducing it by 15--30% at its peak, and that acts on reaction energies mainly in near-iso-orbital regions; against a refitted no-window control, it lowers heavy-atom total-energy errors on GSCDB137 by 29%. With about 400 fits each, SyFES evolution did not improve on its GAS22 seed, whereas the agents found forms 0.10--0.13 kcal lower in validation error by adding an explicit density scale. Self-consistent O159 lowers the held-out MGCDB84 test error of ωB97M-V by 11.7%, and its mean normalized error ratio on 36 GSCDB137 datasets (1.139) is comparable to ωB97M-V (1.144) and below GAS22 (1.190). Frontier-LLM agents thus produced O159, a compact functional whose improvement over ωB97M-V survives self-consistent, physics-based validation.

articles.title: Darmok: Championship Cryptic Crossword Solving via Constraint Tightening and Resilient Orchestration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Darmok, the first automated system to reach superhuman performance on British cryptic crosswords. Unlike American-style crosswords, cryptic clues disguise an unmarked definition and compositional wordplay beneath a misleading surface reading, sparse grids leave nearly half of each word's letters unchecked, and tournament rules rank a grid with even a single wrong or blank square behind all error-free solutions regardless of speed. Competing alongside an elite human field at the 55th Times Crossword Championship in London, Darmok solved all seven championship puzzles error-free and finished faster than every human competitor in every round. It solved the Final puzzle in 6m 52s, a full 3m 13s ahead of the human champion. Today's frontier AI models can on average solve a whole puzzle in a single try with comparable accuracy and speed. However, cloud API calls still stall, time out, trigger safety refusals, or get stuck in reasoning loops. To simultaneously achieve tournament-grade accuracy, speed, and reliability, Darmok cross-checks clues across three independent models in rounds; uses verified crossing letters to unlock harder clues; and uses a whole-puzzle model and dictionary lookups to fill any remaining gaps without overwriting confirmed words. This design maintained near-zero-error performance across a five-month daily evaluation period. Under normal benchmark conditions, removing backup models, fallback steps, or elaborate prompt instructions barely changes accuracy, making the architecture appear over-engineered. Yet during both the worst days of daily operation and a severe slowdown of our primary model in the live Championship Final, the backup paths carried the solve, showing that as foundation models master the average case, the central challenge in building complex AI systems shifts to resilience in the worst case.

articles.title: Earth Embeddings in Environmental Remote Sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Earth observations from satellite platforms have profoundly transformed research and applications across numerous domains. However, uneven observation coverage and frequent data gaps continue to limit their ability to capture Earth's surface dynamics. Moreover, processing multi-modal Earth observations requires substantial computational resources and sophisticated data harmonization frameworks, which may not be readily accessible to many remote sensing practitioners. Earth embeddings have emerged as promising solutions to these challenges. As general-purpose representations converted from multi-source Earth observations, Earth embeddings can support a wide range of downstream tasks with no requirement of task-specific feature design and preprocessing. In this study, we first introduce the theoretical foundations of Earth embeddings. Then, we review several representative Earth embedding products. We next examine the applications of Earth embeddings across six major domains of environmental remote sensing. Finally, we systematically assess the performance of Earth embeddings in four downstream tasks, including hyperspectral image classification, individual tree crown segmentation, crop yield prediction, and aboveground biomass mapping. Our review and case studies suggest that, despite several advantages over conventional Earth observation data, current Earth embeddings do not always outperform remote sensing imagery or hand-crafted features. Earth embeddings should not be viewed as a direct replacement for conventional EO data, but rather as representations that provide stable information across space and time. Remote sensing practitioners may consider evaluating Earth embeddings' suitability for specific tasks and using them strategically, rather than assuming superior performance by default.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.14493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. Our results demonstrate that (1) the information available to the evaluation harness determines evaluation quality, (2) functional and security evaluation are complementary, and (3) LLM-based evaluation harnesses surface subtle errors that human reviewers miss. We recommend a two-framework strategy: trace-based evaluation for functional assessment and adversarial red-teaming for security validation.

articles.title: Code-Grounded Agentic Explanations for Static Analysis Vulnerability Findings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Static application security testing (SAST) tools surface vulnerabilities early and their verdicts are rule-based and auditable. Yet developers routinely dismiss findings they cannot interpret. Large language models can supply the missing explanation, but designs that also hand the model the detection give up the auditability that makes static analysis defensible. We keep detection with the analyser and give the model only the explaining. A preliminary user study with 20 participants and a workshop with 19 practitioners yielded five requirements. Guided by these we redesigned SAFE, an open-source IntelliJ IDEA plugin that explains findings from any analyser reporting in the Static Analysis Results Interchange Format. It tiers explanations by demand, ties them to the reported data flow, and replaces the single-prompt backend with an agent that must consult the repository and the rule that fired before answering. A within-subjects crossover experiment with 24 participants compared the redesign against its predecessor. Perceived usability rose from 77.3 to 85.0 on the System Usability Scale. Actionability gained most among the explanation-quality items, the aspect both earlier studies flagged as weakest, and the odds of a correct remediation were 2.6 times higher. Triage accuracy and time per finding were indistinguishable, which we read as uninformative rather than as equivalence. Trust was the one measure that did not move, and the closing interviews indicate that grounding made findings easier to understand rather than easier to believe. Participants also drew a boundary no requirement anticipated, wanting the tool to find and explain while they judge and apply.

articles.title: AgentScript-Eval: Benchmarking LLMs and Agents for Code Generation in an Enterprise DSL
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.13183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Domain-specific languages (DSLs) are widely used in enterprise software, giving a compact interface to complex tasks, from data access to infrastructure automation. Platforms increasingly extend them to agents, where a developer declares the topics, permitted actions, and guardrails of an agent rather than writing general-purpose code. Large language models (LLMs) write general-purpose code well, but that ability has been measured almost entirely on languages abundant in public pretraining data, and enterprise DSLs are neither abundant nor public. We introduce AgentScript-Eval, an execution-graded benchmark of 100 real tasks for AgentScript, the declarative DSL that Salesforce uses in Agentforce to build conversational agents. Tasks span authoring an agent from a specification, debugging a broken definition, and optimizing a working one. Evaluating five models zero-shot, we find that the regime is hard: the best model reaches only 25.0% pass@3, and every model scores 0% on authoring from scratch. We further find that model scale and price are weak predictors of success -- a 31B open-weight model attains the highest compilation rate of any model tested (48.0%) and matches the strongest frontier model on partial-credit accuracy at the lowest token cost. Adding an agentic compile-and-edit loop is the single largest lever, roughly doubling partial-credit accuracy. Beyond that gain, the wording of domain guidance matters more than its packaging. The same skill pack scores 28% as plain documentation but only 14% as a live plugin. Rewriting one skill inside that plugin then raises it to 37%, our best result, with catalog and tooling untouched. Larger models did not reliably outperform smaller ones; what mattered was the harness surrounding the model and the guidance supplied to it.

articles.title: The Two Clocks of Carbon-Market Governance: National Approval Synchronisation and International Registry Visibility in the CDM-to-PACM Transition
articles.abstract: International carbon-crediting mechanisms combine project-initiated applications with nationally signed acts and centrally published registers. The resulting event dates need not coincide. We construct a project-level audit of the transition from the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) to the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM), comparing a frozen 8 October 2026 UNFCCC export with a separately acquired 9 November export. Among 285 approved Project Activities (PAs) from 20 host countries with at least five approved activities, the mean country-specific share concentrated on the most common approval date is 89.4%, compared with 38.0% for the original transition-request dates of those same projects (difference 51.3 percentage points; country-cluster bootstrap 95% interval 38.2–63.5). In exploratory, week-constrained permutations preserving country-week composition and the global within-week date distribution, no allocation among 1,800 simulations reaches the observed concentration (Monte Carlo p = 0.00056). A separate programme-level audit finds that 24 of 33 distinct host-country-by-date approval events for Programmes of Activities (PoAs) coincide with a same-country PA approval date (week-constrained p = 0.0072). Two official exports differ in 145 cells across 37 common records; two newly visible approvals were dated before the national deadline, while one historically irregular activity disappears from the later export without demonstrated withdrawal. The dated national act and its public appearance therefore encode different observables. These results document cross-activity temporal synchronisation and registry-version sensitivity, not collective governmental deliberation, causal approval preferences, or independent UNFCCC receipt timestamps. We propose event-centred reporting that preserves country, activity type, signed date, publication date and snapshot provenance.

articles.title: Critical Crossings and Quantum Friction in a Finite-Time XY-Chain Otto Engine
articles.abstract: We investigate the finite-time performance of a quantum Otto engine with a transverse-field anisotropic XY spin chain as its working medium. By decomposing the chain into independent momentum sectors, we calculate mode-resolved transition probabilities during linear transverse-field ramps. We determine the resulting excitation density, work, heat, efficiency, and power for driving protocols in which the transverse field is varied linearly between prescribed endpoints during the two unitary strokes, while the anisotropy remains fixed. Protocols crossing one or both quantum critical points exhibit Kibble--Zurek scaling, nₑₓsimτ⁻¹/², whereas protocols that maintain a nonzero energy gap throughout the ramps exhibit the faster decay nₑₓsimτ⁻², where τ is the duration of each ramp. The work separates into an endpoint-dependent adiabatic contribution and a nonnegative contribution associated with quantum friction. At short driving times, quantum friction can exceed the adiabatic work output and prevent heat-engine operation. At long driving times, the thermodynamic quantities approach adiabatic values determined by the endpoint spectra and thermal population imbalances. Increasing anisotropy suppresses excitations and hastens the approach to the adiabatic limit. These results distinguish endpoint thermodynamics from critical-crossing dynamics and clarify their roles in finite-time engine performance.

articles.title: In Situ Block Lifting Strategies for Fragile Waterlogged Archaeological Remains: A Case Study from the Nanhai No. 1 Shipwreck
articles.abstract: Fragile remains from waterlogged and high-humidity environments often present considerable challenges for in situ recovery due to long-term degradation, reduced mechanical strength, and the need to preserve archaeological context. Block lifting can effectively recover fragile remains while preserving spatial relationships, though the choice of strategy depends on preservation conditions and field requirements. This study examines the development and application of in situ block lifting strategies during the long-term excavation of the Nanhai No. 1 shipwreck. Based on archaeological assessment and recovery requirements, three strategies were developed: direct lifting, single-material lifting, and multimaterial lifting. The multimaterial strategy integrated menthol, polyurethane bandages, plaster, and polyurethane foam, with each material performing specific functions in surface protection, conformable reinforcement, and external structural support. These strategies were applied under monitored high-humidity conditions (RH frequently exceeding 85%) to recover wooden components, fragile organic remains, and complex assemblages. The results demonstrate that condition-based selection of lifting strategies enabled safe recovery while preserving morphology and spatial relationships. The Nanhai No. 1 excavation provides practical insights into integrating archaeological assessment, material selection, and structural support during in situ recovery of fragile remains.

articles.title: Porous Cellulose/Zn-Containing Composite Aerogel with Zinc Nitrate Hexahydrate as a Hydrated-Salt Phase Change Material: Synthesis Optimization and Thermal Performance
articles.abstract: Salt hydrates are attractive phase change materials for low-temperature thermal energy storage, but supercooling, phase segregation and leakage limit their use. In this study, cotton cellulose fibers were mixed with aqueous zinc nitrate hexahydrate at 75 or 85°C, at cotton-to-salt mass ratios of 0.5–1%, and freeze-dried. The composites were screened by infrared spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction, and one composite was further examined by scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, thermogravimetry and differential scanning calorimetry. The infrared spectra were dominated by nitrate and water bands, and the surface particles had a composition (Zn 35.5, N 12.8 and O 51.7 wt%) close to that of zinc nitrate. The diffraction patterns showed narrow reflections of crystalline Zn-containing phases, including reflections compatible with layered zinc hydroxide nitrate, whereas zinc oxide was not a major phase. The selected composite melted with an onset of 34.9°C and a peak at 40.4°C, and its enthalpy of fusion (157.1 J/g) was close to that reported for the pure salt hydrate. Dehydration began at about 63°C, which sets the upper limit of the working temperature. Mercury intrusion porosimetry of P2T2M2 showed a dominant peak at 82.73 µm equivalent diameter, a cumulative intrusion volume of 273.86 mm³/g and 13.61% porosity, consistent with accessible pore space after freeze-drying. A small fraction of cotton cellulose can therefore host the salt hydrate without loss of its latent heat, while crystallization behavior, cycling stability and leakage resistance remain to be evaluated before practical use.

articles.title: BMS constrained PSO optimized multistage fast charging of an electric vehicle battery in a PV grid hybrid DC charging station
articles.abstract: Fast charging of electric vehicles (EVs) is limited by the cell voltage and temperature limits enforced by the battery management system (BMS), while hybrid charging stations must also keep grid power quality within standards. This paper presents a BMS constrained multistage constant current (MSCC) charging algorithm optimized by particle swarm optimization (PSO) for a PV grid hybrid DC fast charging station. The station, modelled in MATLAB/Simulink, comprises a unity power factor front end converter, an isolated DC to DC charger, a 14.4 kWp photovoltaic array with perturb and observe maximum power point tracking (MPPT) on an 800 V DC link, and a 54 Ah pack of temperature dependent cells with cell to cell variation. The BMS combines four current stages, a 4.2 V constant voltage loop on the highest cell and thermal derating between 40 and 45 °C; PSO tunes the stage currents and state of charge breakpoints. The optimized profile charges the pack from 20 % to 80 % in 22.6 min, 38.1 % faster than 1C constant current constant voltage (CCCV) charging and 6.1 % faster than CCCV at equal peak current, with all cells below 4.201 V and 43.5 °C. At 45 °C ambient the reduction reaches 29.8 %. Rerating the front end converter lowers the grid current total demand distortion from 9.71 % to 2.66 % (2.91 % with PV), a power factor of 0.991. The MPPT extracts over 98.2 % of the available PV power, supplying up to 34.9 % of the station input without affecting the charging current.

articles.title: Vibrational Intensification of Mass Transfer Across the Interface Between Viscous Liquids
articles.abstract: Vibrations are an effective tool for controlling fluid motion and mass transfer, in particular under microgravity conditions. The study addresses a topical technological problem: the intensification of mass transfer across the interface between immiscible high-viscosity liquids. The time-averaged flow in a flat vertical cell, generated by oscillations of a body at the interface between two viscous fluids, is investigated experimentally. The body has the shape of a parallelepiped elongated along the interface, with straight (beveled) edges. It is found that oscillations of the body perpendicular to the interface induce intense time-averaged flows in the form of a pair of large-scale vortices in each fluid, encompassing the entire cell volume. The flow direction is opposite to that of the known case of steady streaming in low-viscosity fluids. The dependence of the structure and intensity of the time-averaged flows on the vibration parameters is determined. It is shown that the detected time-averaged flow intensifies the mass transfer of a substance dissolved in one of the fluids across the interface; the mass transfer rate exceeds the diffusion rate by several orders of magnitude. The discovered vibration-induced effect is novel and can be effectively used in technological processes, in particular under reduced gravity conditions.

articles.title: Spatio-Temporal Assessment of Glacier Changes (1990-2025) and Their Relationship with Climate Variability in the Tirich Mir Region, Hindu Kush, Pakistan
articles.abstract: Glaciers of the Hindu Kush region in northern Pakistan are important freshwater sources, yet; their response to recent climate variability remains spatially heterogeneous. This study assessed spatio-temporal changes between years 1990 and 2025 in five major glaciers of the Tirich Mir including massif—Dirgoi, Lower Tirich, North Barum, Owir, and South Barum—using multi-temporal Landsat imagery, the Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI), ASTER GDEM terrain data, and GIS-based area analysis. Landsat-5 TM, Landsat-7 ETM+, Landsat-8 OLI, and Landsat-9 OLI-2 images were analyzed for years 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, and 2025, respectively. Climate variability was evaluated using NASA POWER summer-temperature and winter-precipitation data in R/R-Studio through linear regression, the Mann-Kendall test, Sen's slope, and Pearson correlation. Overall study findings show that total glacier extent has decreased from 64.23 km² in 1990 to 52.81 km² in 2025, corresponding to a loss of 11.42 km² (17.8%). The NDSI-derived clean-ice/snow-covered surface has declined from 36.89 km² in 1990 to 5.21 km² in 2010 and subsequently increased to 30.83 km² in 2025. Mapped debris-covered ice has increased from 27.34 km² in 1990 to 54.53 km² in 2010, while declined to 21.98 km² in 2025. Summer temperature showed a significant increasing trend (Sen's slope = 0.070°C yr⁻¹, p = 0.0071) during period of 2005–2025, whereas winter precipitation showed no significant trend. Correlations between the mapped clean-ice surface and temperature (r = -0.17, p = 0.782) and precipitation (r = 0.40, p = 0.508) were non-significant. Hence, glacier shrinkage in the Tirich Mir region occurred concurrently with significant regional warming, whereas precipitation exhibited no statistically significant trend. Overallglacier variability was found to be influenced by factors such as debris cover, topography, and seasonal snow conditions. Focusing on glaciated terrains, present study approach will be helpful in prospective studies of regional cryosphere assessment.

articles.title: An Intelligent Fiber-Shaped Photodetector Array Featuring High-Linearity Opto-Mechanical Response
articles.abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is accelerating the development of fiber-based photodetectors (FPDs), driving further transformation and progress of the electronics industry. Nevertheless, the transition of FPDs from laboratory prototypes to viable daily-use technologies necessitates extensive research on multifunctional capabilities. Addressing this gap, we pioneer a highly intelligent strain-opto dual-mode sensing platform based on MoS₂/PEDOT:PSS heterojunction FPD array for wearable applications. Circumventing traditional vertical heterostructures that focus on piezoelectric-induced intensity enhancement, our work prioritizes linearity optimization through precise interfacial engineering. A key breakthrough of this work lies in the integration of PEDOT:PSS as a conductive pathway, which endows the device with an exceptionally linear strain-dependent photocurrent response (R2ཞ0.93), thereby providing a reliable foundation for co-located photoelectric and mechanical sensing. First-principles calculations uncover that the higher-loaded PEDOT:PSS layer introduces uniformly distributed metal-induced gap states (MIGS) and stabilizes the Fermi level via pinning effects, ensuring that strain-induced band offsets modulate carrier transport in a strictly linear regime. Furthermore, to address the inherent signal coupling in practical wearable scenarios, a system-level AI-driven decoupling framework is implemented, enabling the resolution of complex, overlapping inputs into independent data streams with high fidelity.

articles.title: Flame Retardancy and Reinforcement–Toughening Mechanism of Epoxy Resin Modified with a Phosphorus–Nitrogen Synergistic Imidazolium Ionic Liquid
articles.abstract: Epoxy resin (EP) is widely used in engineering applications, but it has inherent flammability issues, and balancing its flame retardancy with mechanical properties also poses challenges. In this study, a phosphorus and nitrogen-containing amide-functionalized imidazoline ionic liquid − 1-(carbamoylmethyl)-2-methylimidazolium dihydrogen phosphate ([CMMIm][H2PO4]) was synthesized, and it was introduced as a multifunctional flame retardant modifier into EP. Through LOI, TGA, cone calorimeter method, Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscope (SEM), and mechanical tests, the effects of [CMMIm][H2PO4] on flame retardancy, thermal degradation, carbonization formation and mechanical properties were systematically investigated. The addition of [CMMIm][H2PO4] significantly improved the fire resistance of EP. The LOI value of EP-4 increased from 20.41% to 30.68%, while the PHRR value decreased from 923.43 kW·m− 2 to 563.61 kW·m− 2, a reduction of approximately 39%. At 800°C, the carbonized residue content increased from 11.64% to 16.90%, and the ID/IG ratio decreased from 0.85 to 0.78, indicating a more stable carbonization structure. Meanwhile, EP-4 exhibited tensile strength of 73.91 MPa, bending modulus of 3522.38 MPa and impact strength of 16.75 kJ·m− 2. These results indicate that [CMMIm][H2PO4] is an effective strategy that can enhance the flame retardancy of epoxy resin while improving its mechanical properties.

articles.title: Crystal structure of N,N′-bis(tert-butoxycarbonyl)-5,10-dihydrophenazine and periodic DFT- D3(BJ) analysis of the interplay of π-stacking and C-H···O interactions
articles.abstract: The crystal structure of N,N′-bis(tert-butoxycarbonyl)-5,10-dihydrophenazine, a valuable synthetic precursor for phenazine chemistry, and the first example of a carbamate derivative of dihydrophenazine, was determined (triclinic space group P(:stackrel-1) with Z = 2). The 5,10-dihydrophenazine core adopts a boat, i.e. cis-conformation core, while bulky tert-butyl groups hindering tight packing. Hirshfeld surface analysis shows two groups of interactions, the numerically minor, but relatively stronger CH···O (11.5%) and CH···C (19.7%), which are relatively isolated in comparison to weak H···H (65.7%) vdW interactions. Under these constraints, the concave molecules self-assemble in pairs, with one stronger slip-stacked π···π interaction and two weaker, symmetry-equivalent edge-to-face C-H···π interactions acting cooperatively. Periodic density functional theory (DFT; PBE-D3(BJ), validated against four X23 reference crystals) gives 130.7 kJ mol− 1 lattice energy, dominated by dispersion. The symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT) analysis of the symmetry-independent molecular pairs allows direct structural rationalization for the given molecular conformation: four relatively strong pairs were found, the second strongest being the π···π slip stacked pair, whose computed distance closely matches the crystallographic value, although the underlying slip angle differs somewhat. Weaker pairwise interactions, mainly H···H contacts of the tert-butyl groups, contribute little to the lattice energy, isolating the concurrence of the stronger CH···O and CH···C interactions. The SAPT decomposition demonstrates a good structural predictability for weakly interacting dimeric aggregates of dihydrophenazines, while the demonstrated Boc-substituted example represents a general rational approach towards supramolecular dimers for fine-tuning of physico-optical properties.

articles.title: Experimental and Modelling Analysis of Electrolyte Effects in Zinc-Modified MnO₂/Graphene Symmetric Supercapacitor
articles.abstract: Aqueous symmetric supercapacitors are promising and sustainable energy storage devices with low cost, low toxicity, operational safety and simple design, using the same active material in both electrodes. Here, we investigate the effect of electrolyte on the interfacial charge storage by testing zinc-doped manganese dioxide/graphene (Zn-MnO2/G) nanocomposite electrodes in symmetric cells using KOH and Na2SO4 electrolyte. The composite combined the pseudocapacitive redox activity of MnO2 with the electronic conductivity and surface accessibility of graphene, and the Zn incorporation was intended to modify the local defect chemistry and charge-transfer behavior. Nitrogen adsorption-desorption analysis suggested mesoporous texture with cumulative pore volume of 0.0453 cm3 g− 1, pore surface area of about 13.0 m2 g− 1 and dominant pore width of about 3.38 nm that can facilitate electrolyte penetration and access to redox-active sites. Electrochemical measurements demonstrated that the studied symmetric cell configuration showed electrolyte-dependent capacitive behavior. The KOH-based device showed lower impedance, more favorable capacitive relaxation and better energy-density retention than the Na2SO4based device. The rate-capability fitting also showed a smaller rate-induced energy loss in KOH. The improvement in the porous Zn-MnO2/G electrode was ascribed to more favorable ion transport, lower interfacial resistance and more efficient utilization of Mn redox-active sites in the alkaline electrolyte. These results suggest that the device-level performance of Zn-MnO2/G symmetric supercapacitors is significantly affected by the electrolyte selection.

articles.title: Effects of Ground Tire Rubber and Trans-Polyoctenamer on the Rheological Properties and Aging Response of Asphalt Binders
articles.abstract: The sustainable management of end-of-life tires represents a persistent environmental challenge, with declining recycling rates leading to increased landfilling and associated ecological risks. This research aligns with the conference theme by presenting a waste-to-resource pathway that transforms ground tire rubber (GTR) into a high-value modifier for asphalt binders, simultaneously addressing waste diversion and infrastructure performance needs. With transportation agencies increasingly specifying higher performance grades such as PG 82 − 22 for demanding applications, this study investigates whether elevated dosages of GTR can serve as a primary, sustainable modifier to meet these specifications. Through a comprehensive experimental program, base binders (PG 64 − 22 and polymer-modified PG 76 − 22) were modified with GTR contents ranging from 10% to 15% and 3% to 8%, respectively, both with and without the compatibility agent trans-polyoctenamer (TOR). Advanced rheological testing using DSR and BBR coupled with chemical characterization via FTIR spectroscopy, evaluated performance and aging characteristics. Results demonstrate that a 15% GTR dosage successfully elevates the high-temperature grade of a base binder from PG 64 to PG 82, achieving the target specification while maintaining critical low-temperature performance. The incorporation of GTR significantly enhanced rutting resistance and elastic response, with the hybrid use of TOR further improving binder compatibility and long-term durability. Critically, this approach can increase the consumption of recycled tire rubber in asphalt by over 50% compared to conventional practice. This study concludes that high-dosage GTR modification presents a technically viable and environmentally strategic method to produce superior asphalt binders. It provides a direct, scalable pathway to enhance the circular economy for scrap tires, reduce reliance on virgin polymer modifiers, and support the development of sustainable, high-performance infrastructure. The findings offer actionable insights for policymakers, material developers, and transportation agencies seeking to integrate waste recycling objectives with advanced engineering performance.

articles.title: Continuous glucose monitoring earbuds for periodic metabolic sensing
articles.abstract: The applications of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) are expanding into wellness, sports and preventive health, where metabolic information is particularly valuable around specific physiological events. However, conventional CGMs remain tailored to diabetes management, requiring around-the-clock, fixed wear even when periodic monitoring is sufficient. Here, we introduce the continuous glucose in-ear monitor (cGEM), an earbud-integrated platform for periodic, on-demand glucose monitoring from in-ear sweat. The cGEM establishes a skin–sensor interface through simple insertion and removal, enabling repeated monitoring without adhesive fixation. The platform integrates osmotic sweat extraction, microfluidic sampling and electrochemical glucose sensing while retaining audio playback. Computational modelling and in vitro characterization demonstrated controlled fluid transport and reliable glucose sensing. Dual-channel adaptive noise cancellation and personalized calibration reduce on-body signal artifacts and account for individual differences in blood–sweat glucose relationships. Despite periodic use, the cGEM showed close agreement with a continuously worn commercial CGM, achieving a mean absolute relative difference (MARD) of 8.79% across more than 50 h of monitoring. Repeated 1.5–5 h sessions captured event-specific glucose responses with a Pearson correlation coefficient of r = 0.88 relative to the commercial CGM. By integrating molecular sensing into widely used wireless earbuds, cGEM opens new possibilities for widespread adoption of metabolic monitoring, making it as accessible and routine as listening to music.
